Fusion CX Reports Strong Q2FY27 with 22.1% YoY Revenue Growth and PAT at INR 586 Mn up by 31.3% YoY
Kolkata, India – 14th November 2026: Fusion CX Limited (BSE: 544995 | NSE: FUSIONCX), an AI-first customer experience (CX) and AI data service provider, today announced its unaudited consolidated financial results for the Second Quarter and Half Year of FY27, ended 30th September 2026. KEY HIGHLIGHTS – Q2FY27
 Revenue from operations stood at INR 5,253 Mn, a growth of 22.1% on a YoY basis.
 Diversified revenue mix across verticals:
o High-Tech, Travel and Others (HTT) contributed 16.1% of the revenues.
o BFSI contributed 18.2% of the revenues.
o Retail contributed 12.0% of the revenues.
o Healthcare and life sciences contributed 14.5% of the revenues.
 EBITDA stood at INR 976 Mn, a growth of 15.2% on a YoY basis with an EBITDA margin of 18.6%.
 Profit After Tax (PAT) stood at INR 586 Mn, a growth of 31.3% on a YoY basis with a PAT margin of 11.2%.
 Top 5 and top 10 clients contributed 36.5% and 48.9% of revenues, respectively. KEY HIGHLIGHTS – H1FY27
 Revenue from Operations stood at INR 10,158 Mn, a growth of 20.4% on a YoY basis.
 EBITDA was at INR 1,927 Mn, a growth of 27.7% on a YoY basis with an EBITDA margin of 19.0%.
 Profit After Tax (PAT) stood at INR 1,142 Mn, a growth of 56.3% on a YoY basis with a PAT margin of 11.2%.
 Diluted Earning per share (EPS) stood at INR 8.96, a growth of 55.8% on a YoY basis.

COMMENTING ON THE RESULTS
Pankaj Dhanuka, Chairman, Managing Director and CEO, Fusion CX, said: “We are pleased to report a strong quarter, with revenue growth of 22.1% YoY, reflecting the increasing strength and diversification of our business. We are seeing a healthier mix across verticals and clients, a rising contribution from digital solutions, and strong momentum in onshore delivery. Importantly, PAT grew 31.3% YoY against revenue growth of 22.1%, and for the half-year EBITDA grew 27.7% against revenue growth of 20.4%, demonstrating operating leverage as we scale. With continued investments in talent and our AI-first capabilities, we remain focused on building a diversified, technology-led and profitable business. Our recent acquisition of Impacx marks another important milestone for Fusion CX, establishing our presence in Germany and strengthening our capabilities in the European market. Its enterprise relationships, German-language expertise and AI-enabled technology complement our AI-first strategy and global delivery platform, creating opportunities to deliver a broader and increasingly technology-led proposition to our clients. As we embark on our journey as a listed company, our focus remains firmly on sustainable growth, disciplined execution and long-term value creation.” Amit Soni, Chief Financial Officer, Fusion CX, said:
“We delivered a strong performance during Q2FY27, with double-digit growth in revenue and profitability. Reported EBITDA was INR 976 Mn with a margin of 18.6%. PAT rose 31.3% YoY to INR 586 Mn. Cash generation remained strong during the quarter, supporting continued investments in AI capabilities and delivery capacity. With our successful listing in October, we have further strengthened our financial position and flexibility. Around 40% of the IPO proceeds have been deployed to date, primarily towards debt reduction and the Impacx acquisition, in line with the stated objects of the issue. This has also improved our leverage position. The balance proceeds remain allocated towards platform upgrades, overseas debt payments, general corporate purposes and acquisitions, supporting our strategic growth priorities.”

said:
“We are pleased to share our performance for the half year ended September 30, 2026. During the period, the company achieved revenue of
engineered process equipment across pharmaceutical, chemical and allied industries. While we continue to navigate an evolving business
environment, our focus remains on strengthening operational efficiencies, improving profitability and building a sustainable growth trajectory.
During the period, the company continued its efforts towards strengthening its manufacturing infrastructure and optimising its operating cost
structure. A significant initiative in this direction has been the commencement of production in our additional facility, installation of solar power
panels at our manufacturing facility and other operational efficiencies in procurement, planning and sales. Our investment in solar power

We have also continued to focus on strengthening our internal processes, improving production planning and execution, and enhancing operational
controls through the ongoing implementation of SAP and other process improvement initiatives. These measures, coupled with our investments in

efficient and scalable operating environment.

pursuing opportunities across our key end-user industries. Our engineering capabilities, established customer relationships and experience in
executing complex process equipment projects continue to provide a strong foundation for future growth.
As we enter the second half of FY27, our priorities remain centered on profitable business growth, margin improvement, cost optimisation and
disciplined execution. We believe that the operational and cost-efficiency initiatives undertaken by the company, particularly investments in
renewable energy and process improvements, will progressively contribute towards strengthening our financial performance. With improving
manufacturing capabilities and a healthy demand outlook across our key industries, we remain optimistic about the opportunities ahead.
I would like to thank each member of the BEW family, as well as our Clients, Creditors, Banks, Financial Institutions and all other Stakeholders. Their

1. Introduction
We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Standalone Financial Results of Voler
Car Limited ("the Company") for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the year-to-date period
from April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 ("the Statement"), together with the Statement of Assets and
Liabilities as at September 30, 2026 and the Statement of Cash Flows for the half-year ended on that
date. The Statement is being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33
of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended ("the
Listing Regulations"), and has been initialled by us for identification.
This Statement is the responsibility of the Company’s management and has been approved by the Board
of Directors of the Company. Our responsibility is to issue a report on the Statement based on our
review.
2. Scope of Review
We conducted our review in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410,
“Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity”, issued
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the
review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement.
A review is limited primarily to inquiries of Company personnel and analytical procedures applied to
financial data, and thus provides less assurance than an audit. We have not performed an audit and,
accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.
3. Management's Responsibility
This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and has been approved by
the Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and
measurement principles laid down in Accounting Standard 25 "Interim Financial Reporting" ("AS 25"),
prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ("the Act") read with the relevant rules issued
thereunder, and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, and in compliance with
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations.
The Management is also responsible for the design, implementation and maintenance of adequate
internal financial controls relevant to the preparation and presentation of the Statement that is free from
material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and for the comparative figures and other financial
information included in the Statement.
4. Auditor's Responsibility and Scope of Review
Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements
(SRE) 2410, "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the
Entity", issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This Standard requires that we plan
and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material
misstatement.
A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible
for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is
substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with the Standards on Auditing
specified under Section 143(10) of the Act. Consequently, it does not enable us to obtain assurance that
we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we
do not express an audit opinion.
Conclusion
Based on our review conducted as stated above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to
believe that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and
measurement principles laid down in the applicable Accounting Standards prescribed under Section
133 of the Act read with the relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally
accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of Regulation 33
of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any
material misstatement.
Other Matters

[and for the year ended March 31, 2026], included in the Statement, was audited by the predecessor
auditor, M/s Goyal Goyal & Co., Chartered Accountants (Firm's Registration No. 015069C), vide their
report dated 8" May 2026.

Q2& H1 FY27 Earnings Press Release
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Jaspal Singh Chandock, Chairman & Managing Director of BFIL stated:
“H1 FY27 has been a record half for Balu Forge, reflecting the strength of our business and the progress we are
making towards the next phase of growth. Revenue grew 17% to Rs.625 crore, while PAT increased 17% to
Rs.143 crore. EBITDA stood at Rs.179 crore, up 15%, with a margin of 28.6%. Q2 EBITDA margin further improved
by 130 bps to 28.9%. Equally encouraging is the strong cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching
Rs.245 crore, nearly 7x the previous year. Receivables reduced by Rs.31.2 crore, while net debt-to-equity
remained low at 0.04x, reflecting our focus on disciplined execution and a stronger balance sheet.
Building on our 37-year engineering legacy, we are entering the next phase of growth by creating a globally
competitive, integrated precision manufacturing platform. Q2 provides the base before our new capacities
begin contributing to growth. We are scaling forging capacity from 100,000 MTPA to 168,000 MTPA and
precision machining capacity from 58,000 MTPA to 80,000 MTPA . Investments in advanced machining,
automated forging and specialised manufacturing will enable us to bring more complex, higher -value
capabilities in-house and deepen our partnerships with global OEMs.
Our business mix is steadily shifting towards higher-value applications, with Defence, Aerospace and Railways
contributing nearly 50% of our Rs.2,400 crore order book. The new 6.7-metre ring rolling capability further
expands the range and complexity of components we can manufacture. With defence dispatches underway
and expanded capacities progressively coming on stream, we remain confident of delivering 25–30% revenue
growth in FY27.
The promoter group's commitment of up to Rs.162 crore through investments reflects its confidence in our
vision and growth plans. As we move ahead, our focus remains on technology-led expansion, operational
excellence, prudent capital allocation and stronger customer relationships. Our ambition is not just to grow
larger, but to build a globally trusted precision engineering business that creates sustainable, long-term value
for all stakeholders.”

(“the Statement”), attached herewith, being submitted by the Company pursuant to the
requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)
Regulations, 2015, as amended (“the Listing Regulations”).
2. This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company’s Management and approved by the
Company’s Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and
measurement principles laid down in Accounting Standard 25, “Interim Financial Reporting”
(“AS 25”), prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) read with the
relevant rules issued thereunder, and other accounting principles generally accepted in India.
Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review
Engagements (SRE) 2410, “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the
Independent Auditor of the Entity”, issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as
to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement. A review of interim financial
information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and
accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is
substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with the Standards on
Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Act and consequently does not enable us to
obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified
in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.
Basis for Qualified Conclusion
4. Our conclusion is qualified in respect of the following matters:
(a) Capitalisation of furniture, fittings and related labour costs
We draw attention to Note 5 of the Statement regarding Property, Plant and Equipment,
which includes computer, furniture, fittings and related labour costs aggregating ₹286.45
lakh capitalised at multiple locations, having a carrying amount of ₹212.05 lakh as at
September 30, 2026. Management has furnished invoices and a location-wise cost
allocation statement. However, sufficient appropriate evidence establishing the nature
and extent of the work performed, its allocation to individual locations and the dates of
completion (such as a certificate from an architect or other technical expert) has not been
made available to us. In the absence of such evidence, we are unable to comment upon
the adjustments, if any, that may be required to the carrying amount of these assets and
the depreciation charged for the half year, and the consequential impact on the
Statement. The predecessor auditor had modified their opinion in respect of this matter
in their audit report on the financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.
(b) Software development revenue and unreconciled invoice difference
We draw attention to Note 6 of the Statement regarding software development income of
₹97 lakh recognised as unbilled revenue as at March 31, 2026, the corresponding invoice
for which was reported in the GST return for April 2026. In the predecessor auditor’s view,
the software was ready for delivery as at that date and should have been presented as
inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value. The information made available to
us does not establish how the opening unbilled revenue has been adjusted against this
invoice, or the period in which the related revenue and costs should be recognised.
Consequently, we are unable to comment upon the adjustments, if any, that may be
required to the opening balances and the consequential impact on the results for the half
year ended September 30, 2026. The predecessor auditor had modified their opinion in
respect of this matter in their audit report on the financial statements for the year ended
March 31, 2026.
Further, a software invoice of ₹100 lakh recorded in the books of account does not
reconcile with the related accounting records, and a difference of ₹3 lakh remains
unexplained. In the absence of adequate supporting information, we are unable to
comment upon the nature of this difference and the adjustments, if any, that may be
required to the related balances and the Statement.
(c) Revenue from Xera Global Education Private Limited recognised in an earlier
period
We draw attention to Note 7 of the Statement regarding service revenue of ₹332.07 lakh
recognised during the year ended March 31, 2026 from Xera Global Education Private
Limited, a related party, which, in the predecessor auditor’s view, was recognised before
the underlying services had been fully performed. During the half year, the Company has
received ₹19.77 lakh against this receivable. However, such receipts do not by
themselves establish that the services underlying the revenue recognised in the earlier
period have been performed. In the absence of sufficient appropriate evidence, we are
unable to comment upon the recoverability of the balance receivable of ₹365.38 lakh as
at September 30, 2026 and the adjustments, if any, that may be required to opening
reserves, the comparative figures and the related disclosures in the Statement. The
predecessor auditor had modified their opinion in respect of this matter in their audit report
on the financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.
(d) Recoverability of long-outstanding trade receivables
We draw attention to Note 8 of the Statement regarding trade receivables aggregating
₹186.71 lakh as at September 30, 2026 which have been outstanding for a period of two
to three years. Management has represented that recovery of these dues is in progress
and that they are considered good and recoverable. However, management has not
carried out an assessment of doubtful or irrecoverable debts, and no provision has been
made. In the absence of sufficient appropriate evidence to support management’s
contention of recoverability, we are unable to comment upon the provision for doubtful
debts, if any, that may be required and the consequential impact on the Statement. The
predecessor auditor had modified their opinion in respect of the recoverability of trade
receivables overdue for more than two years in their audit report on the financial
statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.
(e) Capital advances for content development
We draw attention to Note 9 of the Statement. Long-term loans and advances include
capital advances of ₹198.40 lakh paid to developers during the year ended March 31,
2026 towards the development of educational video content for USMLE Step 1 and Step
2 courses. In the financial results for the year ended March 31, 2026, management stated
that these advances would be capitalised from the financial year 2026-27 onwards, based

ALEMBIC PHARMACEUTICALS LIMITED
PRESS RELEASE
14th November, 2026 Vadodara, India
Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited receives USFDA Final Approval for Binimetinib
Tablets, 15 mg and 45 mg.
Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited (Alembic) today announced that it has received final
approval from the US Food & Drug Administration (USFDA) for its Abbreviated New Drug
Application (ANDA) for Binimetinib Tablets, 15 mg and 45 mg. The approved ANDA is
therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug product (RLD), Mektovi Tablets, 15 mg,
of Array BioPharma Inc. (Array). Binimetinib is a kinase inhibitor indicated, in combination
with encorafenib, for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with
a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation. It is also indicated, in combination with encorafenib, for
the treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with a
BRAF V600E mutation. Refer label for a detailed indication.
Alembic was one of the first ANDA applicants for 15 mg and sole first applicant for 45 mg to
submit substantially complete ANDA with a paragraph IV certification for Binimetinib Tablets.
Therefore, with this approval, Alembic is eligible for 180 days of generic drug exclusivity for
Binimetinib Tablets, 15 mg and 45 mg.
Binimetinib tablets have an estimated market size of US$ 282 million for twelve months
ending September 2026 according to IQVIA.
Alembic has a cumulative total of 248 ANDA approvals (230 final approvals and 18 tentative
approvals) from the USFDA.
About Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited
Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited, a vertically integrated research and development
pharmaceutical company, has been at the forefront of healthcare since 1907. Headquartered
in India, Alembic is a publicly listed company that manufactures and markets generic
pharmaceutical products all over the world. Alembic's state of the art research and
manufacturing facilities are approved by regulatory authorities of many developed countries
including the USFDA. Alembic is one of the leaders in branded generics in India. Alembic's
brands, marketed through a field force of over 5,800 are well recognized by doctors and
patients.

Key Financial Highlights
Q2 FY27
• Revenue from operations grew 90.3% YoY to ₹1,311.45 Cr; total income rose 88.8% YoY to ₹1,316.62 Cr.

up 127.4% YoY.

• Basic EPS at ₹3.60, against ₹1.35 in H1 FY26.
Key Business Growth Highlights
• Technology is increasingly central to Skyways’ growth strategy, with deeper integration of digital
capabilities and technology -led processes across business verticals supporting higher business volumes,
market share expansion and improved productivity.
• Wider technology adoption is enhancing operational efficiencies and scalability, contributing to EBITDA
improvement and overall business performance while strengthening the Company’s competitive
positioning.

Key Business and Operational Highlights – Reinforcing Its Market Leadership
• India’s No. 1: Skyways continues to be India’s No. 1 Air Exports Logistics Solutions Provider(LSP) as per
WorldACD.
• Growing market share: The Company has further consolidated its leadership in the Indian air export
market, increasing its market share from 6.2% to 6.3% during the quarter.
• Global ranking: Skyways has improved its position to No. 42 in the World in the global ranking for Air Cargo
as per WorldACD, which is an improvement of two places from 44th in the last quarter, reflecting its growing
global presence and strengthening competitive position. Skyways handled 51,115 tons across of Air Cargo
across its offices in India and 11 other countries around the globe in H1 FY 27.
• Qatar Airways renewal: Skyways, acting as Agent, renewed its Global Annual Agreement with Qatar
Airways Group Q.C.S.C. The agreement was signed on 6th November 2026 and is effective from 1st January
2026 for a term of one year. It aims to further increase the mutual air cargo volumes handled.
• Interim dividend: The Board declared a second interim dividend of ₹0.40 per equity share (4% of the face
value of ₹10 each) for FY 2026-27. The record date is Friday, 20th November 2026, and the dividend will
be paid within 30 days of declaration.
Commenting on the results, Mr. Yashpal Sharma, Chairman, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer of
Skyways Air Services Limited, said:
“India’s logistics sector is at an exciting inflection point, with rising exports, new airports and infrastructure -led reforms
creating a strong and lasting tailwind for the industry. Skyways is using this moment um and its Technology solutions to
bringing together Air, Ocean, Express, Cross Border C ustoms Brokerage, Trucking customer needs and by giving the
customers speed, visibility and better control for their inventory . We remain optimistic about the short-term and long-
term growth prospects in times ahead for our business.”
About Skyways Air Services Limited
Skyways Air Services Ltd. (BSE: 544890 | NSE: SKYWAYS) is an Integrated Logistics company headquartered in New Delhi.
Founded in 1984, Skyways continues to maintain its position as India's No. 1 Air Exports LSP and is globally among the top 42
air cargo players. The company offers Logistics solutions across air, ocean, trucking, and technology-led express delivery, backed
by proprietary digital platforms. With partnerships across 56 airlines, a presence in 12 countries and express coverage of over
1,2000 pin codes in India (through own and partner network). Skyways serves over than 9,500 customers across 65 industries.
The company has performance -based agreements with several leading global airlines. For further information, please visit:

Management Commentary
MR. SHREYANS SURANA | Managing Director, Baazar Style Retail Limited
“Our Q2 and H1 FY27 performance reflects the continued scale -up of our retail operations. We reported total income of
₹4,806 Mn in Q2 FY27 and ₹9,705 Mn in H1 FY27, with H1 EBITDA of ₹1,031 Mn. Our retail footprint and operating indicators
also continued to expand, with the network reaching 293 stores as of 6 November 2026 across 10 states.
We remain focused on improving the quality of our business through stronger Private label brand contribution,
disciplined merchandise planning and deeper presence across our core and focus markets. Our Private label brand
contributed 61% of H1 sales, while customer volumes and quantity sold recorded growth during the period. We are also
working to strengthen store productivity and operating efficiencies as the network expands.
We are confident about the opportunity ahead and expect Q3 and Q4 FY27 to be our strongest quarters. Our turnover
ambition is ₹25,000 Mn for FY27, scaling to ₹38,000 Mn in FY28 and ₹56,000 Mn in FY29. Alongside this, we are working
towards expanding our retail network to 600 stores by FY29. Our planned Green SHIFT solar project is another strategic
initiative aimed at supporting long -term energy security and cost efficiency. We remain committed to disciplined
growth, stronger operating capabilities and sustainable value creation for our stakeholders.”
About Baazar Style Retail Limited
Incorporated in Kolkata in 2013, Baazar Style Retail Limited is a value fashion retailer offering affordable apparel, footwear, home
essentials, beauty products and general merchandise through its Style Baazar and Express Baazar formats.
The Company follows a cluster-based expansion strategy, focusing on Tier-II, Tier-III and Tier-IV markets. Its business is supported by
a growing portfolio of private labels, along with investments in warehousing, technology and supply-chain infrastructure.
With a strong presence across Eastern India and expanding operations in other regions, the Company aims to strengthen its
position in India's organised value fashion retail market.

Mumbai, November 14, 2026 – NFP Sampoorna Foods Limited (NSE - SME: NFPSAMPOOR), an
integrated dry-fruit sourcing, processing, and distribution company, announced its financial
results for the half year ended September 30, 2026.

• Revenue from Operations stood at ₹2,538.34 Lakhs in H1 FY27.
• EBITDA stood at ₹334.84 Lakhs, with an EBITDA Margin of 13.20%.
• Profit Before Tax (PBT) stood at ₹147.98 Lakhs.
• Net Profit (PAT) stood at ₹100.62 Lakhs, with a Net Profit Margin of 4.00%.
Key Business Updates
1. Manufacturing Growth and Value Addition
• Manufacturing revenue recorded over 49% YoY growth during H1 FY27.
• Continued focus on strengthening processing capabilities, improving capacity utilisation and
expanding value-added operations.
• The Company is evaluating opportunities to enhance its processing capabilities and move
towards higher-value operations.
2. Growth in Institutional and B2G Supplies
growth.
• Strengthening institutional relationships with customers including Nutraj (VKC Nuts), Farmart,
Om Sweets and Harish Bakeries.
• Continued focus on expanding institutional relationships and developing opportunities across
government and institutional channels.
Press Release

3. Product Portfolio Expansion
• Expanded product range to include golden raisins, black raisins, walnut kernels, black pepper,
sabudana, pista dodi, ajwain and tarbooj magaj, among other products.
• Continued diversification across dry fruits, nuts, spices and seeds to address a wider range of
customer requirements and market opportunities.
4. Disciplined Raw Material Procurement and Trading Approach
• The geopolitical situation, shipping disruptions and volatility in global commodity prices
impacted raw material procurement, particularly in the raw cashew nut (RCN) segment.
• The Company adopted a calibrated approach towards RCN trading, prioritising margin
protection, prudent working capital management and control of inventory -related risks.
• While these external challenges exerted pressure on margins, the Company continued to focus
on revenue growth and strengthening its manufacturing and institutional business.
5. Expansion into Value-Added Processing
• The Company is exploring the establishment of a proposed Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL)
extraction facility.
• The proposed initiative is aimed at expanding the Company's value -added processing
capabilities and creating opportunities to participate in additional segments of the cashew
value chain.
Management Commentary
Commenting on the results, Mr. Yash Vardhan Goel , Managing Director, NFP Sampoorna Foods
Limited, said:
"The first half of FY27 witnessed encouraging progress in our overall business, with revenue from
operations reaching ₹25.38 crore. Our manufacturing business continued to demonstrate strong
146.6% to ₹89.19 lakh from ₹36.15 lakh in H1 FY26.
During the period, the geopolitical situation, shipping disruptions and volatility in global commodity
prices created challenges in raw material procurement, particularly in the raw cashew nut segment.
These factors, along with our calibrated approach towards trading activities, exerted pressure on

margins. However, our focus remained on maintaining operational discipline, protecting margins and
strengthening the quality of our business.
Going forward, we are focused on several initiatives to strengthen our growth trajectory. These include
expanding our B2G business, deepening institutional relationships, widening our product portfolio and
capitalising on the demand opportunities arising f rom the ongoing festive season. We are also
exploring the proposed Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) extraction facility, which represents an
opportunity to expand our value -added operations and strengthen our presence across the cashew
processing value chain.
We believe these initiatives, supported by our growing manufacturing business and expanding
customer relationships, will provide additional avenues for growth. We remain firmly committed to
executing our strategic priorities, improving operational efficien cies and building a stronger and more
diversified business in the coming period."
About Sampoorna Foods Limited
NFP Sampoorna Foods Limited operates an integrated dry-fruit platform spanning sourcing, importing,
in-house processing, grading, packaging, and pan-India distribution. Its portfolio includes cashew nuts,
makhana (fox nuts), almonds, and walnuts, catering to B2B, B2C, and institutional customers.
Direct sourcing from African origins and domestic importers ensures quality, supply security, and cost
efficiency, while in-house processing enables value addition across multiple cashew grades. Its outlet
in Khari Baoli, Delhi —Asia’s largest wholesale dry -fruit market—provides direct access to distributors
and institutional buyers.

Atam Valves Reports Strong Q2 FY27
Revenue Growth of 43.36% YoY and 33.10%
QoQ; H1 FY27 Revenue Rises 20.45% YoY to

_________________________________________________________________________________
Jalandhar, 14th November 2026: Atam Valves Limited (NSE: ATAM | BSE: 543236),
an established Indian manufacturer and exporter of industrial valves, fittings and boiler
mountings, has announced its unaudited financia l results for the second quarter and
half year ended 30th September 2026.
The Company reported strong revenue growth during Q2 FY27, with Revenue from
Operations increasing 43.36% YoY and 33.10% QoQ to ₹1,635.41 Lakhs, reflecting a
notable improvement in its quarterly business performance.
For H1 FY27, Revenue from Operations stood at ₹2,864.10 Lakhs, registering growth
of 20.45% YoY, compared to ₹2,377.91 Lakhs in H1 FY26.
Despite profitability pressures on a y ear-on-year basis, the Company delivered
sequential improvement in operating earnings during Q2 FY27, with EBITDA
increasing 19.03% QoQ to ₹128.18 Lakhs.
Q2 FY27 Performance
 Revenue from Operations: ₹1,635.41 Lakhs, registering robust growth of
43.36% YoY and 33.10% QoQ.
 EBITDA: ₹128.18 Lakhs, growing 19.03% QoQ, compared to ₹107.69 Lakhs in
Q1 FY27.
 Profit Before Tax: ₹92.42 Lakhs, up 8.86% QoQ.
 Profit After Tax: ₹67.66 Lakhs.
H1 FY27 Performance
 Revenue from Operations: ₹2,864.10 Lakhs, reflecting 20.45% YoY growth,
compared to ₹2,377.91 Lakhs in H1 FY26.
 EBITDA: ₹235.86 Lakhs, with an EBITDA margin of 8.24%.
 Profit Before Tax: ₹177.31 Lakhs.
 Profit After Tax: ₹131.17 Lakhs.
 Basic EPS: ₹1.14 for H1 FY27.
Speaking on the performance, Mr. Amit Jain, Managing Director at Atam Valves
Ltd, commented, “We are pleased to report strong business momentum during the
second quarter of FY27, with Revenue from Operations growing by an impressive
43.36% year-on-year and 33.10% s equentially. Our Q2 revenue of ₹1,635 Lakhs
reflects a significant improvement in bus iness performance, while our half-yearly
revenue of ₹2,864 Lakhs demonstrates continued growth in the scale of our
operations.
One of the encouraging aspects of this quarter has been the sequential improvement
in operating profitability, wit h EBITDA increasing by 19.03% and PAT growing by
6.50% compared to the preceding quarter. While profitability remains below the
corresponding period of the pr evious year, we are focused on strengthening cost
efficiencies, improving our operating perfo rmance and ensuring that revenue growth
translates into sustainable profitability over time.
Beyond our financial performance, we believe Atam Valves is entering an important
phase in its business develop ment journey. Our API certification represents a
significant advancement in our capabilities and enhances our credentials to participate
in opportunities within the oil & gas sector, particularly in industrial applications where
quality, technical specifications and manufacturing reliability are critical.
With over four decades of industry experience, established manufacturing
infrastructure and a diversified product portfo lio, we believe we have built a strong
foundation to pursue opportunities across oil & gas, chemicals, power and other
industrial sectors.
Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear : sustain business momentum, strengthen
our presence in higher-value industrial appl ications, improve operational efficiencies
and progressively enhance profitability. We remain committed to building Atam Valves
into a stronger and more competitive indu strial valve manufacturing company while
creating long-term value for our shareholders.”
About Atam Valves Limited:
Atam Valves Limited, established in 1985, is a leading manufacturer of industrial and plumbing
valves and fittings, catering to various industries such as oil and gas, chemicals, and HVAC.
The company produces a wide range of valves, including Gate, Globe, and Ball, designed to

Technocraft Ventures Ltd reported an increase in EBITDA by 40.98 % amounting to
Rs. 37.91 crore during the half year ended 30th September 2026 as compared to Rs
26.89 crore in the same period last year. Net profit after tax grew by 39.51 %
amounting to Rs. 21.70 crore during the half year ended September 30, 2026,
compared to Rs. 15.55 crore in the same period last year. This growth is attributed to
a surge in operating income driven by slightly higher execution of works. Revenue
from operations grew by 27.82% to Rs.192.98 crore during the half year ended
September 30, 2026 compared to Rs. 150.98 crore in the same period last year.
On the company’s performance, Mr Sanjay Tyagi, Managing Director of Technocraft
Ventures Ltd, stated, “We have witnessed growth in our revenues and profits during
the half year and quarter ended September 30th 2026. Our growing orderbook size
not only reflects our extensive expertise in sewerage solutions and water supply
systems but is also a testament of growing faith in our capabilities as a turnkey EPC
player. This positions us favourably for substantial growth in the coming quarters.
Infrastructure development continues to remain a key focus area for the Government
to bolster economic growth, enhance connectivity, and improve the quality of life for
its citizens. Substantial funds allocated to infrastructure project in the latest budget
by the Government, particularly in the sectors of water supply and sewerage
systems aligns with its goal of creating sustainable urban infrastructure to
accommodate the exponential growth of towns and cities.
“These initiatives bode well for us as we foresee a significantly growing order book
size in the future. The strategic allocation of resources by the government further
strengthens our outlook, providing us with ample opportunities to leverage our
expertise and drive significant growth in the upcoming quarters,” he said.
Technocraft Ventues Limited, during the quarter ended September 2026 has
received Letter of Award for the following contracts:-
(i) For the work valuing Rs. Rs. 19646.80 lakhs.(excluding GST) (Rupees
Nineteen Thousand Six Hundred and Fourty Seven Lakhs Only) for
providing , laying and jointing sewer lines of various diameters ranging
from 300mm dia to 630mm OD internal and peripheral sewer lines
including House Service Connection at Bajitpur Thakran & Auchandi Goc
in Bawana AC (under network package -7).
About Technocraft Ventures Ltd:
Technocraft Ventures Limited is a multidisciplinary public infrastructure development
company engaged in the execution of turnkey Engineering, Procurement and
Construction (“EPC”) contracts. We operate across various infrastructure segments,
including Wastewater Treatment (“WWT”), Operation and Maintenance (“O&M”) of
public utilities, Water Supply Scheme Projects (“WSSPs”), electrical transmission
and distribution networks, construction of substations, road and highway works,
micro tunneling, renewable energy, housing, residential buildings, and sector-level
urban development. We operate on a project-based model and execute contracts
awarded through competitive bidding and tender processes. The Company carries
out its operations through project sites located in different states, based on the
nature and location of awarded work orders.
Incorporated in 1998, our Company has demonstrated consistent growth through
strategic expansions. We began our journey in Uttar Pradesh with the construction of
housing and residential buildings, development of planned residential areas such as
sectors and colonies, and execution of road construction and widening and
strengthening projects under Public Works Departments (“PWD”) and was able to
achieve exceptional growth in the field of public infrastructure development through
strategic expansions into the fields of electricity distribution, water supply schemes,
development of wastewater treatment networks and construction of wastewater
treatment plants. As on date, we have successfully laid and commissioned over
1,000 kilometers of sewerage pipelines in cities including Ghaziabad, Agra, Udaipur,
Jaunpur, Etah, Pilakhuwa and Shahjahanpur. Our portfolio includes Sewage
Treatment Plants (“STPs”) with capacities of up to 56 Million Liters per Day (“MLD”)
in Ghaziabad and 40 MLD in Shahjahanpur. These facilities cater to municipal and
industrial applications and adhere to the latest effluent discharge standards, enabling
treated water reuse for non-potable applications such as horticulture and industrial
processes.
We primarily operate in northern India, with projects concentrated in Uttar Pradesh,
governments and their respective agencies.

Mining Logistics
Faridabad, November 14, 2026: Tejas Cargo India Limited (NSE – TEJASCARGO), one of the leading
logistics service providers with a strong nationwide presence, announced its financial results for H1 FY27.
Financial Highlights

Financial & Operational Highlights
 Total Income grew by 13.40% during H1 FY27, reflecting continued business expansion and
contribution from specialised logistics segments.
 EBITDA margin stood at 15.87%, registering an improvement of 4 basis points.
 Profit after tax grew by 10.00% during H1 FY27.
 The Company's owned fleet expanded to 1,381 vehicles, with 43 vehicles added during H1 FY27,
comprising 20 electric vehicles (EVs), 10 car carriers, 10 SXL trailers (32 ft) and 3 tippers.
 Fleet utilisation stood at 83% during H1 FY27.
Strategic Developments & Business Wins
 Secured New Orders worth Rs. 146.11 Cr for H1 FY27 from clients like Hindalco Industries Limited,
Dalmia Cement (Bharat) Limited, CMDC, CSPGCL, Jindal Stainless Steel Limited, and Shivalaya
Construction Limited.
 Entered mining logistics through a bauxite mining work order from CMDC, Chhattisgarh, marking an
important milestone in business diversification.
 Expanded EV-led logistics through leased electric vehicles and customer deployment engagements.
 Strengthened presence across mining, coal logistics, fly ash transportation, multimodal transportation,
freight forwarding and car carrier operations.
 Deployed in-house software platforms for operations, maintenance and HRMS, with HRMS testing
 Added marquee clients including Dalmia Cement (Bharat) Limited, CMDC, Tata Motors Passenger
Vehicles Limited and CSPGCL, strengthening sectoral diversification and improving business
visibility.
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Chander Bindal, Chairman & Managing Director of Tejas Cargo India
Limited, said, “H1 FY27 marked another important phase in our Company's journey towards evolving into an
integrated, technology-enabled and specialised logistics solutions provider. During the period, we continued to
strengthen our operational capabilities and expand our fleet, taking our owned fleet to 1381 vehicles. We are
aligning our fleet capabilities with the growing preference among customers for EV-based transportation
solutions and reinforcing our commitment towards greener transportation. A key milestone during the period
was securing our first mining contract, marking an important step in expanding our capabilities beyond
conventional transportation and entering specialized mining services.
We are well positioned to strengthen our presence across coal logistics, fly ash transportation, freight
forwarding and car carrier operations. We continued to invest in technology-led operational improvements, with
our integrated ERP, fleet monitoring and control tower capabilities supporting greater visibility, efficiency and
be fully operational by April 2027.
Going forward, our focus remains on deepening our specialised logistics capabilities, expanding long-term
customer engagements, strengthening technology integration and driving sustainable, disciplined growth across
our business”
About Tejas Cargo India Limited: Tejas Cargo India Limited is a fast-growing logistics company
headquartered in Faridabad, Haryana, specializing in Full Truck Load services across India. Operating a fleet of
1,381 vehicles, the company leverages technology-driven solutions like ERP, GPS, geofencing, and ADAS for
efficient fleet management. Tejas Cargo has a nationwide presence through branches and serves sectors such as
logistics, cement, steel, FMCG, e-commerce, and chemicals.

Asahi Songwon Colors Limited Reports Q2 & H1FY27 Results Consolidated Revenue - ₹390.27 Cr; Consolidated EBITDA at - ₹59.56 Cr Ahmedabad, November 14, 2026: Asahi Songwon Colors Limited, India’s leading manufacturer of pigments, colorants and API’s, has announced its financial results for the quarter & half year ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated Financial Highlights for Quarter ended September 30, 2026: § Revenue was ₹201.36 Cr for the quarter, as Y-o-Y increase of 66.55%. § EBITDA ₹26.96 Cr during the quarter under review, a Y-o-Y increase of 141.92%. § EBITDA Margin stood at 13.25% for Q2FY27 as compared to 9.09% in Q2FY26. § Net Profit stood at ₹14.89 Cr for the quarter, a Y-o-Y increase of 610.16%. Consolidated Financial Highlights for Half Year ended September 30, 2026: § Revenue was ₹390.27 Cr for H1FY27, a Y-o-Y increase of 44.13%. § EBITDA ₹59.56 Cr during the half year under review, a Y-o-Y increase of 157.29%. § EBITDA Margin stood at 15.15% for H1FY27 as compared to 8.45% in H1FY26. § Net Profit stood at ₹33.92 Cr for H1FY27, a Y-o-Y increase of 622.95%. Revenue from three segments for Q2FY27 are as follows: ₹134.90 Cr Phthalocyanine ₹28.82 Cr AZO ₹37.64 Cr API Revenue from three segments for H1FY27 are as follows: ₹270.82 Cr Phthalocyanine ₹47.35 Cr AZO ₹72.10 Cr API Commenting on the Q2 & H1FY27 performance, Arjun G. Jaykrishna, CEO & Executive Director, commented, “Q2FY27 was a very strong quarter for our phthalocyanine pigment business. Compared with the same quarter last year, we improved on every key measure, with strong growth in revenues and a significant expansion in margins. The improvement in margins reflects the strength of our supply chain, which helped us navigate disruptions in raw material supply and prices. It also reflects sustained work on costs over the past several quarters: we have improved engineering efficiencies across our operations and cut costs at the ground level. A good part of these gains are structural, built into the way our plants run, and we expect them to continue in the coming quarters. We are confident that the business can sustain EBITDA margins of 13–15% over the longer term. Looking ahead, Q3 usually brings some softness in demand, as customers manage their inventories more tightly towards the calendar year-end. Even so, we expect Q3FY27 to be significantly better than Q3 of last year.”
Gokul Jaykrishna, Managing Director, said, “Q2 was a challenging quarter for the Azo business, and its performance was below our expectations. Sales have recovered to earlier levels after a difficult first quarter, and we see a positive trend of steady improvement. We have grown volumes well. Our focus now is on winning larger customers, which will be key to better profitability. The business remains comfortably EBITDA-positive and cash-positive. The pricing environment is still tough, and the industry changes we expected globally have not played out as we anticipated. The next step for us is to improve on both product quality and cost, and our teams are working on both. We expect H2FY27 to be better than H1FY27. In the API business, the business has grown volumes consistently over the last three years at almost 18% per year, however price pressure has kept performance subdued. As price pressure eases, we expect its performance to improve in the second half. Strong cash generation across our businesses has let us continue to deleverage. We reduced gross borrowings by about ₹49 crore during the first half, and our balance sheet is now considerably stronger. As debt falls and profitability improves, we are carefully evaluating the right opportunities for the Group’s next phase of growth.” About Asahi Songwon Colors Ltd. (ASCL): Asahi Songwon Colors Ltd. is a leading player in the Indian Pigment industry and is one of the leading manufacturers of pigments, colorants and API’s. The company manufactures Beta Blue and Blue Crude. The company has also ventured into manufacturing of AZO pigments as well as APIs through its subsidiaries. The company caters to a diverse base of global and Indian customers with more than 50% of business from exports to global MNC’s. It is currently manufacturing products for over 80 international and domestic customers. The company operates via its four manufacturing facilities in Gujarat, India, located at (Padra), Vadodara & (Dahej), Bharuch (manufacturing Pigments) and (Odhav), Ahmedabad & (Chhatral), Gandhinagar (manufacturing APIs).

Key Business Highlights
1. Gurugram Expansion
New Ayurveda & Panchakarma hospital at Sector-47, Gurugram.
Addition of 80 beds.
Facility spread across 27,500 sq. ft.
2. Healthcare Network Expansion
MSS Hospital, Pitampura established with 23 beds.
Facility spread across 5,631 sq. ft., offering both IPD and OPD services.
Karma Ayurveda Day Care Centre, Janakpuri commenced operations in April 2026.
New Karma Ayurveda Day Care Centre commenced operations in Vashi, Navi Mumbai, on 3 September
2026.
3. NABH Accreditation
Bengaluru Panchakarma Day Care Centre received NABH accreditation, valid until May 2029.
Panchakarma Day Care Centre at Dwarka, New Delhi, received NABH accreditation, valid until 20
August 2029.
Panchakarma Day Care Centre at Patna, Bihar, received NABH accreditation, valid until 18 June 2029.
Noida Panchakarma Day Care Centre received NABH accreditation, valid until 3 August 2029.
Gomti Nagar, Lucknow Panchakarma Day Care Centre received NABH accreditation, valid until 20 July
2029.
Accreditations follow assessments of infrastructure, clinical practices, patient-care protocols, quality
management systems and operational processes.
Strengthens the Company's focus on standardized clinical practices, patient safety, quality standards
and operational excellence across its healthcare network.
4. Nutraceuticals & Wellness
Acquired 100% stake in Karma Nutravedics Pvt. Ltd. for a consideration of <1 lakh.
Subsidiary to focus on nutraceuticals, dietary and health supplements, and allied wellness products.
Creates a dedicated platform for the Company's new growth vertical.
No equity dilution for existing shareholders.
5. Asset Optimisation
Entered into an Agreement to Sell for a non-operational property located at G.T. Karnal Road, New
Delhi.
Supports efficient asset utilisation and disciplined capital allocation.
Management Commentary on The Q2 & H1 FY27 Performance & Key Business Updates
“Q2 and H1 FY27 marka significant period of progress for KRM Ayurveda, reflecting the strength of our
operating model and our continued focus on profitable growth. We have delivered a strong financial
performance, with H1 FY27 Total Income growing by 40.10% year-on-year to 68.17 crore, while EBITDA
increased by 79.81% to 723.82 crore. Most notably, Profit After Tax surged by 109.55% to =17.23 crore,
more than doubling over the corresponding period last year.
What makes this performance particularly encouraging is the improvement in profitability alongside
growth. Our EBITDA margin expanded by 772 basis points to 34.95%, while PAT margin improved by
838 basis points to 25.28%. The momentum was equally evident in Q2 FY27, with PAT registering a
growth of 95.37% and EBITDA increasing by 63.60% year-on-year. This reflects our ability to translate
business growth into stronger earnings and improved operating efficiency.
Beyond the financial performance, we continue to build the foundations for our next phase of expansion.
Additional 80 bed Ayurveda and Panchakarma hospital at Sector-47, Gurugram, represents a significant
addition to our healthcare infrastructure, particularly as our existing 95-bed Sector-41 facility continues
Vashi & Ghaziabad further strengthens our reach and accessibility across key markets.
Quality remains central to the way we scale. With NABH accreditations across our Panchakarma centres
in Bengaluru, Dwarka, Patna, Noida and Lucknow, we are progressively strengthening standardized
clinical practices, patient safety and institutional credibility across our network.
We are also broadening our business horizon through the acquisition of Karma Nutravedics Private
Limited, creating a dedicated platform to enter the nutraceuticals, dietary supplements and allied
wellness segments. At the same time, our proposed monetisation ofa non-operational asset at G.T. Karnal
Road reflects our focus on efficient capital allocation and better utilisation of resources.
As we move ahead, our focus is on building a more integrated Ayurvedic healthcare platform, combining
hospitals, day-care centres, clinical expertise, wellness products and accessible healthcare solutions. We
believe that the combination of strong financial performance, disciplined expansion and a broader
wellness portfolio will position KRM Ayurveda to capture the growing opportunity in India's organised
Ayurvedic healthcare market while maintaining our emphasis on sustainable and profitable growth.”
~ Dr. Puneet Dhawan, MD & Promoter
About The Company
KRM Ayurveda Limited, established in 2019, is an integrated Ayurvedic healthcare company that combines
authentic Ayurveda with modern healthcare practices. Originally founded as a kidney-specialty hospital, the
Company has evolved into a multi-specialty Ayurvedic healthcare platform, with an expanding network of
hospitals and clinics across multiple Indian cities. Its integrated offerings include holistic treatment
scalable digital healthcare initiatives to enhance patient reach and accessibility.

inform you that the Board of Directors of Tankup Engineers Limited (“Company”) at its meeting held today, i.e., on

1. Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) (unaudited ) for the half year ended September 30, 2026 along
with the Limited Review Report thereon, as reviewed and recommended by the Audit Committee.

i. Statements showing the Financial Resu lts – Standalone for the half year ended September 30, 2026; Enclosed

herewith as ‘Annexure – A-3’.
iv. Limited Review Report on the Financial Results – Cons olidated for the half year ended September 30, 2026;
Enclosed herewith as ‘Annexure – A-4’.
2. Resignation of Mr. Lalit Gupta as an Internal Auditor of the Company.
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI
Listing Regulations”), we would like to inform you that Mr. Lalit Gupta has resigned from the position of Internal
Auditor of the Company from the close of business ho urs on November 14, 2026, owing to his increased
professional commitments and responsibilities. The Board of Directors has taken note of the said resignation at its
meeting held today.

Pursuant to the provisions of Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 13 of the Companies
(Accounts) Rules, 2014, and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013 and pursuant to
the applicable provisions of Listing Regulations, the Board of Directors of the Company, on the
recommendation of the Audit Committee, has approved th e appointment of Mrs. Avisha Sinha, Chartered
Accountant, as the Internal Auditor of the Company wi th effect from November 15, 2026 till March 31, 2027

Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, is enclosed as

Mumbai, November 14, 2026: Fineotex Chemical Limited (“Fineotex” or the “Company”), a leading
multinational specialty performance chemicals manufacturer, announced its unaudited consolidated
financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.

• Revenue from operations stood at ₹387.65 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹137.71 crore in Q2 FY26.

Operational and Strategic Highlights
• Fineotex is developing its U.S. water and wastewater solutions business through Fineotex America
Inc., with a focus on mission -critical applications in data centres, semiconductor manufacturing and
other advanced industrial facilities. The initiative is intended to bring together specialised treatment
chemistry, technical support and integrated water-management services.
• The emerging platform aims to address requirements across industrial water treatment, cooling-water
systems, water reuse and wastewater management, with a focus on operating reliability, resource
efficiency and customer -specific solutions. Fineotex intends to build these capabilities through its
chemical expertise and complementary technology and service relationships.

• In Oil & Gas Specialty Chemicals, the acquisition of a 53.33% controlling stake in U.S. -based
CrudeChem Technologies Group has broadened Fineotex’s international footprint and added more
than 100 engineered chemical solutions, supported by manufacturing, a pplication engineering and
last-mile field services.
• Our American manufacturing platform, including its Brookshire and Midland operations, has
expansion, proprietary formulations, differentiated chemistry and ex ecution-led growth in oilfield
applications.
• Fineotex continues to develop its Cleaning & Hygiene portfolio through performance -oriented
formulations for institutional, industrial and homecare applications. Its established Textile Specia lty
Chemicals business remains an important foundation, supporte d by customised products, technical
service and sustainability-led innovation.
Management Commentary
Commenting on the financial performance, Mr. Sanjay Tibrewala, Executive Director and CFO, Fineotex
Chemical Limited, said: “Our Q2 and H1 FY27 results reflect the significantly expanded scale of Fine otex’s
operations, with H1 consolidated total income gro wing 166.8% and operating EBITDA increasing 111.2%
year-on-year. Beyond the financial performance, we are positioning the Group for its next phase of growth.
Advanced water and wastewater solutions for data centres and semiconductor facilities represent an
important emerging opportunity for Fineotex America, alongside the scale and technical depth added b y
our U.S. specialty chemicals business position in oil and gas sector. We will pursue these opportunities
while strengthening our cleaning and hygiene and textile businesses, with a continued emphasis on
profitable growth, disciplined capital allocation and cash generation.”
Dr. Aarti Jhunjhunwala, Executive Director, Fineotex Chemical Limited, said: “We see a significant
opportunity to evolve Fineotex into a broader, globally integrated specialty chemicals and industria l
solutions platform. Our approach is to combine chemistr y-led innovation with engineering, service and
delivery capabilities as the business develops. At the same time, our cleaning and hygiene offers fu rther
avenues for value -added growth while o ur textile specialty chemicals franchise continues to provide a
strong base of technical expertise and customer relationships. Together, these businesses give us a
diversified foundation from which to pursue sustainable long-term opportunities.”
About Fineotex Chemical Limited
Fineotex Chemical Limited is an Indian multinational manufacturer of customised specialty performanc e
chemicals, delivering technical services, sustainable solutions and last -mile deliveries across oil & gas,
water treatment, textile processing and cleaning & hygiene.
With state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities strategically located in Brookshire and Midland, Texas, USA;
Selangor, Malaysia; and Ambernath and Mahape, Maharashtra, India, Fineotex has established a strong
international manufacturing footprint to serve customers across global markets. Fineotex serves customers

interim financial results of BGR Energy Systems Limited (“the Company”)
for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026 prepared by
the company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations,2015 as amended
(“the Listing Regulations”).
The results included in the Statement which is the responsibility of the
Company’s Management and approved by the Board of Directors, has been
prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid
down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”
(“Ind AS 34”), prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read
with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles
generally accepted in India and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the
Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the
Statement based on our review.
Scope of Review:

No. 46B, ‘KrishnanComplex' 4th Floor, South Boag Road, T. Nagar, Chennai - 600 017
Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the
review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the financial statements
are free of material misstatement. A review is limited primarily to inquiries of
company personnel and analytical procedures applied to financial data and
thus provides less assurance than an audit. A review is substantially less in
scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing
specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and consequently
does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all
significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do
not express an audit opinion.
Emphasis of Matters:
1. Attention is drawn to Note No.4 to the standalone unaudited interim
financial results wherein it is described that “In respect of the NUPPL
Ghatampur Balance of Plant work contract, there were an additional

customer.

September 2026, the charge to profit and loss account is Rs.3191 lakhs
and cumulative cost charged to P&L from Jul'24 to Sep’26 on account
of this is Rs.44687 lakhs”.
2. Attention is drawn to Note No. 5 to the standalone unaudited interim
financial results wherein it is described that “With respect to the NTTPS
Vijayawada Balance of Plant Works contract, there were additional
works executed by the Company beyond the original scope of the
contract. The Management has raised a claim of Rs 76980 lakhs with
the customer, the claim is pending for admission by customer. The
Company is taking up its claim through legal course.

order, the company has charged the cost/expenses incurred to the
Statement of Profit and Loss Account. During the quarter ended 30th
September 2026, the charge to profit and loss account is Rs.1789 lakhs
and cumulative cost charged to P&L from Jan'26 to Sep'26 on account
of this is Rs. 9362 lakhs”.
3. Attention is drawn to Note No. 11 to the standalone unaudited interim
financial results wherein it is described that "The Company, with the
assistance of an external consultant, has undertaken a detailed review
of the balances outstanding in the operational creditors' ledgers to
assess the existence and extent of its present obligations in respect of
such balances. Based on the outcome of this review and the exercise of
significant management judgment, the Company has concluded that
certain amounts outstanding to operational creditors are no longer
represent present obligations of the Company. Accordingly, commercial
debit notes aggregating to Rs. 4460.25 lakhs have been raised against
the concerned vendors in accordance with the contractual provisions.
Further, the Company has written back operational creditor balances
amounting to Rs.3056.75 lakhs in respect of liabilities which, based on
its legal assessment, have become unenforceable owing to the expiry of
the limitation period prescribed under the Limitation Act, 1963.
Consequently, such liabilities have been derecognised on the basis that
they are no longer considered to represent present obligations requiring
settlement”.

reporting period, the Company has reassessed the recoverability of
certain Trade Receivables, Contract Assets and the Other Current
Assets (BG Encashment) arising from a terminated NCTPS, ETPS,
TANGEDCO and TANTRANSCO Projects in view of the Legal

Pawan Kumar Garg: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining Fujiyama’s earnings call for second quarter
and first half of FY2027. With me today, Mr. Yogesh Dua, our CEO and Joint Managing
Director, and Mr. Prashant Gupta, our Chief Financial Officer.
I would like to use my time a little differently today. The numbers are in the presentation, and
Prashant will take you through them.
I want to talk about what kind of company Fujiyama is and why we believe this business keeps
compounding. I also want to answer two FAQ, the dip in margin this quarter and increase in
inventory. Let us discuss half year in short. In the first six months of FY27, Fujiyama did INR
2,652 crores of revenue. That is practically similar to the INR 2,655 crores we did in the whole
of FY26.
EBITDA for the half year was INR 478 crores, up 129%, and normalized profit after tax was –
INR 298 crores up 128%. In Q2, revenue grew 130% to INR 1,307 crores and EBITDA grew
116% to INR 223 crores. We can say doubled the business in a year during this period. We have
done that while putting money into plant, people and reaching for next targets.
Let us discuss who we are. Sometimes we are grouped with solar module manufacturers. We are
not pure solar module company. Fujiyama is consumer company in household energy. More
than 85% of our revenue comes from retail household and small businesses who buy from a
dealer in their own town.
Fujiyama is a listed company in India that is built exclusively around the rooftop solar solutions
for retail customers and that also makes every core part of the system itself: solar cell, solar
panel, inverter and batteries. We do this across all three system types: on-grid, off-grid and
hybrid. Our range has a wide range of SKUs in different ranges from a 40-watt panel to 120
kVA online UPS.
Fujiyama Power Systems Limited

Why does this matter? A household does not buy a panel, it buys an outcome, a lower electricity
bill, power when the grid fails, or both. Each customer has a different requirement. For example,
a family in Eastern Uttar Pradesh needs backup above everything else. A family in Gujarat wants
to export power to the grid. A shop in Madhya Pradesh wants both.
A company that makes all these types of systems can sell each of them the right solution through
the same dealer with one brand, one warranty, and one service promise. That is our one-stop
shop advantage, and it is very hard to copy. The business was built brick by brick. Our roots go
back to 1996 when we started with inverter and UPS. We were selling off-grid solar in small
towns of India long before the current subsidy existed.
In the last five years alone, we have sold more than 1.4 million inverters, including about 4.5
lakhs in FY26. Every one of those homes is a relationship for life: it will need batteries, panels,
upgrades and services. Let us discuss five strategic moats that are hard to replace.
First moat, distribution and deep retail reach. We have more than 10,200 channel partners,
distributors, dealers and exclusive UTL shoppes across more than 25 states, union territories.
More of these relationships go back 15 years to 25 years. We are now going deeper into new
states. On the map, on Page 18 in our presentation, we are covered in 13 states, growing in 5 and
running special focus programs in 4. 14 more states and UTs are still largely in front of us.
In this half year, we added more than 100 distributors and more than 1,000 dealers. Odisha and
Uttarakhand moved into the fully covered category. This expanding network provides
unparalleled customer proximity in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, supporting rapid product delivery,
installation and after-sales service. Our vision is to expand the number of channel partners in a
similar way.
Second moat, service on the roof and R&D feedback loop. The hardest part of this industry is
not making panels. India today has far more module capacity. The hard part is mounting the
systems on millions of roofs and keeping them working for 25 years. Fujiyama now has more
than 1,000 on-roll service engineers, up from about 650 in March this year. They are our own
employees, not outsourced, and they support dealers in person for on-sales and installation.
Every complaint they log goes back to our 80 plus R&D engineers. That feedback loop is how
we developed products such as our patented rMPPT hybrid inverter technology, as well as
combo UPS systems and solar PCUs.
Third moat, technology that scales service, UTL AI. Serving millions of households across
thousands of small towns is a data problem as much as a field problem.
Our board member, Mr. Sunil Kumar, an IIT Delhi alumni with more than 24 years in software
development, including at Google, has guided our in-house team in building UTL AI. It is one
platform that runs our sales, service and dealer network through WhatsApp and voice chatbots
around the clock. The platform also predicts which spare part each region will need, guides our
service engineers to visit our dealers along with their routes, and uses data to pick up the next

have manufacturing capacity of 1 GW of solar cell, 3.5 GW of solar panel, 4 GW of power
electronics, 545 MW hour of lithium-ion batteries. Inside our inverters, we make sheet metal

Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Release
Tolins Tyres Reports 43.29% Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27 Revenue Rises 11.64%
to ₹173.98 Crore
Strengthens Market Presence Through Improved Capacity Utilization and Export Growth
Focuses on Operational Efficiencies and Sustainable, Profitable Growth
Kerala, November 14th, 2026: Tolins Tyres Limited (“Tolins” or “Company”), a leading player in the Tyre &
Treads industry, today announced its un-audited financial results for the quarter ended September 30th,
2026.
Key Consolidated Financial Summary: -
Financial Highlights for the quarter ended September 2026:
• Revenue from Operations stood at ₹94.72 crore in Q2 FY27, registering a growth of 43.29% compared to
₹66.10 crore in Q2 FY26.
• EBITDA increased by 7.49% to ₹9.61 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to ₹8.94 crore in Q2 FY26. EBITDA margin
stood at 10.15% for Q2 FY27.
• PAT stood at ₹6.50 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to ₹6.95 crore in Q2 FY26, with PAT margin at 6.86%.
Financial Highlights for the Half year ended September 2026:
• Revenue from Operations stood at ₹173.98 crore in H1 FY27, registering a growth of 11.64% compared to
₹155.85 crore in H1 FY26.
• EBITDA stood at ₹18.52 crore in H1 FY27 compared to ₹22.38 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA margin stood at 10.65%
against 14.36% in H1 FY26.
• PAT stood at ₹12.69 crore in H1 FY27 compared to ₹16.26 crore in H1 FY26, with PAT margin at 7.29%.

Commenting on the overall performance of the Company, Dr. KV Tolin , Promoter, Chairman and Managing
Director, Tolins Tyres, said, “Q2 FY27 marked a strong performance in terms of revenue growth, with revenue
from operations increasing by 43.29% to ₹94.72 crore. This growth was supported by improved business volumes,
with tyre sales increasing by 48.83% and PCTR volumes growing by 20.02% during the quarter.
The Indian tyre industry continues to benefit from steady replacement demand, growth in the automotive sector
and increasing mobility requirements. At the same time, the industry is navigating a challenging cost environment,
with volatility in natural rubber and other crude-linked raw materials impacting input costs and profitability.
Against this backdrop, we remain focused on strengthening our operational efficiencies, optimizing our product
mix and improving capacity utilization. Our export contribution increased to 10.65% in Q2 FY27, compared to
6.05% in the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting progress in expanding our international presence.
While revenue growth remained encouraging, profitability continued to be impacted by margin pressures. We are
focused on improving cost efficiencies, strengthening our distribution network and enhancing our market reach.
Going forward, we will continue to leverage our manufacturing capabilities, expand our presence across domestic
and international markets and capitalize on opportunities across the tyre and rubber products industry to drive
sustainable and profitable growth.”
About Tolins Tyres Limited:
Tolins Tyres, founded in 1982 is a leading producer in the tyre industry, specializing in a diverse range of Retreading and
tyre products. The portfolio includes two and three-wheeler tyres, Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV) tyres and Agriculture
tyres. Furthermore, Tolins Tyres takes pride in innovative “Pre-cured Tread Rubber ” and other retreading products,
showcasing its commitment to cutting -edge technology. These products have not only garnered acclaim in India but
have also made a significant impact across 40 countries, including the Middle East, East Africa, Kenya, Jordan, and Egypt.
Tolins stands out as the first Indian retread brand to not only enter but thrive in the highly competitive American market
for pre-cured retreading products . Led by Chairman and MD Dr. Kalamparambil Varkey Tolin, who brings over three
decades of industry experience, the company operates two manufacturing facilities in Kalady, Kerala, strategically
located near Kochi and close to natural rubber sources. Additi onally, its wholly owned subsidiary, Tolins Tyres LLC,
operates in Al Hamra Industrial Zone, Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Backward integration enhances quality control and cost
management, while a network of 8 depots and 3,737 dealers across India ensures efficient sales channels.

Commenting on the performance, Mr. Varun Agrawal, Managing Director, Manaksia Steels Limited,
said:
“We are pleased to report another strong quarter, sustaining the growth momentum established in
previous quarters. During Q2 FY 2026 –27, compared with Q2 FY 2025 –26, the Company recorded
increasing market acceptance and the strengthening of our product portfolio.
The quarter began with subdued demand and softer steel prices in July due to the monsoon, followed
by a sharp price increase from August, driven by higher coking coal costs and improving demand. The
rapid rise in substrate costs moderated margins compared with Q1 FY 2026 –27. However, our focus on
volume growth, product mix and disciplined cost management enabled us to deliver higher absolute
EBITDA and profitability.
Our manufacturing operations continued to demonstrate strong performance. The Aluzinc-Coated Steel
Line operated at around 95% capacity utilisation, while the existing Colour-Coating Line continued to
operate at full capacity. Work on the new Colour-Coating Line (CCL II) is progressing and is expected to
further strengthen our value-added product capacity upon commissioning.
In August 2026, the Board approved a proposed ₹800 crore investment in speciality steel at our Haldia
facility, marking an important step in our journey towards higher-value steel products. We welcome the
West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy, 2026 , announced on 5 th November 2026, which identifies
speciality steel as a thrust sector. As a result, our proposed investment is expected to qualify for the
enhanced incentives available to thrust-sector units under the policy. We are awaiting the detailed policy
guidelines, following which we intend to submit the Certificate of Intent (COI) to West Bengal
Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) for enlistment and approval under the policy.
revenue growth during the quarter. The relative stability and improvement in the Nigerian Naira have
supported a more favourable operating environment, and we remain optimistic about its future growth
prospects.
Looking ahead, our priorities remain focused on expanding value-added product offerings, optimising
capacities, strengthening backward integration and maintaining financial discipline . With these
initiatives, we remain committed to sustainable and profitable growth and creating long -term value for
our shareholders.
ABOUT MANAKSIA STEELS LIMITED
Manaksia Steels Limited (‘MSL’) (NSE: MANAKSTEEL, BSE: 539044) is a prominent manufacturer and
exporter of coated steel products, offering a wide range of high-quality, value-added steel solutions. Our
product portfolio includes cold-rolled steel sheets and coils, hot-dip galvanised and Aluzinc-coated steel
sheets and coils, as well as pre -painted coils and sheets marketed under our established brands —
Austrang, 5 Star Super Colour, 5 Star Superlume, and 5 Star Super Sakti.
All our products are manufactured at our state -of-the-art facility in Haldia, West Bengal. This
strategically located plant—located at Haldia port—enables seamless access to export markets, efficient
import of raw materials, and smooth distribution through coastal domestic routes besides road and rail.
Our galvanised, Aluzinc, and pre -painted steel products are considered new -age building materials,
widely used across sectors such as construction, solar, infrastructure, home appliances, and general
engineering. These materials offer durability, strength, and aesthetic appeal, making them ideal for a
wide range of applications.
MSL leverages most advanced technology and a precision -driven approach to deliver products tailored
to exacting customer specifications. Our relentless focus on quality, operational efficiency, and customer
satisfaction has earned us a strong reputation in both domestic and international markets.
With a commitment to innovation, excellence, and sustainability, Manaksia Steels Limited is well -
positioned to meet the evolving demands and drive long-term value for stakeholders.

Vibhor Steel Tubes PAT jumps 91.55% YoY at Rs 2.72 crore in Q2FY27 riding on higher sales and
better margins from value-added products
 Operating Income increased by 26.99% at Rs 357.81 crore
 EBITDA was up nearly 50% at Rs 14.13 crore
Mumbai, November 14, 2026: Haryana-based high-quality steel tubes and pipes maker, Vibhor Steel
Tubes Ltd (VSTL), registered 91.55 per cent growth in net profit on a standalone basis at Rs 2.72 crore
for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from Rs 1.42 crore sa me period last year. The
growth in profits was supported by increased sales of high margin value -added products such as
transmission line towers and metal crash barriers from the recently commissioned plant in Odisha.
Operating income on standalone basis increased by 26.99 per cent at Rs 357.81 crore for the quarter
ended 30th September, 2026, as compared with Rs 281.76 crore last year. EBITDA on a standalone basis
increased by 50.06 per cent at Rs 14.13 crore for the quarter under review.
EBITDA on a standalone basis for the half year under review increased by 34.70 per cent at Rs 26.50
crore, as compared to Rs 19.67 crore last year. PAT for the half year under review increased at Rs 4.65
crore, as against Rs 4.56 crore for the same period last year.
The co mpany recently incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary - Viyom Steel Infra Pvt Ltd for
manufacturing high-quality steel products such as transmission towers, monopoles, crash barriers,
octagonal poles and high mast poles among others aimed at serving the infrastructure sector.
