Commenting on the performance, Vijay Kaushik, Chairman and Executive Director, Vibhor Steel
Tubes, said, “Our performance during the quarter reflects the continued resilience of our business and
the underlying strength of India’s steel consumption story. Demand for steel tubes and pipes is being
supported by sustained infrastructure and construction activity, expansion in manufacturing,
urbanisation and rising requirements across water, energy and industrial applications. The market is
steadily evolving towards higher-value and application-specific products and with the production at
our plant in Sundargarh in Odisha commissioning we are well pl aced to cater to this demand. We
remain focused on leveraging our expanded capacity, improving product mix and strengthening
operational efficiencies. We expect demand to remain healthy through the second half and see strong
opportunities for sustained, profitable growth.”
VSTL commenced supply of the Electric Resistance Welded (ERW) and Galvanized (GI) Pipes produced
from its greenfield plant located at Sundargarh in Odisha. Commercial production at the 156,000 MTPA
facility in Odisha had started in July 2 025. The plant, which entailed a total investment of Rs 119.83
crore, offers several value -added steel products such as crash barriers, Power Transmission Line
Towers, high mast lighting poles, octagonal poles and monopoles.
The company manufactures steel products such as electric resistance welded pipes, hot-dipped
galvanized pipes, hollow section pipes, primer painted pipes, crash barriers, Power Transmission Line
Towers, high mast lighting poles, octagonal poles and monopoles among others. VSTL, which h as a
contract manufacturing agreement with Jindal Pipes to manufacture and supply finished goods under
the brand name Jindal Star, currently sees over 80 per cent of its total turnover coming from this one
segment.
Crisil Ratings had recently assigned ‘BBB+/Stable’ long-term rating and ‘Crisil A2’ short-term rating to
its bank loan facilities aggregating to Rs 370 crore. The rating s reflect VSTL ’s established market
position in the steel tubes and pipes segment, its consistent operational performance, and prudent
financial management.
About the company
Vibhor Steel Tubes Ltd. (VSTL) is a more than two decades old manufacturer, exporter and supplier of
high-quality steel products to various heavy engineering industries in India. The company ’s product
portfolio includes ERW pipes which can be used in sectors such as water transport, oil & gas, etc.; hot-
dipped galvanized pipes which have applications in agriculture, infrastructure, building materials, etc.;
railways, highways & roads, etc. and; transmission line towers which is primarily used in power sectors,
as well as high mast lighting poles, octagonal poles and monopoles.
VSTL has been working with Jindal Pipes Limited since 2003. It manufactures & supplies the finished
goods to "Jindal Pipes Limited" vide the renewed agreement dated April 01, 2023 under the brand
name "Jindal Star".

Commenting on the allotment, Mr. Puneet Singhania, Whole Time Director of Master Capital Services

successful allotment of ₹75 Cr worth of Non-Convertible Debentures by Master Capital Services
Limited, marking an important milestone for the Company.
The funds raised will strengthen our funding base and diversify our sources of funding, providing
support for the continued growth of our business and working capital requirements. We remain
focused on disciplined capital allocation, operational efficiency and prudent financial management.
Going forward, we will continue to enhance our integrated financial services offerings with a strong
emphasis on technology, innovation and sustainable growth, while creating long-term value for all our
stakeholders.”
About mastertrust group
Master Trust Limited is a diversified financial services company with over 41 years of experience, offering
a comprehensive suite of trading, investment, wealth management, and financial solutions under the
mastertrust group. Established in 1985, the Company has evolved into a trusted financial services
platform with a strong presence across capital markets, serving retail, HNI, corporate, and institutional
clients through technology-driven and research-backed offerings.
The Company has established a pan-India network spanning 22 States and Union Territories, supported
by 63 branches, 1,550+ business partners, over 4.40 lakh registered customers and 1,220 employees,
reflecting its extensive distribution network and strong customer reach.
mastertrust provides a one-stop financial services platform, offering equity and commodity trading,
derivatives clearing, portfolio management, wealth management, depository services, merchant banking,
insurance, research, algorithmic trading, and NBFC services. This diversified product portfolio enables
the Company to cater to the evolving financial needs of investors under a single integrated ecosystem.
Over the years, the Company has strengthened its market position through continuous technology
adoption, digital innovation, and strategic expansion. It has received several industry recognitions,
including being named the Best BFSI Brand by The Economic Times for four consecutive years (2023–

operational excellence and customer-centricity.
Looking ahead, mastertrust aims to deepen its digital capabilities, expand its customer base and
product offerings, and strengthen its integrated financial services ecosystem. With a focus on
technology, innovation, research-driven advisory, and nationwide expansion, the Company is well-
positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for comprehensive financial solutions while creating
long-term value for its stakeholders.

Odisha, 14th November, 2026, Srinibas Pradhan Constructions Limited (SPCON) (NSE: SPCON), one
of the leading infrastructure -focused EPC company engaged in roads & highways, bridges, industrial
projects, and civil construction works, has announced its unaudited Financial Results for H1 FY27.

Segment-wise Revenue Breakup – H1 FY27
• Construction Work: Revenue of ₹3,126.65 lakh, contributing 79.69% to total revenue.
• Transportation: Revenue of ₹696.96 lakh, contributing 17.76% to total revenue.
• Other Operational Segment: Revenue of ₹99.84 lakh, contributing 2.54% to total revenue.
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Srinibas Pradhan, Managing Director of Srinibas Pradhan
Constructions Limited said: “Despite heavy monsoon conditions across Odisha, we maintained
operational efficiency through our in -house machinery, asphalt plant and captive supply of key
construction materials. During H1 FY27, we secured a new order worth ₹8.22 Cr from NTPC Limited for
the connecting road at DSTPP Stage-II and continued progress on the widening and strengthening of
the 18.59 km Bandhabahal –Barihapali road project in Jharsuguda, valued at ₹32.74 Cr, further
strengthening our project portfolio.
Coming to our financial performance, H1 FY27 Total Income stood at ₹3,929.66 lakh. EBITDA increased
17.18% YoY to ₹895.13 lakh, with EBITDA margin improving by 605 bps to 22.81%. Net profit grew 33.87%
YoY to ₹550.04 lakh, reflecting improved profitability.
Looking ahead, with the onset of the main construction season and increasing infrastructure
opportunities in Odisha, we remain focused on strengthening our order book, accelerating project
execution and sustaining profitable growth.”
About Srinibas Pradhan Constructions Limited (SPCON)
Srinibas Pradhan Constructions Limited (SPCON) is an infrastructure-focused EPC company engaged in
roads & highways, bridges, industrial projects, and civil construction works. With over two decades of
industry experience, the company has built a strong pr esence through efficient execution, technical
expertise, and long-standing relationships with government departments and institutional clients.
The company’s structure includes its wholly owned subsidiary, Srinibas Pradhan Infra Private Limited, a
PWD Special Class Contractor in Odisha, while SPCON operates as a PWD Class A Contractor. This enables
participation across a broader range of governmen t tenders while retaining existing contractor
qualifications. SPCON is also certified under ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018 standards.
SPCON operates with an integrated business model supported by in -house construction capabilities,
owned machinery, and quality -control infrastructure. The company maintains operational efficiency
through backward integration and on-site testing facilities, ensuring better execution control and quality
standards.
The transition into a public limited company and listing on the NSE Emerge platform in 2026 marked a
key milestone in the company’s growth journey.
In FY26, SPCON reported consolidated Total Income of ₹9,030.24 lakhs, EBITDA of ₹1,506.53 lakhs, and PAT
of ₹821.02 lakhs.

Dear Sir/ Madam,
This is with reference to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (“CIRP”) of Shirpur
Refinery Site Shirpur, Dist. Dule, Dhulia, Maharashtra, India, 425405 (hereinafter referred as
“Corporate Debtor”) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“Code”) commenced
pursuant to order no. CP (IB) No. 250/MB/2022 dated June 24, 2024 (date of receipt of receipt
of order by IRP is June 25, 2024) passed by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal,
Mumbai Bench - VI (“Admission Order”).
In terms of the Admission Order, the undersigned has been appointed as the Interim Resolution
Professional (“IRP”) and Moratorium has been declared. Further, the first meeting of the
Committee of Creditors was duly convened on July 24, 2024, and based on t he e-voting
concluded on September 14, 2024, the existing IRP was appointed as the Resolution
Professional (“RP”).
Pursuant to the Admission Order and in consonance with the provisions of regulation 15(2A)
of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the provisions of Regulation 17 (“Board of Directors”)
shall not be applicable during the insolvency resolution process period in respect of a listed
entity which is undergoing corporate insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency Code.
Further, the role and responsibilities of the board of directors as specified under Regulation 17
shall be fulfilled by the IRP or RP in ac cordance with sections 17 and 23 of the Insolvency
Code.
Additionally, Regulation 15 (2B) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 states that the
provisions as specified in regulations 18 (“Audit Committee”),19 (“Nomination and
remuneration committee”), 20 (“Stakeholders Relationship Committee”) and 21 (“Risk
Management Committee”) shall not be applicable during the insolvency resolution process
under the Insolvency Code and the roles and responsibilities of the committees specified in the
respective regulations shall be fulfilled by the IRP or RP.
As on today, the RP is facing a severe challenge to complete the financial accounts for the
quarter ended September 30, 2026. There are various issues having impact on financial
accounting, which are not getting resolved in a timely manner with the Suspended Board of
Directors, leading to delay in preparation of the Financial Results.
In view of the above, the RP is not in position to submit the Corporate Debtor’s Unaudited
Financial Results (standalone and consolidated) basis for the quarter ended on September 30,
2025, within the prescribed time limits as mandated under SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015.
Although the RP and his team have been making diligent efforts to collate and compile records
maintained in both physical and electronic formats, the finalization of the Financial Results has
been delayed due to unforeseen circumstances.
You are requested to kindly take the above information on record.
Thanking You,
Yours Sincerely,

Welcomes Tejas Sampat as Chief Financial Officer
Mumbai, 14th November, 2026: Veefin Solutions Limited, a listed enterprise technology company serving banks,
financial institutions and corporates, today announced that Ms. Payal Maisheri will be stepping down from her
position as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and Mr. Tejas Sampat will be joining the Company as its new CFO.
The Company places on record its sincere appreciation for Payal's contribution to Veefin's journey and warmly
welcomes Tejas as he takes on this important leadership responsibility. The transition comes at an exciting stage in
Veefin's growth journey, as t he Company builds on the foundation established over the years and continues to
pursue its strategic priorities.
TEJAS SAMPAT APPOINTED AS CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER
Tejas Sampat brings nearly 17 years of professional experience, including his tenure at Ernst & Young (EY), where
he served as a Director.
During his tenure at EY, Tejas held senior leadership responsibilities and led several significant and complex
transactions for some of India's largest business conglomerates. His experience spans key areas including mergers
and acquisitions, taxation, transaction advisory, corporate finance and strategic financial matters.
His extensive experience in advising leading Indian business groups and handling complex corporate transactions
brings valuable expertise to Veefin as the Company continues to expand its business, strengthen its market
presence and pursue its long-term growth objectives.
As CFO, Tejas will focus on financial strategy, corporate finance, governance, investor relations and strategic
transactions, while working closely with the leadership team to support the Company's business priorities and long-
term value creation.
PAYAL MAISHERI ST EPS DOWN AS CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

the financial services sector, an industry she has long aspired to be part of, given her professional background and
interests.
Payal joined Veefin during its pre -IPO phase and has been an integral part of the Company's financial journey
through several significant milestones. She played a pivotal role in the planning and execution of the Company's
IPO and its successful listing, and subsequently in its migration to the Main Board.
During her tenure, she played an important role in building and leading the finance function, supporting the
Company's growth and navigating the financial, regulatory and governance requirements associated with its
evolution from a pre-IPO enterprise to a listed company on the Main Board.
The Company places on record its sincere appreciation for her commitment, leadership and significant contribution
to Veefin's journey and wishes her continued success in her future endeavours.

Master Capital Services Limited Raises ₹75 Cr through Allotment of Non-
Convertible Debentures
Ludhiana – 14th November, 2026: Master Trust Limited (MASTERTR, BSE: 511768), a diversified financial
services company offering broking, derivatives clearing, depository services, lending, wealth
management, portfolio management, investment banking, merchant banking, insurance and
investment solutions under the mastertrust group through a strong digital platform has informed that
its wholly owned subsidiary, Master Capital Services Limited, has raised ₹75 Cr through allotment of
75,000 Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs), as approved in its Legal, Banking and Finance Committee
meeting held on 12th November, 2026.
Key Issue Highlights
Particulars Details

(NCDs)

Object of the Issue General Corporate Purposes and to meet working capital requirements
Strategic Significance
 Raises ₹75 Cr through NCD allotment, strengthening the company's funding base.
 Diversifies funding sources to support business growth.
 Enhances financial flexibility to meet future business requirements.
 Reinforces focus on disciplined capital allocation and prudent financial management.
 Supports the continued development of its integrated financial services offering.
 Strengthen the working capital of the company & fulfills general corporate purposes.
Commenting on the allotment, Mr. Puneet Singhania, Whole Time Director of Master Capital Services
Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Master Trust Limited said, “We are pleased to announce the
successful allotment of ₹75 Cr worth of Non-Convertible Debentures by Master Capital Services
Limited, marking an important milestone for the Company.
The funds raised will strengthen our funding base and diversify our sources of funding, providing
support for the continued growth of our business and working capital requirements. We remain
focused on disciplined capital allocation, operational efficiency and prudent financial management.
Going forward, we will continue to enhance our integrated financial services offerings with a strong
emphasis on technology, innovation and sustainable growth, while creating long-term value for all our
stakeholders.”
About mastertrust group
Master Trust Limited is a diversified financial services company with over 41 years of experience, offering
a comprehensive suite of trading, investment, wealth management, and financial solutions under the
mastertrust group. Established in 1985, the Company has evolved into a trusted financial services
platform with a strong presence across capital markets, serving retail, HNI, corporate, and institutional
clients through technology-driven and research-backed offerings.
The Company has established a pan-India network spanning 22 States and Union Territories, supported
by 63 branches, 1,550+ business partners, over 4.40 lakh registered customers and 1,220 employees,
reflecting its extensive distribution network and strong customer reach.
mastertrust provides a one-stop financial services platform, offering equity and commodity trading,
derivatives clearing, portfolio management, wealth management, depository services, merchant banking,
insurance, research, algorithmic trading, and NBFC services. This diversified product portfolio enables
the Company to cater to the evolving financial needs of investors under a single integrated ecosystem.
Over the years, the Company has strengthened its market position through continuous technology
adoption, digital innovation, and strategic expansion. It has received several industry recognitions,
including being named the Best BFSI Brand by The Economic Times for four consecutive years (2023–
2026) and the Best Organisation to Work by ET Now in 2025, underscoring its commitment to
operational excellence and customer-centricity.
Looking ahead, mastertrust aims to deepen its digital capabilities, expand its customer base and
product offerings, and strengthen its integrated financial services ecosystem. With a focus on
technology, innovation, research-driven advisory, and nationwide expansion, the Company is well-
positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for comprehensive financial solutions while creating
long-term value for its stakeholders.
In FY26 (Consolidated), Master Trust Limited reported Total Income of ₹5,758.44 Mn, EBITDA of ₹ 2293.76
Mn, and Net Profit of ₹1,260.87 Mn.

United Heat Transfer Limited
Reports Strong H1 FY27 Performance
(Revenue, EBITDA and Net Profit grew ~50%, ~49% and ~76% YoY respectively)
14th November 2026: United Heat Transfer Ltd, e stablished in January 1995, is a manufacturer of shell and
tube heat exchangers, air -cooled heat exchangers, pressure vessels, and process flow skid equipment. Its
broad product range serves critical applications across automotive, marine, compressor, oil & gas, refinery,
and other process industries.
Key Financial Highlights:
Particulars (INR Mn) H1’FY27 H1’FY26 YoY%
Revenue from Operations 321.9 214.4 50.1%
EBITDA 38.1 25.6 49.1%
EBITDA Margin 11.9% 11.9% -
Net Profit 14.7 8.4 75.5%
Net Profit Margin 4.6% 3.9% +66 bps
• Revenue from operations increased by 50.1% YoY to Rs 321.9 Mn in H1 FY27.
• EBITDA grew by 49.1% to INR 38.1 Mn, while EBITDA margin remained stable at 11.9% , despite a
sharp increase in material costs during H1 FY27, reflects the Company's ability to maintain
operating profitability amid input cost pressures.
• Net profit increased by 75.5% to INR 14.7 Mn, compared to the corresponding period.
• Net profit margin improved by 66 bps to 4.6%.
Key Operational Highlights:
• Inventory days reduced significantly to ~262 days as of 30th September, 2026 (TTM), compared to
~464 days as of 30th September, 2025 (TTM).
• Working capital days improved to ~264 days in H1 FY27 (TTM), compared to ~442 days in H1 FY26
(TTM), reflecting a significant improvement in working capital management.
• The Company currently has orders aggregating INR 499.7 Mn under execution, which are expected
to be delivered during the remainder of FY27.
Outlook:
• The Company remains optimistic about its growth trajectory for FY27, supported by a healthy
execution pipeline and ongoing business development initiatives.
• Active negotiations for additional orders provide additional opportunities to strengthen the
Company's business pipeline.
• Based on the current business outlook and order pipeline, the Company expects to achieve revenue
growth of 30% to 35% in FY27 compared to FY26.
• The Company will continue to focus on profitable growth, margin stability, working capital
optimisation and operational excellence.
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Yogesh Patil, Chairman & Managing Director, United Heat Transfer
Limited, stated,
“We are encouraged by our strong H1 FY27 performance, with revenue growing by 50.1%, EBITDA by 49.1%
and net profit by 75.5% YoY. Despite a sharp increase in material costs, we maintained our EBITDA margin at
11.9%, reflecting our focus on operational excellence and cost management. Our performance demonstrates
the strength of our business model and our ability to deliver healthy growth while navigating input cost
volatility and maintaining profitability.
We have also made significant progress in strengthening our working capital management, with both
inventory days and working capital days showing a considerable improvement. With orders worth INR 499.7
Mn currently under execution and additional opportunities under active negotiation, we remain confident of
achieving revenue growth of 30-35% in FY27 over FY26.
We remain committed to strengthening our market position, enhancing operational efficiencies and
delivering sustainable and profitable growth.”

Infrastructure remains a fundamental driver of India's economic growth. Investments across
highways, railways, power generation and transmission, buildings, urban infra, irrigation,
roads, etc, continue at a steady pace, notwithstanding periodic short -term slowdowns. The
growing scale and complexity of infrastructure projects, coupled with an increasing focus on
precision, efficiency, and productivity, are driving sustained adoption of advanced construction
and concreting equipment.
As a leading player in the concreting equipment space, Ajax is strongly positioned to capitalize
on this structural opportunity, leveraging its established brand equity, extensive distribution
network, and comprehensive product portfolio to participate in India's long-term infrastructure-
led growth journey.
Having said that, it is important to recognize that certain segments of the infrastructure sector
have been experiencing near -term headwinds, resulting in temporary delays in project
execution and a moderation in the pace of investments. Government spending on infrastructure
projects, more particularly by some state governments, has been below budgeted allocations,
resulting in this slower pace of execution.
Contractors in some key states continue to experience delays in payments from the respective
state authorities, leading to strained cash flows, dampened sentiment and reduced appetite to
undertake fresh investments in equipment.

Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar. Meanwhile, rising steel prices and other
costs of crude -linked commodities have driven a sharp increase in raw material costs,
prompting several suppliers to seek price revisions.
Consequently, our overall raw material cost increased by close to mid -single digits during H1
FY27. In response to these headwinds, we have been implementing measures that we believe
will best position us to navigate the evolving external challenges.
With infrastructure development in urban regions progressing steadily, we are increasingly
targeting private sector projects to expand the range of applications and use cases for SLCMs.
In parallel, we are accelerating the scale-up and market penetration of our UDAAN series with
the objective of driving wider adoption and democratizing mechanization across the country.
We have received a very encouraging response to the UDAAN Series since its launch. We are
continuing to drive market activation through product demonstrations and customer
engagement initiatives to reinforce its value proposition. At the dealership level, we remain
focused on strengthening process centricity across customer coverage and conversion.
We are also nearing the launch of our ARGO 4000. In fact, it has already been launched. It
will address an important gap in our SLCM portfolio, further broadening our product offering
and strengthening our overall value proposition. Second, over the past year or so, we have
made significant strides in expanding our non-SLCM business.
Building on the B2B channel initiative introduced last year, we are actively pursuing multiple
customer engagements and contracts, several of which are progressing well. We are leveraging
our brand equity and extensive distribution reach to deepen our market presence and increase
market share, with a particular focus on batching plants and pumps.
We expect these efforts to translate into a steady growth trajectory for the non -SLCM business
in the coming years. Third, our focus on operational excellence remains unwavering. We
continue to strengthen our design and engineering capabilities, build a resilient supply chain,
and drive lean, agile, and efficient manufacturing operations.
In response to the sharp increase in raw material prices over the past few months, we are
pursuing a range of initiatives to optimize our cost structure and improve operational
efficiencies. These include diversifying our supplier base and actively engaging with alternate
vendors to secure more competitive procurement terms. To drive greater operational agility
and better execution, we have streamlined our organizational structure by bringing all
manufacturing under a single leader.
The head of the Obadenahalli plant has now moved to procurement and supply chain, while
the services and spares function have been aligned with strategy and product planning to
further strengthen customer excellence. Following the price increase of around 2% that we
took in Q4 FY26, we have taken another price hike of around 1% in September and will

profitability, and cash generation. We continue to maintain a strong cash position of nearly

To begin with, let me briefly touch upon the key trends shaping the Indian health care sector and
the structural growth drivers that continue to underpin our long -term strategy. The Indian health
care sector continues to witness strong structural growth, s upported by rising health awareness,
increasing prevalence of lifestyle-related and chronic diseases, higher health insurance penetration
and growing demand for specialized medical services.
The demand for quality health care is also being driven by an aging population, advancements in
medical technology and increasing affordability of advanced treatments. Despite this growth, India
continues to have a significant gap in health care infrastructure, particularly in hospital bed
availability and access to quality tertiary and specialized care. This creates a meaningful opportunity
for organized hospital chains to expand their presence, especially across Tier 2 cities.
At the same time, the increasing complexity of medical requirements is making technology and
specialized clinical capabilities, important differentiators for hospital operators. Investments in
advanced medical equipment, robotic -assisted procedures and spe cialized treatment infrastructure
enables hospitals to broaden their clinical offerings, address complex medical needs and enhance
their ability to attract patients.
At GPT Healthcare, we are focused on strengthening these capabilities across all our hospitals in
the network. We have introduced robotic -assisted surgery at ILS Salt Lake and ILS Howrah,
alongside investments in advanced oncology and diagnostic infrastruc ture. These initiatives are
aimed at expanding our service capability offerings, improving access to advanced treatment
options and further strengthening our clinical capabilities.
Let me now take you through our operational and financial performance for Q2 and H1 FY27. We

through improved patient volumes, better utilization of our established facilities and a stronger

expectations of the company as on date of this call. These statements are not guarantee of future

As a reminder, all participants lines will be in listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity

Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Rakesh
Chopdar, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer from Azad Engineering. Thank you, and over
to you, sir.
Rakesh Chopdar: Thank you, team SGA. Good afternoon, everyone and a very warm welcome to Azad
Engineering's Earnings Conference Call for the second quarter and first half of Fiscal year 2027.
On behalf of the board and the entire team Azad, my warm wishes to you and your family for
Diwali and the festive season.
Joining me today are Mr. Vishnu Malpani, our Whole -Time Director, Mr. Ronak Jajoo, our
CFO, and our investor relationship advisors from Strategic Growth Advisors. Our standalone
and consolidated results, along with our latest investor presentation, have be en uploaded to the
In August, I began by saying that we are living through a synchronized high-growth cycle across
energy, oil and gas, aerospace, and defence, and that these are structural multi-decade shifts, not
short-term spikes. Three months on, every single we track has strengthened. In our segment,
engine makers continues to raise output, and precision rotating parts remain one of the tightest
links in the supply chains.
In defence, India's push for self-reliance in engines is moving from intent to programs, and our
capability in complete defence assemblies is opening long -cycle domestic and international
opportunities. The backdrop I described in August is intact and stronger. For Azad, the question
is not demand, it's how quickly we convert capacity into revenue and that is the key message for
this quarter.
The foundation is now complete. H1 FY27 was another period of steady progress for Azad. Our
capital deployment plans have stayed on schedule. In September, we inaugurated two new
dedicated lean manufacturing facilities for GE Vernova. All six customer-dedicated facilities are
now commissioned. 44,800 square meters for four global OEMs, namely Mitsubishi Heavy
Industries, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, and Baker Hughes.
We are also in discussions with our aerospace customers about following a similar model as we
have done for our energy customers. In August, I told you that 80% of our foundation initiatives
revenue is in place.
Azad Engineering Limited
November 07, 2026
Page 3 of 18
Talking on the capital deployed, our treasury funds have now gone into capex and the
infrastructure and plants that we have commissioned. Teams in place, we have hired the skilled
manpower needed to run the installed capacity which we have installed recently. Production
readiness, we have built up enough raw material, tooling, and consumables to keep every facility
production-ready.
Customer qualifications, we are running multiple delta qualifications at our new facilities with
various customers at the same time. This setup phase is mandatory in our business. With it
complete, our capacity is now ready to deliver the throughput.
On the Q2 and H1 FY27 financial snapshot, our operation performance remains in line with our
guidance. In Q2 FY27, we delivered our highest -ever quarterly revenue of INR187.8 crores,
which is up by 31.6% year -on-year and about 10% over the first quarter. EBITDA grew faster
by 37.1% YoY, which is to INR70.4 crores, and the EBITDA margin expanded to 37.5% from
36% a year ago. Profit after tax was INR30.8 crores, a margin of 16.4%.
For the first half, revenue grew 29.3% to INR358 crores, ahead of our 25% guidance. EBITDA
grew 34.7% YoY to INR134.5 crores at a 37.5% margin. Profit after tax grew by 6.6% YoY to
INR67.2 crores.
On a consolidated basis, H1 revenue was INR363.5 crores, EBITDA stood at INR136.6 crores,
and a PAT of INR66.1 crores. Growth was balanced across segments. Energy, oil and gas grew
28.5% to INR290 crores, at 81% of revenue. Aerospace and defence grew 28.3% to INR60.4
crores, at a 17% of revenue.
Domestic revenues grew more than two and a half times to INR43 crores, and is now 12% of
our business, up from 6%, helped by our indigenization work with BHEL. Let me speak plainly
about the profit after tax, because I know it matters to you all. This quarter's PAT reflects the
expected lag between investment and revenue.
Treasury income fell from INR12.7 crores to INR4.7 crores, as our IPO and QIP funds went into
the plants. Depreciation doubled to INR21.8 crores as the new facilities were capitalized.
Finance cost rose to INR12.2 crores on the working capital loans that support our growth. We
have hired ahead, so employees costs are INR50.3 crores against INR32.5 crores a year ago.
All of this cost we carry before the revenue from the new capacity flows through fully. That
phase is now largely behind us. Orders and milestones. BHEL approved as a long -term source
with a two -year rate contract worth about INR52.68 crores for their gas turbine airfoils. This
deepens our domestic energy business. Baker Hughes, our supply agreement with Nuovo
Pignone, has extended up to 2030.
Oil and gas, the ramp -up of our dedicated oil and gas facility, tied to the customer's delivery
plans, adds a further growth lever from Q4 FY 2027. Defence, after delivering India's first
indigenous expendable turbojet engine to GTRE, we are now positioned for end -to-end
manufacture, assembly integration of complete engine assemblies of their demands.
Azad Engineering Limited
November 07, 2026

The testings are ongoing. Customer recognition this year, Baker Hughes presented us its Growth
Collaboration Award and GE Vernova for its Delivery Partnership Award. Closing outlook. As
we have said on earlier calls, throughput from the new capacity begins in Q3 of FY27.
We expect revenue to ramp up Q4 of FY27 onwards, and all the plants will be fully ramped up
by Q2 of FY 2028. Our current installed capacity positions us to reach an annual revenue run
rate of over INR1,300 crores by the end of FY28, more than double of our FY 2026 revenue.
With the cost base largely in place, rising revenue should translate directly into better
profitability.
At Azad, we have never chased reckless scale at the expense of our margins. Every facility we
have built is anchored to customers' commitment and long -term contract. We do not engage in
speculative expansion. We are at inflection point, and we reiterate our long-term annual growth
guidance of over 25% plus. I want to thank our customers, our partners, and Team Azad for their
relentless execution, and our shareholders for their continued confidence in our journey. Now,
hand over to our CFO, Mr. Ronak Jajoo. Thank you.

Financial Highlights in Q2 FY27:
• Total Revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹2,743 million, reflecting 75.8% YoY growth.
Revenue performance was supported by strong module volumes, healthy product
realizations, and steady execution.
• EBITDA stood at ₹284 million with an EBITDA margin of 10.4%. The movement
was attributable to lower capacity utilization during the regulatory procurement
pause while fixed costs remained unchanged, coupled with shifts in product mix
and working capital utilization.
• PAT for the quarter was ₹39 million with a PAT margin of 1.4%.
Key Business Highlights:
• Order inflows till date:
- Secured a major order worth ₹628.37 crore from a global renewable energy group
for the supply of N -Type TOPCon 615/620 Wp Glass -to-Glass (G12R) solar PV
modules, representing the largest single order secured during FY27.
- Received a work order worth ₹42.47 crore for the supply of N-Type TOPCon 620
Wp Glass-to-Glass (G12R) solar PV modules.
- Secured domestic work orders aggregating ₹74.77 crore for the supply of solar
PV modules.
- Received a work order worth ₹75.96 crore for the supply of N-Type TOPCon 620
Wp Glass-to-Glass (G12R) solar PV modules.
- Solex Energy and its subsidiary, Solex Green Energy Private Limited, secured two
work orders aggregating ₹194.14 crore (₹180.98 crore and ₹13.16 crore,
respectively) for the supply of TOPCon Bifacial Glass-to-Glass solar PV modules.
Commenting on the results, Dr. Chetan Shah, Chairman and Managing Director
said:
“Q2 & H1 FY27 marked a period of transition for the solar module industry, with evolving
ALMM List-II regulations and changes in customer delivery schedules impacting market
visibility. During the quarter, Solex Energy reported revenue of ₹2,743 million, EBITDA
of ₹284 million and PAT of ₹39 million. Uncertainty around regulatory requirements led
the Company to defer fresh inventory procurement from May until clarity emerged in
mid-July, with supplies received by September.
The Company continues to focus on strengthening its manufacturing capabilities through
its 4 GW module manufacturing platform, automated production lines and MES-enabled
traceability. It is also progressing with its planned 2.2 GW solar cell manufacturing
facility as part of its backward-integration strategy. Order book visibility stands at over
advance payments, while the remaining ₹3,000 crore is at an advanced closure stage,
pending finalisation of pricing and production schedules.”
About Solex Energy Ltd
Headquartered in Surat, Gujarat, Solex Energy Limited has been a pioneer in India’s solar

PRESS RELEASE
Cyient DLM, Hindustan Shipyard Limited Sign MoU to
Explore Collaboration in Maritime & Defence Electronics
Partnership to explore opportunities in indigenisation, advanced electronics,
manufacturing and lifecycle support for maritime & defence applications
Hyderabad, India, November 14, 2026: Cyient DLM, an integrated electronics
manufacturing solutions partner for Design-Led Manufacturing, and Hindustan Shipyard
Limited (HSL) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore opportunities
for collaboration in advanced electronics and technology solutions for maritime and defence
applications.
The MoU brings together HSL's experience in shipbuilding, ship repair and platform
integration with Cyient DLM's capabilities in mission-critical electronics, embedded systems,
power electronics, precision manufacturing, testing and product lifecycle support. The
collaboration will explore areas that can contribute to greater indigenization and technology
development in support of the Government of India's Atmanirbhar Bharat objectives.
Under the framework, the two organizations will evaluate potential areas of cooperation
across electronics, embedded systems, power electronics, testing, manufacturing and
lifecycle support for maritime and defence applications. The companies will also explore
opportunities in areas such as indigenization, obsolescence management, test and support
systems, autonomous and unmanned maritime platforms, power electronics and AI-enabled
maintenance solutions.
Speaking about the partnership, Rajendra Velagapudi, Managing Director & Chief Executive
Officer, Cyient DLM , said, “ India’s maritime and defence ecosystem presents a significant
opportunity to build stronger indigenous technology and manufacturing capabilities. Our
engagement with Hindustan Shipyard Limited brings together complementary strengths in
shipbuilding and platform integration with Cyient DLM’s expertise in mission -critical
electronics and manufacturing. We look forward to exploring opportunities where our
combined capabilities can support indigenization, technology development and long -term
lifecycle requirements for maritime and defence platforms.”
“This MoU provides a framework for Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Cyient DLM to explore
areas where our respective capabilities can complement each other. As India strengthens its
indigenous maritime and defence ecosystem, collaboration across shipbuilding, electronics,
technology and lifecycle support can play an important role. We look forward to evaluating
opportunities that can contribute to greater self-reliance and technology development,” said,
R Adm C Raghuram, VSM (Retd,), Chairman and Managing Director , Hindustan Ship yard
Limited.
About Cyient DLM
Cyient DLM (Estd: 1993, NSE: CYIENTDLM) is a leading Integrated Electronics Manufacturing
Solutions provider that offers Design Led Manufacturing (DLM) solutions to customers. We
take ownership of design, manufacturing, testing, precision machining and certification
support to ensure that customers' products meet robust reliability, safety and performance
standards. We have expertise in safety-critical electronics in highly regulated industries. With
a global presence and a strong commitment to delivering value-driven solutions, the company
has been instrumental in transforming businesses through innovation and technology.
About Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL):
Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) is a premier, Miniratna Category -I defense public sector
undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. Founded in 1941 and based
on the strategic E ast Coast in Visakhapatnam, HSL serves as a critical custodian of India's
national maritime capability. The shipyard is a fully integrated maritime enterprise specializing
in the design, construction, repair, and refit of complex naval platforms, commercia l ships,
and submarines. Backed by an extensive manufacturing footprint and an advanced supply
ecosystem involving thousands of domestic MSMEs, HSL remains a frontline driver of
indigenous defense manufacturing and maritime self-reliance.

the AGM.

accordance with the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat

Sub: Intimation under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended
(“SEBI Listing Regulations”).
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we hereby inform that the
Board of Directors of Pricol Limited (“Company”), at its meeting held on 13 November 2026,
has approved the execution of a share purchase agreement (“Share Purchase Agreement”)
amongst Topaz Terrace Investments (an affiliate entity of Warburg Pincus LLC)
(“Acquirer”), the following members of the promoter and promoter group of the Company
namely, Mr. Vijay Mohan, Mr. Vikram Mohan and Mrs. Vanitha Mohan (Promoters), and
Mr. Viren Mohan, Ms. Manasa Mohan, Ms. Madhura Mohan, Pricol Holdings Private
Limited, Pricol Engi neering Industries Private Limited, Shrimay Enterprises Private
Limited and Pricol Logistics Private Limited (collectively, the “Sellers”), the Company and
Pricol Autotech Limited (“Pricol Autotech”), in relation to the proposed sale of an aggregate
of 4,69,34,833 (Four Crore Sixty-Nine Lakhs Thirty-Four Thousand Eight Hundred Thirty-
Three) equity shares corresponding to 38.51% (thirty eight point five one percent) of the
paid-up equity share capital of Pricol Autotech, on a fully diluted basis, to be collectively
held by the Sellers pursuant to the allotment of equity shares of Pricol Autotech to the
Sellers in terms of the Scheme of Demerger ( defined below) to the Acquirer (“ Proposed
Transaction”).
As intimated earlier vide our letter dated 27 June 2026, the Boards of Directors of the
Company and Pricol Autotech had, on 27 June 2026, approved a scheme of arrangement
between the Company and Pricol Autotech and their respective shareholders and creditors
under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013,
which provides, inter alia, for the demerger of the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle
Solutions (DICVS) Business ( as defined in the Scheme of Demerger ) of the Company into
Pricol Autotech and, in consideration, the issue of 1 (one) fully paid -up equity share of
Pricol Autotech of face value INR 1 each for every 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of the
Company of face value INR 1 each held by the shareholders of the Company (“Scheme of
Demerger”).
The details regarding the Proposed Transaction as required under Regulation 30 of the
SEBI Listing Regulations read with SEBI master circular dated January 30, 2026, bearing
reference no. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 (“Master Circular”) are
enclosed as the ‘Annexures’ to this letter.
Please also find attached a press release in relation to the Proposed Transaction.
We request you to kindly acknowledge the above information on record.
Thanking you
Yours faithfully,

Regaal Resources delivers Highest-Ever Quarterly PAT of ₹232 Million, with a PAT Margin of 7.3% Kolkata, West Bengal, 13th November 2026: Regaal Resources Limited (herein referred to as "RRL"), one of the most trusted names in the maize wet milling industry, announced its Q2 FY27 results today. The Board of Directors of RRL at its meeting held on 13th November 2026 took on record the unaudited Financial Results for the second quarter of Financial Year 2026-27. ₹ Millions Financial Summary Q2 FY27 Q2 FY26 YoY% Q1 FY27 QoQ% H1 FY27 H1 FY26 YoY % FY26 Total Income 3,169 3,203 (1.1%) 2,026 56.4% 5,195 5,671 (8.4%) 11,354 Operating Income 3,166 3,200 (1.1%) 2,021 56.6% 5,187 5,666 (8.5%) 11,342 Value Add 1,290 785 64.3% 805 60.2% 2,096 1,403 49.3% 2,958 Value Add Margin 40.8% 24.5% 1,622 bps 39.8% 92 bps 40.4% 24.8% 1,563 bps 26.1% Operating EBITDA 542 350 54.7% 310 75.0% 852 595 43.2% 1,266 Operating EBITDA Margin 17.1% 10.9% 617 bps 15.3% 180 bps 16.4% 10.5% 592 bps 11.2% PAT 232 167 38.7% 133 73.9% 365 258 41.6% 556 PAT Margin 7.3% 5.2% 210 bps 6.6% 74 bps 7.0% 4.5% 248 bps 4.9% Diluted EPS (₹) 2.24 1.84 21.7% 1.29 73.6% 3.53 2.93 20.5% 5.81 Notes:  Value Add is calculated as Operating Income minus Cost of Goods Sold  Value Add Margin shows value add as a percentage of Operating Income  Operating EBITDA represents profit before tax plus Finance Costs, Depreciation, Amortization, and minus Other Income  Operating EBITDA Margin shows EBITDA as a percentage of Operating Income  Diluted EPS, considering the effect of Split and Bonus Issuance Commenting on the results, Mr. Anil Kishorepuria, Chairman & Managing Director, Regaal Resources Limited said: “We are pleased to report continued momentum in our performance during Q2 FY27, reflecting the benefits of our strategic growth initiatives, disciplined execution and sustained demand across key markets. Operating Income for the quarter stood at ₹3,166 million. Core manufacturing revenue registered a 64.4% year-on-year growth from ₹1,902 million in Q2 FY26 to ₹3,127 million in Q2 FY27, reflecting our manufacturing strength. Value-Add for the quarter stood at ₹1,290 million, registering a growth of 64.3% year-on-year, with a margin of 40.8%. Operating EBITDA stood at ₹542 million, growing 54.7% year-on-year, with a margin of 17.1%. Profit After Tax increased to ₹232 million, reflecting a growth of 38.7% year-on-year, with a PAT margin of 7.3%. Our long-term strategy of procuring maize during the Rabi season to meet year-round requirements is yielding tangible results, as reflected in our financial performance. This approach has strengthened our raw material security, allowing us to build adequate inventory despite elevated prices and supply constraints. Further, with sufficient stock in place, we are well-positioned to support higher crushing volumes as our expanded manufacturing capacities ramp up. The selling environment remains favourable, supported by steady demand across our key end-user segments and healthy market traction for our products. Alongside our domestic growth, our international business continued to gain traction, with exports increasing 64.5% year-on year to ₹366.7 million in H1 FY27.

Our responsibility is to issue a report on the Statement based on our review. 3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410, Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity, issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. A review is limited primarily to inquiries of company personnel and applying analytical procedures and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 4. Technologies Limited ("Transferor Company") with S A Tech Software India
Limited ("Transferee Company") under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act,
2013. The Scheme has received in-principle approval from NSE and is currently

Analytical Approach
Ind-Ra continues to take the consolidated view of SLS and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Sai Life Sciences Inc., Sai Life
Pharma Private Limited and Sai Life Sciences GmbH to arrive at the ratings, as all the companies operate under a similar
line of business and have a common management.
Detailed Rationale of the Rating Action
The upgrade reflects Ind-Ra’s expectation of sustained improvement in SLS’s business and financial profile, supported by
the continued growth across its contract research organisation (CRO) and contract development and manufacturing
organisation (CDMO) businesses, stronger operating profitability, and comfortable credit metrics, despite investments in
capacity/capability building. The business profile has also strengthened with an increase in the late-stage and commercial
molecule pipeline, providing a healthy base for future growth. The integrated drug discovery model and progression of
molecules from development to commercial manufacturing should improve revenue visibility and enable SLS to capture a
larger share of customer spending across the drug-development value chain. The company’s diversified product mix offsets
inventory destocking and patent expiry risks.
However, SLS is entering a sizeable investment phase, with capex of INR11 billion-INR13 billion planned in FY27. While
the capex is likely to support the next phase of growth, incremental debt funding and the time required for the new
capacities to ramp up are likely to keep the net leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDA) elevated, relative to the
current levels, and return ratios subdued over the medium term. The timely commissioning and ramp-up of the enhanced
capacities, as well as improvement in asset utilisation and the consequent recovery in return ratios will be key
monitorables. Historical precedence suggests a timely ramp-up of expanded capacities with an improvement in the return
on capital employed (ROCE) in a time-bound manner.
The Stable Outlook reflects Ind-Ra’s expectation that SLS will sustain its strengthened business profile and healthy
profitability, while managing the higher capex without a significant deterioration in leverage.
List of Key Rating Drivers
Strengths
Supply chain realignment benefits accrue, despite a weakening funding scenario for biotech companies
Significant improvement in financial performance in FY26/1HFY27; likely to remain healthy in near-to-medium term
Weaknesses
Credit metrics to moderate amid sizeable capex; remain comfortable
Geopolitical and inventory destocking risks
Regulatory and forex risks

consolidated revenue in FY26 (FY26: INR7,754 million; FY25: INR6,264 million), while the CDMO business contributed
65% to the revenue in FY26 (FY26: INR14,171 million; FY25: INR10,681 million). The contribution from pharmaceutical and
biotech companies to the total CDMO revenues increased to 94% and 6%, respectively, in FY26 (FY25: 91% and 9%),
while that of CRO revenues increased to 48% and 52%, respectively, (38% and 62%), indicating a more stable business
profile.
SLS offers integrated services across the pharmaceutical life cycle, from discovery services to development and
manufacturing of new chemical entities for global innovator pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. Over its 27
years of operations, the company has completed more than 300 discovery programmes, with over 40 programmes
advancing to clinical phases (from the investigational new drug to phase III). In terms of therapy, the company has worked
on high value-added areas, such as oncology and other key therapy areas, including central nervous system, inflammation
and antivirals. The company is now investing in other high-growth complex chemistries and modalities, namely antibody-
drug conjugate (ADCs) and oligonucleotides.
SLS has a diversified customer base and provided services to 19 out of the top 25 global pharmaceutical companies, by
market capitalisation in FY26 (FY19: 9 out of the top 25), as well as several biotechnology companies.
Supply Chain Realignment Benefits Accrue, despite A Weakening Funding Scenario for Biotech Companies: While
the funding scenario for small biotech companies in the US remains challenging, with 22% of SLS revenues deriving from
biotech companies, Ind-Ra notes that SLS benefits from the supply chain realignment as large global customers have
started diversifying their business away from China due to geopolitical issues. According to SLS’s investor presentation of
2QFY27, its CDMO portfolio constituted 34 commercial molecules, and 14 molecules are under phase III or pre-registration
phase. In its CRO business, more than 65% revenues from customers are derived from integrated discovery programs.
Strong Financial Performance in FY26/1HFY27; Likely to Remain Healthy in Near-to-Medium Term: The consolidated
revenue increased to INR21,925 million in FY26 (FY25: INR16,946 million; FY24: INR14,652 million), driven by robust
demand across both CDMO and CRO segments. SLS continues to benefit from the strong operating leverage, with
consolidated EBITDA improving to INR6,312 million in FY26 (FY25: INR4,057 million; FY24: INR2,855 million). The

million (INR2,668 million), with a margin of 28% (26%).

Mumbai, 13th November 2026 – Imagicaaworld Entertainment Limited (BSE: 539056; NSE:
IMAGICAA), India’s largest amusement & Water Park player, today announced its unaudited
financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30th 2026.
H1FY27 Consolidated Performance Highlights:
 Revenue from Operations grew 15% YoY to Rs. 218 Crs in H1 FY27 from Rs. 190 lakhs in
H1 FY26, driven by robust footfall growth supported by an extended summer season and
healthy demand across parks.
 EBITDA increased 14% YoY to Rs. 72.3 Crs from 63.5 Crs in the corresponding period last
year. EBITDA margin remained at 33% in H1 FY27.
H1FY27 Consolidated Operational Highlights:

Key Updates:
o The divestment strengthens company’s balance sheet to sharpen its focus on the
core entertainment business while unlocking capital for the next phase of growth
• Bennett Coleman Deal –
o Board has approved the issue of warrants for the issue of Equity shares worth Rs
16.25 Crs to Bennett Coleman & Co Ltd (BCCL) as part of a marketing deal. The
funds would be utilized to strengthen brand visibility through advertising,
marketing and promotional activities across the growing brand portfolio.
• Acquisition of Shanku’s Water Park –
o During the quarter, the company invested Rs. 50 Crs to acquire 50.002% share in
Mehsana Next Parks Pvt. Ltd. which operates ‘Shanku’s Water Park’ in Mehsana,
Gujarat.
o IEL now manages the full operations of the park and have initiated expansion plans
to make it an all-weather destination.
Commenting on the Q2 & H1 FY27 performance, Jai Malpani, Managing Director,
Imagicaaworld Entertainment Limited said,
"We continue to build on a strong foundation and a steadfast focus on delivering memorable
experiences and enhancing guest satisfaction across locations. While Q2 is seasonally softer
for the parks industry, our park revenues were up by 10% in Q2 FY27 despite 6% lower footfalls
due to the high impact rains in the catchment in July-August.
Our focus remains on strengthening operational performance and improving the overall guest
experience through continuous enhancements across our offerings. We are seeing a good build
up for Q3 FY27 already.
We are also progressing with our expansion initiatives, with Hello Park Hyderabad expected to
commence operations in the coming months. This will further strengthen our presence in the
family entertainment segment and provide an additional avenue for growth.
As we move ahead, we remain committed to enhancing guest engagement, strengthening our
existing assets and building a scalable platform for sustainable long-term growth.”
About Imagicaaworld Entertainment Limited
Imagicaaworld Entertainment Limited (BSE: 539056; NSE: IMAGICAA) owns and operates
India's leading theme and water parks, including Imagicaa, WetnJoy , Sai Teerth, and Aqua
Imagicaa at various locations. The company offers a wide range of exciting experiences, from
thrilling rides and water slides to spiritual attractions, catering to families and tourists of all
ages. Imagicaaworld is committed to providing world-class entertainment across its parks.

Ref.: GLOBESECURE TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED (Symbol: GSTL)
Dear Sir,
We would like to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e. Friday,
October 13, 2026 thorough video conf erencing at 12.00 p.m. The Board Meeting was initially convened
through Video Conferencing (VC) mode. However, due to technical issues with the Microsoft Teams
platform, the virtual meeting could not be continued. Accordingly, the meeting was discontinued through
VC mode and subsequently conducted physically, with the requisite quorum being present. Following
matters were decided by the Board:
1. The Board took note of the resignation tendered by Ms. Heta Dipen Desai, Company Secretary &
Compliance Officer and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company, vide her resignation letter
dated November 13, 2026, from the position of Company Secretary & Compliance Officer and Key
Managerial Personnel of the Company, due to better career opportunities.
2. Considered and approved the proposal for regularisation of appointment of the Additional
Directors of the Company – Ms. Ranjana Malpani and Mr. Shravan Talwar as Non-Executive
Independent Directors, subject to the approval of the Members of the Company.
3. Considered and approved the proposal for enhancing the aggregate limits for making loans,
investments, providing guarantees and/or securi ties under Section 186 of the Companies Act,
2013, up to ₹100 Crore (Rupees One Hundred Crore Only), subject to the approval of the Members
of the Company by way of a Special Resolution.
4. Considered and approved the initiation of the postal ballot process for seeking approval of the
Members of the Company in respect of the aforesaid matters.
5. Considered and approved the Unaudited Standalone Financial Results of the Company for the half
year ended September 30, 2026, along with the Limited Review Report issued by the Statutory
Auditors of the Company.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Limited

We have with us Mr. Baroruchi Mishra, Managing Director and CEO; and Mr. Debabrata Das,
CFO.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen -only mode and there will be an
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need
assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing s tar and then zero
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Baroruchi Mishra. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Baroruchi Mishra : Thank you. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us for the Hindustan Oil
Exploration Company Limited's earnings call for the second quarter and half year ended
September 30, 2026. I wish you all a very happy Dhanteras, and we are very close to the festival
of lights, so happy Diwali as well.
Given this festive calendar and the Diwali holidays, the company decided to align the results
announcement, and the earnings call on the same day this quarter , rather than have 2
engagements separated by a day as has been the usual practice. We must appreciate that you
have taken time to participate even in this festive season. This is indeed a departure from the
normal schedule and we really, really thank all of you for accommodating this revised timing.
And with that, let me start with a little bit of analysis or view on the global oil and gas scenario.,
and then we will deep dive into how we as a company are performing and indeed contributing
to ensure energy security for the country, both what we have done in the quarter that went by,
but also what we would like to do in the future.
So as you all know, the oil market has been pulled in 2 directions. The Gulf supply disruptions
have supported prices even as higher fuel costs and weaker economic activity have curbed
consumption. In October, the International Energy Agency projected that the global oil demand
would fall by 2.6 million barrels a day in 20 26. A sustained recovery in Gulf exports could ease
prices.
Further disruption, however, could push them higher even with weak demand, and that's a key
thing to note. That range of outcomes reinforces the need for us as a company to exercise capital
discipline until this cycle stabilizes, and that's going to take s ome time. In Gas, the disruptions
through the Strait of Hormuz have reduced Gulf LNG shipments, as you all know. New supply
from North America and Africa have cushioned part of those losses. Even so, the IEA estimates
Asian spot LNG averaged around $21.5 p er MMBTU from March to October. That has given us
a good cushion, although we did not realize the same price for gas sales and because this is LNG
and therefore, there are imported LNG costs.
Page 3 of 22
Further, the capacities are coming in, and that is -- but we have also -- as you all know, 17% of
Qatar LNG's capacity has been taken out in this war. So, we have price-sensitive buyers in India
and reliable domestic gas delivered under firm contracts at a particular value. However, it will
need to be seen how many of those firm contracts can be honored and how much spot cargoes
take over and manage the situation.
So India's crude import bill has risen by 46%, and that is a no -brainer and in this first half, I'm
told it's $91 billion, and the import volumes have increased by less than 1%. So we are fairly
steady on the demand side from that perspective. The domestic -- what is not a very happy news
is the domestic crude and condensate production fell about 3.5% to 1 3.7 million tons.
The domestic production fell about 4.4% in gas, while LNG imports rose about 4.5%. Now crude
dependence continues, as you all know, above 88%, so the gap needs to be bridged. And we --
for HOEC, that opportunity is to deliver more domestic oil and gas reliably. I'm very happy to
say, except for B-80, all our assets and of course, PY -1, which has -- which had low production,
all our assets continue full stream 100% of the days in the last half of the year.
That speaks to the maintenance capabilities and the maintenance competencies of the
individuals in our team who are running these facilities.We have a lot of opportunities, and we'll
talk about them as we go to the next step. PY -1 will make gas, albeit that our coil tubing
intervention, which we were planning to do before monsoon have got a bit delayed because the
coil tubing units could not be mobilized.
We have a firm contract with SLB for this, and that will increase production from PY -1. That is
intervention in the existing wells. Then we also have plans to drill 2 new wells. I will talk a little
bit about that, but that will be middle of next year. In Dirok, we have to do a lot of work where
we have the capacity to increase production as we speak.
There has seen a good increase from the time that we talked last quarter. We were averaging
around 0.4 million, 0.5 million standard cubic meters on a gross basis. We are now averaging
around 0.7. But there is an opportunity to go up to 1.2 million standar d cubic meters, and we'll
talk a lot about that as we speak later in the call.
So, B-80 is our focus. It is the sort of -- I don't say it's the backbone because Dirok has done
remarkably well. But B-80, where we have 2 subsea wells, a MOPU- Mobile Offshore Production
Unit, and a tanker tied to the -- moved to the SBM is our flagship asset because when it works,
it works really well. So, we have 2 wells there, D1 and D2 and we have had some issues, as you
know about HPCL -- with HPCL to say last year, and we'll talk a little bit about that. We have the
INR260 crores worth of 417,000 barrels of crude, which we had sold to HPCL.
For various reasons related from HPCL's point of view, after a few days of processing, they felt
the quality was not up to scratch, and they had to stop processing. So, there was a situation
where we could have got into an arbitration or there was an arbitration, but we delayed, we
Page 4 of 22
requested for deferment. We are trying to work hard to get to an amicable supplement, and we
will soon get there. We have started lifting and we have made decent progress there.
Now D1 and D2, these are 2 wells and D2 has watered out. I mean, it has 93% -94% water. That
is the nature of the beast. You can't do much about it. If water coning happens, it happens.What
you will therefore -- of course, there is a reservoir management issue also that we have to be
taking into consideration. But if water ingresses in the well, then you have to go for remedials.
That's exactly what we are doing in our 2 workover plans.
For D2 well, we will shut off the water zone through rig intervention. So the rig, the LOA,
etcetera, has all been awarded or the contract has been -- and the LOA has been given, the
contract is awarded. We will have the rig on location by end of November or early December
and start work over on D2 and D1.
On D2, we'll blank off or shut off the water zone and we'll open up new zones, perforate new
plays and there we have quite a few plays, including a very decent gas cap, which can produce

and we will also perforate new zones to be able to produce more from D1 and D2.

 Pipeline under process: With the 4.5 GW cell plant nearing commissioning, ~2.5 GW of
proposals across strategic MOUs, partnerships and direct supply orders are currently
under internal evaluation — expected to grow significantly once the cell line becomes
operational.
 Backward Integration: The 4.5 GW TOPCon cell facility at Narmadapuram is nearing
commissioning, with machinery installation underway and trial production on schedule;
FCO targeted in Q4 FY27. Secured power and bulk water supply at the lowest industrial
tariffs.
 Strategic technology partnership: Five-year partnership with Caelux Corporation, USA,
to develop 3 GW of Hybrid-Tandem™ modules at Sawarda, combining Caelux’s Energy
Producing Glass with INA’s N-type TOPCon technology and targeting up to 29% module
efficiency by 2029.
 RIPS-2022 incentives: Entitlement Certificate received for the Sawarda facility (Phase 1
investment: ₹179.12 Cr), providing a 1.98% turnover-linked incentive of up to ₹224 Cr
over ~9 years and 100% electricity duty exemption, expected to save over ₹1 Cr annually
at current consumption.
 Project execution: Executed 70 MW of solar projects during H1FY27, with the IPP
portfolio targeting 400 MW+ by FY27.
 Operational milestone: Subsequent to the quarter, INA achieved a record single-day
dispatch on November 4, 2026, moving ~16 MW (26,660 modules) across 40 trucks.

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY
Mr. Manish Gupta - Chairman, Insolation Energy Limited
“H1FY27 has been a period of strong execution for INA, with revenue doubling year-on-year to
₹1,582.09 crore. While EBITDA grew 23.30% to ₹140.31 crore, margins remained under pressure
due to the prevailing industry pricing and input-cost environment. However, with global supply-
chain disruptions settling down and prices correcting, we are already seeing positive momentum
and a revival in margins. Over the next two quarters, we expect EBITDA and margins to improve,
with full-year FY27 margins and EBITDA reaching FY26 levels. The commissioning and ramp-
up of the captive 4.5 GW TOPCon cell facility and aluminium frame plant will further improve
cost competitiveness and support margin expansion going forward.

Chennai, 13th November, 202 6: TVS Supply Chain Solutions Limited (NSE: TVSSCS, B SE:
543965), a global supply chain solutions provider and one of the largest and fastest growing
integrated supply chain solutions providers in India, today announced its consolidated
unaudited financial results for the quarter ended 30th September, 2026 and the first half of
FY2027.
The company delivered a strong performance across all geographies in Q2 FY27, with
consolidated revenue from operations growing 38% year-on-year to ₹3,687.2 crore compared to
₹2,662.6 crore in Q2 FY26. The company also recorded strong sustainable improvement in
operating profitability, with EBITDA increasing 50 .2% year -on-year to ₹268.1 crore. EBITDA
margin improved to 7. 3%, compared to 6.7% in Q2 FY26, reflecting the improved operating
performance.
Profit before tax (PBT) increased 108% to ₹50.6 crore, compared to ₹24.4 crore in Q2 FY26. Profit
after tax (PAT) more than doubled to ₹3 6.5 crore, over ₹16.3 crore in the corresponding quarter
last year.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue grew 33.6% to ₹7,022.4 crore, compared to
₹5,254.9 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA increased 42.2% to ₹500.3 crore, with margins improving to
7.1% from 6.7% in the corresponding period last year. PBT for H1 FY27 st ood at ₹82.7 crore,
compared to ₹43.2 crore in H1 FY26, a growth of 91.4%.
Key highlights – Q2 FY27:
• ISCS revenue grew 24.8% to ₹2487.9 Cr while GFS revenue increased 79.1% to ₹1199.3
• Margin improvement: ISCS EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 9.2% from 8.7%, while
GFS EBITDA margin improved 170 bps to 3.9% from 2.2%
• India Geography business: Revenue grew by 64.1% to ₹1,177.4 Cr vs ₹ 717.4 Cr
• Rest of the World revenue grew 29% YoY
• Visibility: Order Pipeline for the quarter continued to grow to reach ₹ 8,200 Cr
• Business momentum: Revenue from new business at ₹ 523 Cr

(SLM) with effect from 1st July 2026. After revival under the resolution plan approved by the Hon'ble NCLT, the Kota and Guna plants have been refurbished and are

over their remaining useful lives; SLM better reflects this pattern. The change is a change in accounting estimate and has been applied prospectively in accordance

acquisitions.

capabilities across all business verticals and creating an organization that was ready to scale.

increasingly evident that becoming a truly integrated infrastructure services provider would
require us to develop stronger capabilities serving India's rapidly expanding industrial and
infrastructure sectors.

Management Commentary and Business Developments
Strong Performance Amidst Challenging Business Conditions
The first half of FY 2026 -27 witnessed considerable volatility in commodity prices, largely influenced
by geopolitical developments in the Gulf region. In addition, the impact of El Niño conditions adversely
affected agricultural commodities, creating challenging business conditions for the Company.
Despite these external headwinds, the Company remained focused on strengthening its business
operations, improving operational efficiency and pursuing opportunities for profitable growth.
Encouraging Financial Performance and Return to Profitability
The concerted efforts of the Company's team, supported by various initiatives undertaken by the
Management, have translated into an encouraging improvement in financial performance.
The Company recorded total revenue of ₹35,482.43 lakh during the half year ended 30th September
financial year.
More significantly, EBITDA increased to ₹551.58 l akh from ₹137.41 lakh in the corresponding
previous period, reflecting a substantial improvement in operating performance. EBITDA margin also
improved from 0.57% to 1.55%.
The improvement in operating performance has enabled the Company to achieve a significant financial
turnaround, reporting a Profit Before Tax of ₹257.52 lakh and Profit After Tax of ₹168.02 lakh, as
against losses in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.
The consolidated financial performance also reflects this positive trend, with consolidated Profit After
Tax of ₹177.21 lakh as against a loss of ₹120.35 lakh in the corresponding previous period.
These results reflect the Company's resilience and the Management's continued focus on navigating
market uncertainties while strengthening the underlying business.
Expansion of Product Portfolio – Entry into Industrial Gloves
As part of its strategy to diversify its product portfolio and explore new avenues of business growth,
the Company has introduced a new product line in its Fashion Accessories Division.
The Company has commenced manufacturing industrial gloves, a product category offering promising
business opportunities and potential for better margins. This initiative represents an important step
towards broadening the Company's product portfolio and enhancing its value proposition.
The Management is optimistic about the prospects of this new product line and is focused on
developing the market, expanding its customer base and achieving economies of scale. The Company
expects this initiative to contribute positively to its business performance and profitability over the
medium term.
Outlook
While uncertainties arising from geopolitical developments and volatility in agricultural commodity
markets continue to present challenges, the Company remains cautiously optimistic about its business
prospects.
The Management will continue to focus on operational efficiencies, prudent cost management, product
diversification and strengthening its market presence.
With the initiatives alre ady undertaken and the introduction of new product lines, the Company
remains committed to consolidating the gains achieved during the first half of FY 2026 -27 and
pursuing sustainable and profitable growth in the periods ahead.

which Forensic Audit was undertaken for the period starting from April 01, 2025 to July 31,
2026 and subsequently misappropriation of funds was established in the Forensic Audit
Report.
d) Person(s) involved: Mr. Yogish Mallya, former Chief Financial Officer (Key Managerial

outstanding from subsidiary as at March 31, 2026.

Statutory Auditors have noted in their report that the matter falls under Section 143(12) of
the Companies Act, 2013, and that Form ADT-4 will be filed with the Central Government.
g) Corrective actions taken by the listed entity on account of such fraud / default:
1. Removal of KMP: The Board of Directors, in its meeting on October 31, 2026, removed
Mr. Yogish Mallya from the position of Chief Financial Officer after providing him
adequate opportunity of being heard.
2. Financial Accounting: the Company has recognised the amount of ₹760.79 lakh as

equivalent impairment loss under exceptional items in the Statement of Profit and Loss for

entries, review of approval related matters and related -party transactions, evaluation of

controls and approval mechanisms. The Company is actively pursuing recovery of the

Name of the Entities: H-One India Private Limited
(“Transferor Company ”) and Belrise Industries Limited
(“Transferee Company”).

Transferee Company.

(Amount in Rs. Million)
Particulars Turnover Net Worth Net
Profit
