2 Whether the transaction would
fall within related party
transactions? If yes, whether the
same is done at “arm’s length”.
No, as per Ministry of Corporate Affairs General Circular No.
30/2014 dated 17 th July 2014, transactions arising out of
Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations dealt with
under specific provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, will not
attract the requirements of related party transactions as
specified under section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013.
3 Area of business of the
entity(ies).
H-One India Private Limited is engaged in the business of
manufacturing of pressed, welded panels and sub -
assemblies for automobiles, both for four and two-wheelers.
Belrise Industries Limited is an automotive component
manufacturing company based in India offering a diverse
range of safety critical systems and other engineering
solutions for two -wheelers, three -wheelers, four -wheelers,
commercial vehicles and agri-vehicles.
4 Rationale for amalgamation/
merger.
The Transferee Company is an automotive component
manufacturing company based in India offering a diverse
range of safety critical systems and other engineering
solutions for two -wheelers, three -wheelers, four -wheelers,
commercial vehicles and agri -vehicles whereas the
Transferor Company is engaged in the business of
manufacturing of pressed, welded panels and sub -
assemblies for automobiles, both for four and two-wheelers.
As both the Companies are engaged in similar line of
businesses, accordingly, in order to leverage the existing
strength and capabilities of group entities engaged in similar
businesses, it is proposed to amalgamate the Transferor
Company with and into the Transferee Company.
Thus, the Amalgamation (as defined in the Scheme) would,
inter-alia, have the following benefits:
(a) the consolidation of business would create synergies
between the businesses of the Companies, thereby
enabling pooling of financial, marketing, technical,
distribution and other resources along with optimum
utilization of resources.
(b) the Scheme would lead to efficient and economical
cost management, cost savings, better alignment,
coordination and streamlining of day-to-day operations
of the units and will provide a larger and stronger base
for potential future growth.
(c) the consolidation of business would result in
simplification of the existing corporate structure and
eliminate administrative duplications, consequently
rationalization of administrative expenses/ services as
well as reducing multiple legal and regulatory
compliances.
(d) the consolidation of business would allow for
streamlined decision making process, help in better
utilization of human resources and providing access to
a larger and more diverse talent pool leading to
improved expertise, skills and capabilities.
(e) thus, this Scheme, as envisaged, is in the interest of
the shareholders, creditors, employees, and other
stakeholders of each of the Companies by pursuing a
focused business approach under a single entity,
thereby resulting in overall maximization of value
creation of all the stakeholders involved.
The Board of Directors of the Transferor Company and the
Transferee Company are of the opinion that the Scheme is
not prejudicial to the shareholders, directors, key
management personnel, creditors, lenders, employees and
other stakeholders of the Companies.
5 In case of cash consideration –
amount or otherwise share
exchange ratio.
There will be no cash or share consideration involved in the
Scheme.
Since, the Transferor Company is a wholly owned subsidiary
of the Transferee Company, accordingly, upon the Scheme
becoming effective, all the equity shares as held by the
Transferee Company in the Transferor Company either by
itself or through its nominee shall stand cancelled and
extinguished. Therefore, there will be no issue and allotment
of shares as consideration by the Transferee Company to the
shareholders of the Transferor Company upon coming into
effect of the Scheme. The investments in the shares of the
Transferor Company, appearing in the boo ks of account of
Transferee Company shall, without any further act or deed,
stand cancelled.
6 Brief details of change in
shareholding pattern (if any) of
listed entity.
There will be no change in shareholding pattern of the listed
Transferee Company pursuant to the Scheme.

EBITDA margins, (c) continued improvement in operating parameters. Additionally, PVR INOX’s recalibration of the capex
strategy to capital-light model, along with higher operating profits have led to a consistent decrease in financial debt over
the last few years, with PVR INOX achieving net cash position at the end of 1HFY27. Ind-Ra expects that continued strong
content pipeline, along with a continued improvement in operating parameters and likely growth in margin structure would
help sustain ROCE at 1HFY27 levels, which would remain a key monitorable.
List of Key Rating Drivers
Strengths
Strong business profile; market leader position
Sustained improvement in revenue and profitability in 1HFY27
Improvement in capital structure
Limited risk from over-the-top (OTT) players
Weaknesses
Exposure to potentially volatile box office performance
Capital-intensive business
Detailed Description of Key Rating Drivers
Strong Business Profile; Market Leader Position: PVR INOX continues to hold a dominant position in the Indian
multiplex industry, with a presence across 114 cities. It had 358 cinemas and 1,797 screens as of September 2026, making
it the largest multiplex chain in India. Additionally, PVR INOX’s multiplex network is well spread-out over the northern,
southern, western and central parts of India, with a reasonable presence in the eastern part of the country as well, thereby
insulating it from any unfavourable developments in specific regions.
Ind-Ra expects PVR INOX to maintain its dominant market position, as the agency believes that barriers such as: (a)
relationships with distributors and producers, (b) early-mover advantage of the existing players, (c) already large scale of
operations of the existing players, (d) a lack of real estate availability for new developers to open cinemas, apart from the
regulatory barriers, will pose challenges for new players to make a significant presence in the movie exhibition industry.
Sustained Improvement in Revenue and Profitability in 1HFY27: In 1HFY27, PVR INOX exhibited strong improvement
in its overall scale of operations, with the consolidated operating revenue rising to INR37.3 billion (1HFY26: INR32.5 billion)
and EBITDAR increasing to INR13.0 billion (INR10.2 billion). This comes at the back of recovery in performance in FY26,
wherein the company’s revenue grew to INR66.5 billion (FY25: INR 57 billion) and EBITDAR rose to INR20.9 billion
(INR15.6 billion) after a muted performance in FY25. This was due to favourable admits and occupancy metrics, which rose
to 82.9 million in 1HFY27 (1HFY26: 78.5 million) and 27.9% (25.4%) respectively. Furthermore, the average ticket price
(ATP) grew 11% yoy to INR287 in 1HFY27, with spend per head (SPH) also rising by the same percentage to INR156 in
1HFY27 (1HFY26: INR140), leading to higher profitability levels. PVR INOX’s EBITDA (post-Ind-AS adjustments) also rose
to INR6.8 billion in 1HFY27 (1HFY26: INR4.3 billion).
The agency expects the financial and operational performance to continue to sustain in the subsequent quarters on
account of a likely improvement in the admits and occupancy on the back of strong content pipeline, along with initiatives
undertaken by PVR INOX (such as Blockbuster Tuesday, Students Special, among others). This, along with organic growth
in the ATP and SPH, and operating leverage would enable PVR INOX to continue to report growth in the overall profitability.
Improvement in Capital Structure: A consistent decline in financial debt, in addition to the recovery in the profitability is
likely to support the improvement in the company’s capital structure in the near to medium term. The company’s financial
debt has been declining (1HFYE27: INR5.0 billion; FYE26: INR7.6 billion; FYE25: INR14.9 billion). The overall debt level
(including lease liabilities) also declined to INR63.1 billion at 1HFYE27 (FYE26: INR67.8 billion; FYE25: INR77.7 billion).
As a result, the consolidated credit metrics improved in FY26 with PVR INOX becoming net cash company in 1HFY27 with
net leverage (net debt excluding lease liabilities/EBITDA) at negative 0.1x in 1HFY27 as against net debt position in
previous years (FY26: 0.2x; FY25: 2.2x). Net leverage (net debt including lease liabilities/EBITDAR) decreased
meaningfully to 2.2x in 1HFY27 (FY26: 3.0x; FY25: 4.7x) and interest coverage (EBITDAR/gross interest expense)
improved to 4.0x (2.9x, 1.9x) owing to the rise in profitability. Ind-Ra expects the credit metrics to continue to improve in the
near-to-medium term, owing to an improvement in profitability and a consistent decline in the debt levels.
The ROCE also rose sharply during 1HFY27 and FY26 to 16.5% and 10.2% , respectively, from negative in FY25. Ind-Ra
expects the anticipated improvement in profitability to support a further strengthening of ROCE over the near to medium
term. (ROCE = [profit before tax + finance costs excluding lease payouts + exceptional items – other income] / [total equity
+total financial borrowings – goodwill and other intangible assets]
Limited Risk from OTT Players: The agency believes the emergence of OTT platforms will continue to pose only a limited
risk to multiplexes. The COVID-19 pandemic has been instrumental in the emergence of OTT as an alternative medium for
small- and medium-budget movies and other new contents. Also, multiplexes will continue to benefit from the guideline of
maintaining a gap of at least eight weeks between a theatrical release and its OTT premiere. Overall, the agency believes
the multiplex experience remains an integral and affordable entertainment option in India and growth in the overall content
pie should augur well for PVR INOX. However, any significant change in the competition landscape/demand for the
multiplexes owing to the OTTs will remain a key rating monitorable.
Exposure to Potentially Volatile Box Office Performance: PVR INOX's chief sources of revenue are net box office
collections from cinema goers, food and beverage revenue, and advertisement revenue. The strong performance of films
screened in multiplexes is a key driving factor for footfalls, which lead to robust net box office collections, and food and
beverage sales. While consistent footfalls and high occupancy levels lead to strong advertisement revenue, a weak movie
pipeline or overall macroeconomic slowdown could weaken the same. The box office collections depend on a strong
pipeline of films being released over a particular period. That said, PVR INOX’s exposure to a combination of Bollywood,
Hollywood and regional cinemas helps the company mitigate the risk arising from the weak performance of any segment.

Other Business & Financial Highlights (Q2 FY27)

o Manufacturing EBITDA Margins stood at 13.1%

Key Operational Highlights for Q2 FY27
Diversification Beyond Automotive
• Entered electronics manufacturing with a maiden LoI (Letter of Intent) for the supply of
companies. Discussions are underway for other categories, including Main Logic Board (MLB)
fixtures and Final Assembly, Testing and Packaging (FATP) fixtures.
• Chester Hall (UK), UK -based subsidiary, secured its first incremental order since
acquisition, an additional order for track beams on a legacy program for one of the largest
aircraft platforms of the world’s leading aircraft OEM , with improved commercial terms
including price increases.
Technology Partnership
• Subsequent to the quarter, entered into a License and Technical Assistance Agreement with
Yamato Co., Ltd., Japan, granting Belrise exclusive rights to manufacture and sell air filters, oil
filters and resin air intake manifolds in India for automotive and industrial OEMs.
New Order Wins
• Progressing towards Tier-0.5 in commercial vehicles : won a program from one of India’s
leading CV OEMs to supply complete chassis frame assemblies across its HCV platforms
from a new facility at Dharwad, expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28. The incremental content
per vehicle is ₹60,000–1 lakh, with peak annual revenue potential of ₹1,500–2,000 million.
• Entered complete 3W body manufacturing: selected as the second source for complete body
and chassis assemblies for one of the highest -selling models of one of India’s largest 2W &
3W OEMs, adding incremental content per vehicle of ~₹9,000. Production from the new facility
at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28, with peak annual revenue
potential of ₹1,000–1,200 million.
• Continued to scale the suspension portfolio: onboarded our 6th OEM customer , one of the
largest premium 2W manufacturers in South India, with supplies commenced in Q3 FY27; and
secured additional orders from a fast-growing 2W & 3W OEM, with production expected from
Q4 FY27.
Commenting on the Q2 & H1 FY27 performance, Mr. Shrikant Badve, Managing Director of
Belrise Industries Limited said,
“Q2 FY27 was a quarter of strong execution supported by a healthy demand environment. Manufacturing
revenue grew 26% year-on-year to ₹23,441 million, and adjusted PAT grew 25% to ₹1,663 million.
This quarter, Belrise stepped into a new industry altogether. We secured our maiden LoI (Letter of Intent)
companies. Electronics manufacturing in India is set to become one of the country’s largest , best-cost
manufacturing ecosystems, and this order gives us an opportunity to showcase the precision engineering
capabilities we have built over the years.
We also secured an incremental track beam order for one of the world’s largest aircraft OEMs, marking
our first order extension since the acquisition of Chester Hall in the UK. The order strengthens our
participation in the legacy program of one of the world’s largest aircraft platforms, with an extended long-
term supply commitment.
After the quarter, our technology partnership with Yamato of Japan added air filters, oil filters and resin
air intake manifolds technologies to our R&D repertoire, strengthening our position with Japanese OEMs
and increasing our lightweighting capabilities.
We remain confident in diversifying business beyond automotive , increasing partnership s with global
OEMs and growing our order book while maintaining a healthy balance sheet. This positions us well for
the second half of the year and beyond.”
About Belrise Industries Limited (BIL)
Belrise Industries Limited is a leading automotive component company providing technology led solutions based in
Pune, India. BIL offers a diverse range of safety critical systems and other engineering solutions for two -wheelers,
three-wheelers, four-wheelers, commercial vehicles and agri-vehicles.
The Company's product portfolio includes metal chassis systems, polymer components, suspension systems, body-in-
white components and exhaust systems, among others. The products are largely agnostic to vehicle powertrain types,
reflecting their ability in catering to both electric vehicles and internal combustion engine vehicles. BIL specializes in
precision sheet metal pressing and fabrication with 24% market share in two -wheelers metal fabrication. BIL has 2 7
manufacturing facilities across 10 states in India and 2 countries outside India, with long standing customer
relationships with more than 38 OEMs.
BIL leverages its expertise in precision engineering by diversifying into non -automotive segments like aerospace &
defense, renewable energy and electronics.

So we have announced a third phase of expansion that will add about 15,000 MVA of capacity,

the new capacity to go live within 18 to 24 months.
The project will be funded with about INR100 crore from internal accruals and about INR80
crore to INR100 crore of debt. As of today, we have no debt on our books. This facility will be
dedicated to EHV transformers, 132 kV, 220 kV and 400 kV transformers, taking Danish Power
into the 400 kV class for the first time ever.
We have sized this expansion on the demand we see from our existing domestic and international
clients. 70% to 80% of our orders are typically from our repeat clients, repeat customers and
anything beyond our existing clients is an addition that we are looking forward to. We also intend
to dedicate about 30% to 40% of this new capacity to international market.
Our exports to Europe and Middle East are extremely important and a fast-growing segment,
and capacity has been a key constraint in committing more volumes to our international
customers. With this expansion, we will be in a position to serve that demand. Over the last few
months, we have seen the major external challenges to our industry, in fact to the entire country,
entire world.
There has been extremely high volatility in the raw material pricing and availability following
our suppliers, along with our team's brilliant execution under pressure, has been the key factor
to ensure that the impact is minimum during these challenging times.
I'm incredibly proud of how our team has turned obstacles into opportunities by streamlining
our operations and maximizing our resources when it mattered the most. Demand, however,
remains strong. Our inquiry inflow has stayed healthy with strong demand from across sectors
such as battery storage, generation both in renewables as well as thermal, transmission and
distribution, as well as exports.
With our recent expansion getting live in January earlier this year, the power transformer
division is also activated. Power transformers are now in this upcoming order book, will account
about 15% of our product mix on the entire financial year FY26-27.
Further, our backward integration has also progressed. We now manufacture about 20% of our
total requirement of tanks in-house, and our fully automated state-of-the-art radiator
manufacturing plant is scheduled to be commissioned by end of this month. Radiators have been
one of our bottlenecks on lead times as well as quality consistency, and this plant will meet about
80% to 90% of our radiators requirement.

ended September, 2026.

subscription money (344.50 per warrant; i.e 32,00,25,000/-), aggregating to Total Warrant value of
%8,01,00,000/-.

SEBI Circular No. SEBVHO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/123 dated July 13, 2023 is enclosed as

These shares shall rank Pari-passu, in all respects with the existing equity shares of the company. The Application for

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held today i.e. on Friday, 13th November 2026
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015,
we wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of Destiny Logistics & Infra Limited, at its meeting held
on Friday, 13th November 2026, at the registered office of the Company, inter alia, transacted the following
businesses:
1. Resignation of Company Secretary and Compliance Officer
The board took note of the resignation of Mrs. Rinky Shaw from the position of Company Secretary and
Compliance Officer of the Company, with effect from 13th November 2026.
2. Appointment of new Company Secretary and Compliance Officer
The board c onsidered and approved the appointment of Ms. Kajal Sharma as the Company Secretary
and Compliance Officer of the Company with effect from 14th November 2026.
3. Resignation of Statutory Auditor of the company
The board accepted and took note of the resignation of M/s. S.K. Basu & Co. as Statutory Auditors of
the company effective from closing hours on 13th November 2026. The disclosure of detailed reason will
be submitted in due course.
4. Lapse of Convertible Warrants and Forfeiture of Upfront Consideration
The Board approved the lapse of 20,43,000 Share Warrants issued on 8th May 2025 owing to the failure
of the warrant holders to remit the balance 75% of the warrant subscription amount within the stipulated
period of eighteen (18) months from the date of allotment, in accordance with the terms and conditions
governing the issue of the said warrants.
The Board approved the forfeiture of the upfront subscription amount of ₹1,68,54,750 received against
these warrants. No equity shares will be allotted against the lapsed warrants.
The details required with respect to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with SEBI Circular
No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025 -CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, and other relevant circulars/

GOCL Corporation Signs Strategic MoU with Blaze Automation for Product
Development and Scaled Electronics Manufacturing
~The partnership will use design innovation and manufacturing excellence to accelerate
market delivery timeline and build supply chain resilience~
~Strategic MoU establishes product co-development, engineering, new product introduction
and scaled manufacturing~
Hyderabad, 13 November 2026: GOCL Corporation Ltd, a Hinduja Group company,
specialising in Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider has signed a strategic
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Blaze Automation Services Pvt. Ltd, a leading
Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) in the IoT industry , to develop and supply integrated
electronic design and high-volume manufacturing to Indian and global customers.
The strategic MoU to establish a long -term, multi-year partnership focused on product co -
development, new product introduction, scaled manufacturing and supply chain
collaboration, across industrial, automotive, defence, and e-mobility sectors. Further, the
initiative would bridge the gap between hardware engineering and scaled production. The
collaboration is aimed at creating an integrated ecosystem that will accelerate product
development, reduce time-to-market, enhance quality and cost competitiveness, and provide
customers with a more resilient and sustainable electronics manufacturing ecosystem.
The collaboration comes at a significant juncture for the Indian electronics manufacturing
industry, which is witnessing accelerated growth driven by domestic demand, government -
led manufacturing initiatives, increasing localisation and global supply chain diversification.
FY2025, is projected to exceed US$150 billion by FY2030. Globally, the EMS market, estimated
billion or more by 2030, presenting substantial opportunities for companies with integrated
design, engineering and manufacturing capabilities.
Speaking on the occasion Mr. Kalyana Putrevu, Chief Operating Officer, GOCL Corporation
Ltd (EMS Division) commented, “By integrating our manufacturing expertise with Blaze
Automation Services Pvt. Ltd.’s design and engineering strengths, we are creating a seamless
pathway from product conceptualisation to scaled manufacturing. Built on a foundation of
trust, transparency and shared ambition. As we strengthen our presence in the Electronics
Manufacturing Services sector, we see significant opportunities to drive innovation, deliver
greater value to customers and create a strong foundation for sustainable, long-term growth.”
Mr. Arjun Valluri, Chairman, Blaze Automation Services Pvt Ltd, said, “This strategic
partnership with GOCL Corporation (EMS) brings together complementary strengths in
product design, engineering and manufacturing, creating an integrated platform to accelerate
innovation and market delivery. By combining our ODM capabilities with GOCL’s
manufacturing expertise and operational scale, we aim to streamline the journey from product
development to commercial production. We believe this collaboration will enable us to
respond more effectively to evolving customer requirements, enhance operational efficiencies
and build competitive, high-quality electronics solutions for the Indian and global markets.”
About GOCL Corporation Ltd (EMS):
GOCL Corporation Limited (EMS) part of the Hinduja Group is built on a foundation of trust,
integrity, and operational excellence. The Company is committed to delivering world -class
Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) by continuously investing in advanced
manufacturing technologies, quality systems, digitalization, and skilled talent.
With growing capabilities in Printed Circuit Board assembly, box-build integration, supply
chain management, and value -added manufacturing, GOCL -EMS serves customers across
Industrial, Automotive, Defence, IoT, Consumer Electronics, and E -Mobility sectors as a
trusted long-term manufacturing partner.
About Blaze Automation Services Pvt Ltd:
Founded in 2007, Blaze Automation is a leading Original Design Manufacturer in the IoT
industry. The Company partners with a global customer s to design, develop, test,
manufacture, and certify a wide range of hardware products and software solutions tailored
to the clients' needs. The Company’s unparalleled expertise spans connectivity protocols,
silicon platforms, app development, and cloud architectures, allowing them to significantly
reduce time-to-market for customers. Serving industries including Smart Homes, Energy
Management, Industrial, Access Control, Utilities, and Consumer Electronics, the Company is
dedicated to delivering innovative and efficient solutions.
About Hinduja Group:
The Hinduja Group is a 111-year-old transnational conglomerate with over 250,000 employees
across 100 countries. Founded in 1914 by Late Shri Parmanand Deepchand Hinduja, the Group
has evolved into one of India’s most respected diversified business houses, with leadership in
automotive, financial services, lubricants & specialty chemicals, energy, digital solutions, real
estate and healthcare. Through its enterprises, the Group has contributed to India’s industrial
evolution and economic progress while building strong global partnerships and market
presence worldwide. Anchored in robust governance, disciplined risk management and long-
term value creation, the Hinduja Group is guided by its enduring credo, “My Dharma is to work
so that I can give,” reflecting a legacy that combines global enterprise with nation-building and
community commitment.

the first half of the financial year '27, revenue grew 3.9% to INR1,159.9 crores. These numbers
should be read in the context of the festive calendar.

and a lot of the demand has shifted into Q3. Q2 and H1 are therefore not strictly comparable
with last year, and we believe nine months taken together will give a fairer picture, offering
reasonable comparison.
On margins, the cost environment remains challenging. The West Asia conflict and volatile
crude prices have pushed up the cost of polymers, fuel and gas, and packaging. Higher natural
gas prices have also added to our cost in glassware and the opalware operations.

which has moved from Q2 to Q3, should support performance. For financial year 2027, our

CPS Shapers Limited reports 17.8% revenue growth in H1 FY27; loss before tax reduces by 36.5%
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: CPS Shapers Limited (NSE Symbol: CPS), operating under its brand Dermawear, is engaged in the
manufacturing of shapewear, compression garments, lingerie and athleisure products. The Company today announced its u naudited
financial results for the half year ended September 30, 2026 (H1 FY26-27).
During H1 FY26-27, the Company recorded revenue from operations of ₹13.82 crore, registering a year -on-year growth of 17.8%
compared to ₹11.73 crore in H1 FY 25-26. The Company has demonstrated an improvement in its profitability, with the loss before
tax declining by 36.5% to ₹1.78 crore from ₹2.79 crore in H1 FY25-26. Further, the EBITDA loss reduced to ₹1.02 crore from ₹1.97
crore in the corresponding previous period, reflecting improved operational performance.

 Improvement in Operating Performance: EBITDA loss reduced to ₹1.02 crore in H1 FY26-27 compared to ₹1.97 crore

 Reduction in Losses: Loss before tax reduced by 36.5% to ₹1.78 crore from ₹2.79 crore in the corresponding previous
period. Loss after tax also narrowed to ₹1.77 crore from ₹2.03 crore.
 Finance Cost Management: Finance costs declined by 17.6% to ₹34.67 lakh in H1 FY 26-27 compared to ₹42.07 lakh in

Key Business Highlights
 Expansion of Manufacturing Infrastructure: The Company is in the process of establishing an additional manufacturing
unit, where new machinery and equipment will be installed to strengthen its manufacturing infrastructure. This expansion
is aimed at enhancing production capabilities, improving ope rational efficiency and supporting future business
requirements.
 Growing Contract Manufacturing Business: The Company is receiving manufacturing contracts from different vendors,
providing opportunities to expand its customer base and strengthen its presen ce in the contract manufacturing segment.
These engagements are expected to support better utilisation of manufacturing capabilities and diversify revenue streams.
 Expansion into Export Markets: The Company has started receiving export orders, marking an i mportant step towards
expanding its presence in international markets. This provides an opportunity to leverage its manufacturing capabilities and
product expertise to cater to customers beyond domestic markets and gradually build its export business.
 Product Portfolio and Market Expansion: The Company continues to focus on strengthening its product portfolio across
shapewear, compression garments, lingerie, sportswear and athleisure categories, catering to evolving consumer
requirements across different market segments.
Management Commentary
Commenting on the Company's performance, Mr. Abhishek Kamal Kumar, Managing Director, CPS Shapers Limited , said:
"We are focused on strengthening the Company's manufacturing capabilities and expanding our business acros s multiple growth
avenues. The establishment of an additional manufacturing unit, growing contract manufacturing opportunities and commencement
of export orders mark important steps in this direction. We are confident of delivering an improved performance in the second half
of the year, with a stronger focus on operational efficiencies, business growth and profitability. Going forward, we remain committed
to building strong business partnerships and expanding our market presence to drive sustainable growth and long-term shareholder
value."
About CPS Shapers Limited
CPS Shapers Limited, operating under the brand Dermawear, is engaged in the design, development and manufacturing of shapewear,
compression garments, lingerie and athleisure products. Established in 2012, the Company has progressively expanded its product
portfolio from compression support garments to a wider range of functional and lifestyle apparel for men and women.
The Company's product portfolio includes shapewear, compression stoc kings, sports bras, bonded cotton bras and panties, T -shirts
and athleisure wear. With a focus on product functionality, comfort, quality and innovation, the Company caters to diverse consumer
requirements across different product categories and size ranges.
The Company operates through a combination of its own brand, distribution network, online sales channels and contract
manufacturing opportunities. With its manufacturing infrastructure and expanding business relationships, CPS Shapers Limited
continues to focus on strengthening its presence in the Indian apparel and intimate -wear industry while exploring opportunities in
international markets.

and involve risk and uncertainties that are difficult to predict.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen -only mode, and there will be an
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your
over to Mr. Ashish Kehair, MD and CEO. Thank you, and over to Mr. Kehair.
Ashish Kehair: Thank you, Nirav. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us for Nuvama's Quarter
2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings call. On behalf of all of us, I would like to wish our shareholders,
clients, all the analysts, investors, everybody a very, very happy Diwali. Joining me today, as
usual, Bharat, our Group CFO, and SGA, our investor relations advisors.
We will quickly begin with an overview of the performance and key developments, and then we
can open the floor for the questions. Just to summarize, we delivered a reasonably good quarter
of strong performance. Client assets now are about INR5.5 lakh crore s. Revenue was about
INR937 crores. Operating PAT about INR319 crores, with a yearly growth of 26%.
And ROE remains strong at about 29%. Special mention on both Wealth Management
businesses now, over last three years, both these businesses have consistently compounded at
more than 20% growth across all parameters. This quarter, I think the performance was not only
well, but also a significant contribution came from our institutional businesses, particularly Asset
Services and Capital Markets, which continue to scale well across different products and
customer segments.
I think our integrated approach, which we have always mentioned, spanning multiple businesses
within the financial services , capital markets ecosystem across asset classes, client segments,
gives us multiple growth engines and also reduces dependency on any single market product or
revenue source. It basically, in a sense, makes the business more resilient to any kind of adverse
impact that may happen.
I think the second thing which we followed for the last couple of years that also is playing out
now, in Wealth Management, we particularly said that, while many providers go and seek the
equity managed assets of the clients, our view has been that asset class performances are cyclical,
specifically equities.
For the last two and a half years, we kept harping on the importance to the clients of allocating
to other asset classes. I think that has served us extremely well, which reflects in our strong net
flows, despite the markets not doing anything for almost last two years. I think the second was
a recognition that technology and what generative AI can deliver can actually be path-breaking.

Technology, of course, we always knew, but when the layer of generative AI came on top of it,
it basically opened up many new avenues, not only to improve client experience, but also to
improve efficiencies within the firm. I think this is also playing out reasonably well across all
our businesses now.
I will move on to the business segment updates now. We start with Nuvama Wealth. Managed
Products and Investment Solutions, which is MPIS, remains our core focus and growth engine.
Client assets have now crossed about INR46,000 crore s, and net flows were very, very strong.
For the last six months, we have had more than INR6,000 crore s, and Q2 was about INR3,300
crores.
Revenue for Q2 may look slightly moderated, but if you look at some seven, eight quarters,
every quarter out of these seven, eight, the revenue growth was more than 25% Y -o-Y. This
quarter, because last year Q2 had a very, very strong transactional income opportunity with our
real estate fund, so that basically has had a base effect.
Otherwise, there is no structural change either in flows or yields for this. Lending, we have now
kept saying that, this is an avenue which we will exploit for growth, and we have demonstrated
this now over the last 12 months. Our loan book in this business is about INR6,000 crore s,
growing about 60% year-over- year.
You know that the composition is all liquid assets like LAS, ESOP financing, margin financing,
or MTF, with LAS and ESOP being almost 75% of the portfolio. Yields also saw an uptick in
this quarter with marginal improvement in NIM, because we have always maintained that a part
of our borrowing happens through MLD, and some hedging gains and losses can lead to these
changes in the NIM. For Q2, we were on the positive side of the same.
On sales capacity, we have added about 90 RMs over the last one year and continue to strengthen
the franchise with deliberate focus on senior talent. The outcomes are actually encouraging. You
can see them in the net flows, and also you can see them in the NPS scores, which have now
reached an all-time high of 89 for us in this business.
Lastly, on the technology and AI front, as I said, we continue to embed this across different parts
of the value chain. We rolled out a new AI -powered client profiling and meeting prep tool for
RMs in this quarter. Efficiencies for this are visible, like net new money and client assets per
RM have increased by 25 -30% year -over- year. Overall margins or cost income ratios have
improved by about 200 basis points year-over- year.
Now I move to Nuvama Private, and starting with our strategic focus there, the ARR assets. The
ARR assets have now crossed about INR60,000 -INR62,000 crore s. Again, very strong
momentum in net new money in Q2. We saw about INR5,000 crore s getting added. Q1 was a
bit moderated because we saw one outflow in advisory asset which was low yielding.
If I take Q1 plus Q2 put together, we are about 11% to 12% of the opening balance, and our
guidance has always been that we will be between 22% to 25%, which I think we are on track.
ARR now contributes about 64% of the revenue. On our initiatives to improve this even further,
we spoke about Pinnacle as one of our UHNI offering, which brings together multiple things.

share. I think we are seeing an impact of this now happening. We may, over the next two to three

financial performance would largely be on a six-m onth basis, given that we are

interesting discussions developing at this point of time.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, we welcome you all to Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of
Paras Healthcare Limited, hosted by JM Financial. This conference call may contain forward -

expectations of the company as on date of this call. These statements do not guarantee the
future performance of the company and may involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to
predict.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Abin Benny with JM Financial. Over to you, sir.
Abin Benny: Thank you and good evening, everyone. I am Abin Benny, and on behalf of JM Financial, I
would like to extend a warm welcome to all of you on the second quarter and H1 FY27
earnings call of Paras Healthcare Limited. At the outset, I would like to thank the management
of Paras Healthcare for giving us the opportunity to host the call. We look forward to having
an engaging and insightful discussion on the company's quarterly performance and the outlook.
From the company, we have with us today Mr. Dharminder Kumar Nagar, Managing Director,
Mr. Dilip Bidani, Group Chief Financial Officer, and Mr. Vineet Aggarwal, Chief Operating
Officer.
With that, I would now like to hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks.
Over to you, sir.
Dharminder Kumar Nagar: Good evening to each and every one of you. Thank you all for joining Paras Healthcare's first
Earnings Call as a listed company. Wishing you all a happy Dhanteras, happy Diwali, and my
apologies for keeping you all engaged with our call, given that the holidays are here and
everybody must be eager to go back to their homes and start the celebrations.
We were listed on the NSE and BSE on 28th of October. On behalf of our Board and our
teams, I want to thank every investor who's placed their trust in us. Thank you also to our
doctors, nurses, and staff across our hospitals. These results essentially are their hard work.
With me is Mr. Dilip Bidani, our CFO, and our Chief Operating Officer, Vineet Aggarwal.
Paras Health has been built exactly in the last two decades on a single idea.
We wanted to solve for North and East India's accessibility issues. Quality and tertiary
healthcare should not be a privilege of few and in few metros. We built and run hospitals in
Gurgaon, Patna, Darbhanga, Ranchi, Udaipur, Panchkula, Srinagar, Kanpur, with a single
belief that patients should not have to travel far, pay a lot for complex care. It should be
delivered where they live. Our promise is partners in health, accessible, affordable, high -
quality, and compassionate care close to home.
Coming to our Q2 results, it clearly demonstrates why our model is working. Revenue from
operations was INR 511 crores, up 23% year -on-year. Operating EBITDA was INR 120
crores, up 47%. Margin expanded by 390 basis points to 23.5%. Profit before tax was INR 54
crores, that is 2.7 times last year's. Profit after tax was INR 40 crores, 3.3 times last year.
Paras Healthcare Limited
November 06, 2026
Page 3 of 16
For the half year, revenue grew 25% to INR 981 crores. Operating EBITDA grew 58% to INR
225 crores. Where has this growth come from? We are currently managing three clusters of
our hospitals. The mature hospitals, Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, and Darbhanga, revenue grew
8.5%. Margins rose to 29.5%.
Emerging hospitals, Ranchi and Udaipur, revenue grew 27%. Ranchi had an exceptional
quarter. New hospitals, Srinagar and Kanpur, revenue grew 2.4 times last year, and the cluster
moved from an EBITDA loss last year to about a margin of 19% in the H1 . Q2, Kanpur and
Srinagar are now profitable at EBITDA level. That has happened faster than our earlier
hospitals, and it is clearly showing a playbook that can be repeated a number of times.
What drives the next phase of our growth? The ramp -up of newer hospitals, because we have
tremendous capacity and we have room to grow. What else is happening? Better clinical and
surgical mix in every hospital, more complex specialty work, and we are tracking that by
hospital and by the doctor-wise.
Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, the line for the management has been disconnected. Please stay
connected while we reconnect the line for the management. Ladies and gentlemen, thank you
for patiently holding. We have the line for the management reconnected. Yes, sir, please go
ahead.

of growth? Where does it come from? Essentially, we're talking about four levers. Ramp -up of
our newer hospitals, which have room to grow in their capacities, better clinical surgical mix in
every hospital, more complex specialty work, tracked by hospital and doctor by doctor.
Growth in outpatient and inpatient volumes. Disciplined new capacity. We are building new
capacity in Golf Course Extension, Gurgaon, and very, very selective expansion that is going
to come up in the future, Ludhiana being an immediate expansion of 500 beds coming in next
year.
Our balance sheet has strengthened. Of the INR 500 crores of fresh issue, INR 375 crores has
already gone to repay and prepay borrowings. Of course, this lower interest cost should
support profit growth from here. And of course, not every hospital of ours has performed this
quarter. Udaipur was softer, and of course, the teams will talk about it, our operations will talk
about it.
I will now hand over to Dilip, our CFO, who will take us through detailed numbers. Thank
you.
Dilip Bidani: Thank you, Dr. Nagar. And a very warm welcome to all on our earnings call for Paras
Healthcare. I will take you through the financial numbers, and before I give you some of the
numbers, some of which at the cost of repetition, I will repeat. A detailed presentation has been
number of details would be available to you there as well.

growth of 23% on a year -on-year basis. Sequentially, the revenues for Q2 grew by 8.6% over

quarter of record performance for Surya Roshni. Consolidated revenue grew by 33% year -on-
year and 20% sequentially to INR2,448 crores. EBITDA stood at INR143 crores and PAT at
INR77 crores, up 19% and 29% quarter-on-quarter respectively.

18% to INR263 crores and PAT grew by 26% to INR136 crores, driven by 22% volume growth
in Steel Pipes and Strips, and 16% revenue growth in Lighting and Consumer Durables.

half traditionally being our strongest period, we enter H2FY27 with strong visibility and remain
on track to deliver our FY27 targets and promises.

quickly.

Hitesh Joshi: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining us for GIC Re's earnings call
for Q2 FY 2027. Before turning to our financial performance, let me briefly touch upon the
broader operating environment. The global operating environment remains s haped by
geopolitical uncertainty, changing trade dynamics, and broader economic developments. Natural
catastrophe activity, rising asset values, and elevated loss costs continue to influence risk
assessment, pricing, and demand for insurance and reinsurance protection.
Catastrophe exposure remains a key industry consideration. The frequency and severity of
events, concentrations of economic value in exposed regions, and higher repair, reconstruction,
and replacement costs reinforce the importance of adequate capacity, pr icing adequacy, and
disciplined risk assessment. Global reinsurance capacity remains healthy, increasing
competition across certain business lines and geographies. Against this backdrop, GIC Re
remains selective in its underwriting, prioritizing pricing adequacy and sustainable risk-adjusted
returns over premium growth alone.
Underlying demand for protection remains strong, supported by growing asset values, greater
awareness of evolving risks, growing accumulation, and increasing focus on financial resilience.
In India, economic growth, infrastructure development, an expandin g base of insurable assets,

Let me now take you through some of the key financial highlights.
The gross premium income of the company was INR11,228.21 crores for Q2 FY 2027 as
compared to INR9,601.70 crores for Q2 FY 2026. Gross premium income for half year FY 2027
was INR24,703.57 crores compared to INR21,989.71 crores. The investment income stood at
INR4,238.26 crores in Q2 as compared to INR3,791.67 crores.
Investment income for half year 27 was INR7,503.78 crores compared to INR7,105.41 crores in
the corresponding period of the previous year. Incurred claims ratio stood at 87.39% in Q2 FY
2027 as compared to 81.50% during the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Combined
ratio in Q2 FY 2027 stood at 110.23% versus 109.15% during the corr esponding quarter of the
previous year.
The incurred claims ratio for H1 27 was 86.19% compared to 86.45% in H1 FY 2026. The
combined ratio was 107.39% compared to 107.41% in the corresponding period of the previous
year. The adjusted combined ratio, taking into consideration the policyholders' investment
income, works out to 85.92% for the half year ended 30th September 26 as compared to 83.74%
in half year FY 2026. Underwriting loss for H1 27 was INR1,709.06 crores compared to
INR1,234.59 crores in H1 FY 2026.
Profit before tax stood at INR3,101.54 crores in Q2 FY 2027 as against INR3,472.76 crores.
Profit after tax stood at INR2,455.62 crores in Q2 FY 2027 compared to INR2,866.79 crores.
Profit before tax for H1 27 was INR5,591.79 crores compared to INR5,716.30 crores. Profit
after tax was INR4,377.66 crores compared to INR4,619.02 crores. Our solvency position
remains strong.
The solvency ratio stood at 4.18 as on 30th September 26 compared to 3.85 as on 30th September
25. Net worth excluding fair value change to date INR53,402.32 crores as on 30th September
26 compared to INR46,669.38 crores as on 30th September 25. Net worth of the company
including fair value change to date INR93,138.68 crores as on 30th September 26 as against
INR88,709.19 crores as on 30th September 25.
On the premium breakup side, domestic premium for H1 FY 2027 was INR19,794.41 crores and
international premium was INR4,909.16 crores. The percentage split was domestic 80% and
international 20%. Domestic premium recorded a year -on-year growth of 15.9%, while
international premium remained broadly unchanged year-on-year in this half year. The first half
recorded healthy premium growth a nd a broadly stable claims ratio. Underwriting losses,
however, increased year-on-year.
Strengthening underwriting profitability remains a key priority, and our efforts are directed
towards better risk selection, appropriate pricing, and active portfolio management. The
international portfolio recorded an improvement in its combined ratio to 108.24% in H1 27 from
119.87% in H1 FY 2026. This is encouraging progress, although the portfolio has yet to achieve

employment generation. Despite the expansion of formal credit, a significant section of our
smaller businesses and individual entrepreneurs continues to remain underserved. Recent
industry data also highlights the growing importance of individual business borrowers and the
opportunity to deepen formal credit access.

disciplined approach to lending. At Moneyboxx, we remain focused on addressing this

Dear Madam/Sir,
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations, we wish to inform you that the board of
directors (“Board”) of Relaxo Footwear Limited (“Company”), at its meeting held today i.e. Friday,
November 13, 2026, has approved the proposal for setting up a joint venture with the Kenafric
Group (defined below ) through Relaxo Kenafric Footwears Limited (“RKFL”), a company
incorporated under the laws of Kenya, for undertaking the business of manufacturing, marketing,
sale and distribution of footwear products in Kenya and such other agreed territories as
contemplated under the definitive agreements.

agreements:

the Company, Zarrar Holding Limited, Chehar Bharatkumar Shah and Mikul Nilesh Shah

Only), representing 51% of its issued and paid-up share capital on completion, while the Kenafric
Group will collectively subscribe to equity shares representing the remaining 49% of its share
capital. Upon completion of the transactions contemplated under the SSHA, RKFL will become a
subsidiary of the Company.

Manufacturing Limited (“KML”) and RKFL, pursuant to which the Company proposes to transfer
certain identified movable assets, including plant, machinery, equipment and tools, and
assign/novate identified customer and supplier contracts relating to its footwear business to
RKFL, against cash consideration payable by RKFL to the Company, in accordance with the
terms of the agreement.

November 13, 2026 i.e. today has, inter alia, considered and approved the following:

Let me begin by giving you a perspective on the industry environment and then take you through
the key highlights of the company. Industry environme nt. Q2 FY27 has commenced a positive
note for infrastructure sector, supported by an increase in domestic highway project awards.
Additionally, encouraging opportunities are emerging across other key segments, including
railways, power transmission, power distribution, international infrastructure projects, providing
further impetus to the sectoral growth. As far as fresh project awarding is concerned, there is a
significant improvement.
awarded around 95 kilometer of highways. Cumulatively, NHAI's awards reached 329 kilometer
by August end. More importantly, ministry reported that national highway project awards
reached 2,236.3 kilometer during April to September FY27, up by 62.9%. NHAI plans to award
5,200 kilometer in FY27, which is up by 66% compared to last year.
If you look at construction progress, we still see a weakness. Despite the improvement in
awarding, construction activity remained under pressure. August 2026, construction declined by
NHAI targeted to construct 4,950 kilometer of road in FY 2027, down 7% year-on-year. While
we remain positive on long -term fundamentals of road infrastructure, we believe the sector is
currently undergoing a period where the focus is shifting from simply awarding more kilometers
to ensuring these projects are properly appraised, land is made available and execution can
proceed efficiently.

For us, this makes diversification particularly important. At the same time, the medium to long-
term opportunity in Indian infrastructure remains very strong. T he Union Budget has provided
a significant push to the railway sector, which is our focus now, with a record capital expenditure
The government has also announced seven new high-speed rail corridors covering around 4,000
kilometer, with an estimated investment potential of nearly INR16 lakh crores, along with 2,052
kilometer of dedicated freight corridors between Dankuni and Surat. This is important because
the opportunity in railways is no longer limited to traditional track construction.
It necessarily spans over electrification, signalling, safety systems, freight infrastructure, station
development, and other specialized EPC requirements. For Ashoka, this creates an opportunity
to leverage its existing execution capabilities and participate in infrastructure spending beyond
the traditional road segment.
The Power T&D segment is another area where we see strong structural growth. India is adding
renewable generation capacity at a rapid pace, but the success of this transition depends equally
on the ability to evacuate and transmit that power to consumption centers. This is driving
significant investment in interstate transmission systems and energy corridors.
Let me now highlight some key business developments post Q1 FY 2027 earnings call. During
Q2 FY 2020, the company received LOA from RVNL, Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, for the project
of new BG rail line in the state of Uttarakhand. The project cost is INR602 crores, including
GST.
During Q2 FY 2027, LOA re ceived from REC Power Development and Consultancy Limited
for the project establishment for establishment of 400, 220, and 132 KV lines at Sakoli district
Bhandara on TBCB, that is Tariff -Based Competitive Bidding, with completion period of 24
months and operation and maintenance period of 35 years.
This is first-ever Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding, which is popularly known as TBCB project
by the company, and this project is in the state of Maharashtra. What makes this project
strategically relevant is that it represents our entry into TBCB framework in transmission sector,
thereby adding another vertical to our infrastructure portfolio.
Updates post Q2 FY27 till date. Recently, we have received a letter of acceptance from North
Eastern Railway, NER, for the project at a value of INR290 crores, including GST. Received
commercial operation COD, Commercial Operation Date, COD, for NHAI project for four -
laning of Tumkur-Shivamogga of HAM project in Karnataka for balance 45.05 kilometer.
Thus, now SPV is eli gible to receive the first annuity. During Q2 FY 2027, third provisional
COD was received for NHAI project for its four-laning from Tumkur to Shivamogga in package
three for 4.22 kilometer after de-scoping by NHAI. Thus, now SPV is eligible for receipt of full
annuity.
As a part of portfolio streamlining, no development in this quarter. Coming to the order book
status, as on September 30, 2026, order book stands at INR15,964 crore s, excluding orders

Total income stood at INR1,356.24 crores as compared to INR1,302.62 crores in Q2 FY 2026,

Rationale and key rating drivers
CARE Ratings Limited (CareEdge Ratings) has reaffirmed ratings for bank loan facilities of Birla Corporation Limited (BCL) at CARE
AA; Stable/ CARE A1+ and simultaneously withdrawn ratings on its non-convertible debentures (NCDs) issue pursuant to the full
The rating assessment continues to factor in BCL’s healthy competitive position in grey cement manufacturing, supported by
installed capacities of 21.4 metric tonne per annum (MTPA) as on March 31, 2026, which are well diversified across central,
northern, western, and eastern India. In FY26, installed capacities grew by 1.4 MTPA, with the commencement of the Kundanganj
line (grinding unit) in Uttar Pradesh (UP) in FY26. The company has further plans to expand its capacities to 27.6 MTPA by FY29.
The company has established a healthy brand recall of its cement products, which is supported on ground by its distribution
network leading to higher retail trade mix. BCL enjoys cost competitiveness in its business driven by captive limestone mines ,
coal block mine s, power generation with a healthy mix of thermal, and green power and high proportion of blended cement,
which further reduces its fuel requirements.
With reduction in debt, the company’s capital structure and debt coverage indicators improved in the last two years. However,
this remains sensitive to ongoing debt-funded capital expenditure (capex) plans to fund its capacity enhancement.
These strengths are partially tempered by moderate operating efficiencies driven by high fuel requirements in BCL (Standalone )
as one of its plants is a very old cement manufacturing unit. However, efficient units under its subsidiary, RCCPL Private Li mited
(RCCPL), continue to support profitability margins at a consolidated level.
CareEdge Ratings notes that the company remains exposed to cyclicality in the cement industry, and volatility in input costs and
realisations. Ongoing geopolitical tensions may lead to volatility in pet coke prices. The impact is partly mitigated by the availability
of raw material inventory sufficient for 2 -3 months of operations. Prolonged input cost pressure could lead to higher operating
costs and remains a key monitorable.
Rating sensitivities: Factors likely to lead to rating actions
Positive factors
• Significant increase in scale of operations and/or profitability.
• Sustained strengthening of debt coverage metrics particularly, net debt (inclusive of security deposits [SD] and letter of credit
[LC] acceptances) to profit before interest, lease rentals, depreciation, and taxation (PBILDT) of less than 2x, on a sustained
basis.
Negative factors
• Moderation in net debt/PBILDT levels (inclusive of SD and LC acceptances) of over 3.50x on a sustained basis.
• Announcement of major debt programme leading to expectation of moderation in capital structure.
• Significant deterioration in liquidity from current levels, particularly reduction in cash and cash equivalents (including current
investments) below ₹300 crore.

Analytical approach: Consolidated
CareEdge Ratings has considered a consolidated view of the parent, BCL, and its subsidiaries owing to significant business,
operational, and financial linkages between the parent and subsidiaries. Details of subsidiaries consolidated are listed unde r
Annexure-5.
Outlook: Stable
‘Stable’ outlook reflects CareEdge Ratings’ expectation of the company, which is sustaining its current financial risk profil e,
particularly, debt coverage metrics, while continuing strong operating performance.
Detailed description of key rating drivers
Key strengths
Healthy competitive position supported further by diversified geographical profile
BCL is among the oldest cement manufacturing companies in India. Over the years, it established a strong presence in cement
markets in central, eastern, and northern India. The company’s standalone cement capacity of 10.19 MTPA is supplemented by
11.21 MTPA capacity of RCCPL, BCL’s wholly owned subsidiary. RCCPL’s capacity increased by 1.4 MTPA, with the commencement
of the Kundanganj line (grinding unit) in UP in FY26. The company derives ~50% sales volumes from central India, catered by
dedicated 10.75 MTPA cement capacity in the region, followed by ~20% share from eastern region, 16% share from western
region, and 13% share from the northern region in FY26. In June 2026, BCL also commenced the Bikram coal block, which is
expected to augment coal production.
In FY26, the consolidated cement sales volume stood at 18.72 MT, registering a growth of 3.6% year-on-year (y-o-y). BCL’s total
operating income (TOI) improved by 5% y -o-y in FY26, to ₹9662 crore, supported by healthy volume sales while overall
realisations were reported at ₹4,818/tonne in FY26 (₹4821/tonne in FY25), remaining largely stable. Consolidated cement sales
volume for BCL were reported at 9.59 MT in H1 FY27, growing by ~6% y-o-y. In H1 FY27, the TOI grew by 9% y-o-y at ₹5,111
crore, with overall realisations of ₹4,934/tonne (~2% increase y-o-y). The company continued to maintain a healthy capacity
utilisation of 87-88% in FY26 and H1 FY27 (90% in FY25), though slightly moderated on a y -o-y basis because of increase in
consolidated cement capacities. Going forward, no steep price hikes are anticipated; however, volume growth and capacity
expansion in the medium term is expected to provi de overall support to the company’s TOI with steady expected capacity
utilisation of ~90%.
Large retail trade mix driven by healthy brand recall and established distribution network
Despite being a commoditised business, BCL has been able to establish its brand over the years with its flagship cement brand
“MP Birla Cement”. The company has a portfolio of 11 cement brands with varied characteristics, where “M.P Birla Perfect Plus ”
and “Rakshak” are its premium brands. This is further characterised by a distribution network of 310 sales promoters, 9000
dealers, and 41,000+ sub-dealers, which significantly supports on-ground sales of BCL’s products.
The company largely sells blended cement, which is consumed by the retail trade segment. Accordingly, the company’s retail

V.C. Sehgal: Thank you. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us on the Q2 Financial Year
2027 earnings call of SAMIL. We are pleased with SAMIL's performance during the quarter,
particularly given the evolving global environment and continued inflationary and
commodity-related pressures. Our results demonstrate the resilience of our business and
the continued trust of our customers.
Our teams continue to remain focused on operational efficiency and excellence, cost
optimization, and automation, helping us navigate higher commodity and other input
costs while progressively integrating our newly acquired businesses. Our booked
business has reached USD 106 billion and providing strong growth and reflecting the
confidence our customers place on Motherson across businesses and geographies.
Looking forward, our priorities remain clear: support our customers, improve the
performance of the existing businesses, realize synergies from recent acquisitions, and
pursue opportunities that create sustainable long-term value.
With that, I conclude my opening remarks. For in-depth details on the results, I would hand
over to Vaaman for a team walkthrough and business insights. Thank you. Over to you,
Vaaman.
Laksh Vaaman Sehgal: Thank you, Papa. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us for Q2 FY 2027
earnings call. We are pleased to report our highest-ever quarterly and half-yearly revenues
despite a challenging global environment, like Papa said. In Q2 FY 2027, our revenue stood
at INR38,280 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 27% and a sequential increase
of 9%. This growth was primarily driven by the integration of Autoelectric and Yutaka
Giken, along with robust performance in our wiring harness business.
For the first half of FY 2027, revenues exceeded INR73,500 crores, reflecting a year-on-
year growth of 22%. This performance was achieved against a relatively weak global
automotive production backdrop. Global light vehicle production declined by 2.3% year-
on-year, while China witnessed a decline of 5.5%. North America declined by 3.8%, and
Europe just down at -0.6%. India, however, remained a clear bright spot, recording a
growth of 15%.

Rationale
The rating upgrade along with revision in the outlook of the long-term rating of E2E Networks Limited (E2E) favourably factors
in the strong growth in revenues in FY2026 (Rs. 246 crore) and H1 FY2027 (Rs. 380 crore), with H1 FY2027 revenue representing
a YoY growth of 375%, and ICRA’s expectations of sustenance of the same over the near to medium term. The rating is further
supported by healthy utilisation and monetisation of its GPU infrastructure amid increasing demand for AI computing services,
hence, aiding capacity expansion, and healthy customer additions. With continued healthy utilisation levels and ongoing
deployment of additional GPU capacity, ICRA expects E2E to sustain the strong growth momentum over the near to medium
term. E2E's operating margins have expanded steadily to 75% in H1 FY2027 from 51% in FY2026 and 44% in FY2022, supported
by higher revenue realisations and improved utilisation levels. The rising scale of operations is expected to continue to support
profitability over the medium term.
Building on its industry experience and long -standing relationships with global technology partners, E2E has established a
among the leading domestic AI infrastructure providers. During H1 FY2027, the company secured a Rs. 1,000 -crore contract
from a S overeign AI Company, valid until June 2029, which provides medium-term revenue visibility, and supports capacity
utilisation. The revenue growth prospects are further supported by the company's participation in the Ministry of Electronics
and Information Technology (MeitY)'s IndiaAI Mission, aimed at expanding the country's AI computing infrastructure.
Supported by these order wins, healthy capacity expansion plans and favourable demand prospects arising from the increasing
adoption of AI across industries, the company is expected to maintain strong growth momentum over the medium term.
Additionally, the rating continues to factor in the decade-long operational track record and extensive experience of its
promoters in the cloud computing industry, specifically in delivering infrastructure -as-a service (IaaS) solutions to customers
across diverse end-user industries.
The rating is however limited by the capital-intensive nature of the business, which requires investments in GPU infrastructure
to support growth and maintain technological competitiveness. E2E is expected to incur capital expenditure over the medium
term towards expansion of its GPU infrastructure (the company has secured an additional 12.8 MW of data centre capacity,

through a mix of debt and internal accruals. Going ahead, w hile the planned capex is expected to support future growth, the
resultant leverage profile will depend on the scale of investments and the proportion of debt utilised for funding the same.
That said, the board -approved proposal to raise up to Rs. 1,500 crore through QIP or other permissible routes provides
additional financial flexibility to support its capacity expansion. The proposed capital raise offers an alternative source o f
funding, thereby, providing support to the company’s existing financial arrangements and potentially reducing reliance on
incremental debt funding. The timely commissioning and ramp -up of the proposed capacities, along with their progressive
monetisation, will remain important factors in achieving the anticipated returns on capital employed thus, supporting the
company’s credit profile.
Key rating drivers and their description
Credit strengths
Established operational track record and extensive experience of promoters in the industry – Incorporated in 2009, E2E is
led by its founder, Mr. Tarun Dua, having an experience of over two decades in the cloud computing infrastructure industry,
along with an experienced management team. Over the years, the company’s established operational track record in setting
up adequate GPU capacities across its data centres in Noida, Chennai and Mumbai, along with healthy service capabilities to
operate the same has enabled the business to scale up.
Operational synergies from strategic partnership with L&T – In November 2024, L&T entered into a strategic partnership with
E2E and has a 16.5% stake as of September 2026 in the company. Both E2E and L&T continue to drive synergies while operating
at arms-length basis, and the partnership provides benefits to the company wherein the company may utilise L&T’s data centre
capacity and offer cloud computing services to customers through the installed GPUs.
Favourable demand prospects and recent order wins to support future growth – Given the increasing demand for high -
performance computing software and integration of generative AI in applications across the end -user industries, the demand
for computing infrastructure is likely to increase multi -fold in future. The company's investmen ts in expanding GPU capacity,
coupled with strategic collaborations and the rollout of AI -focused offerings, positions it to benefit from the growing demand
environment, supporting its revenue growth and market presence over the medium term
Credit challenges
Capital-intensive business model requiring continuous investments and resulting in elevated leverage - E2E operates in a
highly capital-intensive business, which requires investments in next -generation GPU infrastructure to support growth and
maintain technological competitiveness. The company is expected to incur capital expenditure towards expansion of its GPU
infrastructure, to be funded through a mix of debt and internal accruals. However, the board approval received for a fund raise
of up to Rs. 1,500 crore, provides additional financial flexibility to support its capacity expansion plans while maintaining the
credit metrics.
Ability to maintain optimum utilization of incremental GPU cluster capacity will be key for sustaining credit metrics - E2E’s
ability to achieve and sustain healthy utilisation levels across its incremental GPU capacity remains a key monitorable. The
company has allocated a part of its GPU capacity towards the recently secured contract with Sovereign AI company and is

timely ramp up and optimal utilisation of the incremental capacity remains a key monitorable to sustain earnings profile.

Redington Partners with Salicru to Expand Access to
Power Protection Solutions across the Middle East & Africa
The partnership combines Salicru’s power electronics expertise with Redington’s channel
reach to help businesses protect critical technology and maintain operational continuity.
Dubai, UAE, 13th November 2026: Redington, the technology ecosystem orchestrator shaping
how technology is brought to market, scaled and adopted across geographies, has announced
a distribution partnership with Salicru , a Spanish manufacturer of power electronics and
uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, for the Middle East and Africa region. The
collaboration will broaden access to power protection solutions and create opportunities for
channel partners to address business continuity requirements across the country.
Reliable power is fundamental to the technology businesses depend on every day. From
servers and networking equipment to critical operational systems, interruptions and electrical
disturbances can damage equipment, disrupt services and put data at risk. Th e partnership
brings together Salicru’s engineering expertise and Redington’s local market capabilities to
help partners address these requirements as part of a broader infrastructure offering.
Founded in 1965, Salicru develops and manufactures solutions that protect professional,
industrial and household systems against power supply disturbances. Its UPS range spans
smaller IT environments, online single -phase and three-phase solutions in mega-watts, and
modular configurations for applications requiring scalability and high availability. Multi-Mega
watt deployments in the region, places Salicru as one of the unique power electronics
manufacturer to adapt customer needs by its customs tailormade solutions.
These capabilities are particularly relevant to data centres, where power continuity underpins
critical workloads and service availability. Salicru’s UPS solutions help keep servers, storage
and networking systems operational during power interruptions, wh ile its modular systems
allow protection capacity to grow alongside infrastructure. This gives partners an opportunity
to integrate power protection into data centre expansion and modernisation projects.
Through its channel network, market knowledge and distribution capabilities, Redington will
connect Salicru with resellers and systems integrators across the region. The collaboration
aims to help partners identify power protection opportunities alongside their existing
technology deployments, strengthening their ability to deliver more complete solutions.
Sukhil Nair, President, UAE, Redington, said, “As businesses deepen their reliance on digital
infrastructure, power continuity becomes a strategic consideration in how they invest, operate
and grow. Our partnership with Salicru strengthens our ability to help partners address this
requirement as part of a complete technology offering. As an ecosystem orchestrator,

Information Classification: Public
Redington brings together specialist expertise, market access and channel capabilities to
support technology adoption. Together, we can help partners move the conversation beyond
equipment to protecting the operations and services that businesses depend on.”
Raheel Islam, Director Salicru Middle East & Africa, said, “Working with Redington gives us a
strong platform to reach a wider network of partners and businesses across the region. Our

of the Companies Act, 2013, and other accounting principles generally acc epted in India. Our responsibility

2410 “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity”, issued
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This Standard requires th at we plan and perform the
review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material misstatement. A review
of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial
and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less
in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable
us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an
audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.

Statement has not been prepared in all material respects in accordance with the r ecognition and
measurement principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standard and other ac counting
principles generally accepted in India and has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms

• Q2 FY27 Total Income stood at ₹2,549.0 million, compared with ₹1,407.2 million in Q2 FY26,
registering a growth of 81.1% YoY.
• Q2 FY27 EBITDA stood at ₹151.5 million, while PAT was ₹41.9 million.
• H1 FY27 Total Income reached ₹4,329.3 million, with EBITDA of ₹358.2 million and PAT of
₹136.9 million.
• Board approved a 50:50 joint venture with Rays Power Infra to establish a 2.4 GW solar PV
cell manufacturing facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, with an estimated project
• Successfully commissioned its 50 MW AC solar project in Assam and received charging
permission for the 200 MW AC / 272 MW DC Khavda project in Gujarat.
• Expanded its clean energy portfolio with the launch of residential and C&I BESS products, a
central power conversion system and solar modules.
• Exploring opportunities in the Data Centre EPC segment through discussions with global
players for a potential technical collaboration.
Noida, 13th November 2026: Solarworld Energy Solutions Limited, a leading provider of solar EPC
and clean energy solutions, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half
year ended September 30, 2026.
During Q2 FY27, the Company reported Total Income of ₹ 2,549.0 million, EBITDA of ₹ 151.5 million
and Profit After Tax (PAT) of ₹ 41.9 million. For H1 FY27, Total Income stood at ₹ 4,329.3 million,
while EBITDA and PAT stood at ₹ 358.2 million and ₹ 136.9 million, respectively.

Key Business & Strategic Highlights
In September 2026, the Company's Board approved a 50:50 joint venture with Rays Power Infra to
develop a 2.4 GW solar PV cell manufacturing facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh. The project
crore. Commercial production is targeted to commence by June 2027.
The proposed facility marks an important step towards strengthening the Company's manufacturing
capabilities and advancing its integrated clean energy strategy.
The Company successfully commissioned its 50 MW AC solar project in Assam and received charging
permission for its 200 MW AC / 272 MW DC Khavda project in Gujarat. These developments reflect
continued progress across its project portfolio and execution capabilities in key renewable energy
markets.
The Company continued to broaden its clean energy offerings with the launch of LFP -based home
energy storage batteries, a 2,500 kVA central power conversion system developed in collaboration
with Belectriq, and AQUILA bifacial G12 solar modules with capacities of up to 715 Wp. These additions
strengthen Solarworld's capabilities across power generation, conversion and storage, enabling it to
address a wider range of residential, commercial and utility-scale requirements.
As part of its broader growth strategy, the Company is in discussions with global players for a potential
technical collaboration to enter the Data Centre EPC segment. This initiative reflects Solarworld's
intent to explore opportunities in adjacent infras tructure segments and leverage its existing
engineering and project execution capabilities. The Company currently has a solar project portfolio of
over 1.5 GW and a BESS EPC and IPP portfolio exceeding 1.2 GW, reflecting its growing presence across
the clean energy value chain.
Management Commentary
Solarworld Energy Solutions Limited, said:
“India's clean energy landscape is evolving beyond capacity additions towards the development of an
integrated ecosystem spanning manufacturing, power conversion and energy storage. As the sector
scales, the ability to offer solutions across these intercon nected segments will become increasingly
important.
Our proposed solar cell manufacturing joint venture is a significant step towards strengthening our
backward integration and building greater depth across the solar value chain. Alongside this, our
expanding product portfolio and progress across project execution reflect our focus on addressing the
changing requirements of the market. We are also evaluating opportunities in adjacent infrastructure
segments, including Data Centre EPC, as we look to build on our engineering and execution capabilities.
Going forward, our priorities will remain centred on strengthening our manufacturing footprint,
expanding our integrated clean energy offerings and maintaining a disciplined approach to execution
and capital allocation.”
Priorities Ahead
Solarworld will continue to focus on strengthening its position across the clean energy value chain
through the development of its proposed solar cell manufacturing facility, expansion of its module
manufacturing and EPC capabilities, and growth in the BESS and power conversion segments. The
Company will also continue to evaluate opportunities in complementary infrastructure businesses
while maintaining an emphasis on operational efficiency, disciplined capital allocation and
sustainable growth.
About Solarworld Energy Solutions Limited:
Solarworld Energy Solutions Limited (SOLARWORLD | 544532 | INE0TY101024) has over 13 years of
experience and a 1.5 GW+ Solar project portfolio and 1.2 GW+ B ESS EPC/IPP Portfolio across India.
Headquartered in Noida, the company offers end -to-end Solar EPC, large -scale Solar Park
Development, and customised rooftop and ground-mounted solar solutions for commercial, industrial
and utility clients. With a state -of-the-art 1.552 GW solar module manufacturing facility, a 5 GW
junction box manufacturing line developed through a joint venture, and a 3. 4 GW battery energy
storage system (BESS) manufacturing facility in Roorkee, Uttarakhand, Solarworld ensures world-class
quality and performance across its solar and storage offerings. The company is also backward
integrating into solar cell manufacturing through a joint venture in Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh.
Solarworld was listed on the NSE and BSE in September 2025.
