We wish to inform you that Archean Chemical Industries Limited (“Company”) has entered into
a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (“MoU”) with the Andhra Pradesh Economic
Development Board, Government of Andhra Pradesh, to explore the establishment of a
Battery Energy Storage Giga Factory at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.
The Company, leveraging its established presence in specialty chemicals, had made a strategic
investment in Offgrid Energy Labs, which is developing advanced chemistry-based battery
energy-storage systems, particularly for stationary and long-duration energy-storage
applications. Offgrid Energy commenced operations of its pilot plant in July 2026 and is now
further evaluating initiatives towards technical and commercial scale up.
Considering the evolving energy-storage landscape and the increasing focus on domestic
battery manufacturing, the Company has entered into the aforesaid MoU. The proposed project
envisages a manufacturing capacity of up to 5 GWh per annum, with an indicative investment
collaboration with technology and/or ﬁnancial partners.
The proposed investment is subject to feasibility assessment, technology validation, ﬁnancing
arrangements, requisite Board and regulatory approvals, mutually acceptable government
incentives, applicable land allotment/bidding processes and execution of deﬁnitive agreements.
The MoU is non-binding and does not constitute a ﬁrm investment commitment by the

Manipal Hospitals Delivers 37.3% Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27, EBITDA Rises 29.8%.
Patient-led growth momentum support performance across the network
Bengaluru, Karnataka, November 13, 2026: Manipal Health Enterprises Limited (Manipal Hospitals),
India’s largest pan -India multi -specialty hospital networks by bed capacity, today announced its
financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27).
The company delivered a strong operating performance during the quarter, supported by sustained
patient demand, growth in high-acuity specialties and capacity absorption. Improving occupancy and
operating efficiencies further strengthened the performance of the expanded network.
Operating Performance
Revenue from operations stood at ₹ 3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, registering 37.3% year -on-year growth,
while EBITDA stood at ₹ 882 crore, up 29.8% year -on-year. EBITDA margin was 26.0%, and 26.8%
excluding Sahyadri. For H1 FY27, revenue reached ₹ 6,490 crore, u p 37.7%, and EBITDA reached ₹
1,631 crore, up 28.2%. Excluding the ₹ 15 crore one -off gain in H1 FY26, EBITDA growth was 29.8%.
Sahyadri, acquired on October 3, 2025, is included in the current -period consolidated results but not
in the corresponding prior-year periods.
70.1%, with average operational capacity of 7,331 beds and average length of stay of 2.8 days. The
300-licensed-bed Electronic City hospital in Bengaluru opened during the quarter, taking the
network’s licensed bed capacity to 13,440 as of September 30, 2026.
Reported PAT stood at ₹ 285 crore in Q2 FY27. PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹ 380 crore, up
21.6% year-on-year; additionally excluding ₹ 75 crore of post -tax interest on the NCD raised for the
Sahyadri acquisition, PAT was ₹ 455 crore, up 45.6%. Consolidated ARPOB stood at ₹ 70,600 per day;
excluding Sahyadri, ARPOB was ₹ 76,600 per day, up 8.5%. Net debt, excluding lease liabilities, stood
at ₹ 343 crore at quarter-end, with net debt to annualised EBITDA of 0.10 times.
Sahyadri Integration Supports Growth
Sahyadri Hospitals contributed ₹ 375 crore in revenue and ₹ 73 crore in EBITDA during Q2 FY27. For
H1 FY27, revenue reached ₹ 707 crore, up 17.8%*, and EBITDA reached ₹ 131 crore, up 24.1%*. H1
occupancy was 67.0%, up 270 basis points, while ARPOB increased 12.5% to ₹ 44,100 per day.
Integration progressed through the rollout of centralised procurement rates and the addition and
enhancement of clinical capability & programs. Digital revenue contribution at Sahyadri reached 11%,
supported by continued digital engagement and community outreach initiatives. The phased brand
transition has been initiated with a Q4 FY27 timeline, while the nine -hospital Pune cluster is being
developed as an integrated network with shared leadership, referrals and clinical capabilities.
High-Acuity Specialties Continue to Drive Momentum
The six CONGO -R Centres of Excellence —Cardiac Sciences, Oncology, Neurosciences,
Gastroenterology, Orthopedics and Renal Sciences—continued to support high-acuity care across the
network. In H1 FY27, oncology revenue grew 51% year -on-year, neurosciences 47% and orthopedics

Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited ("CMLL"), a leading player in mining and logistics services, today announced
its unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the second quarter and half year ended

Revenue: Revenue from operations for H1 FY27 rose 89.13% YoY to ₹1,176.50 Cr, driven by higher volumes at
existing sites and the start of three new contracts won in Q1 FY27. Excluding the diesel cost pass -through of
₹184.10 Cr, normalised revenue grew 59.5% YoY to ₹992.40 Cr. Q2 FY27 revenue more than doubled YoY to
₹519.45 Cr.
EBITDA: EBITDA for H1 FY27 grew 48.69% YoY to ₹183.57 Cr. In Q2 FY27, EBITDA grew 163.48% YoY to ₹73.20 Cr
and the normalised EBITDA margin improved by 446 bps YoY to 16.60%.
PAT and cash profit: H1 FY27 PAT of ₹22.25 Cr was marginally lower than ₹23.71 Cr in H1 FY26. Q2 is the
monsoon quarter, when mining volumes are seasonally lower, while depreciation and finance costs on the
expanded fleet are incurred through the year. Even so, the Q2 net loss narrowed to ₹7.51 Cr from ₹14.23 Cr in
Q2 FY26. Cash profit for H1 FY27 grew 59.30% YoY to ₹100.83 Cr, and Q2 FY27 cash profit was 4.7 times that of
Q2 FY26.
Seasonality: Q2 revenue was 20.94% lower QoQ, significant improvement on 41.8% QoQ decline in Q2 FY26.
H2 is seasonally the stronger half, to demonstrate: in FY26, H2 revenue was 1.7 times of H1 FY 26 and EBITDA
2.5 times that of H1 FY26.
Operational highlights
The Company achieved its highest half -yearly YoY volume growth in H1 FY27, with overburden removal up 72%
and coal extraction up 41%.

In Q2 FY27, despite the monsoon, overburden removal and rake loading more than doubled YoY. The fleet

new contracts – Dhoptala-2, Dudhichua-2 and Jayant-2 – won in Q1 FY27.

(from Crisil BBB+ / Stable) and its short-term rating to Crisil A2+ (from Crisil A2).
Order book, growth capex and FY27 guidance
Order book: As on September 30, 2026, CMLL's order book stood at ₹8,633.94 Cr (including GST) . In H1 FY27,
the Company added ₹4,045 Cr of new orders and executed ₹1,079 Cr.
Growth capex: Capex of ₹584.88 Cr in H1 FY27 was undertaken to mobilise the new contracts and to meet
strong customer demand to execute beyond 100% of targeted volumes amid the coal supply crunch.
Guidance intact for FY27: With H1 revenue of ₹1,176.50 Cr and H2 seasonally the stronger half, the Company
reiterates its FY27 guidance of:
• Revenue growth of 45–50% YoY
• EBITDA growth of 35%+ YoY
• PAT growth of 35%+ YoY
Management commentary
Commenting on the results, Mr. Mohit Chadda, Chairman & Managing Director, Caliber Mining and Logistics
Limited, said:
"H1 FY27 has been a period of strong growth for CMLL. Revenue from operations rose 89% and EBITDA
49% year on year, on the back of our highest half-yearly volume growth, with overburden removal up
72% and coal extraction up 41%. Q2 is our monsoon quarter, and its seasonal impact is reflected in H1
profit after tax. Even so, Q2’s performance was substantially better than last year, with revenue more
than doubling and the quarterly loss narrowing sharply."
"We have invested ₹585 Cr in fleet, equipment and site infrastructure in the first half to mobilise the
three contracts won in Q1 and to meet strong customer demand for volume beyond targeted
quantities amid the coal supply crunch. Equally important, we have done this with financial discipline:
net debt to equity has improved to 0.95x . Happy to inform that CRISIL has upgraded our rating to A -
with a Positive outlook."
"With an order book of ₹8,634 Cr and H2 traditionally our stronger half, we remain confident of
delivering on our FY27 guidance. I thank our customers, employees, shareholders and all other
stakeholders for their continued support."
About Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited
Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited (formerly known as Caliber Mercantile Private Limited) is engaged in the
business of mining and logistics services, including overburden (OB) removal, excavation and transportation
services for the mining sector. The Company is headquartered at Chandrapur, Maharashtra. Its equity shares are
listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited (BSE) with effect from July 24, 2026.

Sub: Intimation of delay in submission of financial results for the half year ended September 30,
2026 under Regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
Dear Sir/Madam,
Pursuant to Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the Company is required to submit
its financial results for the half year ended September 30, 2026 on or before November 14, 2026. We
wish to inform you that the Company will not be able to convene the Board Meeting and submit the
said results within this timeline, for the following reasons:
1. The books were closed late because of the earlier periods: The audited financial statements for
FY 2025-26 were finalised only in September 2026. The opening balances for FY 2026-27
could be frozen only after the related audit adjustments had been carried forward, so the closing
of accounts for the half year ended September 30, 2026 started late. The finance team has also
had to clear the backlog of the earlier periods at the same time. During October 2026, the audit
team of the Statutory Auditors was busy completing tax audits and other pending assignments
early November 2026, when both the Company’s accounts and finance team and the audit team
had limited availability. As a result, there was very little time available for the limited review
of the half-yearly results.
2. Confirmation from the NCD holder(s) is pending: During FY 2025-26, the NCD holder(s)
invoked the shares pledged as security, in settlement of the Company’s dues on its Non-
Convertible Debentures. The amount realised from these shares and its adjustment against the
principal and interest outstanding have not yet been confirmed by the NCD holder(s). The
Statutory Auditors need this confirmation to verify the outstanding NCD balance and the
related finance cost as at September 30, 2026. These are material items in the results and affect
the reconciliation of other balances. The Statutory Auditors are therefore unable to complete
their limited review and issue their report, without which the results cannot be placed before
the Board.
The delay is due to the circumstances explained above, including a dependency on a third-party
confirmation outside the Company’s control, and is not deliberate. The Company has also put in place
measures to strengthen its closing process so that future results are submitted on time.
The Company will finalise the date of the Board Meeting to consider and approve the said results once
the Limited Review is complete. It will give the Exchange prior intimation of the meeting under

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Saurabh Mittal, Managing Director. Thank you, and over

Saurabh Mittal: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the quarter 2 and H1 FY27 earnings call
of Greenlam Industries. I am pleased to have all of you on the call, and thank you for your time.
I am joined by Ashok, our CFO, Samarth from the finance team, and SGA, our Investor
Relations Advisor. I hope you all have been able to see the results and the investor presentation
I will give you an update on the business side before I hand over the call to Ashok, and Ashok
will run you through the maths and the data of each segment and the business, etcetera. On the
business side, in Q2, we haven't personally been, or as a team, been very satisfied with how Q2
has panned out for us. Despite our best efforts, certain things were out of our control. I will go
business-wise on what went well, what didn't go so well, and how we look at things.
On the laminates business, which is a core business, I think after, what, nearly several years, we
haven't grown in a particular quarter, which was Q2 of FY27. Largely, the miss was on the
international front, and there were multiple challenges on the freight cost, connectivity, vessels,
competitive landscape, etcetera. The domestic business also didn't grow to the extent we wanted
it to grow, and Ashok will talk a bit more on that front.
From a business point, I think the product range, product quality, customer satisfaction, I think
be able to pull up the business in laminates for both domestic and exports. Actually, Q2 should
be seen as an aberration, and we are quite confident on driving back the business to a better
profit margin and a better revenue growth.
As far as the expansion is concerned, we are adding two more lines in Andhra Pradesh plant,
and that's running on schedule, and we should be able to begin commercial production by Q4 of
this FY. On the plywood and allied business, the veneer, flooring, door business have all turned
EBITDA positive. The ply business has grown reasonably well in Q2, and losses have come
down.

So if you see at an overall level, we have now marginal losses in this segment, and we are hopeful
as we move ahead, we will be able to put this business to growth and a profitable growth, and
we should stop losing money at the EBITDA level in the plywood and allied business. The
product acceptance of all our categories are quite high in the market, and we are continuing to
build this part of the business.
On the chipboard business too, again, we did reasonably well there too. We crossed INR100
crores revenue, INR107 crores exactly. We more than doubled our revenue versus year-on-year,
and about we were 12%, 13% more than Q1. And at the EBITDA level too, I think we were
about 8% profitability.
Product acceptance, quality of product, I think is doing very well in the market, and we are
continuously working to improve both volume and value mix. There have been product
introductions in the past, and we are looking at a few more products to be intro duced in this
category. We are hopeful that this category will also start doing better for us as we move ahead.
Broadly, if you take all the businesses, I think each of our segments, we are paying attention,
and we are looking at winning business across all the segments. I think H2, in our view, will be
better than what we have done in H1. We focus on driving utiliz ation at our plants, and at this
moment, the entire energy is focused on execution. We are on top of things and driving the
business well.
I will have Ashok give you an update on the numbers, and then I will be happy, we will be happy

sales, fluctuation in raw material prices, and change in product mix. EBITDA margin before
forex fluctuations declined by 330 basis points and stood at 9.9%. EBIT DA in absolute terms
declined by 19% to INR87 crores. Net profit during the quarter stood at INR24.5 crores.

term grew by 4% to INR168 crores. Net profit stood at INR46 crores.
Now moving on to segmental performance, laminates and allied segment. Laminates revenue
remained flat on a year -on-year basis to INR658 crores. EBITDA margin before forex

Ahmedabad – November 12th, 2026 – Dev Information Technology Limited (DEV IT), (NSE – DEVIT, BSE

Enterprise Applications, and Managed IT Services, has secured two work orders from Vadodara Municipal

management and staff augmentation.
• The engagement will support VMC’s initiatives in application development, cybersecurity,
database management, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and emerging technologies.
• The Company will deploy qualified IT consulting professionals to support VMC’s technology
• Work order for the Autodesk Forma Model Management Bundle and Forma Build Cloud, including
implementation guidance, training and support.
• The solution will strengthen GMRCL’s digital construction and Building Information Modelling
(BIM) capabilities through centralized model management, improved collaboration and more
effective construction workflows.
Together, these orders reinforce DEV IT’s presence in government and public -sector technology
engagements, spanning specialized IT consulting, digital construction and infrastructure -focused
technology solutions.
Commenting on the new orders, Mr. Pranav Pandya, Chairman, Dev Information Technology Limited,
said: “These two work orders represent further progress in expanding DEV IT’s engagement with
government and public -sector organizations. The Vadodara Municipal Corporation assignment
highlights our ability to provide skilled IT consulting teams across critical technology areas, while the
Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation order adds to our work in digital construction and model management
solutions.
We see growing opportunities to support public -sector organizations as they modernize technology
systems and infrastructure project workflows. Our focus is on delivering these assignments effectively,
strengthening long -term client relationships and buildi ng on our capabilities across digital
transformation, cybersecurity and enterprise technology services.”
About Dev Information Technology Limited
Dev Information Technology Limited (DEV IT), founded in 1997, listed on NSE & BSE, and certified to ISO
20000, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 & CMMI Level 5, has evolved from a small-scale business automation software
solutions provider into a global IT services powerhouse. Over the years, the company has empowered
businesses worldwide with a blend of information technology, innovation, and digital transforma tion.
Headquartered in Ahmedabad, with offices across India and Canada, the company emphasises
continuous innovation, quality, streamlined processes, and technological prowess. The company’s people-
and client-centric approach involves collaborating with clients globally to understand their specific goals
and to empower them to achieve their business objectives.
The company offers a comprehensive end -to-end range of services, including Cloud Services, Digital
Transformation, Enterprise Applications, Managed IT Services, and Application Development. The
company’s products comprise Talligence, an accounting data analytics platform, and ByteSigner, a digital
signing solution.
With its foundation in one of India’s fastest -growing metros, the company has continuously evolved to
meet the dynamic demands of the IT industry. The leadership, comprising experienced professionals,
drives the company towards achieving its vision of empo wering businesses worldwide through cutting-
edge technology solutions. The company's steadfast commitment to innovation, quality, and client
satisfaction underpins its growth and success in the IT services sector.
In conclusion, the company remains dedicated to driving digital transformation and delivering
unparalleled value to its clients. As the company moves forward, it continues to embrace new challenges

Consolidated Revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹ 1,539 crores up by 15%
Consolidated PAT for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹ 113 crores up 25%
Order Book as September 30, 2026 stood at ₹22,711 crores
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: J. Kumar Infraprojects Limited (JKIL), a pure play EPC
company having a niche in construction of Urban Infra Projects including Metros,
Elevated Corridors / Flyovers, Roads & Road Tunnels etc. today announced its
Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
Key Financial Highlights (Consolidated) are as follows:
Consolidated Performance highlights for Q2 FY27
Revenue from Operations for Q2 FY27 increased by 15% to ₹ 1,539 crores as compared
to ₹ 1,343 crores in Q2 FY26.
EBITDA for Q2 FY27 increased by 18% to ₹ 229 crores as compared to ₹ 195 crores in
Q2 FY26. EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 improved at 14.9% as compared to 14.5% in Q2
FY26.
PAT for Q2 FY27 improved by 25% to ₹ 113 crores as compared to ₹ 91 to crores in Q2
FY26. PAT margin for Q2 FY27 stood at 7.4% as compared to 6.7% in Q2 FY26.

Consolidated Performance highlights for H1 FY27
Revenue from Operations for H1 FY27 increased by 8% to ₹ 3,050 crores as compared
to ₹ 2,826 crores in H1 FY26.
EBITDA for H1 FY27 increased by 8% to ₹ 443 crores as compared to ₹ 411 crores in H1
FY26. EBITDA margin for H1 FY27 stood at 14.6% as compared to 14.6% in H1 FY26.
PAT for H1 FY27 increased by 9% to ₹ 211 crores as compared to ₹ 194 crores in H1
FY26. PAT margin for H1 FY27 stood at 6.9% as compared to 6.9% in H1 FY26.
Net Debt as on September 30, 2026 stood at negative ₹ 69 crores.
Working capital days for H1FY27 stood at 100 days as compared to 99 days for FY26.
Total Order book as on September 30, 2026 stood at ₹ 22,711 crores. The order book
inter alia includes Metro projects (elevated and underground) contributing ~ 7%,
Elevated Corridors / Flyovers , contributing to ~ 47%, Roads & Road Tunnels projects
contributes ~19% and others contributing ~26%.
On the p erformance Mr. Nalin J. Gupta, Managing Director commented, “We are
pleased to report a strong performance for Q2 FY27, reflecting the strength of our
business model, execution excellence across projects, and our continued focus on
operational efficiency. Revenue from Operations grew by 15% y-o-y to ₹1,539 crores,
while PAT registered a robust growth of 25% to ₹113 crores, underscoring the benefits
of disciplined project execution, prudent cost management, and a focus on
profitable growth.
Our strong financial performance is complemented by a healthy balance sheet, with
the Company maintaining a net cash position of ₹69 crores as on September 30, 2026.
This financial strength provides us with the flexibility to pursue growth opportunities
while maintaining discipline in capital allocation and working capital management.
The quarter also reinforced the strength of our order pipeline. With significant order
inflows already secured and a healthy bid pipeline across our key business verticals,
we remain confident of sustaining momentum in order intake. This robust project
pipeline provides strong revenue visibility and positions us well to accelerate execution
in the coming quarters, supported by our expanding operational capabilities and
proven execution track record.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on disciplined execution, agility in navigating
evolving market dynamics, and delivering high -quality infrastructure assets that
contribute meaningfully to India’s growth story. Supported by a strong order book,
healthy financial position, and the dedication of our team, we believe FY27 will mark
the beginning of an accelerated growth phase for the Company, enabling us to
create sustainable long-term value for all our stakeholders.”

JKIL is among the few EPC players in the country that conforms to global ISO standards
– ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management Systems) , ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental
Management Systems) , and OHSAS 18001:2007 (Occupational Health & Safety
Management Systems) – reflecting the company’s steadfast commitment to quality,
safety, and sustainability.
With a proven track record in executing complex and large -scale infrastructure
projects, JKIL continues to maintain a strong presence in key segments such as Metro
Rail Systems, Elevated Corridors/Flyovers, Roads & Road Tunnels, Civil Construction,
and Water Infrastructure.

I now hand the conference over to Vinay Menon. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Vinay Menon: Thank you. Good morning, everyone. Today on the call, we have Mr. Kapal Pansari, Managing
Director and Promoter of the company; Mr. Rajesh Goenka, Director and CEO; and Mr.
Himanshu Shah, CFO of the company.
I hand over the call to you, sir. Thank you.
Kapal Pansari: Hi. Good morning. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Rashi Peripherals' Earnings Call
for the Second Quarter and First Half of Financial Year 2026 -'27. Thank you for joining us. I
will cover 3 things this morning.
What we are seeing in the market, how we performed and most importantly, what kind of
company we are building and why we believe it is different. In the first part of the market, India
has held up better than most. IDC reported that India's PC market grew by about 12% in the
April to June quarter, led by commercial, education and small business demand and also by
premium and AI-capable notebooks.
We should be clear eyed though part of the strength reflects channel part ner buying ahead of
future price increase and higher prices are now affecting consumer affordability. We expect
commercial and enterprise demand to be steadier part of the market in the second half, and we
are managing inventory and credit accordingly.
The second part of our performance, on a consolidated basis, revenue for the second quarter
grew by about 48.8% year-on-year with PAT and EBITDA margins more than doubled. For half
year, revenue grew by 54.5% with EBITDA and PAT margin trends doubling. Our CFO will
share more details in the later part of the call.
To put that in perspective, in the first 6 months, we have earned more than 80% of our profits
we earned in the whole of last year. The quality of that profit matters as much as its size. Gross
margins improved by close to 100 basis points in the quarter. So, the expansion is coming from
mix and pricing discipline, not only operating leverage.
Annualized returns on capital employed and return on equity were both close to 23% for the
quarter and highest since our listing. And working capital days also improved to 55 for the half
from 61 a year ago. I also want to be direct about 2 numbers you will see in our balance sheet.
Operating cash flows for the half was negative and debt to equity rose to 0. 76 -- net debt to
equity rose to 0.76x. Both reflect deliberate choice.

projects. We also funded VDA acquisition through this route. Converting the cash inventory into
cash in the second half is a priority, and we will report on our progress next quarter.
On the third piece, what makes Rashi different is now the question that I think most of long -
term investors are interested. First, we are an Indian company by choice. All of our capital,
management attention and network are focused on one market, the market with longest runway
in technology adoption.
We carry no geopolitical drag from distant geographies and every rupee we invest goes where
our customers are. Second, our profits grow faster than our revenue. This quarter, profit grew to
roughly 2.5x the rate of revenue, and this is a trend, not a single quarter.
In a business often described as low margins, we have built margin profile that we believe is
among the strongest in Indian technology distribution. The third part, we choose depth and
breadth in tandem. We work with 89 global brands, each of whom we c an be genuinely
meaningful for.
Our branch head structure keeps decision close to the customer and our 57 branches, 50 service
centers and 728 locations reach deep into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, where penetration is lowest
and growth is highest.
Fourth, we are building engineering capability, not only resale capacity. In semiconductors, our
field application engineers work with manufacturers at the design stage, so the components we
supply are designed into their products for the years. Our joint venture with Restar Corporation
adds Japanese design expertise and a dedicated engineering team in India. That is a capability a
few distributors have in India.
And the last, fifth, we are now one platform with 3 engines. We distribute through our core ITC
business. We integrate through our VDA solutions in which we have acquired a 67% stake,
bringing system integration, cybersecurity, cloud and managed services.
And we enable through our embedded and semiconductor business. Each engine draws on the
same channel relationship and customer access, which means a larger share of each customer's
technology spend at higher value without a proportionate increase in acquisition cost.
Lastly, our priorities for second half are clear: convert inventory to cash and bring working
capital back towards our historical levels, integrate VDA carefully and retain its people and

growing our core faster than the market while protecting margin and credit quality. We remain
cautious on consumer demand and disciplined on credit.

Key Business Highlights
✓ Cellulosic Fibres: Revenue up 29% YoY led by volume growth & favorable product mix
✓ Chemicals: Revenue up 15% YoY led by Chlorine derivatives & resilience in Caustic-soda
✓ Cement: Revenue up 19% YoY, mainly led by volume growth and pricing discipline
✓ Birla Opus: Revenue at ₹1,337 Cr., up by 35% YoY, aim to cross double-digit RMS* in H2FY27
✓ Birla Pivot: Revenue at ₹2,785 Cr., up by 66% YoY, ARR trending above ₹11,000 Cr.
✓ Financial Services: Total Lending portfolio (NBFC + HFC) grew 32% YoY to ₹2,33,930 Cr.
Standalone: Revenue for Q2FY27 reached an all -time high of ₹12,747 Cr., up 33% YoY, led by continued
growth momentum across Core and Growth businesses. Despite global volatility, key businesses, Cellulosic
Fibres, Chemicals and Textiles continues to demonstrate resilience. Growth engines, Paints and B2B E -
commerce businesses continue their momentum, with strong consumer and brand traction. EBITDA stood
at ₹4,615 Cr., up by 158% YoY, led by dividend income from UltraTech of ₹3,968 Cr. & favourable product
mix, partially offset by higher inputs prices. Cash profit for Q2FY27 stood at ₹3,968 Cr., up 151% YoY.
Consolidated: On a trailing twelve -month basis, consolidated revenues stood at ₹1,94,234 Cr., up by 11%
vs. FY26, now at a striking distance of ₹2,00,000 Cr. The TTM EBITDA stood at ₹28,816 Cr., up 11% vs. FY26
mainly led by Cellulosic Staple Fibres, Building Materials and Financial Services businesses. The Standalone
business now contributes nearly 24% to the Consolidated Revenue and EBITDA. The TTM PAT (owners share)
before exceptional items stood at ₹5,861 Cr., up 13% vs. FY26.
Cellulosic Fibres (Cellulosic Staple Fibres: CSF and Cellulosic Fashion Yarn: CFY)
China’s CSF market remained strong, with operating rates at 93% in Q2FY27 vs. 89% in Q2FY26. Inventories
continue to remain low at 6 days at the end of Q2FY27, signaling a healthy demand-supply balance. Global
CSF prices have now risen for four consecutive quarters, with the Q2FY27 average at $1.85/kg, up 23% YoY.
Higher global prices, coupled with rupee depreciation, have led to stability in domestic realisation.
Grasim’s CSF sales volumes stood at 224 KT, up 7% YoY, mainly driven by strong exports. CFY volumes grew
by 2% YoY to 11.6 KT, amid subdued downstream demand from end -user industries, however, EBITDA was
lower due to elevated sulphur cost and continued low-priced imports from China. Cellulosic Fibres segment
revenue grew by 29% YoY to ₹5,344 Cr., supported by volume growth, favourable product mix and stable
domestic realisation, despite geo-political issues and higher input and logistics costs. EBITDA stood at ₹522
Cr., up 49% YoY, aided by revenue growth and higher share of specialty fibres.
Chemicals (Caustic-soda, Chlorine Derivatives and Specialty Chemicals)
Caustic soda international average spot prices (CFR -SEA) stood at five -year low levels of $390/ton in
Q2FY27, down by 13% YoY . Despite softness in global caustic soda prices, domestic realisations remain
relatively resilient, supported by rupee depreciation, healthy end-user demand, lower import dependence
and tighter domestic supply pan-India availability. Chemicals business, caustic sales volumes stood at 317
KT, up 8% YoY. Chlorine realisation continues to remain negative, which resulted in moderation of ECU which
was marginally up by 2% YoY to ₹33,587/ton.
Chemicals segment revenue stood at ₹2,759 Cr., up 15% YoY led to volume growth and robust performance
in Chlorine derivatives business . Specialty Chemicals revenue share , in the overall Chemicals segment,
stood at 28%. EBITDA stood at ₹326 Cr., down by 11% YoY due to higher power costs in Caustic and lower
profitability in Specialty Chemicals business . Specialty Chemicals profitability impacted due to elevated
input prices and softer demand across end-user industries.
Building Materials (Cement, Paints and B2B E-commerce)
Building Materials revenue stood at ₹27,378 Cr., up 23% YoY, led by all-round performance across Cement,
Paints and B2B E -commerce. EBITDA stood at ₹3,510 Cr., up 19% YoY, led by improved profitability in the
Cement business . This was partially offset by higher investments in Paints business to address input-cost
inflation, rupee deprecation and competitive intensity and one-time employee-related expenses in B2B E-
commerce business.
Cement business, UltraTech’s consolidated sales volumes stood at 38.2 MT, up by 12.9% YoY and ready-mix
concrete sales volumes grew by 23% YoY to 4.7 Mn m3. During the quarter, UltraTech added 4.6 mtpa of
grey cement capacity, taking total capacity (India + Overseas) to 210.1 mtpa . The business has target to
reach total grey cement capacity of 242.9 mtpa by exit of FY28. UltraTech Building Solutions (UBS) outlets
increased to 6,289, up by 1,205 outlets on YoY basis. Green power mix for Q2Y27 stood at 46.4% with a target
to reach 85% by FY30. Cement business revenue stood at ₹23,295 Cr., up 19% YoY mainly led by volume
growth.
Decorative Paints business, Birla Opus, is shifting focus from rapid market entry towards building a stronger,
sustainable and profitable market share. Traditionally, Q2FY27 remains a weak quarter due to monsoon -
related slowdown in decorative paints and higher competitive intensity. Despite challenging market
conditions, the combined market share, including Birla White Putty, remained in the early teens. The
revenue for Q2FY27 stood at ₹1,337 Cr., up 35% YoY and for H1FY27 stood at ₹2,999 Cr., up 50% YoY,
outpacing organised decorative paints industry growth.
The Q2 volume grew by 20% YoY & H1FY27 volume grew by 33% YoY. The focus extends beyond quarterly
seasonality towards building a business capable of converting market acceleration into enduring growth.

description: Indian Toners & Developers Limited (INDTONER) filed a "Reasons for Delayed/Non-submission of Financial Results" announcement on NSE on 13 Nov 2026: Indian Toners & Developers Limited has informed the Exchange about reasons for Delayed/Non-submission of Financial Results
body:
November 13, 2026
National Stock Exchange of India

“Exchange Plaza”
Bandra – Kurla Complex,
Bandra (E), Mumbai – 400 051

SUB.: Reason for Delay in Submission of Financial Results
Sir/Madam,
Meeting and delay in submission of financial results for the quarter and half year ended
September 30, 2026, we wish to submit the following clarification for your kind
consideration.
At the outset, we would like to clarify that October 30, 2026, was the date on which the
equity shares of the Company were listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited
(NSE) for the first time. Interestingly, the said date also coincided with the date of the
Company's Board Meeting convened for consideration and approval of the financial
results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
In this regard, we wish to submit that the Company could not have submitted prior
intimation of the aforesaid Board Meeting to NSE before its actual listing on the Exchange,
as the Company was listed on NSE only on October 30, 2026, i.e., the very same date on
which the Board Meeting was scheduled and the financial results were considered and
approved. Accordingly, the non -submission of prior intimation to NSE was due to this
peculiar timing and circumstances and was neither deliberate nor intentional.
Further, we would like to clarify that the Company duly submitted the outcome of the
Board Meeting within the prescribed timeline. The financial results were also submitted
to BSE and through the integrated filing portal within the stipulated timeline.
However, while uploading the financial results (UFR) on the NEAPS portal of NSE, the
Company encountered a technical and procedural glitch, resulting in a marginal delay of
only a few minute approx. 4 minutes in the successful submission of the financial results
on the NSE portal.
We respectfully submit that:
1. The Board Meeting Outcome was duly submitted to NSE within the prescribed
timeline.
2. The financial results were submitted to BSE and through the integrated filing
portal within the prescribed timeline.
3. The marginal delay of a few minutes in uploading the financial results on the
NEAPS portal was purely attributable to technical and procedural difficulties
encountered during the Company's initial filing process with NSE, particularly
considering that October 30, 2026, was the Company's first day of listing on NSE.
conceal or delay disclosure of any material information, financial figures or facts
from the investors or the general public.
The Company has always endeavoured to maintain the highest standards of transparency
and timely compliance with the applicable provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
In view of the aforesaid facts and exceptional circumstances, we request your good office
to kindly take the above clarification on record and consider the non-submission of prior
intimation and the marginal delay approx. 4 minutes in uploading the financial results on
the NEAPS portal as inadvertent and arising solely due to the peculiar circumstances of
the Company's first -time listing on NSE and the associated technical/procedural
difficulties.
We sincerely regret the inconvenience caused and assure the Exchange that the Company
shall exercise additional care and diligence to ensure timely and seamless compliance
with all applicable filing and disclosure requirements in future.
We request you to kindly take the above submission on record and oblige.
Thanking you,
Yours faithfully,

Unaudited, Limited Reviewed Results Second Quarter Financial Year 2027
Edelweiss reports Consolidated PAT (Post MI) growth of 50% YoY to INR 193 Cr
Robust Profitability * Growing Customer Franchise * Strong Balance Sheet
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Six months ended September 26 Highlights
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 315 Cr, up 61% YoY
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 5,021 Cr, up 20% YoY
Quarter ended September 26 Highlights
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 193 Cr, up 50% YoY
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 2,602 Cr, up 37% YoY
Robust growth in key metrics of operating businesses in the quarter
 Alternative Asset Management Fee Paying AUM (FPAUM) grew by 28% YoY to INR 49,164 Cr
 Mutual Fund business Equity AUM increased 40% YoY to INR 1,07,600 Cr ; SIP Book reached INR 618 Cr, up 26%
YoY
 Asset Reconstruction business recovered INR 1,387 Cr in the quarter, up 13% YoY while INR 605 Cr of assets
acquired in the same period, up 70% YoY
 MSME loans of INR 560 Cr disbursed in the quarter, up 3x YoY
 Gross Written Premium for General Insurance increased to INR 366 Cr, up 40% YoY ; the business turned
profitable this quarter with profit after tax recorded at INR 5 Cr
 Life Insurance recorded a Gross Premium of INR 558 Cr in the quarter, up 11% YoY; AUM increased by 13% YoY
to INR 11,067 Cr
Key Focus areas for FY27
 Listing of Edelweiss Alternatives – successfully completed its INR 1,200 Cr Initial Public Offering
 Carlyle came in as a strategic majority investor in Nido Home Finance – with an investment of ~INR 2,000 Cr
 Scaling up of profitability in Asset Management businesses – PAT for six months ended September grew by
35% YoY for Alternative Asset Management and 64% YoY for Mutual Fund
 Insurance businesses on track to be profitable – Zuno turns profitable this quarter; combined losses for six
months ended Sep reduced by 58% YoY
 Steady scale up in MSME business with 2x YoY growth in AUM and 3x YoY growth in disbursals for six months
ended Sep period
Customer Franchise continues its growth trajectory
 Our customer base remains on a steady growth trajectory, with customer reach up by 24% YoY to nearly 15
million while customer assets witnessed an increase of 24% YoY to INR 2.9 Tn – demonstrating the continued
trust reposed in us by our customers
Resilient Balance Sheet with well capitalised businesses
 Net Worth at INR 5,615 Cr
 Consol Net Debt at INR 8,435 Cr, down 26% YoY
 Corporate Net Debt
declined by 18% YoY to INR 5,415 Cr
 Independent operating businesses with capital adequacy of over 23% across credit entities
Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
Unaudited, Limited Reviewed Results Second Quarter Financial Year 2027
Speaking on the occasion, Rashesh Shah, Chairman, Edelweiss Financial Services Limited said:
“India’s growth has remained resilient despite a challenging global environment. While geopolitical tensions and
macroeconomic uncertainties continue to weigh on the gl obal outlook, sustained public investment and healthy
domestic demand continue to support the Indian economy. Rural demand remains resilient, while urban
consumption is showing signs of gradual recovery. With continued policy support and strong domestic demand
providing a firm foundation, India remains well placed to sustain its medium-term growth trajectory.
At Edelweiss, in this quarter we reported a consolidated PAT (post MI) of INR 193 Cr, up 50% YoY. The businesses
continued to demonstrate robust earnings growth with PAT in Alternative Asset Management at INR 88 Cr, up 27%
YoY and Mutual Fund PAT at INR 37 Cr, up 114% YoY. Further, our balance sheet remained resilient as corporate net
debt declined by 18% YoY.

Alternatives successfully completed its INR 1,200 Cr IPO and Carlyle is now a strategic majority investor in Nido Home
Finance with an investment of ~INR 2,000 Cr. Our Asset Management businesses continued to scale strongly, while
our Credit businesses witnessed a calibrated scale-up, with MSME disbursements growing threefold YoY in six
months ended September. Our Insurance businesses are on track to be profitable with combined losses down by
58% YoY in six months ended September; our General Insurance business, Zuno, turned profitable this quarter. These
achievements reflect our focus on strengthening our businesses, maintaining robust balance sheet and creating long-
term value for all stakeholders.”
Steady Performance across Businesses – Healthy metrics & Robust growth
Alternative Asset Management:
- Fee Paying AUM grew 28% YoY to INR 49,164 Cr and PAT for the quarter increased 27% YoY to INR 88 Cr
- Annualized ROE improved to 29%, up ~270 bps YoY
- Raised INR 8,000 Cr+ across Special Situations, Infra Yield and Private Equity strategies and INR 12,000 Cr+ in
InvITs during six months ended Sep
- Launched third flagship infrastructure fund, Infrastructure Yield Plus III (IYP III)
Mutual Fund:
- Equity AUM grew 40% YoY to INR 1,07,600 Cr; AUM grew 18% YoY to INR 1,83,200 Cr
- Net equity inflows of INR 10,800 Cr, highest ever in a quarter, up 2.5x YoY
- SIP book increased by 26% YoY to INR 618 Cr
- Launched Altiva Equity Long – Short SIF; SIF AUM at INR 13,200 Cr
Asset Reconstruction:
- Acquired INR 605 Cr assets in the quarter, up 70% YoY
- Recovered INR 1,387 Cr in the quarter, up 13% YoY
- Share of retail assets in capital employed increased to 29%
- Annualized RoE for the quarter at 18%

- MSME disbursals of INR 560 Cr in the quarter; tripled YoY
- Portfolio continues to strengthen with GNPA at 2.10%, improved by 125 bps YoY
- Wholesale SR wound down to zero from INR 18,000 Cr in Mar 19
General Insurance:
- Turned profitable this quarter, with PAT of INR 5 Cr
- Gross written premium (GWP) increased by 40% YoY in the quarter; Motor accounted for 60% of GWP

To the Board of Directors of The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation Limited
1. We have reviewed the accompanying statement of standalone unaudited financial results

by the Company's Board of Directors , has been prepared in accordance with the
recognition and measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34,
Interim Financial Reporting ('Ind AS 34'), prescribed under section 133 of the Companies
Act, 2013 ('the Act'), and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and is in
compliance with the presentation and disclosure requirements of Regulation 33 and
Regulation 52(4) of the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion
on the Statement based on our review.
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review
Engagements (SRE) 2410, Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the
Independent Auditor of the Entity, issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons

Q2FY27 EBITDA Rises 28% YoY to ₹12.7 Cr; Revenue Up 17% YoY to ₹51 Cr H1FY27 Revenue Up 34% YoY to ₹104 Cr;
NCLT Sanctions Commerce Demerger; In-principle Listing Approvals Received for listing of J.K.Shah Commerce Education Limited
Chennai, 13th November, 2026: Veranda Learning Solutions Limited, a public listed Education company (BSE: 543514, NSE: VERANDA) and a
pioneer in the industry offering end-to-end Education services and solutions, announced its financial results for the quarter and half year ended
September 30, 2026.
Overall Theme for Q2FY27 – profitable growth and a stronger balance sheet. Government Test Prep led the quarter with 31% YoY revenue
growth and 79% YoY EBITDA growth. PAT for Q2 FY 27 turned to ₹13.4 Cr from a loss of ₹12.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. For H1FY27, enrolments grew 12%
YoY to 41,559 and collections rose 17% YoY to ₹117 Cr. The Commerce Demerger, sanctioned by the NCLT on August 20, 2026, became effective
on August 31, 2026, and J.K.Shah Commerce Education Limited has received in-principle listing approvals from NSE, BSE and SEBI relaxation for
listing.
Financial Snapshot – Seventh consecutive PAT positive quarter

2. The discontinued Commerce business contributed a PAT of ₹31.36 Cr during the two months of Q2FY27 prior to the completion of the Demerger. Including the
PAT contribution of ₹21.69 Cr during Q1FY27, the discontinued operations reported a cumulative PAT of ₹53.05 Cr for 5 months ended Aug 2026 . This
represents the contribution of the Commerce business during the five months for which it remained part of Veranda’s operations in FY27. Against the full-year

3. Reported Q2FY26 PAT of ₹120.5 Cr included a one-time, non-cash exceptional gain of ₹133.4 Cr.
4. During the quarter, the consolidated financial statements also recognised an exceptional, one -time item of ₹1,047 Cr arising from the fair valuation of the

Key Consolidated Financial Highlights:
• Revenue from operations for Q2FY27 stood at ₹51 Cr, up 17% YoY, led by 31% YoY growth in Government Test Prep. H1FY27
revenue rose 34% YoY to ₹104 Cr.
• EBITDA grew 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹12. 7 Cr, with EBITDA margin expanding to 2 5% from 23% in Q2FY26, reflecting continued
operating leverage. H1FY27 EBITDA rose 39% YoY to ₹24.4 Cr.
• PAT stood at ₹13.4 Cr in Q2FY27, against a loss of ₹ 12.8 Cr in Q2FY26; this includes a tax credit of ₹13.4 Cr. For H1FY27, PAT was
₹25.6 Cr against a loss of ₹24.5 Cr in H1FY26.
• Current quarter, on account of scheme being effective, commerce segment has been shown as discontinued operations in the P&L
and accordingly comparatives have been restated
Segmental Performance
Key highlights during Q2FY27
1) Government Test Prep:
• Financials: revenue up 31% YoY to ₹43 Cr; EBITDA up 79% YoY to ₹10.7 Cr.
• Expansion: opened two new centres at Tenkasi and Dharmapuri and a new PV at Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu; Partnered with
Dr.Rajkumar Academy of Civil Services (DRACS) who is leading government test preparation player and onboarded its team.
• Enrolments: H1FY27 enrolments up 14% YoY to 36,083.
2) Commerce Demerger – J.K.Shah Commerce Education:
• NCLT order: the composite scheme was sanctioned by the NCLT on August 2 0, 2026 and became effective on August 31 ,
2026; the Commerce business is now presented as discontinued operations.
• Listing approvals: in-principle approvals received from NSE, BSE and relaxation from SEBI for the listing of J.K. Shah Commerce
Education Limited; shareholders as on the record date of October 6, 2026 receive one J.K.Shah share for every Veranda share
held (1:1).
3) Academics (K12):
• Experience centres set up in Perungudi, Trichy and Bengaluru; new ERP (School Canvas) initiated.
What Lies ahead?
1) Government Test Prep
• Network: 3 more offline centres planned in Tamil Nadu.
• Karnataka: Dr.Rajkumar Academy of Civil Services (DRACS) centres to open in Mysuru and Kalaburagi (Gulbarga).
2) J.K.Shah Commerce Education
with dedicated capital allocation.
3) Academic Segment – K12
• Launch of Veranda Sprouts preschool (Playgroup to UKG) at Perumbakkam, a feeder to Bollineni school; admissions open in
January 2027 and the first batch starts in June 2027.
• School Canvas ERP rollout to parents and students;
Veranda Learning Solutions – Management Statement on Q2FY27 Performance
Mr. Suresh S. Kalpathi, Chairman & Managing Director of Veranda Learning Solutions, said, “Q2FY27 was a quarter of profitable growth and a
much stronger balance sheet. Revenue grew 17% year on year to ₹51 Cr and EBITDA rose 28% to ₹12.7 Cr, led by our Government Test Preparation
business, which grew revenue by 31% and grew its EBITDA by 79%. Profit after tax before exceptional items was ₹13.4 Cr, compared with a loss
of ₹12.8 Cr a year ago. For the first half, revenue is up 34% and EBITDA up 39%.
We continue to widen our reach, with new centres in Tamil Nadu, the D r. Rajkumar Academy of Civil Service (DRACS) partnership taking us into
Karnataka, and new hiring partnerships through Phire. In K12, we are preparing to launch Veranda Sprouts, our preschool brand, with admissions
opening in January.
The Commerce demerger reached a key milestone with the NCLT sanctioning the scheme on August 2 0, 2026, effective from August 31, 2026. I
am pleased to share that we have received in- principle approvals from NSE, BSE and relaxation from SEBI for the listing of J .K.Shah Commerce
Education Limited, which we expect to list within a week. Post demerger, both businesses will have sharper strategic focus, greater operational
agility and dedicated capital allocation.
Across the organisation, we will continue to focus on digital-led admissions, expanding corporate and hiring partnerships, and driving operating
leverage. These initiatives, coupled with disciplined execution, position us well to deliver sustainable growth, improve profitability and create
long-term value for all stakeholders.”
About Veranda Learning Solutions:
Veranda Learning Solutions is a leading provider of educational services in India, offering K -12 education, test preparation, vocational training,
and professional certifications. The company combines online and offline models for scalable, efficient growth and is committed to empowering
individuals for global career opportunities.

2QFY27 Conference Call Transcript
Section 1 – Opening Remarks
Dinesh Kamath, Moderator:
Good morning, everyone. Welcome to V -Marc India Limited's Q2 FY27 conference call, hosted by Emkay
Global Financial Services Limited. I would like to welcome the management and thank them for this
opportunity. We have with us today, Mr. Vikas Garg, Managing Director; Mr. D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial
Officer; and Mr. Deepak Tikle, Executive Director. I shall now hand over the call to the management for the
opening remarks. Over to you, gentlemen.
Section 2 – Management Commentary
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. For those joining us for the first time, let me briefly
introduce our company. V -Marc is one of the... We make high -tension (HT) power cables, low -tension (LT)
cables, building wires, industrial cables, and solar cables. Our customers include government utilities, EPC
contractors, and a network of more than 1,200 dealers. We also started exports last year. We are one of the
few Indian manufacturers using e-beam irradiation technology. Our Flexituff wire is p ositioned as India's safest
wire.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
In August, we reported the best first quarter in V -Marc's history. I am happy to share that our second quarter
was even better. Q2 revenue was 719 crore. This was 72.6% higher than the same quarter last year and
29.6% higher than Q1. With these two strong quarters, H1 FY27 has become our best half -year so far.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Let me now share the first half -year numbers. Revenue from operations was 1,275.4 crore, up 84.4% from
691.5 crore. EBITDA was 147.3 crore, also up by 84.3% on a YoY basis. Our EBITDA margin was 11.6%,
within our guidance of 11% to 12%. Profit after tax was Rs. 76.4 crore, up 103.8%. Earnings per share was
Rs. 5.22 compared with Rs. 2.56. Both earnings per share figures have been adjusted for the 5:1 bonus issue.
In just six months, we have achieved 71 [Inaudible / Audio Dropout: 00:02:39 –00:02:41] recorded in the full
financial year FY26.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
The second quarter was even stronger. EBITDA was Rs. 87.9 crore, up 77.5 % from the same quarter last year
and 48% compared to Q1. The EBITDA margin was 12.2%. Profit after tax was 47.9 crore, up 79.7% from the
same quarter last year and 68% compared to Q1.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Our gross margin improved sequentially during Q2 FY27. It was under pressure in Q1 FY27 at 19.6%, but
recovered to 22.5% in Q2 FY27. Again, Q2 FY27 gross margin was slightly above the 22.2% recorded in Q2
last year. For the half year, our gross margin was lower at 21.24% versus 22.56% in H1 [last year], but
employee and other expenses costs came down as a share of revenue from 11% to 9.7%. The operating
leverage helped offset the lower gross margin; as a result, EBITDA margin for H1 almost equaled H1 last year
at 11.55%. Finance costs also fell as a share of revenue from 2.7% to 2.4%. This helped improve our profit
after tax margin by 57 basis points to 6%.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Coming to our product segments for H1: HT cables were our largest segment with 585 crore sales and 46% of
total revenue. This segment grew 62% YoY. Building wires and industrial cables, with total sales of 485 crore,
were next with 38% of total revenue. It grew 181% on a YoY basis. LT cables, with 204 crore sales, were 16%
of total revenue. It grew 29% YoY. In Q2 alone, HT cables grew 58% from the same quarter last year. Building
wires and industrial cables grew 130% over the same period.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Coming to our customers: our government sales (B2G segment) revenue grew by 86.9% to 453 crores during
H1. B2B revenue grew 75% to 432 crores. Together, these two businesses made up about 70% of H1
revenue. Exports were 181 crores, or 14.2% of H1 revenue. This is already 2.9 times the 62-crore exported in
full financial year FY26, which was our first year of exports. Q2 exports alone were 118 crores, up 89% from
Q1. Dealer sales, also called B2C revenue, were Rs. 207 crores, up 3% compared to H1 previous year.
D.K. Bansal, Chief Financial Officer:
Let me now talk about our balance sheet and cash flow. We are closely managing both as the business grows.
Our net worth was 365 crores on 30th September, compared with 288 crore in March. Such fast growth needs
more working capital. Inventory increased by 222 crore during the half year to 488 crore. Inventory days rose

capital—meaning trade receivables plus inventory less trade payables —increased from 251 crore on 31st
March to 406 crore on 30th September . The working capital cycle increased by 7 days, from 51 days to 58
days. As a result of working capital deployment, operating cash flow for the half year was an outflow of 45.7
crore. In comparison, the full year FY26 had an inflow of Rs. 114 crore—Rs. 108 crore standalone.

We used borrowings to fund these needs. Borrowings excluding lease liabilities increased from 213 crore to

One more point: during the half year, the company issued bonus shares in the ratio of 5:1. The total number of

Gillette India Ltd. Announces Second quarter results
Driving consistent balanced growth - Sales up 4%, PAT up 11% for quarter ended September 30, 2026
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: Gillette India Limited (GIL) today announced its financial results for the
quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company delivered strong growth during the quarter, with sales
of ₹846 crore, up 4% versus year ago. Profit After Tax (PAT) was reported at ₹159 crores, up 11% versus year
ago. This balanced and broad -based growth was driven by the strength of its strategic portfolio,
meaningful innovation that addresses evolving consumer needs, and superior retail execution across
channels.
Kumar Venkatasubramanian, Managing Director, Gillette India Ltd. said, “Our consistent delivery of
balanced growth quarter on quarter is a true reflection of the strength of our integrated growth
strategy, and the exceptional execution of these strategies by our people. This consistency is also
reflected in our innovation – both in terms of our propositions as well as how we engage with consumers.
We remain committed to our strategy to delight consumers with superior products at a superior value
by putting the consumer first in everything we do.”
He added, “Our integrated growth strategy is a nchored in a focused portfolio, superiority (of product
performance, packaging, brand communication, retail execution and value), productivity, constructive
disruption and an empowered, agile organization.”
For the quarter, profitability was impacted by significant commodity headwinds. However, the Company
has been able to leverage its robust productivity program to mitigate the headwinds and deliver
profitable growth.
The company’s power Oral Care business delivered strong results, growing double digit, driven by
superior execution of strategies and the launch of Oral B iO2 - built for the easiest switch from manual to
power oral care, enabling consumers to pick one of Oral-B’s most impactful oral health tools that provides
perfect clean even on the last tooth.
The first half of FY 2026 –27 has been defined by bold innovation across the vectors of superiority. This
momentum was anchored by key product introductions – including the launch of Gillette Guard 3in1 and
Gillette AIO Trimmer series – and an evolving media model designed to reach consumers where they are.
Recently, the company also participated in P&G Loop, a first- of-its-kind, mega immersive brand
experience event organized for content creators.

Gillette India Limited (GIL) is one of India’s well- known FMCG Companies that has some of the world’s
leading brands Gillette and Oral B; and has carved a reputation for delivering superior products to meet
the needs of consumers. GIL brands take pride in being socially conscious via their participation in P&G
Shiksha, P&G India’s flagship CSR program that supports the education of underprivileged children in
India. Please visit in.pg.com for the latest news.

Blackbox Delivers Second Consecutive Quarter of Record-Breaking Financial Performance
Order Backlog of US$1.04 billion, up 88% YOY | Revenue of ₹1,936 crore in Q2 FY27, up 22% YOY
EBITDA of ₹175 crore in Q2 FY27, up 23% YOY | PAT of ₹73 crore in Q2 FY27, up 31% YOY
Mumbai, November 13, 202 6: Black Box Limited (BSE: 500463 | NSE: BBOX), a global digital
infrastructure solutions provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half
year ended September 30, 2026.
Black Box reported record quarterly revenue of ₹1,936 crore, up 22% year -on-year and 13%
sequentially. EBITDA increased 23% YOY to ₹175 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 31% to
₹73 crore.
Growth was driven by continued execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise
solutions, supported by growing momentum in the Company's Technology Products business.
The Company's order backlog reached a record US$1,044 million, up 88% YoY, strengthening visibility
for continued growth.

Sanjeev Verma, Whole -time Director & Chief Executive Officer, Black Box Limite d said, “Black
Box is building strong growth momentum, with record quarterly revenue and an order backlog exceeding
US$1 billion. These results reinforce our confidence in scaling the business towards our immediate
growth goal of US$2 billion in revenue.
Our data centre business is a powerful growth engine, with significant orders from multiple hyperscalers
and repeat wins expanding our role in their infrastructure investments. Our strong U.S. presence, deep
expertise and proven execution position us to ca pture a greater share of accelerating data centre
investment, supported by a substantial opportunity pipeline. Growing Enterprise and Technology
Products businesses across the United States and international markets further strengthen our growth
outlook.
With secured orders and proven delivery capabilities, we are ready to execute at greater scale.
Continued hiring, investment in our people and expansion of delivery capacity strengthen our ability to
deliver larger projects and drive our next phase of growth.”
Deepak Kumar Bansal, Executive Director & Global CFO, Black Box Limited
“Our Q2 performance demonstrates the growing earnings strength of Black Box, with PAT rising 31%
to ₹73 crore, ahead of revenue growth of 22%. H1 EBITDA margin expanded 50 basis points to 9.2%,
while operating cash flow reached ₹115 crore for the first half of FY27. We are translating growth into
stronger profitability and cash generation.
Our expanding data centre business and significant order pipeline provide a strong foundation to scale
revenue and earnings. As secured orders convert into revenue, we see further opportunities to improve
operating leverage and build on this earnings momentum.
We are confident of achieving our FY27 guidance of 23–27% revenue growth and 38–50% PAT growth,
with profit growth expected to remain in high double digits for the next few years along with stronger
cash flow generation. Disciplined working capital managem ent and prudent capital allocation remain
central to converting this opportunity into sustained shareholder value.”
Hyperscale Infrastructure: Capturing AI-Driven Investment Opportunities
Accelerating investment in AI infrastructure is driving demand for hyperscale data centre capacity,
connectivity and network infrastructure. Black Box is expanding its participation in this market through
established hyperscaler relationships, technical expertise and large-scale project delivery capabilities.
Black Box secured over US$250 million in data centre orders in H1 FY27. A substantial pipeline of large
hyperscale deals is expected to drive significant order wins and accelerate growth in the coming
quarters.
Black Box supports infrastructure projects associated with large -scale data centre developments with
gigawatt-scale capacity. Its experience in delivering complex projects provides opportunities to expand
existing customer relationships and participate in larger infrastructure projects.
The Company continues to strengthen its engineering and delivery capabilities, particularly in the United
States, to support this demand.
Record Backlog Strengthens Revenue Visibility
Black Box secured US$298 million in new orders during Q2 FY27, up 37% YOY. The order backlog
backlog includes a growing proportion of larger, multi-year engagements, with project-led wins providing
revenue visibility over 24 to 36 months.
Supported by its order pipeline across hyperscale, enterprise and presence across multiple countries,
Black Box management is confident to achieve its FY27 guidance of:
• Exit order backlog: US$1.3–1.4 billion
• Order bookings: US$1.3–1.5 billion
• Revenue growth: 23–27%
• EBITDA growth: 27-32%
• PAT growth: 38–50%
Enterprise and Technology Products: Expanding Growth Opportunities
Black Box continues to deepen its enterprise relationships across the United States and international
markets, supporting customers across technology, healthcare, financial services, industrial and retail
markets.
During Q2 FY27, the Company secured engagements involving network infrastructure, connectivity,
data centre integration and digital workplace solutions. Key wins included projects with a leading Indian
pharmaceutical company, a major US financial institution, and retail and public sector customers. These
engagements reinforce the Company's diversified customer base and its strategy of expanding
relationships with 300 strategic enterprise accounts.
The Technology Products business is gaining momentum as customers modernise critical operations
and invest in secure, resilient control room platforms. This creates further opportunities for Black Box’s
specialised technology portfolio.
Together, Enterprise Solutions and Technology Products businesses provide complementary growth
opportunities alongside the expanding hyperscale data center business.
Investing in Capabilities for Sustainable Growth
Black Box continues to strengthen its leadership, engineering, sales and delivery capabilities to support
larger and more complex customer projects. The Company is progressing with its plan to recruit nearly
3,000 professionals by FY30, primarily in the United States, with hiring already underway for major data
centre projects. These investments support the Company's ambition of reaching US$2 billion in annual
revenue by FY30, driven by expanding customer relationships, broader capabilities and disciplined
execution.
About Black Box Limited
Black Box (BSE: 500463 | NSE: BBOX) is a global leader in digital infrastructure solutions, delivering
network and systems integration, managed services and technology products to 120 Fortune 500
companies and other leading global enterprises. With a prese nce across the United States, Europe,
India, Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America, Black Box serves customers across financial
services, technology, healthcare, retail, public services and manufacturing.

Its Technology Products portfolio supports business operations with solutions across AV, IoT, KVM,

New Delhi, 12 November 2026
Apex Ecotech Limited ("Apex" or "the Company"), an engineering -driven EPC company specializing in
turnkey water, wastewater and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) solutions, today announced its un -audited
financial results for the half-year ended 30 September 2026 (H1 FY27).
H1 FY27 Key Financial Highlights
Particulars (In ₹ Crore) H1 FY27 H1 FY26 YoY Change
Revenue From Operations 94.27 32.57 +189%
EBITDA 5.25 3.00 +75%
PAT 4.00 2.58 +55%
Performance & Margin Movement
• The Company recorded a substantial increase in revenue as project execution scaled up during the
period. Absolute EBITDA and PAT also increased year -on-year, although EBITDA margin
moderated to 5.57% from 9.21% and PAT margin to 4.25% from 7.91%.
• Direct material costs represented 83.78% of revenue, compared with 75.95% in H1 FY26. The
reported margin profile was influenced by input cost movements on orders secured in earlier
periods, alongside the timing and mix of project execution, recognition of associated costs, and
customer verification and certification cycles.
• The Company continues to prioritise disciplined project execution, cost control and operational
efficiency. Working -capital management, particularly project billing and receivable realisation,
remains an important focus as the business scales.
Management Commentary
H1 FY27 reflects a significant scale -up in Apex Ecotech’s operations, with revenue growing
55%, respectively.
The moderation in reported margins during the period was primarily driven by two factors — input cost
inflation on orders secured in earlier periods and the timing of revenue certification, rather than any
change in the underlying economics of our projects.
Apex Ecotech Limited reports 189% year-on-year revenue growth in H1 FY27;
Revenue from operations rises to ₹94.27 crore;
EBITDA and PAT grow 75% and 55%, respectively.
First, elevated global inflation, geopolitical disruptions and firmer crude oil prices led to higher costs of
steel, polymers, membranes and other mechanical and electrical inputs. Since a significant portion of H1
execution related to earlier orders witho ut price variation provisions, passing on these increases
remained challenging. However, commodity cycles are temporary, and we expect this impact to
normalize over time.
Second, substantial installation and commissioning work was completed during H1, with the associated
costs already recognized. However, the corresponding revenue remains subject to client verification and
certification. As per the Company’s revenue-recognition policy, this revenue is expected to be recognized
progressively in H2 FY27, resulting in a temporary timing mismatch that has impacted reported margins.
We remain focused on disciplined execution, cost optimization, faster project cycles and timely customer
certifications, which will support margin improvement and stronger cash flows.
Looking ahead, we continue to see encouraging opportunities across our core markets, with several
significant projects at advanced stages of discussion. While order finalization and execution timelines
remain key, we remain confident in our competitive positioning and long-term growth prospects, with a
continued focus on sustainable revenue growth, improved profitability and stronger cash generation.
~ Mr. Anuj Dosajh, Chairman & Managing Director of Apex Ecotech Limited
Outlook Going Forward
• Revenue Growth: Management targets 30–40% year-on-year revenue growth in FY27, subject to
order finalizations, execution milestones and customer certifications.
• Margin Normalization: Margins are expected to improve through H2 FY27 as H1 -executed
projects receive certification and corresponding revenue is recognized, along with invoicing of new
orders.
• Execution & Cost Efficiency: Focus remains on disciplined execution, cost optimization, shorter
project cycles, timely certifications and collections to strengthen margins and cash flows.
• Order Pipeline: Several significant projects are at advanced stages of discussion across core
markets, with conversion dependent on order finalizations.
• Diversification – O&M Services: The Company is developing a recurring revenue stream through
operations and maintenance services for commissioned projects. The business plan is being
finalized, with commercialization expected in H2 FY28.
About Apex Ecotech Limited
Apex Ecotech Limited is an ISO 9001:2015 certified, engineering -driven company led by a team of
seasoned professionals specializing in turnkey solutions for Water and Wastewater Treatment,
Membrane Recycling, Evaporators, and Zero Liquid Discharge Systems. The company ’s integrated
approach enables industries and infrastructure projects to effectively recycle and reuse water across
various process applications.
Focused on sustainability, Apex Ecotech delivers low -carbon, energy -efficient, and environmentally
responsible treatment solutions that address the challenges of global water scarcity. Its innovative
technologies promote recycling, reuse, and conservation driving progress toward a water-secure future.
Through strong collaboration with industries and communities, Apex Ecotech designs and implements
customized systems that enhance water management practices. The company remains committed to
creating long-term environmental and social value through responsible water stewardship.

Subject: Outcome of Board Meeting
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors (“the Board”) of the Company at its
meeting held today, i.e. on Friday, November 13, 2026, inter-alia, unanimously
approved the following business:
1)Approval of Unaudited Financial Resu lts for the quarter and half-year ended
September 30, 2026
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and 33 (read with Part A of Schedule Ill) and other applicable
provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations,
2015, the Board of Directors considered, approved and took on record the Unaudited
Standalone and Consolidated Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and

Statutory Auditors of the Company. A copy of the same is enclosed herewith as

27.

Hrs.

September 2026
➢ Announced the acquisition of the 150-bed ‘Mehar Hospital’ in Zirakpur at a valuation of INR 1,070 mn. The facility
will take our capacity in Tricity to ~1,000 beds post commissioning of the capacity expansion currently underway in
Mohali. It is expected to get commissioned in the 1st week of December 2026.
➢ Announced a long-term Operations and Management (O&M) arrangement to operate and manage a 300-bed multi-
super-speciality hospital in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The facility is expected to get commissioned in Q4 FY’27.
➢ Together with the upcoming commissioning of our Febris multi-super-speciality hospital in Narela, Delhi with a
capacity of 200 beds and the 100-bed expansion of our existing Palam Vihar facility, the Company expects to
commission 1,430 beds in FY’27, marking a capacity addition of c.40% in FY’27 over the closing capacity of 3,610
beds in FY’26. This is the single largest capacity addition by the company in any fiscal.
Q2 FY’27 HIGHLIGHTS

➢ EBITDA recorded of INR 1,017 mn, with EBITDA margin of 19.9%
➢ Net Profit recorded of INR 545 mn, with Net Profit margin of 10.7%
Commenting on the overall performance of the Company, Dr. Ajit Gupta, Chairman and Dr. Ankit Gupta,
Managing Director, Park Medi World, said, “H1 FY’27 has been a period of record growth and significant
investment for Park Medi World. We treated more than half a million patients and delivered our highest-ever half-
yearly Revenue of INR 9,867 mn, up 22% YoY, with Q2 Revenue rising 25% to a record INR 5,110 mn. At the same
time, we added 680 beds in just six months through Rudrapur and Panchkula, taking our capacity to 4,290 beds.
As expected, onboarding this new capacity has had a near -term bearing on occupancy and profitability, as new
facilities take time to ramp up. With the commissioning of Febris (Delhi), the Palam Vihar expansion (Gurugram),
Mehar Hospital (Zirakpur) and the Kanpur facility, we expect to tal additions of 1,430 beds in FY’27 — c.40% over
our FY’26 closing capacity and the largest addition in our history. Our priorities now are the seamless integration of
these assets, improving utilisation and margins. With cash of INR 3,713 mn against term debt of INR 1,779 mn, we
have the balance sheet strength to fund this growth while remaining committed to affordable, high -quality
healthcare and long-term value for all our stakeholders."
About Park Medi World Limited:
Park Group is North India's 2nd largest hospital chain, currently operating 17 hospitals with a combined capacity
of 4,290 beds as on date. The Group is in the process of integrating 6 additional hospitals and expanding capacity
at 3 existing units. These are in various stages of execution and will add 2,300 beds to our network. With these,
Park Group's total capacity is expected to reach 6,590 beds, underscoring its commitment to leadership and
growth in healthcare delivery.
The Group has established a strong presence across 15 key cities including Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Panipat,
Karnal, Sonipat, Ambala, Mohali, Patiala, Bathinda, Behror, Jaipur, Agra, Panchkula and Rudrapur, and is
expanding into Zirakpur (Punjab), Gorakhpur, Prayagraj, Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) and Rohtak (Haryana). Built on a
commitment to accessible, high-quality healthcare, Park Group offers a comprehensive range of clinical services—
spanning super-specialities such as cardiology, neurology, oncology, orthopaedics, gastroenterology, critical care,
nephrology, organ transplants, and women & child health. Each facility is equipped with modern medical
infrastructure, advanced diagnostics, 24×7 emergency support, and multi-disciplinary teams delivering evidence-
based care. Through continuous expansion and strategic investments, Park Group is strengthening its mission to
build a dependable, technology-enabled healthcare ecosystem that serves both metropolitan and regional
communities across North India.

Rationale and key rating drivers
Reaffirmation of ratings assigned to bank facilities of Trident Limited (Trident) continues to derive strength from its experienced
management, diversified, and integrated operations across the textile value chain, apart from its presence in paper and chemicals
segments, and established customer relationships with reputed global brands in its home textile segment. Ratings also factor in
Trident’s stable operating and financial performance, comfortable capital structure and debt coverage indicators, strong liquidity,
and continued support from fiscal incentives available to the textile sector.
Ratings also take cognisance of Trident’s planned capacity expansion and modernisation debt-funded capex programme of ₹4,650
crore, proposed to be implemented in phases up to FY30 (FY refer to April 01 to March 31). The capex is expected to strengthen
the company’s scale, product portfolio , and operating efficiency. However, the proposed debt funding is expected to moderate
the company’s capital structure and leverage indicators, with net debt/ profit before interest, lease rentals, depreciation, and
taxation (PBILDT) expected to remain above 2.00x during the implementation period. Trident’s ability to complete the projects
within envisaged cost and timelines, ramp up operations , and achieve the envisaged returns will remain monitorable. However,
proposed phased debt drawdown and fiscal incentives available in form of capital and interest subsidy under the Madhya Pradesh
State Textile Policy provide comfort.
However, long-term ratings remain constrained by Trident’s moderate return indicators and low fixed asset turnover ratio amid
under-utilisation of its existing capacities, working capital intensive operations, operating profitability susceptible to raw material
price volatility, and foreign exchange rate fluctuations. Ratings also factor in execution and stabilisation risks associated with the
sizeable debt-funded capex, trade related uncertainties and risks associated with changes in government policies, and Trident’s
presence in inherently cyclical, competitive, and fragmented textile industry.
Rating sensitivities: Factors likely to lead to rating actions
Positive factors
• Significant growth in scale of operations aided by improved performance across each business segment, resulting in
significant improvement in its PBILDT margin and return on capital employed (ROCE) on a sustained basis.
• Improvement in its net debt/ PBILDT to below unity and total outside liabilities to total new worth (TOL/TNW) to ~0.50x
on a sustained basis.
• Diversification of its customer base by tapping newer geographies with customised product offerings and entailing higher
margins.
Negative factors
• Deterioration in capital structure with net debt/PBILDT of over 2.00x on a sustained basis.
• Elongation in operating cycle or significantly higher-than-anticipated capex , resulting into significant moderation in
liquidity on a sustained basis.
Analytical approach: Consolidated.
CARE Ratings Limited (CareEdge Ratings) has considered consolidated financials of Trident and its subsidiaries, as its subsidiaries
are primarily set-up for undertaking marketing and distribution of Trident’s products in different geographies. Subsidiaries whose
financials have been consolidated in Trident are listed under Annexure 5.
