Outlook: Stable
Stable outlook reflects CareEdge Ratings’ expectation that Trident will continue to maintain its market position, given its
established presence in domestic and export markets and generate healthy cash accruals. While the sizeable debt -funded capex
is expected to moderate the company’s financial risk profile during the implementation period, it is expected to improve gradually

Detailed description of key rating drivers
Key strengths
Experienced management and established relationships with reputed global brands
Trident is promoted by Mr. Rajinder Gupta, who has over three decades of business experience. He currently serves as Chairman
Emeritus and provides mentorship and strategic guidance to the board. The company is supported by a qualified and experienced
management team, with each business vertical headed by an experienced professional.
brands. In the home textile segment, its customers include Target Global Sourcing Limited, Wal -Mart Stores Inc., Amazon Inc,
and Costco, among others. Trident has derived ~60 -65% of its home textile revenue from top five customers in the last few
years. Trident also has a diversified customer base in its yarn and paper divisions. Top five customers accounted for ~25-30% of
yarn revenue and ~15-20% of paper revenue in the last few years.
Diversified and integrated operations
Trident has diversified and integrated operations across the textile value chain, with a presence in yarn and home textiles,
comprising bath and bed linen, apart from paper and chemicals segments. Trident is among the leading home textile players in
India and has an established position in the terry towel segment.
Segment-wise revenue contribution:

Trident’s integrated operations provide better control over raw-material availability, product quality, and operating costs. Around
50% of the yarn produced is captively consumed and the company also undertakes weaving and processing of fabrics in-house.
Its operations are further supported by solar power capacity of 57.38 MW and co -generation captive power capacity of 67.60
MW. Around 40% of Trident’s power requirements are met throug h captive sources. The captive power share is expected to
improve following commissioning of the proposed renewable power capacity addition. Paper and chemicals segments provide
further business diversification. Trident manufactures agro -residue-based paper products, including branded copier paper, and
sulphuric acid for industrial applications. Integration across the textile value chain, captiv e power generation , and large-scale

net liquidity of INR223 crores, a balance sheet that supports both shareholder returns and
growth.

y-o-y to INR264 crores in Q2, and 18% to INR512 crores in H1 of FY27.

Windlas can grow alongside them. Sustaining that confidence quarter after quarter remains our

INR25 crores, 9.5%, while H1 FY27 EBITDA stood at INR70 crores, 13.7%, and PAT INR50
crores, 9.7%.

and INR56 crores and INR36 crores for half year. We delivered this while continuing to invest

strategy.

Rationale
(1) YES BANK Limited (YES BANK or the Bank) is a universal bank that ranks sixth among India’s private-
sector banks in terms of total assets. It is an equity-method affiliate of Sumitomo Mitsui Banking
Corporation (SMBC), the core commercial bank of the SMBC Group. JCR considers the Bank’s
creditworthiness to be three notches below the SMBC Group’s creditworthiness equivalent to “AA,”
given the Bank’s management importance to the SMBC Group and the Group’s involvement in its
management, including the nomination of directors. However, the Bank’s rating is constrained by the
sovereign rating on India (Foreign Currency Long-term Issuer Rating: A-/Stable), as its operations,
centered on banking, are susceptible to the country’s domestic regulatory environment and economic
and financial conditions.
(2) The Bank was established in 2003 and is headquartered in Mumbai. In addition to commercial banking,
it engages in securities businesses through its subsidiary. Although it has a relatively short operating
history, the Bank had rapidly expanded its business, primarily through wholesale lending. However,
problems with governance and risk management under the management structure prior to 2020 led
to an increase in higher-risk lending to large corporations, and a large amount of such loans were
recognized as nonperforming loans in the fiscal year ended in March 2020. The Bank consequently
faced a crisis and was placed under a moratorium imposed by the authorities in March 2020.
Nevertheless, under a reconstruction scheme formulated by the Reserve Bank of India, State Bank
of India, the country’s largest state-owned bank, and several private-sector banks injected capital into
the Bank, thereby averting its failure. Since then, its earnings and asset quality have recovered
following measures including governance improvements involving changes in management and the
sale of nonperforming loans to an asset reconstruction company and subsequent capital raise.
(3) In 2025, SMBC acquired a 24.9% stake in the Bank and became its largest shareholder. SMBC is
involved in the Bank’s management through the nomination of two directors. The Bank is expected
to serve as an important platform in India, a priority market under the SMBC Group’s Asia multi-
franchise strategy. JCR therefore considers the Bank’s management importance to the SMBC Group
to be reasonably high.
(4) The Bank’s performance has been on a recovery trend since bottoming out in FY2020. In the course
of its reconstruction following the crisis, the Bank reviewed its previous growth-oriented business
operations and shifted to a more prudent risk management policy, including application of stricter
credit standards. At the same time, it has been building a more diversified loan portfolio by reducing
the proportion of loans to large corporations and increasing the proportions of retail and small and
medium-sized enterprise (SME) loans. Against this background, the Bank has steadily increased its
loan balance while keeping credit costs under control. Net profit attributable to shareholders of the
bank reached INR35.1 billion in FY2026, the highest level since the crisis. Earnings continued to
increase in the first and second quarters of FY2027, indicating that the Bank’s recent performance
remains solid. On the other hand, current profitability remains below that of peers, with further scope
for improvement. Return on assets (ROA) based on pre-provision operating profit was at 1.2% in
FY2026. Nevertheless, ROA has been gradually improving, supported by factors including lower
funding costs resulting from the strengthening and expansion of the Bank’s deposit base, as
evidenced by the rise in the ratio of current account and savings account (CASA) deposits. In October
2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the permanent write-down of additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds
implemented in 2020 as part of the Bank’s reconstruction was invalid. While the ruling could put
downward pressure on the Bank’s net profit, JCR considers that it will not significantly impair its
earnings capacity over the medium term.
(5) The Bank’s nonperforming loan (NPL) ratio stood at 1.3% at the end of FY2026 and 1.2% at the end
of the second quarter of FY2027. The ratio has dramatically improved from 16.8% at the end of March

Indian Terrain delivered a steady performance in Q2 FY’27, with Revenue from Operations increasing by 5.6%
year-on-year to ₹106.59 Crore, 30.4% higher than in Q1 FY’27. For the first half of FY’27, revenue grew by 11.0%
to ₹188.33 Crore, and rolling twelve -month revenue reached ₹396 Crore against ₹356 Crore a year ago. Gross
Margin improved to 40.8% in Q2 FY’27 from 40.3% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, while H1
Gross Margin expanded by 112 basis points to 40.9%. Gross Margin value increased by 7.0% in Q2 and 14.1% in
H1, supported by disciplined merchandise planning, a better product mix and cost efficiencies.
Operating EBITDA increased to ₹9.58 Crore in Q2 FY’27, compared with ₹8.51 Crore in Q2 FY’26, with the margin
improving to 9.0% from 8.4%. For H1 FY’27, Operating EBITDA grew 64.5% to ₹15.66 Crore, with the margin
expanding to 8.3% from 5.6%. Profit Before Tax stood at ₹2.93 Crore for Q2 FY’27, compared with ₹1.15 Crore in
the corresponding quarter last year. For H1 FY’27, the Company reported a positive PBT of ₹3.07 Crore against a
loss of ₹4.89 Crore in H1 FY’26, reflecting the improvement in operating pe rformance and continued focus on
cost discipline. Profit After Tax for Q2 and H1 FY’27 stood at ₹5.09 Crore and ₹4.26 Crore, respectively, including
the impact of deferred tax.
Business Highlights – Q2 & H1 FY’27
 Exclusive Retail grew 12.1% in Q2 to ₹44.09 Crore and 9.9% in H1 to ₹84.99 Crore, contributing 41.4% of Q2
revenue. The network stood at 172 exclusive stores as on 30 September 2026, after 7 additions and 11
closures during the quarter, as the Company continued to optimise the network for store productivity.
 Large Format Outlets grew 2.8x in Q2 to ₹20.43 Crore and 93.4% in H1, lifting the channel’s share of Q2
revenue to 19.2% from 7.1%. New concept shop -in-shops were rolled out in large format stores during the
quarter.
 Multi-Brand Outlets grew 11.5% in Q2 to ₹37.99 Crore as dispatches deferred from Q1 were executed; H1
sales of ₹50.73 Crore are 1.4% ahead of the previous year.
 Online net primary sales were ₹(2.77) Crore in Q2, as returns exceeded fresh billing in the channel; H1 online
sales stood at ₹7.99 Crore against ₹15.99 Crore. The Company relaunched its web store, indianterrain.com,
on 14 September 2026 with enhanced features and readiness for omni-channel integration.
 Working capital improved, with gross working capital at 300 days in September 2026 against 326 days a year
ago and net working capital at 235 days against 258 days. Inventory stood at 67 days against 79 days and
receivables at 233 days against 247 days.
 Key initiatives during the quarter included the web store relaunch, the new look for LFO shop -in-shops, new
experience-led concept stores and the Festive Edit campaign, backed by improved product availability ahead
of the festive and wedding season.
 The Company recognised a provision of ₹1.66 Crore for interest on delayed payments to MSME suppliers in
accordance with the MSMED Act, 2006; the amount is included in Other Expenses.
Management Commentary:
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Charath Ram Narsimhan, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer,
said:
“The second quarter of FY’27 reflects continued progress in our efforts towards strengthening business
performance, improving operating efficiencies and driving sustainable profitability. Revenue from
operations grew by 5.6% year -on-year to ₹106.59 Crore, while gross margins improved to 40.8%. Our
continued focus on disciplined merchandising, product mix and cost optimisation enabled us to deliver
Operating EBITDA of ₹9.58 Crore, with a margin of 9.0%, and Profit Before Tax of ₹2.93 Crore, registering
a meaningful improvement over the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
For the half year, the Company achieved revenue from operations of ₹188.33 Crore, registering 11.0%
growth over the corresponding period last year. More importantly, Operating EBITDA improved to ₹15.66
Crore from ₹9.52 Crore, while Profit Before Tax turned positive at ₹3.07 Crore against a loss of ₹4.89 Crore
in H1 FY’26. This improvement reflects the benefits of our continued emphasis on margin enhancement,
operational efficiencies and disciplined cost management.
During the quarter, we continued to strengthen our presence across our diversified distribution channels,
with encouraging growth across Exclusive Retail, Large Format Outlets and the Multi-Brand Outlet business.
Our focus remains on improving channel productivity, strengthening distribution reach, enhancing product
assortment and delivering a consistent customer experience across physical and digital touchpoints. We
also continued to rationalise and optimise our retail network, ensuring greater focus on st ore productivity
and sustainable business economics.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on capitalising on the opportunities presented by the festive and
wedding season through improved product availability, sharper merchandise planning and enhanced
customer engagement. Our priorities will continue to be profi table growth, inventory optimisation,
receivables management and cost discipline. With a strong brand presence, diversified distribution network
and a focused operating strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our financial performance and
creating sustainable long-term value for all stakeholders.”
Outlook:
The Company expects steady consumer demand to sustain, and early festive sales momentum indicates
improving consumer sentiment. For the second half of FY’27, the Company will focus on optimising its exclusive
store network for productivity, scaling new con cept stores and shop -in-shops, and leveraging the relaunched
web store for omni-channel integration. It will continue to improve channel productivity across Exclusive Retail,
Large Format Outlets and Multi-Brand Outlets, and to capitalise on festive and wedding season demand through
improved product availability, sharper merchandise planning and enhanced customer engagement, while
maintaining disciplined inventory management, receivables control and cost efficiencies. Consumers remain
selective, and a milder and shorter winter, together with uncertainties arising from the West Asia conflict, may
affect consumer demand and sales of winter wear products.

Kolkata, 12 November 2026: Pushpa Jewellers Limited (NSE: PUSHPA | ISIN: INE154801018), a leading
B2B gold jewellery manufacturing company known for its lightweight 22K and 18K traditional and
contemporary designs, has announced its unaudited standalone financial results for the half year ended
30 September 2026 (H1 FY27).
Key Financial Highlights
Total Income 82.85%
EBITDA 59.79%

Operational Highlights
e Expanded the wholesale distribution network with the commencement of operations at a new
B2B Trade Fulfilment Centre in Mumbai on 4 August 2026, to better serve regional retail and
corporate clients.
e Continued to strengthen its portfolio of lightweight 22K and 18K traditional and contemporary gold
jewellery designs during the half year.
e Built up inventory to 2119.57 Cr as of 30 September 2026 (291.06 Cras of 31 March 2026) to support
anticipated demand in the upcoming festive and wedding season.
e Board authorised a committee of directors to identify and acquire commercial showroom premises
for an aggregate consideration of up to 2100 Cr, supporting the Company’s next phase of expansion.
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Anupam Tibrewal, Chairman & Managing Director, said:
“We are delighted to deliver a landmark first half for Pushpa Jewellers. Total Income grew 83% year-on-
year to %314 crore; EBITDA rose 60% to %27 crore and Net Profit climbed 83% to %20 crore. This
performance reflects the growing preference of retail jewellers for our lightweight, BIS-hallmarked 22K
and 18K gold jewellery, which enables them to offer attractive designs at accessible price points ina
high gold-price environment. With a strengthened post-/PO balance sheet and deepening relationships
with wholesale and retail partners across India, we are well positioned to capture the significant
opportunity arising from the formalisation of the jewellery industry and the shift towards organised,
trusted B2B suppliers. We are confident of carrying this momentum forward and creating long-term
value for all our stakeholders.”
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Mridul Tibrewal, Promoter, Whole-Time Director & CEO, said:
“HI FY27 marks a strong step forward in scaling our B2B platform. The launch of our B2B Trade Fulfilment
Centre in Mumbai on 4 August 2026 expands our wholesale reach into one of India’s key jewellery
trading hubs and brings us closer to our regional retail and corporate clients. We have strategically
built-up inventory to meet the strong demand we foresee in the festive and wedding season ahead, while
our CAD-CAM-led design capabilities and Kolkata’s skilled artisan network continue to give us speed
and flexibility in launching new collections. Going forward, we will focus on widening our distribution
footprint, introducing fresh lightweight designs and driving operational efficiencies to deliver
sustained, profitable growth.”
About Pushpa Jewellers Limited
Pushpa Jewellers Limited (“Pushpa Jewellers” or “the Company”), founded in 2009 in Kolkata, India,
specialises in the design and manufacture of lightweight gold jewellery, combining traditional Indian
craftsmanship with contemporary aesthetics. Its product range spans traditional and modern designs,
including pieces with detailing in stones such as emerald, jade, pearl and meena. The Company supplies
its jewellery on a B2B basis to wholesalers and retailers across India and has also catered to international
markets.
The Company is supported by an experienced team with expertise in jewellery design, manufacturing and
quality assurance, focused on creating refined, high-quality designs at competitive price points. Building
on this expertise, Pushpa Jewellers focuses on product quality, design innovation and efficient
manufacturing processes to deliver reliable offerings to its wholesale and retail partners.
In FY26, the Company reported Standalone total income of 2419.55 Cr, EBITDA of 239.39 Cr and Net Profit of
25.89 Cr.

Samita Shah: VP CFTRM - Tata Steel Limited
Thanks, Shohom. Good afternoon, everyone. Wishing you all a very happy Diwali and thank you for joining us today on this
call to discuss our results for the second quarter of FY 2027. We have with us Mr. T. V. Narendran, CEO and Managing
Director, and Mr. Koushik Chatterjee, ED and CFO. The results hav e been sent to the stock exchanges, as well as a
presentation that gives you a little bit of the background. We will answer any questions you may have on this call. I would just
like to remind all our participants that the entire proceedings of this call will be governed by the Safe Harbour clause, which
is on page two of the presentation. I will now request Naren to make a few opening comments, and then we will move on to
Koushik. Thank you, and over to you, Naren.
T. V. Narendran: CEO & MD - Tata Steel Limited
Good afternoon, everyone. Happy Diwali to all of you, and sorry to drag you out on a weekend.
Tata Steel delivered an improved performance in a seasonally softer quarter, despite significant cost inflation across the
value chain due to the ongoing conflict in West Asia. Since the conflict has started, oil and freight rates have risen by about
40%, and spot coking coal prices have also moved from about $235 per ton to $280 per ton, though they have come down
a bit in the last few days. Key inputs u sed in value-added and downstream products, such as zinc, have also gone up. The
disruption has also resulted in higher logistics costs through elevated vessel charter rates, demurrage charges, and insurance
premia across key shipping routes, while currenc y movements in India have also added to the cost pressures. At the same
time, Chinese steel exports continue to be over 10 million tons a month, and that has an impact on global trade flows.
However, we were able to successfully navigate this higher -cost environment and generate close to 90 bps improvement in
EBITDA margin, from 15% in 1Q to 16% in 2Q, on a consolidated basis.
Let me now take you through each geography. In India, we focused on maximi sing volumes to offset the cost pressures.
India's deliveries grew 16%, outpacing production growth of 7% on QoQ basis. Higher deliveries reflect healthy demand and
our ability to translate market opportunities into performance despite the seasonal headwinds of monsoons. Our extensive
market reach, combined with a sustained focus on product mix and customer centricity, ha ve enabled us to maintain strong
market traction across chosen segments.
Our Automotive & Special Products vertical continued to deepen presence in advanced applications, with hi -end sales
growing 26% YoY. We secured approval for the CR IFHS340 grade for automotive skin panels, developed a chrome -free
galvannealed product for 2 - wheeler fuel tanks, and progressed on customer approvals for specialised suspension and
transmission applications. These developments reflect our ability to co-create solutions with our customers. Our flagship retail
brand, Tata Tiscon, grew 13% YoY, supported by a distribution network that reaches nearly 97% of India's districts. In the
last twelve months, Tata Tiscon sold ~2.7 million tons to around 500,000 customers. Embedded within Tata Steel, w e now
have Tata Tiscon retail franchise of about $1.8 billion, and the recently commenced 4.8 MTPA NINL expansion will support
further growth of our retail business. Our digital platforms help us improve market access from districts of India to pin -codes
across the country. We have also focused on strengthening our presence in solution -oriented and value-added businesses,
moving beyond steel supply to provide next-gen construction solutions that address customer pain points and create mutual
value. Our expanding portfolio includ ing Sm@rtFAB, ReadyBuild (which are Cut & Bend , and Bore pile cage s) and plate
fabricated sections, all of which are seeing strong market acceptance. Overall, ready-to-use construction solutions grew 32%
YoY in the second quarter, and we launched India's first CBRI -certified Mesh Masonry Reinforcement as an alternative to
conventional RCC beams. We also secured the first order for low-carbon steel at a green premium from our Ludhiana facility.
In addition, Tinplate and Tata Steel Colors grew 17% and 49% YoY, respectively. We are making good progress in sectors
such as Oil & Gas and Shipbuilding, including supplies for Sagar Manthan, the ocean research vesse l being built under the
Government of India's Deep Ocean Mission.
Moving to the UK, deliveries were ~0.38 million tons. While prices remained firm, volumes were impacted by elevated imports
under the transitional safeguard arrangements. Orders booked before 14 th March 2026 were exempt from quota utilisation
during July – September’26, this led to a surge in imports and inventory accumulation across the supply chain. which is taking
some time to be flushed out. In addition, UK steel exports to the EU are now subject to quota restrictions, creating a further
constraint on market access. We remain engaged with the authorities on a trade framework, including CBAM, that better
reflects product-level demand and market dynamics.
In Netherlands, Liquid steel production was ~1.52 million tons while deliveries were ~1.30 million tons. The Direct Sheet Plant
restarted in early August under the terms agreed with the regulator. The technical measures implemented are delivering the
intended outcomes, with Chromium -6 emissions reducing materially and currently remaining below prescribed limits. We
continue to closely monitor developments regarding the EU ETS, CBAM and other regulatory matters that could influence
the operating environment.
With this, I will hand over to Koushik for his comments. Thank you.
Koushik Chatterjee: ED & CFO - Tata Steel Limited
Thank you, Naren. Good afternoon to all who have joined in. Before we begin, I would like to wish you all a very happy Diwali.
The first half of this financial year was characterised by significant external volatility. The conflict in West Asia continued to
disrupt global trade flows, with vessels rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope, extending transit times by 10 – 14 days,
increasing fuel consumption by almost 40%, and keeping war-risk insurance costs materially above pre-conflict levels. Freight
rates remained elevated and European gas prices were more than twice the January 2026 levels. Meanwhile, Chinese steel
exports remained persistently high at 86 million tons yea r-to-date and are expected to again exceed 100 million tons this
calendar year.

Visakhapatnam, November 12, 2026: In a significant step towards strengthening India's fertilizer
self-sufficiency, GAIL (India) Limited (GAIL) and Krishak Bharati Cooperative Limited
(KRIBHCO) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Andhra Pradesh

present.

Angul Natural Gas Pipeline (SAPL).

Systematix Reports Strong Q2 FY27 Performance; Adjusted Revenue Up 102% QoQ
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Systematix Corporate Services Limited and its Subsidiaries” (“Systematix Group”) , a
diversified financial services group, announced its Q2 and H1 FY27 results, reporting a strong sequential recovery and
robust execution across its businesses.
Adjusted Revenue from Operations rose 102% QoQ to ₹56.04 crore. PBT stood at ₹17.18 crore against a loss of ₹3.08
crore in Q1 FY27, while PAT turned positive at ₹13.13 crore against a loss of ₹4.89 crore.
On a year-on-year basis, Q2 Adjusted Revenue from Operations remained stable at ₹56.04 crore versus ₹55.72 crore
in Q2 FY26 (+0.5%). PBT stood at ₹17.18 crore versus ₹19.37 crore, while PAT was ₹13.13 crore against ₹14.48 crore.
For H1 FY27, Adjusted Revenue from Operations stood at ₹84.06 crore versus ₹89.07 crore in H1 FY26 , while PAT
stood at ₹8.24 crore against ₹24.94 crore.
Key Highlights:
buybacks and M&A. Total capital raised during the quarter, including Block Deals, stood at ₹3,744 crore.
• Strong Pipeline: DRHPs exceeding ₹3,000 crore filed during the quarter; transaction pipeline stood at
₹12,600+ crore across 27+ active opportunities.
• Landmark Transactions: Executed ₹1,325 crore Viyash Scientific/Carlyle and ₹80 crore OIJIF/DCB Bank Block
deals.
• Asset Management: India SME Growth Fund, Category I AIF achieved its first investment exit, with two
portfolio companies listed, three DRHP filings, seven investments completed and 65% capital drawdown.
Category II AIF received investor interest/commitments exceeding ₹170 crore, while Category III AIF received
SEBI approval.
• Business Expansion: AUM grew to ₹1,151 crore and AUC to ₹12,200 crore . The Asset Management team
expanded to 38 members, with four new offices across Mumbai, Indore, Kolkata and Delhi.
• PMS & Institutional Equities: Expanded PMS offerings with Emerging Leaders and Million to Billion strategies.
Institutional stock coverage reached 330 companies, with 129 Corporate Access interactions during the
quarter.
Commenting on the results, Mr. Nikhil Khandelwal, Chairman & Managing Director, Systematix Corporate Services
Ltd., said:
"We are pleased with the strong sequential improvement in our performance and the momentum across our
businesses. Our Investment Banking franchise delivered robust transaction execution, while Asset Management
achieved significant milestones across its AIF and PMS platforms. We continue to invest in strengthening our Private
Wealth business through leadership, technology, talent and geographical expansion. These initiatives reflect our
commitment to building a diversified, scalable financial services franchise with multiple engines of sustainable growth."
About Systematix Group:
Founded in 1985, Systematix is a diversified financial services group with businesses spanning Investment Banking,
Institutional Equities, Merchant Banking, NBFC, Asset Management and Wealth Management. The Group provides
integrated financial solutions to corporates, institutions and investors through a diversified and research -driven
platform.

operational at South Extension and Gurgaon under planned 19-centre expansion
New Delhi, 12th November, 2026: Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited, a leading fertility and women’s
healthcare platform in India, announced its unaudited financial results today for the quarter and half year ended 30th
September 2026.

Key Financial Highlights
Q2 FY27
• Revenue grew 17.9% YoY to ₹37.4 Cr, supported by seasonally stronger patient volumes at mature hubs and
initial contribution from the new South Extension hub.
• EBITDA stood at ₹13.5 Cr, with margin at 36.0%. The quarter absorbed one-off rollout expenses for the two
new hubs at South Extension and Gurgaon, along with the higher fixed-cost base of new hubs in their initial
ramp-up phase.
• PAT stood at ₹9.4 Cr, up 0.4% YoY, with margin at 25.2%.
H1 FY27
• Revenue at ₹56.8 Cr, up 14.7% YoY
• EBITDA at ₹15.9 Cr; margin at 28.0%
• PAT at ₹11.2 Cr; margin at 19.7%
Key Operational Highlights
• South Extension hub, New Delhi: Commenced commercial operations on 16th July 2026, the first milestone
of the planned 19-centre expansion under the IPO objects. The centre houses the Gaudium Signature Lab
with AI-powered embryology tools SiD and ERICA.
• Gurgaon hub, Haryana: Commenced commercial operations on 24th September 2026 at Civil Lines,
Gurugram, the second new hub of FY27, built on the Gaudium Signature Lab framework.
Page | 3
Key Metrics
• As on 30th September 2026, the Company operates a network of 9 hubs and 28 spokes, with a clinical
pregnancy success rate of 62% on the first IVF attempt.
Commenting on the results, Dr. Manika Khanna, Chairperson and Managing Director, Gaudium IVF and Women
Health Limited said:
“In Q2 FY27, revenue from operations stood at ₹37.4 crore, up 17.9% year-on-year, taking H1 FY27 revenue to
₹56.8 crore. Q2 is seasonally one of our stronger quarters, and patient volumes at our mature hubs picked up as
expected. Reported EBITDA of ₹13.5 crore reflects one-off rollout expenses for the two hubs we launched this
quarter, while margins in our existing IVF business remain stable. New hubs also carry a relatively high fixed cost
in their initial phase, as clinical teams, laboratory infrastructure and premises are in place ahead of patient
volumes. This will weigh on consolidated margins until each hub matures, after which operating leverage should
start to kick in.
During the quarter, we commenced operations at two new IVF hubs under our IPO expansion programme: South
Extension, New Delhi, in July and Gurgaon, Haryana, in September. Both centres house our Gaudium Signature
Lab, bringing AI-led embryology through SiD and ERICA, internationally benchmarked laboratory standards and
our standardised clinical protocols to every patient. Our historical new hubs have broken even within about three
to six months of launch, and we expect both centres South ex and Gurgaon to follow a similar trajectory.
Historically, H1 has been the leaner half for us, with H2 contributing the larger share of annual revenue as Q4 is
typically our strongest quarter. With mature hubs continuing to grow, the new hubs scaling up and more centres
coming on stream in H2, we expect a stronger second half.”
About Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited
Founded in 2009, Gaudium IVF and Women Health Limited is a leading fertility and women’s healthcare provider in India,
offering advanced reproductive solutions and holistic care to women and couples. With centres across Delhi, Mumbai,
Bangalore, Patna, Ludhiana, and Srinagar, Gaudium IVF provides a comprehensive suite of services, including IVF, ICSI, IUI,
fertility preservation, infertility treatments, advanced genetic testing, high-risk pregnancy care, and minimally invasive
gynecological procedures supported by integrated pregnancy care and 24/7 patient services.
Led by its Chairperson and Managing Director, Dr. Manika Khanna who is an internationally trained infertility specialist,
Gaudium IVF combines global expertise with state-of-the-art technology and personalized treatment protocols to deliver
trusted clinical outcomes. Committed to ethical, accessible, and patient-centric care, Gaudium IVF also drives impact
through the Gaudium Foundation, promoting women’s health, empowerment, and equality.

New Delhi, November 10, 2026 : Brace Port Logistics Limited reported a strong financial
performance for the half year ended September 30, 2026, with consolidated revenue from
operations rising 34.9% year -on-year to ₹44.43 crore, compared with ₹32.94 crore in the
corresponding period last year. Profit after tax (PAT) increased 39.5% to ₹3.47 crore, against ₹2.49
crore in H1 FY26, while profit before tax (PBT) grew 38.7% to ₹4.67 crore.
Building on this performance, the management is targeting a doubling of revenue in FY28 and
remains bullish on the business outlook for H2 FY27. The company is focused on scaling its
integrated logistics operations, expanding its service capabilities and p ursuing strategic
opportunities to strengthen its position across the logistics value chain.
As part of this strategic expansion strategy, the Board has approved the acquisition of a 76% stake
in SageRoute Logistics Private Limited for a consideration of ₹0.76 lakh, following which it will
become a subsidiary of the Company. The Board has also approved a further investment of
₹75.24 lakh in SageRoute Logistics Private Limited, alongside a proportionate investment of
₹23.76 lakh by the other shareholder.
The company’s expansion plans also include a proposed investment of up to ₹7.50 crore in
warehousing infrastructure and related services, including third-party logistics (3PL) and fourth-
party logistics (4PL), subject to the necessary statutory and regulatory approvals.
Commenting on the performance and outlook, Mr. Sachin Arora, Chairman and Managing
Director, Brace Port Logistics Limited, said:

increasing by nearly 35% and profit after tax growing by close to 40% year -on-year. We remain
bullish on the outlook for H2 and are working towards our ambition of doubling revenue in FY28.
Our investment in SageRoute, alongside our plans to expand warehousing and 3PL and 4PL
capabilities, is aimed at building scale, broadening our service portfolio and creating new
avenues for growth. We remain focused on strengthening our integrated logistics offering and
delivering sustainable value to our customers and stakeholders.”

Key Financial Highlights — H1 FY27 vs H1 FY26
■ Revenue Growth: Total revenue increased by 5.83% for the half year to ₹152.18 crore in H1 FY27, compared
with ₹143.80 crore in H1 FY26.
■ EBITDA Growth: EBITDA grew by 10.02% for the half year to ₹39.57 crore, outperforming revenue growth.
■ Margin Expansion: EBITDA margin improved to 26.00% from 25.01% in the corresponding period last year,
an expansion of 99 basis points.
■ Profit Before Tax: PBT stood at ₹25.94 crore compared with ₹26.25 crore in H1 FY26, a marginal decline of
1.17%.
■ Profit After Tax: PAT stood at ₹19.60 crore compared with ₹21.32 crore in H1 FY26, a decline of 8.06%.
Performance Overview
■ Q-Line Biotech delivered growth in its operating performance during H1 FY27, with EBITDA growth outpacing
revenue growth. The improvement in EBITDA margin from 25.01% to 26.00% reflects stronger operating -
level profitability.
■ The growth in the trade business and reagent segment, alongside stable government -order revenue,
represents important elements of the Company's business performance during the period.
■ Profit before tax was broadly stable, while PAT was lower than in H1 FY26. This was mainly due to higher
depreciation (₹7.89 crore vs ₹4.09 crore) following the capitalisation of Unit 4 and higher finance costs (₹9.84
crore vs ₹8.31 crore), partly offset b y higher other income (₹4.09 crore vs ₹2.67 crore). H1 FY26 PAT also
included a write-back of earlier years' tax of ₹1.95 crore, which did not recur in H1 FY27. PBT margin declined
to 17.05% from 18.25%, while PAT margin stood at 12.88% compared with 14.82% in H1 FY26.

■ During H1 FY27, Q-Line Biotech continued to strengthen its trade business, which recorded growth of 20.13%
compared with H1 FY26. This performance reflects increasing traction in the Company's trade channel and
progress in expanding its market reach.
■ Revenue from government orders remained stable compared with the corresponding period last year,
providing continuity to the Company's institutional business.
■ At the product level, reagent revenue registered strong half year growth of 19.23%, highlighting the
continued strength of the Company's consumables business and recurring revenue potential.
■ Instrument revenue declined by 29.71% in the half year, primarily due to the non -availability of consignees
for government orders in hand, which affected the execution and delivery of instrument supplies during the
period.
■ The Company continues to focus on strengthening its trade distribution network within India and overseas,
expanding reagent sales and improving the execution of institutional and government orders.
Key Business Developments
■ Manufacturing Expansion: The Company has made significant progress in operationalising its new
manufacturing facility, Unit 4. While the regulatory approval process took longer than initially anticipated,
the Company had obtained 9 product licences as of September 30, 2026. Subseq uently, through continued
engagement with the regulatory authorities, the Company has successfully increased the number of product
licences to 36 as on date, with additional licences currently under various stages of approval. With a
substantial number of regulatory approvals now in place, the Company expects to progressively scale up

PRESS RELEASE
PICCADILY AGRO DISTILLERY REVENUE GROWS 30.5% YOY TO INR 271.3 CR IN
Q2 FY27 AS PREMIUM SPIRITS SUSTAIN GROWTH MOMENTUM
12th November 2026, New Delhi - Piccadily Agro Industries Limited (PAIL), one of India’s leading
producers of premium alcoholic beverages, today announced its financial results for the quarter
ended September 30, 2026.
The Company reported Revenue from Operations of INR 277.9 crore in Q2 FY27, up 19.4% YoY
from INR 232.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, driven by continued momentum
in its Distillery business.
Distillery revenue increased 30.5% YoY to INR 271.3 crore and accounted for 97.6% of the
Company’s quarterly revenue, compared with 89.3% in Q2 FY26, further strengthening its
position as the principal growth engine of the Company.
The Company continues to advance its strategic focus on strengthening its premium, super-
premium and luxury spirits portfolio, expanding market presence and distribution, enhancing
brand equity and leveraging its expanded manufacturing capabilities to drive sustainable long-
term growth.
As part of this strategy, recent product introductions, including Indri Ilika, an exclusive
expression developed for the travel retail market, Indri Agneya and the highly anticipated Indri

CIN No.: L01115HR1994PLC032244
Diwali Collector’s Edition 2026, further reinforce the depth and premium positioning of its
portfolio.
The Company's commitment to product innovation and craftsmanship continues to receive
international recognition. Indri Diwali Collector’s Edition 2026 secured Double Gold with 96
points at the USA Spirits Ratings 2026, where it was also conferred the titles of Indian Single
Malt Whisky of the Year and Spirit of the Year – India. Further strengthening this recognition,
Indri Agneya was named Indian Single Malt Whisky of the Year at the London Spirits
Competition 2026.
These accolades reinforce the growing international recognition of Indian single malts and
support the Company's ambition to strengthen its presence in premium spirits markets in India
and globally.
Q2 FY27 – Key Highlights
 Revenue: INR 277.9 crore, up 19.4% YoY
 Distillery Revenue: INR 271.3 crore, up 30.5% YoY
 Distillery contribution to Revenue: 97.6%, compared with 89.3% in Q2 FY26
 EBITDA increased 9.6% YoY to INR 53 crore, supported by revenue growth
 Maturation Capacity: Achieved 96,000 barrels against the current FY target of 1,00,000
lakh
Commenting on the results, Mr. Natwar Agarwal, Chief Financial Officer, Piccadily Agro
Industries Limited, said, “Q2 FY27 saw continued momentum in our core Distillery business,
which grew over 30% YoY, while overall Company revenue increased by 19.4%. Our H1 FY27
PAT is higher than the corresponding period last year, reflecting the underlying strength of our
business and continued progress towards our financial objectives. The Distillery business
remains our principal growth engine, and its increasing contribution reflects the progress we
are making in strengthening Piccadily’s spirits-led business.
Our Branded Alcobev portfolio continues to expand, supported by our focus on the premium,
super-premium and luxury segments. The scaling up of the Chhattisgarh Distillery, together with
our enhanced manufacturing capabilities, positions us well to support our long-term growth
ambitions.
The Company remains firmly on track to achieve its business objectives, with a continued focus
on building differentiated brands, expanding its distribution footprint, strengthening
manufacturing capabilities and deepening its presence across domestic and international
markets.”

Premium Spirits Sustain Growth Momentum
Piccadily continues to strengthen its presence across the premium alcoholic beverages segment
through its portfolio of Indri Single Malt, Camikara Aged Rum, Cashmir Vodka and Whistler
Whisky.
The Company is gearing up for multiple new product launches, further strengthening its
portfolio, accelerating premiumization and unlocking new growth opportunities across
markets.
The Company remains focused on strengthening its existing brands, launching new offerings to
expand its portfolio across attractive spirits categories and widening its presence across
domestic and international markets.
Piccadily’s enhanced distillation capabilities at the Indri Distillery and the Chhattisgarh Distillery
will provide additional capacity to support the growth of its branded spirits portfolio.
The Company will continue to leverage its integrated manufacturing capabilities and growing
business portfolio to pursue long-term value creation for its stakeholders. The Company firmly
believes that the quality and maturation of brown spirits should be achieved naturally, without
the addition of colour or flavours. In line with this approach, the Company has revised its spirit
maturation target to over 1,00,000 barrels by the end of the current fiscal year.

33 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)

To the Board of Directors of
NMDC Limited
1) We have reviewed the accompanying statement of unaudited standalone financial results of NMDC
Limited ("the Company") for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 ("the Statement "),
being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the Securities and
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as
amended (the 'Listing Regulations").
2) This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and approved by the
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and
measurement principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial
Reporting" ("Ind AS 34"), prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with relevant
rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India. Our responsibility
is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
3) We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements
(SRE) 2410 - "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the
Entity", issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) and also considering the
requirements of Standard on Auditing {SA 600) on "Using the work of Another Auditor". These
standards require that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether
the financial statements are free of material misstatement. A review of interim financial information
consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters,
and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an
audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable us to
obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identifi ed in an
audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion .
4) Conclusion
Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe
that the accompanying statement prepared in accordance with recognition and measurement
principles laid down in the applicable Indian Accounting Standards {Ind AS) and other recognized
accounting practices and policies has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms
of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any
material misstatement.
5) Emphasis of Matter
We draw attention to the following matters included in the statement for the quarter and half year
ended September 30, 2026.
a) Note No. 3 regarding the Karnataka (Mineral Rights and Mineral Bearing Land) Tax Bill, 2024
proposing retrospective levy of taxes, which is pending the assent of the Hon'ble President of
India. Considering the current status, the estimated amount of INR 16,188.56 crores, if enacted
in its current form, has been considered as contingent liability.
b) Note No. 4 regarding recoverability of dues from NMDC Steel Limited ("NSL"), consisting of an
amount of INR 1,501.39 crores arising from demerger and INR 4921.06 crores of trade and other
receivables.
c) Note No. 5 regarding recoverability of trade receivables of Rashtriya !spat Nigam Limited (RINL)
amounting to INR 5,564.88 crores.
d) Note No. 7 regarding status of advance of INR 639.61 crores paid by the Company to Karnataka
Industrial Area Development Board (KIADB) towards the cost of land allotted to its wholly owned
subsidiary, Karnataka Vijayanagar Steel Limited (KVSL).
e) Note No. 8 regarding demand of INR 1623.44 crores relating to compensation based on Common
Cause Judgement, which is sub-judice.
f) Note No. 9 regarding order I notice alleging mineral dispatches without timely Railway Transit
Passes (RTP), resulting in a penalty of INR 1,620.50 crores, which is sub-judice.
g) Note No. 10 regarding financial position of Legacy Iron Ore Ltd, a foreign subsidiary of the
company.
The impact of the above on the financial results is dependent on the outcome of the
proceedings/matters as described in the said notes.
Our Conclusion on the statement is not modified in respect of these matters.
6) Other Matters
a) We did not review the financial results of six branches included in the unaudited standalone
financial results of the Company, whose results reflect total income of INR 6,950.32 Crores and
INR 14,057.83 Crores and total profit before tax of INR 2,068.69 Crores and INR 4,643.80 Crores
for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 respectively, as considered in the
respective unaudited financial results of the Branches included in the unaudited standalone
financial results of the Company. The financial results of these branches have been reviewed by
the branch auditors whose reports have been furnished to us, and our conclusion in so far as it
relates to the amounts and disclosures included in respect of these branches, is based solely on
the review report of such branch auditors.
b) The standalone financial results include the result for the quarter ended September 30, 2026
being the balancing figures between unaudited result in respect of the half year ended
September 30, 2026 and the unaudited published result for the quarter ended June 30, 2026,
being the date of the end of the first quarter of the said financial year which were subjected to
limited review.
c) The Statement includes comparative figures for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, corre.sponding
quarter & half year ended September 30, 2025 which have been reviewed by the Predecessor
Statutory Auditors of the Company , where they had expressed an unmodified conclusion . on such
Standalone Financial Results.
The Statement also includes result for the year ended March 31, 2026, which have been audited

November 12, 2026: Travel Food Services Limited (TFS), a leading operator of Travel QSR outlets and Lounges in
India, announces its results for the second quarter and the first half-year ended September 30, 2026.

Key Financial Highlights – Q2FY27 & H1FY27
➢ System-wide sales increased to Rs. 8,654 million (up 18. 8% YoY) in Q2FY2 7 and Rs.17,090 million (up 18.4%
YoY) in H1FY27, driven by a combination of net contract gains3 and Like-for-like (LFL) sales growth4.
o Net contract gains were 11.1% YoY in Q2FY27 and 13.5% YoY in H1FY27, supported by the
mobilisation and ramp -up of new units across airports and contribution f rom the lounge
aggregation business. Over the last one year, more than 70 units have been mobilised, primarily
across New Delhi, Cochin, Navi Mumbai, Noida and Bhogapuram airports.
o LFL sales growth was 3.5% YoY in Q2FY27 and 2.2% YoY in H1FY27 at the system-wide level. During
the quarter, while passenger traffic declined at TFS-managed airports due to factors influenced by
the West Asia crisis, LFL sales growth has been supported by menu enhancement and
premiumisation initiatives. On a system-wide basis, passenger traffic declined by 4.8% YoY for the
second quarter and 2.2% YoY for the first half of the year.
➢ Consolidated sales stood at Rs.4,253 million (up 19.5% YoY in Q2FY27), and Rs.8,775 million (up 20.1% YoY
in H1FY27) mainly driven by:
o Net contract gains of 11.0% YoY in Q2FY27 and 15.7% YoY in H1FY27, supported by the mobilisation
of new units and contribution from the lounge aggregation business. In the last 12 months, n ew
units have been mobilised at the Delhi Airport (Terminal 1 and Terminal 2), Cochin Airport
(Domestic Terminal 1), and the recently opened Noida Airport.
o LFL sales grew 6.6% YoY in Q2FY27 and 5.3% YoY in H1FY27, supported by our continued focus on
premiumisation and menu optimisation, despite a decline in passenger traffic.
➢ Consolidated PAT was Rs.1,473 million in Q2FY27 and Rs.2,761 million in H1FY27, representing YoY increases
of 50.5% and 43.2%, respectively. Profitability was supported by sales growth, higher other income and an
increase in share of profit from joint ventures. PAT included write-back of provisions (net of tax) amounting
to ~Rs.468 million in Q2FY27 and ~Rs.566 million in H1FY27 (also includes a partial GST provision write-back
of ~Rs.98 million (net of tax) recognised in Q1FY27).
➢ Our balance sheet remains strong and debt-free, supported by a strong liquidity position with cash balance
of Rs.10,309 million as of September 30, 2026.
Operating Environment and Industry Dynamics
➢ Geopolitical uncertainties, elevated airfares, changes in airline schedules and capacity rationalisation
weighed on passenger volumes and travel patterns in the first half. This has also led to inflationary pressures
and hampered consumer confidence. However, the operating environment is expected to improve gradually
in the second half, supported by the potential easing of geopolitical pressures and seasonally stronger travel
demand. While the pace of recovery in passenger traffic remains a key monitorable, thes e factors should
provide a more favourable backdrop for travel volumes.
➢ TFS continues to navigate the evolving environment through strong execution, an efficient supply chain, and
flexible manpower deployment. The Company remains focused on driving productivity across the existing
network, ramping up recently opened locations, progressing its development pipeline and scaling new
growth initiatives, positioning the business well for continued growth as passenger traffic improves.
Key Operational Highlights
➢ TFS expanded its airport presence to 22 airports as of September 30, 2026, on a system-wide basis (from
18 airports as of September 30, 2025), with start of operations at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport,
Bhogapuram.
➢ The system-wide Travel QSR portfolio expanded to 535 outlets as of September 30, 2026, from 464 outlets
a year earlier, with over 70 outlets added across New Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Cochin, Noida and other key
airports. The lounge portfolio stood at 35 lounges, compared with 37 lounges a year earlier, primarily
reflecting closures related to terminal transitions and airport infrastructure renovations.
➢ Our brand portfolio expanded to 156 brands as of September 30, 2026, on a system-wide basis, with 21 in-
house, regional and international brands added over the last 12 months. The broader portfolio enhances
our ability to curate the right brand mix across locations and address evolving traveller preferences.
➢ Under Elite Assist Technology and Services Private Ltd. (EATS), we continue to broaden the EATS ecosystem
by extending lounge access distribution beyond banking and card-network channels.
➢ For the second consecuti ve year, Kyra Lounge at Hong Kong International Airport has been named Asia’s
Leading Airport Lounge at the World Travel Awards 2026.

operating environment. Despite these headwinds, TFS' system-wide sales grew 18.8% year-on-year and the business
continued to deliver healthy underlying profitabilit y, demonstrating the resilience of our portfolio and expanding
network. This performance reinforces our confidence in the business and its ability to grow through periods of near -

growth avenues in passenger services, including EATS.

Nupur Recyclers Limited clocks record Q2 FY27, with PAT more than doubles YoY to ₹879.84 Lakh,
registering a growth of 103.06%.
New Delhi, 12th November, 2026: Nupur Recyclers Limited (NSE: NRL) (“Nupur Recyclers”, “NRL” or the
“Company”), a leading player in the import, processing and recycling of non-ferrous metal scrap in India, today
announced its Unaudited Financial Results for the Quarter and Half Year ended September 30, 2026.
Key Financial Highlights (Consolidated)

Key Business & Operational Highlights
A. Financial Performance
Q2 FY27
● Revenue: Total Revenue surged 124.86% YoY to ₹11,620.80 Lakh, supported by enhanced production capacity
at Frank Metals Recyclers following the commissioning of its new 4-inch extrusion plant, Execution of new
orders received from Sundram and Tata at Tycod Autotech, and further capacity utilisation at Nupur Extrusion.
● EBITDA: EBITDA surged 148.48% YoY to ₹1,572.95 Lakh, achieving a margin of 13.54%, supported by a
higher share of manufacturing-led revenue, favourable metal price trends, and operational efficiencies coupled
with stringent cost management.
● PAT: Profit After Tax expanded 103.06 % YoY to ₹879.84 Lakh, with a PAT margin of 7.57 %.
H1 FY27
● Revenue: Total Revenue stood at ₹19,923.85 Lakh, up 90.27 % YoY.
● EBITDA: EBITDA stood at ₹2,858.55 Lakh, up 130.34 % YoY, with a margin of 14.35 %.
● PAT: Profit After Tax stood at ₹1,618.41 Lakh, up 93.19 % YoY with a margin of 8.12 %
B. Core Subsidiaries’ Performance
● Tycod Autotech Private Limited (51%): Acquired on September 1, 2025; contributed for the full quarter in
Q2 FY27, against one month in Q2 FY26. Reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹ 1,583.30 Lakh, with capacity
utilisation rising to 30% from 10% in Q1 FY27.
● Frank Metals Recyclers Limited (80%): Recently entered aluminium extrusion (about approx. 2,000 MTPA
installed, fully utilised in Q2 FY27), alongside its zinc ingot, aluminium ingot and aluminium billet operations.
Reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹ 6,422.80 Lakh.
● Nupur Extrusion Private Limited (70%): Continues to serve solar manufacturers, construction and OEM
customers from its Sampla (Haryana) facility. Reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹ 1,347.96 Lakh, with capacity
utilisation of 50%.
C. Capacity Expansion & Projects
● Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) Battery Recycling, Sampla (Haryana): Construction of the 6,000 MTPA
Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) Battery Recycling facility is underway. The project is held directly by Nupur
Recyclers Limited at the standalone level, not through any subsidiary. It is based on hydrometallurgical
technology and involves an investment of ₹50 - ₹70 Cr, which is being funded entirely through internal accruals.
Commissioning is targeted during Q4 FY27.
Management Commentary
Commenting on the results, Mr. Rajesh Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, Nupur Recyclers Limited said:
“Q2 FY27 has been the strongest quarter in the Company’s history, with Total Revenue of ₹11,620.80 Lakh, up 124.86%
year-on-year, and PAT of ₹ 879.84 Lakh. The performance was led by higher volumes in our core non-ferrous scrap
business and a growing contribution from our subsidiaries as their downstream operations scaled up. Our diversified
sourcing network across Europe, the USA and the UAE, combined with disciplined procurement, enabled us to sustain
margins amid volatile metal prices.
Our capacity expansion programme is progressing as planned. Construction of the 6,000 MTPA Lithium Iron Phosphate
(LFP) battery recycling facility at Sampla, Haryana is underway on a 5-acre land parcel, with an approximate covered
area of 1,35,000 square feet. The plant is based on hydrometallurgical technology for the recovery of battery materials,
is funded through internal accruals, and remains on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27. It positions us early in a
segment we expect to see significant growth as India’s EV and energy storage ecosystem matures. At Frank Metals, an
additional aluminium extrusion plant with capacity of 3600 MTPA is under installation, with commissioning expected
in Q4 FY27. At Nupur Extrusion, will add 150 MT per month incremental capacity of aluminium extrusion to the existing
200 MT per month.
Looking ahead, we see two clear growth levers. The first is operating leverage as utilisation improves across our existing
capacities. The second is incremental volume from the new capacities coming online. Together, these would support
sustained revenue growth, improve margin and a richer value-added product mix. We will remain disciplined in capital
allocation and committed to a strong balance sheet as we scale.”
About Nupur Recyclers Limited
Nupur Recyclers Limited (NSE: NRL) is a leading importer, trader, Recyclers, extruder and processor of non-ferrous
metal scrap, including shredded zinc, zinc die-cast scrap, Zurik scrap and aluminium scrap grades. Through its
subsidiaries, the Company has forward-integrated into zinc and aluminium alloys, ingots and billets, aluminium
extrusion and precision auto components, and is setting up a 6,000 MTPA Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery
recycling plant using hydrometallurgy technology. The Company is committed to promoting sustainable business
practices, environmental responsibility and the adoption of eco-friendly and green energy initiatives. Through its
operations in the recycling and processing of metals, the Company plays a vital role in conserving natural resources,
reducing waste, minimising environmental impact and supporting the efficient utilisation of resources. The Company
endeavours to contribute towards a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future by encouraging responsible recycling

Manappuram Finance Q2FY27 Consolidated Net Profit Rises 222.90% YoY to ₹701 crore; Consolidated AUM at ₹73,303 crore, a growth of 60.1 % year on year Valapad, Keralam; November 12, 2026: Manappuram Finance Ltd, a leading non-banking financial company (NBFC), today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026 (Q2FY27 and H1FY27). The gold loan NBFC reported a 222.90% year-on-year (YoY) growth in consolidated net profit to ₹701 crore. In the same quarter of the previous fiscal year (Q2FY26), consolidated net profit stood at ₹217 crore. For the quarter under consideration, the consolidated revenue from operations grew 46.2% YoY to ₹3,356 crore, compared with ₹2,296 crore in Q2FY26. Consolidated assets under management (AUM) as on September 30, 2026 grew 60.1% YoY to ₹73,303 crore. Gold loan AUM stood at ₹60,640 crore, a growth of 92.5% YoY. Non-gold loan businesses accounted for 17.27% of consolidated AUM. The gold tonnage for Q2 was 70 tonnes and it grew year on year to 22 % and 3.5 % sequentially. For the quarter under consideration, the customer base grew sequentially 2.3 % to 46.9 lakh customers. Asirvad Micro Finance Ltd, the company’s microfinance subsidiary, reported a profit of ₹32 crore for the quarter, with AUM of ₹7,919 crore as on September 30, 2026. For the half-year ended September 30, 2026 (H1FY27), consolidated net profit stood at ₹1,286 crore, compared with ₹350 crore in H1FY26, while consolidated revenue from operation stood at ₹6,403 crore, against ₹4,546 crore in H1FY26. On a consolidated basis, the company’s branch network stood at 5,375 as on September 30, 2026. The Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of ₹1 per equity share of face value ₹2 each for FY27. Mr V.P. Nandakumar, Chairman and Managing Director, Manappuram Finance Ltd, said: “In Q2, we have delivered strong growth in profitability and AUM. The year-on-year growth in consolidated net profit sets a strong tone for the coming quarters. Our subsidiaries have also shown improved performance on a year-on-year basis. Looking ahead, the outlook for the gold loan business remains positive as we continue to strengthen the business to navigate future challenges. We are confident of achieving our targets for this fiscal year.”
About Manappuram Finance Ltd Manappuram Finance Ltd is one of India’s leading gold loan NBFCs, engaged in providing finance against gold jewellery. Incorporated in 1992, the company was promoted by Mr V.P. Nandakumar, whose family has been involved in the gold loan business since 1949. It is headquartered in Valapad, in the Thrissur district of Kerala. The company went public in August 1995, and its shares are listed on the BSE and NSE. Commenting on the results, Mr. Vinod Kumar Gupta and Mr. Binay Kumar Gupta , Managing Director s, Dollar
Industries Limited said:
“We are pleased to report our results for the second quarter and first half of FY27, with healthy value and volume growth.
Operating Income for the quarter rose by 14.3% YoY to ₹53,928 lacs. For H1 FY27, Operating Income stood at ₹94,409 lacs,
registering growth of 8.4% YoY.
For the quarter ended Q2 FY27, Gross Profit grew by 4.5% YoY to ₹17,139 lacs, with a Gross Profit Margin of 31.8%. The
moderation in gross margin was primarily attributable to higher cotton prices, a key raw material for the company. Operating
EBITDA stood at ₹6,054 lacs, with a margin of 11.2%. While gross margins came under pressure, disciplined cost management,
stringent overhead controls and operating leverage helped cushion a part of the impact at the Operating EBITDA level. Profit
After Tax attributable to owners stood at ₹3,579 lacs, with a PAT Margin of 6.6%.
For H1 FY27, Operating EBITDA stood at ₹10,831 lacs, with a margin of 11.5%, while PAT stood at ₹6,181 lacs, with a margin of
6.5%. As we move into the second half of the financial year, our focus remains on driving profitable growth through improved
operating efficiencies, disciplined cost management and higher volumes.
Our newer growth channels and product categories continued to gain momentum during the quarter. Quick commerce recorded
growth of 58.5% in value and 52.4% in volume terms, with its contribution to overall revenue increasing from 4.0% in Q2 FY26 to
5.4% in Q2 FY27. This reflects the growing consumer preference for convenient, on -demand access to everyday essentials and
underscores the importance of strengthening our presence across emerging distribution channels.
Dollar Thermal, our winterwear segment, registered a growth of 17.7% in value and 10.2% in volume terms during the quarter,
contributing 12.6% to overall revenue. Dollar Protect, our rainwear segment, also witnessed strong traction, recording value
growth of 208.1%, supported by a favourable monsoon season. These categories continue to strengthen our product portfolio
while enabling us to address evolving consumer needs across adjacent product segments.
Page | 2
Our export business also delivered a strong performance during the quarter, with value growth of 56.8% and volume growth of
45.5%. We view international markets as an important long-term growth opportunity and will continue to focus on expanding
our global presence.
We remain confident that our initiatives across core markets, emerging channels and exports will keep driving growth in the
coming quarters. With our strong brand portfolio, extensive distribution network and sustained focus on execution, cost
discipline and profitability, we are well positioned to capitalise on the opportunities ahead a nd deliver sustainable value to our
stakeholders.”
“Milestones Achieved in Q2 FY27”
• Operating Income of ₹ 53,928 Lacs in Q2 FY27, registering a growth of 14.3% YoY
• Gross Profit of ₹ 17,139 Lacs in Q2 FY27, registering a growth of 4.5%. Gross margin was at 31.8%
• Operating EBITDA of ₹ 6,054 Lacs in Q2 FY27, growing 0.4% YoY, with a margin of 11.2%
• PAT of ₹ 3,579 Lacs in Q2 FY27, with a margin of 6.6%
• Diluted EPS stood at ₹ 6.31 in Q2 FY27 as against ₹ 6.20 in Q2 FY26
“Milestones Achieved in H1 FY27”
• Operating Income of ₹ 94,409 Lacs in H1 FY27, registering a growth of 8.4% YoY
• Gross Profit of ₹ 32,263 Lacs in H1 FY27, registering a growth of 5.6% YoY. Gross Margin was at 34.2%
• Operating EBITDA of ₹ 10,831 Lacs in H1 FY27, registering a growth of 5.0% YoY, with a margin of 11.5%
• PAT of ₹ 6,181 Lacs in H1 FY27, registering a growth of 9.4% YoY, with a margin of 6.5%
• Diluted EPS stood at ₹ 10.90 in H1 FY27 as against ₹ 9.96 in H1 FY26
About Dollar Industries Limited
From a humble beginning as a hosiery brand to a leading name in the innerwear segment, Dollar Industries Limited ranks among
the top hosiery and garment manufacturing giants in India, covering entire range of knitted garments, from basic wear to oute r
wear. Behind its success lay a saga of business transformation, dedication, courage and confidence to swim against the tide and
go beyond the call of duty. The focus has always remained on the demanding needs of a globalized world and end customer
satisfaction. Today through its advanced quality products, Dollar has focused on achieving global excellence in cost, quality, and
productivity. The styles introduced by Dollar have always stayed in tune with the latest fashion.
Identical with top quality and value for money products, the brand Dollar enjoys the trust of millions of satisfied consumers across
the globe, leaving far-reaching footprints in the global market.
The company has a substantial pan -India presence and has established its market abroad, in countries like UAE, Oman, Jordan,
Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Yemen, Iraq, Nepal, and Sudan in past few years. The Company got listed in NSE & BSE a few years ago.
Dollar Industries Limited holds ~ 15% of the total market share in the organized segment and is the first Indian innerwear company
to have a fully integrated manufacturing unit which is equipped with all the latest processing technology and the top-most finishing
range to produce finished raw material dyed in any possible color.

A New Ambani Orgochem Is Taking Shape
Super Specialty Chemistry. Stronger Performance. A New Growth Trajectory.
MUMBAI | 16TH OCTOBER 2026:
Ambani Orgochem Limited, a super-specialty chemicals company established in 1985, with a diverse portfolio
spanning peroxide derivatives, salicylic acid and salicylates, metal octoates, and water based acrylic polymer
emulsions and dispersions, announces its Unaudited Financial Results for H1 FY27.

“Our strategic direction is to move beyond scale alone towards stronger value creation. This half-yearly
performance is a testament to our operational focus on expanding our super-specialty chemicals portfolio.
The emulsion expansion, salicylate development pipeline, addition of peroxide molecules and selective
backward integration are interconnected initiatives driven by one objective: building a resilient portfolio with
broader applications and a stronger technical foundation. Disciplined execution and customer validation will
remain central to translating these developments into sustainable business outcomes.”
~ Mr. Aashay R. Shah, Strategy Director, Ambani Orgochem Limited
02 / THE STRATEGIC SHIFT
From price-driven competition to value-driven chemistry
The transformation is not simply a change in product mix. It is a move towards a chemistry platform where
specialised products, process kn ow-how, application understanding and manufacturing consistency
increasingly work together. The Company’s current roadmap connects near -term capacity additions with a
wider pipeline of molecules and derivatives, laying the groundwork for a portfolio built around more than
volume alone.
THE OPERATING THESIS
Specialised Chemistry + Technical Capability + Application Knowledge + Manufacturing Consistency
03 / Four Platforms. One Evolving Chemistry Story.
Acrylic Waterborne Emulsions
From Traditional Emulsions to Next-Generation Waterborne Chemistry
Ambani Orgochem is rapidly growing and expanding it’s specialty acrylic waterborne emulsions divisions,
targeting applications across paints, coatings, adhesives, carpets, construction, textiles and paper.
CAPACITY EXPANSION
~2,000 T/month → ~4,500 T/month | 2.25x planned capacity
The ongoing Tarapur MIDC expansion aims to strengthen manufacturing scale and support applications
including waterproofing, pressure-sensitive adhesives, carpet binders and road infrastructure amongst
others.
STRATEGIC FOCUS | Scaling capacity. Advancing formulations. Unlocking application-led opportunities.
Salicylic Acid & Derivatives
Beyond the Core Molecule. Into Higher-Value Chemistry.
Building on its in-house salicylic acid manufacturing capability, Ambani Orgochem is expanding into value-
added derivatives for potential applications in cosmetics, fragrance, personal care, pharmaceuticals and
specialty chemicals.
CAPACITY ROADMAP
~40 → ~200 T/month
Planned 5 x expansion
DEVELOPMENT PIPELINE
12+ salicylate molecules
Selected molecules progressing towards plant trials
The identified pipeline includes octyl, 2-ethylhexyl, cyclohexyl, amyl, benzyl, isopropyl, hexyl, heptyl, homo-
menthyl, sakura, iso-amyl and iso-butyl salicylates.
STRATEGIC FOCUS | Moving downstream. Broadening the molecule portfolio. Pursuing higher-value
opportunities.
Peroxide Derivatives
Expanding the Molecule Playbook—and Strengthening the Input Chain
With 20+ existing products, specialised manufacturing infrastructure and in-house R&D, Ambani Orgochem is
expanding its peroxide portfolio for polymer processing, composites, rubber, elastomers and other industrial
applications.
PRODUCT INNOVATION
5 additional peroxide molecules
under development
BACKWARD INTEGRATION
2 critical raw materials
under in-house development
The Company has developed di-tert-amyl peroxide (DTA) through in-house R&D. Pilot trials for the two
raw materials are nearing completion; these inputs could potentially support ~6 additional peroxide
molecules, subject to validation and commercial assessment.
STRATEGIC FOCUS | Expanding molecular capabilities. Securing critical inputs. Building a more resilient
platform.
Metal Octoates
Established Chemistry. Expanding Industrial Relevance.
Ambani Orgochem’s cobalt, zirconium and calcium octoates serve coatings, composites, printing and
woodcare applications, including paint driers, FRP accelerators, inks and wood preservation.
The Company is focused on product innovation, deeper industrial engagement and expanding global reach—
reinforcing its application-led specialty chemistry offering.
STRATEGIC FOCUS | Deepening product expertise. Expanding market reach. Strengthening application-led
differentiation.
04 / MANAGEMENT PERSPECTIVE
Turning capability into value
“The next chapter for Ambani Orgochem is about converting years of preparation into a more differentiated
chemistry platform. On a consolidated basis, H1 FY27 reflects encouraging business momentum, with
Net Revenue from Operations rising 54.87% YoY to ₹171.22 crore, EBITDA increasing 43.00% to ₹11.32
crore, and Net Profit surging 1,709.33% to ₹3.45 crore. EPS also rose 1,514.46% YoY to ₹4.02, reflecting
a significant improvement over the corresponding period last year.
Across our businesses, we are working to deepen product capabilities, expand downstream opportunities
and strengthen the technical and manufacturing foundations behind our offerings. Our focus is on building
chemistry that is harder t o replicate, where application understanding, process discipline and consistent
quality matter alongside the molecule itself.”
~ Mr. Rakesh H. Shah, Managing Director, Ambani Orgochem Limited
“The past few years were about building the foundation.
The next phase is about converting that foundation into value.”
About Ambani Orgochem Limited
Ambani Orgochem Limited, incorporated in 1985, is a super -specialty chemicals-focused company engaged in
the manufacturing, processing, importing, supplying and exporting of high-performance Peroxide Derivatives,
Salicylic Acid & Salicylates, Metal Octoates, and Eco-Friendly Acrylic Coatings & Adhesives.
With over four decades of experience, the Company serves domestic & international markets with high -
performance, environmentally friendly solutions aligned with sustainable development goals.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon and welcome to Shiprocket's Q2 FY27 Earnings
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will remain in listen-only mode, and there
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the management's opening remarks. For
participants connected on only audio, if you need any assistance during the conference call,
please signal the operator by pressing star followed by zero on your touch-tone keypad.
We have with us today Mr. Saahil Goel, MD and CEO, Mr. Tanmay Kumar, CFO, and Mr.
Shreyanse Jain, Director, Investor Relations.
I now hand the call over to Mr. Tanmay Kumar for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over
to you, sir.
Tanmay Kumar: Good evening, and welcome to the call, our second as a listed company. Thank you. This quarter,
our revenue is up 35%, and adjusted EBITDA is up 3.3x to INR14 crores. Our Emerging
Businesses grew 60% plus, with much better economics, and we have turned PAT positive.
I will walk you through a short earnings presentation, and post that, we can have our
conversation and question answers. Shiprocket remains focused on its purpose. 300-320 million
Indians shop online today.
Online is about 8% of retail, heading to about 15% by 2030. India has about 60 million retail
MSMEs, and about 45% of online retail GMV already comes from tier two and beyond. Our
view on the market remains unchanged. We are very bullish on D2C and on quick commerce.
The merchants driving this growth will not build their own logistics, their own checkout, their
own marketing stack. They will rent it, they will use it from the people who build it, and that is
what we serve, and that is what we provide. Shiprocket is an enabler of Indian e-commerce via
technology and technology first.
A seller in Jaipur or Coimbatore opens one dashboard and gets everything that happens after
discovery - payments, fulfillment, shipping, customer experience, returns, and so on. 42+ courier
partners, 250+ ecosystem partners, one dashboard, data, money, trust flows through one
platform.
Our merchants do not need to worry about logistics. She just needs to make a great product, and
we’ll take care of everything else. That is what we are. Let me walk you through key financial
numbers.
Overall, revenue was INR670 crores plus, up 35%, and Adjusted EBITDA was INR14 crores
plus at 2.1% margin. Core revenue was about INR460 crores, up 25%, and Adjusted EBITDA
about INR59 crores at 12.8% margin. Emerging segment revenue was about INR210 crores, up
61%, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from minus 31.5% to minus 21.2%.
Shiprocket Limited

There is a 10 percentage point improvement. Growth is broad-based, core is scaling profitably,
and Emerging continues to scale faster. We generated about INR55 crores of cash from
operations in first half. That is about 2.3x the INR23-odd crores that we made in H1 of last year.
Overall, both engines are performing, growing, and with better economics. We will walk you
through quarterly growth metrics.
On a trailing 12-month basis, we are at our highest ever on all the three, 233 million transactions,
about INR37,400 crores of GMV, and over 236,000 active merchants. All metrics have grown.
In the quarter, GMV grew 33%, transactions grew 34%. This operating number shows we are
delivering ahead of what we set out in the beginning of the year.
We are excited about overall 34% plus transaction growth. We are reaching more merchants, we
are getting deeper into transactions, and that is exciting. Revenue grew 35%, and the build is
simple. We keep adding merchants, which was up about 8%, and merchants do more business
with us, and revenue per merchant is up 25%. The ARPU is up with more and more Emerging
adoption, while we continue to drive overall merchant count. Adjusted EBITDA up 3.3x,
obviously from a very small base.
It was INR4 crores last year, same time, and it is now INR14.2 crores. More importantly, we are
now PAT positive, and this is delivered largely due to operating leverage from platform scale.
We will talk about it subsequently. Growth is volume-led, broad-based, and it is not price-led,
just to put that point across. Overall contribution was INR130 crores, up 43% against the
revenue, which grew 35%. So profitability has been improving overall for the platform.
On a unit economics perspective, we continue to grow profitably. The sequential growth in
revenue for overall business was 7% in Q1 over Q4, and now it is 14%, Q2 over Q1. Margin is
at 19.3%, up 108 basis points. The interesting fact here is that every incremental rupee of revenue
this year came in with about 22% contribution margin. That is how you see the growth in margin.
Sequentially, we held contribution margin even if Emerging became much bigger share of the
mix. So contribution margin is growing faster than revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was at INR14.2
crores, margin at 2.1% against 0.9% a year ago and 1.5% last quarter. So it is improved both
YoY and sequentially, and both Core and Emerging improved year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA
excludes other income entirely. So this improvement is all operating.
PAT at INR6 million against a loss of INR20 crores a year ago is about INR21 crores swing. To
read the PAT walk, the INR21 crores swing, I would break into three parts. About INR10 crores
coming from higher Adjusted EBITDA, which is half this. About INR5 crores coming from
lower ESOP costs, and about INR5.5 crores from higher other income from IPO funds.
Everything else just showed about INR4 million. So the ESOP charge now keeps falling as a
share of revenue. It is under 4% from 6% a year ago. So about 70% of the PAT improvement is
operating, and yes, there is higher other income due to stronger balance sheet post IPO. We have
an effect of only half a quarter of the stronger balance sheet post IPO in the numbers for quarter
two.

November 12, 2026: Travel Food Services Limited (TFS), a leading operator of Travel QSR outlets and Lounges in
India, announces its results for the second quarter and the first half-year ended September 30, 2026.
