Key Financial Highlights – Q2FY27 & H1FY27
➢ System-wide sales increased to Rs. 8,654 million (up 18. 8% YoY) in Q2FY2 7 and Rs.17,090 million (up 18.4%
YoY) in H1FY27, driven by a combination of net contract gains3 and Like-for-like (LFL) sales growth4.
o Net contract gains were 11.1% YoY in Q2FY27 and 13.5% YoY in H1FY27, supported by the
mobilisation and ramp -up of new units across airports and contribution f rom the lounge
aggregation business. Over the last one year, more than 70 units have been mobilised, primarily
across New Delhi, Cochin, Navi Mumbai, Noida and Bhogapuram airports.
o LFL sales growth was 3.5% YoY in Q2FY27 and 2.2% YoY in H1FY27 at the system-wide level. During
the quarter, while passenger traffic declined at TFS-managed airports due to factors influenced by
the West Asia crisis, LFL sales growth has been supported by menu enhancement and
premiumisation initiatives. On a system-wide basis, passenger traffic declined by 4.8% YoY for the
second quarter and 2.2% YoY for the first half of the year.
➢ Consolidated sales stood at Rs.4,253 million (up 19.5% YoY in Q2FY27), and Rs.8,775 million (up 20.1% YoY
in H1FY27) mainly driven by:
o Net contract gains of 11.0% YoY in Q2FY27 and 15.7% YoY in H1FY27, supported by the mobilisation
of new units and contribution from the lounge aggregation business. In the last 12 months, n ew
units have been mobilised at the Delhi Airport (Terminal 1 and Terminal 2), Cochin Airport
(Domestic Terminal 1), and the recently opened Noida Airport.
o LFL sales grew 6.6% YoY in Q2FY27 and 5.3% YoY in H1FY27, supported by our continued focus on
premiumisation and menu optimisation, despite a decline in passenger traffic.
➢ Consolidated PAT was Rs.1,473 million in Q2FY27 and Rs.2,761 million in H1FY27, representing YoY increases
of 50.5% and 43.2%, respectively. Profitability was supported by sales growth, higher other income and an
increase in share of profit from joint ventures. PAT included write-back of provisions (net of tax) amounting
to ~Rs.468 million in Q2FY27 and ~Rs.566 million in H1FY27 (also includes a partial GST provision write-back
of ~Rs.98 million (net of tax) recognised in Q1FY27).
➢ Our balance sheet remains strong and debt-free, supported by a strong liquidity position with cash balance
of Rs.10,309 million as of September 30, 2026.
Operating Environment and Industry Dynamics
➢ Geopolitical uncertainties, elevated airfares, changes in airline schedules and capacity rationalisation
weighed on passenger volumes and travel patterns in the first half. This has also led to inflationary pressures
and hampered consumer confidence. However, the operating environment is expected to improve gradually
in the second half, supported by the potential easing of geopolitical pressures and seasonally stronger travel
demand. While the pace of recovery in passenger traffic remains a key monitorable, thes e factors should
provide a more favourable backdrop for travel volumes.
➢ TFS continues to navigate the evolving environment through strong execution, an efficient supply chain, and
flexible manpower deployment. The Company remains focused on driving productivity across the existing
network, ramping up recently opened locations, progressing its development pipeline and scaling new
growth initiatives, positioning the business well for continued growth as passenger traffic improves.
Key Operational Highlights
➢ TFS expanded its airport presence to 22 airports as of September 30, 2026, on a system-wide basis (from
18 airports as of September 30, 2025), with start of operations at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport,
Bhogapuram.
➢ The system-wide Travel QSR portfolio expanded to 535 outlets as of September 30, 2026, from 464 outlets
a year earlier, with over 70 outlets added across New Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Cochin, Noida and other key
airports. The lounge portfolio stood at 35 lounges, compared with 37 lounges a year earlier, primarily
reflecting closures related to terminal transitions and airport infrastructure renovations.
➢ Our brand portfolio expanded to 156 brands as of September 30, 2026, on a system-wide basis, with 21 in-
house, regional and international brands added over the last 12 months. The broader portfolio enhances
our ability to curate the right brand mix across locations and address evolving traveller preferences.
➢ Under Elite Assist Technology and Services Private Ltd. (EATS), we continue to broaden the EATS ecosystem
by extending lounge access distribution beyond banking and card-network channels.
➢ For the second consecuti ve year, Kyra Lounge at Hong Kong International Airport has been named Asia’s
Leading Airport Lounge at the World Travel Awards 2026.
Commenting on the Q2 & H1FY27 performance, Mr. Varun Kapur, Managing Director and CEO, TFS, said:
‘It was one of the most challenging quarter s for passenger traffic in recent periods, amid an unusually volatile
operating environment. Despite these headwinds, TFS' system-wide sales grew 18.8% year-on-year and the business
continued to deliver healthy underlying profitabilit y, demonstrating the resilience of our portfolio and expanding
network. This performance reinforces our confidence in the business and its ability to grow through periods of near -
term volatility.

are still ramping up, and with a significant pipeline of outlets yet to be mobilised acros s new and existing airports,
we have good visibility of continued growth as these operations mature. Alongside this, we continue to develop new

was felt on 2 fronts. First, average prices across our key polymers rose by 40% to 45% and prices
that had begun to stabilize in Q1 of FY '27 moved sharply higher once again compared to Q4 of
FY '26.

products remain resilient. Revenue from operations for Q2 FY '27 grew 18% year -on-year and

Q2 FY27: Delivers Highest Ever Core Business EBITDA
Consolidated EBITDA at ₹190 crore, up 86.6% YoY; consolidated PAT grew 121.7% YoY to ₹82 crore
Mumbai, 12 th November 2026: MAN Industries (India) Limited (BSE: 513269, NSE: MANINDS), one of India's leading
manufacturers of large -diameter carbon steel line pipes and coating systems for the oil & gas sector, today announced its
financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
Key Highlights — Q2 FY27
• Record Core Business Revenue & EBITDA: Consolidated EBITDA of ₹190 crore, the highest -ever for a quarter, was
up 86.6% YoY and 22.4% QoQ, with margin expanding 310 bps YoY to 15.6%, driven mainly by the contribution of
NPC, which has been consolidated since its acquisition on 21 May 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations grew
49.3% YoY to ₹1,216 crore, while consolidated PAT rose 121.7% YoY to ₹82 crore.
• Impact of Shipping Disruption: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia has disrupted key maritime routes, particularly the
Strait of Hormuz, causing port congestion and delays in dispatches of finished goods. As a result, revenue of
since nominated alternate ports, and these shipments are being executed.
• NPC Performance: In Q3 CY26 (July–September 2026), Saudi Arabia -based National Pipe Company (NPC) reported
revenue of SAR 191 million (~₹486 crore) and EBITDA of SAR 34 million (~₹88 crore), with EBITDA margin of ~18%;
PAT was SAR 30 million (~₹77 crore), with net margin of 15.8%.
For 9M CY26 (January–September 2026), including the period before its acquisition by MAN, NPC reported revenue
of SAR 415 million (~₹1,062 crore) and EBITDA of SAR 76 million (~₹194 crore), with EBITDA margin of 18.2%; PAT
was SAR 67 million (~₹171 crore), with net margin of 16.1%.
MAN completed the acquisition of NPC on 21 May 2026 and has consolidated it from that date. For the period from
21 May to 30 September 2026, NPC contributed revenue of SAR 208 million (~₹532 crore), EBITDA of SAR 37 million
(~₹94 crore) and PAT of SAR 31 million (~₹79 crore) to MAN’s consolidated results.
• Consolidated Order Book: Order book stands at ~₹ 3,500 crore across India and Saudi Arabia, with the majority
executable over the next 6–9 months.
• Merino Shelters Progress: The joint development agreement (JDA) project with the Paradise Group at Navi Mumbai
was launched on 26 October 2026. Cash flows of ₹700–800 crore is expected over the next 5–6 years.
• Jammu Greenfield Update: Implementation of the greenfield stainless steel seamless pipe plant at Jammu is on
track, with production expected by April 2027.
• Dammam Coating & Double Jointing Facility: Operations are targeted to commence by March 2027, further
strengthening MAN’s integrated manufacturing and value-added processing capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
• Establishment of Manufacturing Facility in USA: Establishment of a HSAW pipe facility in USA with a capacity of
350,000 MTPA and planned capex of US$110 million through its wholly owned subsidiary.

PRL Reports Revenue Growth with Sequential Profitability Recovery Amid Cost Pressures
Delhi, India, November 12, 2026: Premier Roadlines Limited (NSE: PRLIND), a niche logistics player delivering tailored
solutions in cargo handling, transportation, and project logistics today announced its financial results for the first half of
the year ended September 30, 2026.
Key Business Highlights
• Revenue and Operating Growth: Revenue from operations increased 18.3% YoY to Rs 166.8 Cr in H1FY27, supported
by steady demand from the power, transformer and renewable energy sectors. Total orders increased 2.8% YoY to
17,487, while average revenue per order improved 15.1% YoY to Rs 95,367, reflecting higher revenue realisation per
assignment.
• Stronger Customer Engagement: The Company served 415 customers in H1FY27, compared with 467 in H1FY26,
reflecting its focus on high-quality, long-term customer relationships. Despite a more focused customer base, the
number of orders increased, indicating deeper customer engagement and repeat business.
• Contract Logistics Margin Pressures: Geopolitical disruptions, rising non -fuel operating costs and tighter credit
availability for smaller fleet operators constrained vehicle availability, leading to higher vehicle hiring costs. While
diesel-related escalations are largely passed through, limited recovery of non-fuel cost increases under existing
contracts impacted EBITDA margins, despite growth in absolute EBITDA.

• Resilience Through Specialised Logistics: Project Logistics and ODC contributed 52% of revenue in H1FY27,
compared with 50% in H1FY26. Strong execution and high-capacity utilisation in these segments helped mitigate
margin pressures, while flexible spot -market pricing in General Logistics enabled more effective cost recovery.
Going forward, the Company plans to increase the contribution of Project Logistics and ODC , given their higher
margins. Contracts nearing expiry are expected to be renewed at revised prices , which is expected to further
support margins.
• Sequential Profitability Recovery: Despite continued operating cost pressures, EBITDA and PAT increased 19.7%
and 29.5% HoH, respectively, compared with H2FY26, accompanied by an improvement in profitability margins.
• Higher Vehicle Handling Activity: The Company handled 13,216 vehicles in H1FY27, up 5.2% YoY , reflecting
continued transportation activity despite prevailing fleet availability constraints.
• Expansion of Specialised Fleet Capabilities: In line with its strategic focus on specialised logistics, the Company
added 1 heavy-duty puller and 16 hydraulic axle lines during H1FY27, taking its total specialised fleet to 12 pullers
and 160 hydraulic axle lines, strengthening execution capabilities for complex cargo movements.
• Positive Operating Cash Flow and Debt Reduction: Generated operating cash flow of Rs 22.4 Cr in H1FY27 , while
total borrowings declined from Rs 55.9 Cr as of March 31, 2026 to Rs 41.9 Cr as of September 30, 2026.
Management Commentary
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Virender Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, said:
“H1FY27 witnessed steady business momentum across our key logistics segments, particularly Project Logistics and
ODC, supported by strong demand from the power, transformer and renewable energy sectors. We delivered revenue
growth, with absolute EBITDA and PAT improving YoY despite operating cost pressures. Importantly, profitability also
improved sequentially compared with H2FY26.
During the period, the transportation ecosystem continued to face challenges arising from geopolitical developments,
rising operating costs and tighter credit availability for smaller fleet operators, resulting in reduced fleet availability and
higher vehicle hiring costs. The impact was more pronounced in Contract Integrated Logistics, where limited pass -
through of non-fuel cost increases under existing contracts resulted in margin pressure. However, strong execution in
Project Logistics and ODC, along with flexible spot-market pricing in General Logistics, helped mitigate these pressures.
Looking ahead, H2 typically witnesses stronger business activity compared with H1, providing a favourable seasonal
backdrop. With certain contracts approaching renewal in Q3FY27 and Q4FY27, we are adopting a more disciplined
approach to contract pricing to better reflect prevailing operating costs and improve cost recovery. Going forward, we
remain focused on execution efficiency, customer servicing, and strengthening our specialised Project Logistics and
ODC capabilities to support sustainable long-term growth.”

About Premier Roadlines Limited
Founded in 2008, Premier Roadlines Ltd (PRL) is an IBA -approved and ISO-certified provider of surface logistics for dry
cargo, handling shipments from 1MT to 250MT. PRL offers a range of services including project logistics, over dimensional
cargo, contracted integrated logistics, general logistics and Fleet Rentals. The company serves leading clients like Tata,
Thyssenkrupp, L&T, and KEC across sectors such as energy, infrastructure, renewables, and heavy engineering. Utilizing
third-party operators and a fleet of trucks, trailers, and hydraulic axles, PRL operates a comprehensive PAN India network
with operations in Nepal and Bhutan as well. Acquired PRL Supply Chain Solutions as a wholly owned subsidiary, it
expands services to Ocean Freight, Air Freight, Project Logistics, and Warehousing & Distribution.
With its corporate office in Delhi, 28 branch offices, and a workforce of 233 employees, PRL managed 17,487 orders for
415 customers in H1FY27, overseeing a total of 13,216 vehicles.

profitability.

market. We are also moving our portfolio up the price ladder – with premium launches across our brands.

2. This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and approved by the
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement
principles laid down in Accounting Standard 25 Interim Financial Reporting'prescribed under Section
133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with relevant rules issued thereunder (hereinafter referred to as the
said Accounting Standard") and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, Our
responsibility is to issue a report on the Statement based on our review.
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE)
2410 Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity", issued
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial information consists of
making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying
analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in
accordance with the Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Aet, 2013 and
consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters
that might be identified in an audit. We have not performed an audit and accordingly, we do not express an
audit opinion.
Basis for Qualified Conclusion
4. Our conclusion is qualified in respect of the following matters
a) We have not been provided with balance confirmations for certain significant trade receivables, advances
from customers, trade payables and advance to vendors. Accordingly, these balances remain subject to
reconciliation and confirmation, and the consequential impact, if any, on the Statement has not been
ascertained by the management
b) The Company has outstanding dues to Micro and Small Enterprises beyond the credit period prescribed under
the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Aet"). The Company has not
recognized interest liability on such delayed payments as required under the provisions of the MSMED Aet
In the absence of adequate records and information necessary to compute the interest payable, we were unable
to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence regarding the amount of interest liability required to be recognized.
Accordingly, we are unable to determine the consequential impact, if any, on the Company's liabilities, profit
for the period and net worth as at and for the period ended September 30, 2026.
e) The Company has made export sales of INR 69.24 lakhs to a party, the proceeds of which have not been
realised within the period prescribed under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and
Services) Regulations, 2015, as amended. The Company has not applied to its Authorised Dealer bank for
extension of the time limit for realisation, and such non-realisation constitutes non-compliance with the
aforesaid Regulations. While the Company has recognised a provision against the aforesaid export receivable
in the Statement, no provision has been made for any penalty or other consequences that may arise from such
non-compliance.

goods. However, such advances have not been adjusted against the supply of goods within a period of 365

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sumedh from EY. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Sumedh: Thank you, Ra yo, and good afternoon, everyone. We welcome you to the Q2 and H1 FY27
Earnings Conference Call of ADF Foods Limited. To take us through the results and to answer
your questions, we have with us today the top management of ADF Foods, represented by
Mr. Bimal Thakkar, the Promoter, Chairman, Managing Director, and CEO; Mr. Sumer
Thakkar, Vice President, Sales & Strategy; and Mr. Srinivas V. Ayyagari , the Chief Financial
Officer.
We will start the call with an overview of the business and the recent updates by
Mr. Bimal Thakkar, and then Mr. Srinivas will give his comments on the financials. As usual,
the standard Safe Harbor clause applies while we start the call. Over to you, Bimal, sir.
Bimal Thakkar: Thank you, Sumedh. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I am pleased
to share that we continued our strong growth momentum during the second quarter of FY27 ,
delivering consecutive quarters of strong double-digit year-on-year revenue growth.
During Q2 FY27, our consolidated revenues from operations increased by 23.6% year -on-year
to INR200.9 crores. This represents our highest-ever quarterly revenue and marks the first time
that ADF has crossed INR200 crores in quarterly revenue.
On a standalone basis, revenue increased by 16.6% year -on-year to INR 163.3 crores. The
performance reflects healthy demand across our brands, deeper penetration in our key markets,
expansion of shelf space, and continued execution across both our processed foods and
distribution businesses.
Our order book remains strong, providing healthy visibility for the coming quarters. However,
the conversion of our strong order pipeline was partly constrained by limited container
availability and disruptions across key shipping routes. Importantly, we delivered this growth
despite these logistical challenges and elevated ocean freight costs.
Demand remained resilient across our international markets, supported by growing preference
for convenient, authentic Indian foods. Our diversified portfolios across frozen foods, ready-to-
eat, ready -to-cook, and meal accompaniments continue to enable us to address multiple
consumer segments and consumption occasions.
Let me now share an update on our key brands. Ashoka, our flagship brand, continued to deliver
strong growth driven by sustained demand from the South Asian diaspora and deeper penetration
across core and emerging international markets. Ashoka has delivered a revenue CAGR of over
20% during the last five years, reflecting the strength of the brand, the breadth of its portfolio,
and our consistent investments in distribution, consumer engagement, and innovation.

securing new retail listings, and driving deeper penetration across existing accounts.
In India, Soul continued to expand its portfolio and channel presence. During the quarter, we
launched A2 Gir Cow Danedar Ghee, prepared using the traditional bilona process. This addition
expands Soul's 'better-for-you' product portfolio and gives the brand an entry level into a large
everyday kitchen category.
We will continue to build the brand in a measured manner through product innovation, broader
distribution, and targeted consumer engagement. On manufacturing, our Surat greenfield facility
continues to make steady progress towards achieving its targeted operational performance. The
facility enhances our frozen food manufacturing capabilities and provides us with capacity
required for future demand.
Alongside Surat, Nadiad and Nashik further strengthen our manufacturing platform and improve
our ability to scale efficiently. On growth investments, we continue to maintain financial
discipline. Our balance sheet remains strong, with a net surplus of INR97.4 crores at the end of
H1 of FY27. The Board has also declared an interim dividend of 30% of the face value of share,
continuing our track record of consistent shareholder returns.
Looking ahead, we remain confident in structural growth opportunities across our categories and
markets. Our growth will continue to be supported by deeper brand penetration, new retail
listings, distribution expansion, innovation, and ramp- up of recently added capacities. At the
same time, we remain watchful of vessel availability, ocean freight costs, and geopolitical
developments impacting our shipping routes and markets.

Dynacons Secures its First International Order worth USD 6.83 Million from the
Ministry of Public Works, Public Utilities and Digital Economy, Caribbean Digital
Transformation Project Unit, Commonwealth of Dominica
Dynacons Systems & Solutions Limited (“Dynacons”), a leading IT infrastructure and digital
solutions company, is pleased to announce that it has secured its first international order,
marking an important milestone in the Company’s journey towards expanding its presence in
global markets.
The prestigious contract, valued at USD 6.83 million, has been awarded by the Ministry of Public
Works, Public Utilities and the Digital Economy, Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica,
under the Caribbean Digital Transformation Project for the Health Management and Information
System (HMIS) IT Infrastructure.
Under the project, Dynacons will undertake the supply, installation, configuration and
maintenance of comprehensive IT infrastructure supporting the HMIS ecosystem across 3
hospitals, 49 health centres and 2 wellness centres in Dominica. The engagement is spread
over three years and includes ongoing support, warranty, preventive maintenance and
corrective maintenance.
The scope encompasses a broad range of critical healthcare IT infrastructure including endpoints
for HMIS applications, radiology workstations supporting PACS, computers on wheels, laptops,
printers, barcode scanners and printers, SAN switches and storage, Microsoft infrastructure and
licences, firewalls and Network Access Control solutions, patient identification wristbands and
related equipment.
This order represents a significant milestone for Dynacons as its first international project and
marks the Company's entry into the Caribbean market. It demonstrates Dynacons’ ability to
leverage its proven capabilities in designing, deploying and supporting mission-critical digital
infrastructure in India and extend these capabilities to international markets.
The project also builds on Dynacons’ experience in supporting healthcare and HMIS-related IT
infrastructure in India. The Dominica engagement further strengthens Dynacons’ credentials
in digital healthcare infrastructure, systems integration and managed services, while opening
opportunities for the Company to participate in similar digital transformation initiatives across
international markets.
Commenting on this milestone, Mr. Shirish Anjaria, Chairman cum Managing Director of the
Company said:
“Securing our first international order is an important milestone in Dynacons’ growth journey.
The project provides us an opportunity to take the capabilities and experience we have built
over several years in India to an international market.
Healthcare technology infrastructure is a mission-critical area, and we are pleased to have been
entrusted with supporting the Health Management and Information System infrastructure across
hospitals and healthcare centres in Dominica. Our experience in implementing and supporting
complex IT environments, provides us with a strong foundation for successful execution of this
project.
More importantly, this order marks the beginning of Dynacons’ international expansion and we
believe it can serve as a reference point for pursuing similar digital transformation opportunities
in global markets.”

joining us for the H1 FY27 Earnings Call of Effwa Infra & Research
Limited. On behalf of the board and the entire Effwa team, I extend a
warm welcome to our shareholders, investors, analysts and all
stakeholders. We appreciate your continued trust and support as we
execute our growth strategy and strengthen our position in India's water
and environmental engineering sector.
Before reviewing our financial performance, I would like to begin with
a significant milestone that many stakeholders have consistently
inquired about during our previous interactions. I'm delighted to
announce that Effwa has formally filed a patent applic ation for our
proprietary zero material discharge technology.
This marks an important step in our journey to build a differentiated
technology-led business, while conventional zero liquid discharge
systems, that is ZLD systems, recover and recycle water, they still leave
behind salt residues that industries must dispose of as hazardous waste,
often at a considerable cost.
Our ZMD technology is designed to eliminate this challenge by
recovering high- purity commercially usable byproducts efficiently,
effectively ensuring that no material is sent to landfill, promoting
circular economy. For customers, this translates into lowe r operating
and waste disposal costs, improved sustainability outcomes and
enhanced resource recovery.

strong half year marked by robust revenue growth, healthy profitability
and disciplined execution.
For the 6 months ended 30th September 2026, revenue from operations
increased 44.8% year -on-year to INR130.6 crores. EBITDA grew
37.1% to INR21.2 crore, while PAT rose 48.8% to INR15.1 crores. PAT
margin improved to 11.6% and earnings per share increased to 6.52 from
4.38 in H1 financial year '26.
These results reflect the strength of our execution capabilities,
improving project mix and continued focus on profitable growth. The
period was also marked by several important operational achievements.
We successfully completed a 48 MLD ZLD for Rourkela Steel Plant,
SAIL, with a contract value exceeding INR200 crores, which was
delivered on time.
In addition, we completed and handed over projects for Vedanta, Indian
Oil, Tata Steel Mining as well as international projects for Afcons
infrastructure in Ivory Coast and two projects in Tanzania, further
strengthening our credentials across diverse geographies and industries.
In July, we secured a INR44.3 crores end-to-end ZLD project from JSW
and maintenance revenue over a 3-year period.
This order reflects our strategy of increasing recurring revenue streams
by integrating long-term O&M contracts alongside EPC execution. I am
also pleased to share that CRISIL upgraded our bank facility ratings to
CRISIL BBB/+ STABLE for long-term facilities and CRISIL A2 for
short-term facilities.
This upgrade reinforces the strength of our financial profile, execution
track record and prudent capital management. Further validating our
innovation-led approach, Effwa was recognized with the Afcons
Innovation Partner f or the Year 2025- 26, an acknowledgment of the
value we bring to our customers through technology and engineering
excellence.
As we prepare for the next phase of growth, we have planned a dedicated
innovation center which is expected to become operational within a
period of next 12 to 14 months. This facility will accelerate product
development, technology commercialization and r esearch initiatives,
strengthening our ability to deliver differentiated solutions to customers
and to develop trained human resources.
To deepen customer engagement and improve project delivery
capabilities, we are also establishing regional operations in Kolkata and
New Delhi, enabling us to better serve clients across Eastern and
Northern India. Additionally, we are pleased to welcome Dr. Arun
Tripathi, former Director General of Solar Energy Corporation of India,
to our advisory board.
His extensive experience in renewable energy and large -scale
infrastructure development projects will provide valuable guidance as
we expand into adjacent high- growth sectors. Looking ahead, we are
actively building a presence in three attractive and strategically aligned
segments like desalination, high-purity water treatment for data centers
and compressed biogas (CBG).
Each of these sectors is supported by strong long-term structural drivers.
Rising water stress is increasing demand for desalination solutions.
Rapid expansion of India's digital infrastructure is creating significant
opportunities in high- purity water sys tems for data centers and the
country's transition towards cleaner energy resources is accelerating
investment in compressed biogas.
We are witnessing encouraging inquiry activity across all three areas and
are actively participating in multiple bid opportunities. While these
initiatives remain at an early stage, we believe they have the potential to
evolve into meaningful growth engine s and diversify our revenue base
over the coming years.
At Effwa, every strategic decision is guided by our commitment to
creating long-term shareholder value. We remain disciplined in project
selection by selective bidding and continue to fund growth through
internal accruals and prudent banking facilities rat her than equity
dilution.
To summarize, H1 FY27 reflects the successful execution of our

stood at ₹16.99 crore and ₹7.52 crore, respectively. On a consolidated basis, the Company
reported total Revenue of ₹328.77 crore for the quarter and ₹656.29 crore for the half year.
Consolidated Profit After Tax (PAT) stood at ₹184.73 crore compared to ₹164.29 crore in the
corresponding quarter last year, while for half year, PAT stood at ₹184.78 crore compared to
₹163.82 crore in the same period last year.
The Company continued to drive operational efficiency and performance across its businesses
during the quarter. The Sugar, Power & Ethanol division recorded a 7% increase in sugar sales
during the quarter to 3.9 lakh quintals, compared to 3.7 lakh quintals in the corresponding
period last year. For the half year, sugar sales grew by 18% to 8.6 lakh quintals, compared to 7.3
lakh quintals in the corresponding period of the previous year. Average sugar realisation
improved by 14% to ₹4,588 per quintal during the quarter owing to an uptick in sugar prices.
The real estate arm, Zuari Infraworld India Limited, continued to make progress across its
portfolio. At St. Regis, Dubai, handovers are currently underway, and profit repatriation has
commenced. During the quarter, the Company did a formal launch of Zuari Gangothri Tribhuja,
a residential project in Hyderabad, and Zuari KinetiX, a plotted development project in
Bengaluru, both under the Development Management model. Progress also continued across
other Development Management projects in Kolkata.
The engineering arm of the Company, Simon India Limited continued to advance its project
pipeline and execution efforts. During the quarter, SIL secured orders for engineering and
and remains focused on expanding its order book across its core sectors, while advancing
digitalization and AI-led initiatives across project execution and key processes.
The Company's joint venture, Zuari Envien Bioenergy Private Limited, has stabilised operations
following plant commissioning and submitted its bid for the annual OMC tender.
Key Financial Snapshot (Standalone)
“The second quarter is an important period for our Sugar, Power & Ethanol business as we prepare for
the new crushing season. We commenced crushing operations in October 2026, in line with last year,
with a focus on maximising crush during the season. I am encouraged by the improvement in operating
margins during the quarter, both sequentially and year-on-year, supported by stronger sugar prices,
improved operating efficiencies and cost management. Our continued focus on financial discipline has
also helped reduce borrowing rates and finance costs.
Our Real Estate business continues to make encouraging progress. Handovers at the St. Regis
Residences, Dubai have commenced, with profit repatriation from the project supporting our
deleveraging efforts. During the quarter, we also formally launched Zuari Gangotri Tribhuja, a residential
project in Hyderabad, and Zuari Kinetix, a plotted development project in Bengaluru, both under
development management model.
Our Engineering business is seeing positive momentum, securing engineering and feasibility
assignments. I am also pleased with the progress of our bioethanol plant, developed in partnership with
Envien, which has stabilised and demonstrated robust operations.
Looking ahead, our focus remains on strengthening our existing businesses, pursuing growth
opportunities and maintaining financial discipline. We remain committed to leveraging technology and
sustainability initiatives to build resilient businesses and create long-term value for our stakeholders.”

Q2 FY 2026-2027 marked a quarter of gradual recover y, supported by healthy demand

During the quarter, global market conditions remai ned dynamic, with geopolitical developments
in the Middle East and disruptions across key shipp ing routes impacting raw material
availability, input costs, and freight rates.
While these factors resulted in higher input and l ogistics costs, they also supported an
improvement in product prices across certain segmen ts. As we close the quarter, the company
reported a consolidated revenue of INR1,323 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 28%.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR111 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 158%.
Getting into some of the details, our paste PVC bu siness, we delivered a strong performance
during the quarter, with the demand peaking in Sept ember, supported by robust domestic
demand, particularly from the automotive and footwe ar sectors. Customers' buying activity
remained healthy throughout the quarter, with demand also gaining traction beyond our regular
customer base.
The limited availability of domestic material, cou pled with constrained imports, supported the
market prices. Further, customers increased their i nventory purchases amid rising prices. This
translated into a healthy sequential growth of 23% on our sales volumes.
On the regulatory front, the Madras High Court sin gle bench had directed provisional assessment

JMA/CSCors/2026-27/Dt: 12th November, 2026 The Manager National Stock Exchange of India Exchange Plaza, Plot No. C/1 G Block, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai – 400 051 Scrip Code: JMA Sub.: Outcome of the Board Meeting. Dear Sir/ Madam, This is in continuation of our intimation dated 06th November, 2026 about convening of meeting of the Board of Directors of Jullundur Motor Agency (Delhi) Limited (“the Company”) on Thursday, 12th November, 2026. Pursuant to Regulation 30, 33 and any other regulation, if applicable, of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations, 2015”) read with Part- A of Schedule III of Listing Regulations, we are pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors, in its meeting held today, viz. 12th November, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: (i) the Standalone and Consolidated Un-audited Financial Results for the Second (02nd) Quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 and taken on record Limited Review Reports thereon, issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company, copies of which are enclosed herewith as “Annexure-I”. Aforesaid approved Un-audited Financial Results together with Limited Review Reports are (ii) Proposal for Buyback of up to 20,00,000 (Twenty Lakh) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Rs. 2/- each (“Equity Shares”) from the equity shareholders of the Company as on the record date, i.e. Wednesday, November 18, 2026 (“Record Date”), at a price of Rs. 112/- (Rupees One Hundred and Twelve Only) per share for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs. 22,40,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Two Crore and Forty Lakh Only) (hereinafter referred to as the “Buy Back Size”), on a proportionate basis through the Tender Offer route (hereinafter referred to as the “Buyback”) in accordance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (“Buyback Regulations”) and the Companies Act, 2013 (the “Act”) (including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment of the Act or Buy-back Regulations, for the time being in force). The Buyback is within the statutory limit of 10% of the aggregate of the total paid-up equity share capital and free reserves of the Company based on the latest Audited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company as on March 31, 2026 through the Board approval route under Section 68(2)(b) of the Act and pursuant to the proviso to Regulation 5(i)(b) of Buy-back Regulations. This Buyback Size does not include any expenses incurred or to be incurred i.e. brokerage costs, fees, turnover charges, applicable taxes such as securities transaction tax, goods and service tax, stamp duty, any expenses incurred or to be incurred for the Buyback like filing fees payable, advisors, legal fees, intermediary fees, public announcement publication expenses, printing, dispatch expenses and other incidental and related expenses (“Transaction Cost”). JULLUNDUR MOTOR AGENCY (DELHI) LTD. The Maximum Buyback Size represents 9.77% and 8.29% of the aggregate of the total paid- up equity capital and free reserves of the Company based on the Audited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company, for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026, respectively. a. The board has constituted a Buyback Committee (the “Buyback Committee”) and has inter alia delegated its powers to the Buyback Committee to do all such acts, deeds, matters and things as it may, in its absolute discretion, deem necessary, expedient, usual or proper in connection with the Buyback. b. The Board noted the intention of the Promoter and Promoter Group of the Company, to not participate in the proposed Buyback. c. The Board has approved the appointment of Corporate Professionals Capital Private Limited, a SEBI registered Category I Merchant Banker as the Manager to the Buyback Offer, SMC Global Securities Limited as Broker to the Buyback Offer, MAS Services Limited as Registrar to the Buyback Offer and Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited as Escrow Agent to the Buyback Offer. d. In terms of Regulation 5(via) of the Buy-back Regulations, the Board / Buyback Committee may, till one working day prior to the record date, increase the Buyback price and decrease the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back, such that there is no change in the aggregate Buyback Size. e. The public announcement setting out the process, timelines and other requisite details will be released in due course in accordance with the Buyback Regulations. The dates of the Buyback offer will be mentioned in the public announcement. f. Details as required under Regulation 30 read with SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026 pertaining to the proposed Buyback are enclosed as “Annexure - II”. g. Pursuant to Regulation 42(2) of Listing Regulations and Regulation 9(i) of the Buyback Regulations, as amended, it is further notified that the Company has fixed Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as the record date for the purpose of ascertaining the eligibility of shareholders for Buyback of Equity Shares. The intimation of Record Date is attached as “Annexure III”. Board Meeting was commenced as per its scheduled time i.e. at 12:00 P.M. (12:00 hrs) and concluded at 04:35 P.M. (16:35 hrs). This is for your kind information, record and meeting the disclosures requirements as prescribed under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and Circular(s) / Notification(s) issued from time to time. JULLUNDUR MOTOR AGENCY (DELHI) LTD. JMA/CSCors/2026-27/Dt: 12th November, 2026 The Manager National Stock Exchange of India Exchange Plaza, Plot No. C/1 G Block, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai – 400 051 Scrip Code: JMA Sub.: Outcome of the Board Meeting. Dear Sir/ Madam, This is in continuation of our intimation dated 06th November, 2026 about convening of meeting of the Board of Directors of Jullundur Motor Agency (Delhi) Limited (“the Company”) on Thursday, 12th November, 2026. Pursuant to Regulation 30, 33 and any other regulation, if applicable, of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations, 2015”) read with Part- A of Schedule III of Listing Regulations, we are pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors, in its meeting held today, viz. 12th November, 2026, has inter-alia, considered and approved the following: (i) the Standalone and Consolidated Un-audited Financial Results for the Second (02nd) Quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 and taken on record Limited Review Reports thereon, issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company, copies of which are enclosed herewith as “Annexure-I”. Aforesaid approved Un-audited Financial Results together with Limited Review Reports are (ii) Proposal for Buyback of up to 20,00,000 (Twenty Lakh) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Rs. 2/- each (“Equity Shares”) from the equity shareholders of the Company as on the record date, i.e. Wednesday, November 18, 2026 (“Record Date”), at a price of Rs. 112/- (Rupees One Hundred and Twelve Only) per share for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs. 22,40,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Two Crore and Forty Lakh Only) (hereinafter referred to as the “Buy Back Size”), on a proportionate basis through the Tender Offer route (hereinafter referred to as the “Buyback”) in accordance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (“Buyback Regulations”) and the Companies Act, 2013 (the “Act”) (including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment of the Act or Buy-back Regulations, for the time being in force). The Buyback is within the statutory limit of 10% of the aggregate of the total paid-up equity share capital and free reserves of the Company based on the latest Audited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company as on March 31, 2026 through the Board approval route under Section 68(2)(b) of the Act and pursuant to the proviso to Regulation 5(i)(b) of Buy-back Regulations. This Buyback Size does not include any expenses incurred or to be incurred i.e. brokerage costs, fees, turnover charges, applicable taxes such as securities transaction tax, goods and service tax, stamp duty, any expenses incurred or to be incurred for the Buyback like filing fees payable, advisors, legal fees, intermediary fees, public announcement publication expenses, printing, dispatch expenses and other incidental and related expenses (“Transaction Cost”). JULLUNDUR MOTOR AGENCY (DELHI) LTD. The Maximum Buyback Size represents 9.77% and 8.29% of the aggregate of the total paid- up equity capital and free reserves of the Company based on the Audited Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company, for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026, respectively. a. The board has constituted a Buyback Committee (the “Buyback Committee”) and has inter alia delegated its powers to the Buyback Committee to do all such acts, deeds, matters and things as it may, in its absolute discretion, deem necessary, expedient, usual or proper in connection with the Buyback. b. The Board noted the intention of the Promoter and Promoter Group of the Company, to not participate in the proposed Buyback. c. The Board has approved the appointment of Corporate Professionals Capital Private Limited, a SEBI registered Category I Merchant Banker as the Manager to the Buyback Offer, SMC Global Securities Limited as Broker to the Buyback Offer, MAS Services Limited as Registrar to the Buyback Offer and Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited as Escrow Agent to the Buyback Offer. d. In terms of Regulation 5(via) of the Buy-back Regulations, the Board / Buyback Committee may, till one working day prior to the record date, increase the Buyback price and decrease the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back, such that there is no change in the aggregate Buyback Size. e. The public announcement setting out the process, timelines and other requisite details will be released in due course in accordance with the Buyback Regulations. The dates of the Buyback offer will be mentioned in the public announcement. f. Details as required under Regulation 30 read with SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026 pertaining to the proposed Buyback are enclosed as “Annexure - II”. g. Pursuant to Regulation 42(2) of Listing Regulations and Regulation 9(i) of the Buyback Regulations, as amended, it is further notified that the Company has fixed Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as the record date for the purpose of ascertaining the eligibility of shareholders for Buyback of Equity Shares. The intimation of Record Date is attached as “Annexure III”. Board Meeting was commenced as per its scheduled time i.e. at 12:00 P.M. (12:00 hrs) and concluded at 04:35 P.M. (16:35 hrs). This is for your kind information, record and meeting the disclosures requirements as prescribed under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and Circular(s) / Notification(s) issued from time to time. Rationale and key rating drivers
The upgrade in the rating assigned to bank facilities of Brooks Laboratories Limited (BLL) factors in significant improvement in its
liquidity and financial risk profile following receipt of funds to the tune of ₹106.33 crore from partial divestment of its stake in
Brooks Steriscience Limited. The same is expected to strengthen the company’s capital structure, reflected in improvement in its
debt coverage metrics and adjusted overall gearing levels. The resultant financial flexibility is likely to support its planned capital
expenditure requirements and provide adequate headroom for business expansion and operational growth.
The rating further factors in the substantial reduction in contingent liabilities, with the outstanding corporate guarantee exposure
reducing to ~₹48.15 crore as on the latest date from ~₹116.77 crore as on March 31, 2026.
The operating performance also witnessed improvement in FY26 (refers to April 01, 2025 to March 31, 2026 ), with the profit
before interest, lease rentals, depreciation and taxation (PBILDT) margin increasing to 8.88% from 6.03% in the previous year,
supported by a better product mix, enhanced procurement efficiencies, and higher contribution from the manufacturing segment.
Going forward, profitability is expected to remain healthy, with oper ating margins estimated in the range of 10 -11%, aided by
capacity expansion and improvement in scale of operations.
However, these strengths are constrained by the company's modest scale of operations, exposure to a highly regulated and
competitive pharmaceutical industry, and the residual corporate guarantee exposure towards associate company ’s debt. These
risks are mitigated to an extent by the company's experienced management, and established track record of operations.
CARE Ratings Limited (CareEdge Ratings) takes cognisance of the proposed demerger of the manufacturing business of BLL into
its wholly owned subsidiary, Abridge Speciality Limited (ASL). Upon implementation of the scheme and receipt of necessary
regulatory approvals, ASL will house the manufacturing business and will be renamed Brooks Laboratories Limited, while the
existing BLL entity is proposed to be renamed Xuri Lifesciences Limited or any other appropriate name approved by ROC . The
proposed demerger is expected to enhance operational focus and management oversight through segregation of business
activities. This is likely to support improved execution efficiency and strengthen the business risk profile of the respective entities
over the medium term.
Rating sensitivities: Factors likely to lead to rating actions
Positive factors
• Improvement in the scale of operations with total operating income (TOI) above ₹100 crore and profit before interest, lease
rental, depreciation and taxation (PBILDT) above 7.00%, on a sustained basis.
• Reduction in the corporate guarantee backed debt alongside investment in the associate entity, leading to adjusted overall
gearing of 1.5x on a sustained basis.
Negative factors
• Significant decline in the company’s scale of operations or profitability margins as marked by PBILDT margin below 3.50%
on a sustained basis.
• Any major debt-funded capex or increase in dependence on working capital borrowings, resulting in significant deterioration
in the capital structure and liquidity position.
Analytical approach: Standalone
Outlook: Stable
The “Stable” outlook reflects CareEdge Ratings’ expectation that the entity would continue to benefit from its experienced
promoters and established track record of operations.

Sameer Kothari: Thank you so much. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to our Q2 FY 27 earnings
conference call. Joining me on today's call are Ganesh Argekar, Executive Director , Mayank
Samdani, Group CFO, Vimal Solanki, Head Corporate Communications, and SGA, our Investor
Relations Advisor.
I trust all of you had an opportunity to review our earnings presentation, which has been
performance during the quarter, maintaining healthy growth across both Q2 and H1 FY27.
This quarter's performance was a vindication of our business model and the underlying strength
of the diversified manufacturing platform that we have built over the last few years. To illustrate,
1.5 months of operational disruption.
However, our diversification came to our rescue. Our footwear division, which had gone through
a challenging Q1 due to the raw material costs and wage pressures, returned to profitability in
Q2. Thus, in spite of some challenges in Silvassa, we managed to deliver a record adjusted PAT
of INR46 crores in Q2 FY27, registering a year-on-year growth of 22%. For the half yearly
FY27, adjusted PAT grew by 30% to INR89 crores. These kinds of situations give us the
confidence about our business model and future growth.
On the demand side, we continue to see healthy volume growth across all our verticals, supported
by a favorable demand environment. Our ongoing discussions with both existing and prospective
customers indicate encouraging growth opportunities across our business divisions. Beyond the
projects that are nearing commercialization, our broader project pipeline remains strong and
continues to expand, reflecting the opportunities available to us.
We are also investing steadily to capture this demand. In addition to the various capex going on
in many locations that Ganesh and Mayank will walk you through, we have also strengthened
our leadership team. We have now appointed dedicated business heads across all our divisions.
This gives us and the business a sharper focus and a clearer ownership as we scale.
To sum up, as our capacities ramp up, new projects come on stream and the footwear business
which is coming back on track, we believe that we are well positioned for a strong second half
of FY27 and for a sustained earnings growth into FY28 and beyond.
I'm also pleased to share that we will be hosting a Capital Markets Day in early December, where

secured at revised prices that reflects the current cost structure. Alongside that, we also improved
our raw material procurement and continue to drive efficiencies on the shop floor. As a result,
the footwear division returned to profitability in Q2 FY27.

1. We have reviewed the accompanying statement of standalone unaudited financial results of RAVI
KUMAR DISTILLERIES LIMITED ('the Company') for the quarter ended 30th September, 2026 and
the year-to-date results for the period from 1st April, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 ('the Statement'), being
submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (as amended) ('Listing Regulations'). The Statement
includes the Statement of Assets and Liabilities as at 30th September, 2026 and the Statement of Cash Flows
for the half year ended on that date.
2. The Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's management and approved by the Company's
Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid
down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, Interim Financial Reporting ('Ind AS 34'), prescribed under
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ('the Act'), and other accounting principles generally accepted in
India, and is in compliance with the presentation and disclosure requirements of Regulation 33 of the
Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE)
2410, Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity, issued
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial information consists of
making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying
analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in
accordance with the Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Act, and consequently
does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be
identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.

Basis for Qualified Conclusion
4. We draw attention to the following matters:
(a) 'Amounts recoverable under Dispute' of Rs. 2,900.25 Lakhs have been classified as 'Other Non-Current
Assets'. The Company has filed various cases against the parties and initiated action for recovery. Further,
the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), vide its Order dated 12-03-2019, directed the above
parties to repay the amounts to the Company; the appeals filed by those parties before the Securities
Appellate Tribunal are pending, with orders reserved on 08-09-2026. We are unable to comment on the
recoverability of these amounts, and no provision for Expected Credit Loss under Ind AS 109 for doubtful
recovery of such advances has been considered necessary by the Company.
(b) Investment in 'Liquors India Limited' of Rs. 825.71 Lakhs, loan to 'Liquors India Limited' of Rs.
1,640.52 Lakhs, and the amount of Rs. 1,094.00 Lakhs received from 'Lemonade Shares & Securities
Private Limited' are under dispute, and no adjustment for the sale has been incorporated in the financial
results by the Company. The sale agreement entered into with 'Lemonade Shares & Securities Private
Limited' for sale of the entire undertaking was challenged before the National Company Law Tribunal to
rectify the Register of Members. The company petition was dismissed as not maintainable, and the
Company's appeal against that order is pending before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal with
a interim stay dated 28.11.2023 by NCLAT to “maintain a status quo, as it exist today, in regard to the
disputed shares”. A civil suit (O.S. No. 103 of 2013) is pending before the XVI Additional District and
Sessions Court, Malkajgiri, Hyderabad, with prayers, inter alia, to rescind the agreement as void and restore
the parties to the position prior to the MOU dated 05-09-2012. The Company has also filed an SLP before
the Supreme Court of India, apart from complaints with the Police, SEBI and the Enforcement Directorate
Enforcement Directorate has attached 100% Shares of Liquors India Limited and Building, Plant &
Machinery held in the name of Liquors India Limited at Plot No.A-3, 4 & 10, Indutrial Development Area,
Nacharam, Hyderabad vide order dt.25.03.2026 and confirmed by Adjudicating Authority vide order
dt.07.09.2026 . Management does not anticipate any liability on this account and accordingly has not
provided for diminution in the value of the investment or for Expected Credit Loss on the loan to 'Liquors
India Limited' for the quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026. As the matter is sub judice, we
are unable to comment on whether any adjustment is needed to the carrying amounts of the investment and
the loan. Accordingly, the impact on the loss for the period and on the carrying amounts, if any, is
unascertainable.
(c) Confirmations have not been obtained as of 30th September, 2026 in respect of certain financial assets
and liabilities such as trade receivables, trade payables and balances with tie-up parties. Trade receivables
of Rs. 2,914.95 Lakhs include significant balances outstanding for more than three years, and the allowance
for expected credit loss has not been reassessed even though indications of increase in credit risk were
observed. The consequential impact on the financial results has not been ascertained by the Company.
(d) Statutory dues amounting to Rs. 314.70 Lakhs as at 30th September, 2026 (Rs. 291.15 Lakhs as at 30th
June, 2026) are pending to be deposited with the appropriate government authorities, including Tax
Collected at Source of Rs. 155.44 Lakhs collected from customers and not deposited. The Company has
not made provision for interest on account of the delay in depositing these dues. Since the management has
not estimated the overall liability on account of interest, the financial impact on the Statement is not
ascertainable.
(e) Other current financial assets include a loan of Rs. 2,544.25 Lakhs to 'S V Distilleries Private Limited',
a company in which a director of the Company is interested, on which no Expected Credit Loss has been
assessed. Further, the Company's investment in equity shares of 'S V Distilleries Private Limited' of Rs.
247.79 Lakhs is carried at cost and not measured at fair value as required by Ind AS 109, Financial
Instruments. In the absence of a credit-risk assessment and a fair valuation, we are unable to comment on
the adjustments, if any, required to these carrying amounts, and the impact on the Statement is not
ascertainable.
Qualified Conclusion
5. Based on our review conducted as above, except for the possible effects of the matters described in
paragraph 4 above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying
Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the

issued thereunder, and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the

manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.

CMD Statement – Q2 & Half-Yearly FY 2026–27 Business Update
Dear Shareholders and Stakeholders,
I hope you and your families had a joyful Diwali and a Happy New Year.
As we conclude the second quarter and first half of FY 2026–27, I extend my sincere gratitude to our
shareholders, customers, employees, bankers, vendors, business associates and all stakeholders for
their continued trust and confidence in Crown Lifters Limited.
Q2 and Half-Yearly Financial Performance
For the six months ended 30 September 2026, the Company recorded a turnover of ₹14.80 crore.
While the reported financial numbers may not fully reflect the operational efforts and strategic
progress achieved during the first half, the period invo lved significant fleet repositioning, yard
realignment, crane maintenance, disposal of older equipment and securing of long-term orders.

operations. It is important to note that the EBITDA margin from Crown -owned crane operations

overall or consolidated EBITDA margin.
Monsoon, Project Movements and Regional Disruptions
Monsoon conditions led to the idling of certain higher-tonnage cranes deployed in the green energy
sector, impacting monthly revenue by an estimated 15 –20%. Regional conflict also affected planned
export opportunities for certain older non - Chinese cranes and resulted in additional idle time for
these units.
From late September through October, several cranes were relocated between project sites, involving
additional transportation costs and mobilisation time. We expect fleet occupancy to remain steadily
above 90% over the remaining five months of FY 2026–27.
Fleet Renewal and Asset Optimisation
During Q2 and into November, we sold selected cranes that were more than 15 years old. This ongoing
fleet rationalisation has helped reduce the weighted average age of our fleet from over five years to
just over three years. It also enables us to focus on a technically upgraded fleet aligned with current
sector and customer requirements, while reducing the complexity of maintaining older models,
specialised spares and support expertise.

Yard Infrastructure and Logistics
The relocation of our parking and maintenance yards, which continued during Q2, has now been
completed. The improved arrangement will support more efficient handling, storage and movement
of cranes and accessories to and from key project sites, helping us improve mobilisation efficiency and
control costs. The second-quarter expenses also include costs incurred in shifting accessories between
the yards as part of this realignment exercise.
Fleet Expansion
From the fourth quarter of FY 2026 –27 onwards, we intend to progress the procurement of higher -
tonnage cranes along with supporting equipment, primarily for the green energy sector, with the
flexibility to deploy them in thermal power, cement, steel and refinery projects as required. These
acquisitions are expected to be funded largely through term loans and/or suitable fund -raising
initiatives. However, if fund -raising cannot be undertaken at reasonable pricing and on acceptable
terms, the Company may proceed on the strength of its balance sheet, supplemented by funding from
banks and NBFCs. The proposed procurement will remain subject to commercial evaluation, OEM
delivery schedules and financing arrangements. We will make separate announcements as and when
the arrangements are finalised.
People, Leadership and Systems
Throughout FY 2026–27, our focus will remain on consolidating and aligning our people, machines and
systems—the three core pillars of our growth. This will be an ongoing priority for the full financial year
as we strengthen our execution capabilities and prepare the organisation for its next phase of growth.
We are pleased to welcome Mr. Vinay Shetty as Chief Operating Officer . He brings over 20 years of
leadership experience across equipment rental, logistics, warehousing and supply cha in, including
senior roles at Allcargo Logistics and Supreme SCS. At Allcargo, he led pan -India operations covering
more than 500 equipment assets across 30+ locations, while at Supreme SCS he helped scale the
warehousing network to over 45 locations and 1 million sq. ft. At Crown Lifters, he will focus on
strengthening execution, improving asset utilisation, enhancing operational controls and building
scalable processes to support the Company's next phase of growth.
Operating Environment and Challenges
Margins continue to face pressure from the growing availability of imported cranes in the Indian
market, even as demand across sectors remains strong. Retaining skilled, site-based talent is another
challenge, as employees increasingly prefer opportunities cl oser to their home regions. This has
increased recruitment, retention and training costs. Our focus remains on strengthening our people
and execution capabilities to respond to the opportunities in the market.
Outlook
The demand environment across our targ et sectors remains encouraging. With expected fleet
occupancy of over 90% during the balance of the financial year, continued fleet rationalisation,

questions after the presentation concludes. Please note that this conference is being recorded.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Harsh Gosavi from Kirin Advisors Private Limited. Thank
you, and over to you, sir.
Harsh Gosavi: Good day. On the behalf of Kirin Advisors, I welcome you all to the H1 FY27 conference call
of Adisoft Technologies Limited. From the management team, we have Mr. Ajay
Chandrashekhar Prabhu, Chairman and Managing Director, Ms. CA Mayura Darvekar, Chief
Financial Officer. Now, I hand over the call to Mr. Ajay Chandrashekhar Prabhu for opening
remarks. Over to you, sir.
Ajay C. Prabhu: Thank you, sir. Good afternoon, everyone and thank you for joining us. I am Ajay
Chandrashekhar Prabhu, Chairman and Managing Director. On behalf of the management team,
I would like to welcome all our investors, analysts, and partners to Adisoft earnings call for the
first half of financial year '27.
The first half of FY27 has been a strong period for Adisoft. Growth during this half came from
a healthy demand across our customers, a richer mix of smart factory solutions, and a steady
execution across our different projects. What makes this more encouraging is that the first half
is usually our lighter part of our year, as large orders generally tend to come in the second half.
The quality of our business has also overall improved. A large share of our work is now coming
from high-value smart factory solutions, where we connect to our customers' IT systems with
their shop floors machines. As much of our design and software is developed in-house, we are
able to reuse these proven solutions across different projects, and this has supported our margins
as volumes have also grown.
Alongside our work with existing automotive customers, we are also focusing on greenfield
projects of existing as well as new automotive customers. These include automotive plants
focused primarily on manufacturing EV vehicles as well as in export vehicles. We are seeing
growing interest from other sectors such as pharmaceuticals, packaging, warehouse logistics,
and white goods. At the same time, we are also building our capabilities in robotics and machine
vision, industrial IoT, and flexibility to serve these different sectors.
To support our growth, we are building a new 70,000 square feet integrated facility at MIDC
Bhosari, Pune, and the overall work is progressing well. The facility will bring manufacturing,
engineering, software, design, assembly, and testing under one roof.
It is expected to be partially operational from the end of quarter 3 financial '27 and is designed
to support at least four to five times of our current revenue base. With the current premises nearly
operating to full capacity, it will really allow us to take on larger and more complex projects.
This half also has brought recognition for our work.
Adisoft Technologies Limited

Adisoft received five national awards from Mitsubishi Electric India, including the President's
Global Award for Industrial Digitalization Excellence, and was named the All India Number 1
Channel Partner for the third consecutive year. We also received the MSMECCII Bharat Ratna
Award 2026 and the Best Sustainable Company of the Year 2026 at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi.
Our quality management system was certified to ISO 9001:2015, and our listing on NSE Emerge
has really strengthened our visibility and governance framework.
Now, coming to our financial performance. For H1 financial year '27, on a standalone basis,
total income stood at INR73.52 crores, a growth of around 48.14% year-on-year from INR49.63
crores in H1 financial year '26.
EBITDA grew 106.17% year-on-year to INR17.05 crores, and EBITDA margin improved by
653 basis points to 23.19%. The net profit grew by around 117.89% year-on-year to INR11.57
crores, and the net profit margins improved by 504 basis points to 15.74%.
The first half has seen a really strong growth along with a clear improvement in our margins.
The demand for automation and smart factory solutions remains healthy as manufacturers across
different sectors continue to invest in productivity and quality.
As we move into the second half, traditionally our strong season, our focus will be on bringing
the Bhosari facility on stream, widening our presence in non-automotive sectors, and growing
our international projects. For the financial year '27, we are targeting a revenue growth of around
25%, a sustainable PAT margin of around 13% to 14% and a debt-free balance sheet by the end
of this financial year.
Before I close, I would like to thank our employees, customers, partners for their continued
support, and all of you for your trust in Adisoft. With that, we would be happy to take your
further questions. Thank you.

Memorandum of Association: Subject to the approval of the members, increase in

Memorandum of Association. Details are given in Annexure A.

such other statutory / regulatory approvals as may be required, sub-division of 1
(One) Equity Share of face value of ₹ 10/- (Rupees Ten only) each, fully paid-up, into

and consequential alteration of the capital clause of the Memorandum of Association.

the ratio of 5:1, i.e. 5 (Five) fully paid- up Equity Shares of face value of ₹ 5/ - each
for every 1 (One) fully paid- up Equity Share of face value of ₹ 5/ - each (post sub-

52,50,00,000/- out of the Securities Premium Account and Free re serves of the
Company, subject to the approval of the members. Details are given in Annexure C.

the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulat ions, 2018, the
number of Equity Shares to be allotted on conversion of the 8 ,40,000 outstanding
adjusted for the sub-division and the bonus issue, so that each war rant shall entitle
the holder to 12 (Twelve) Equity Shares of face value of ₹ 5/ - each, aggregating to
1,00,80,000 Equity Shares, without any change in the aggregate con sideration
payable. The Company shall reserve such number of Equity Shares out of its
Authorised Share Capital. Details are given in Annexure D.
5. Approval of Postal Ballot Notice for seeking approval of the members for items 1 to 3
above by way of Postal Ballot through remote e-voting only, with cut-off date Friday,
13th November, 2026 and appointment of Mr. Nayan Pitroda, Proprietor of M/s. Pitroda
Nayan & co., as Scrutinizer.
The Record Date for determining the members entitled to the sub-divided shares and
Listing Regulations.

During the second quarter of financial year 2027, sales of our customers were INR3,515 million,

performance should have been viewed with the context of a meaningful shift in the festive
calendar. While Navratri commenced in September during FY 2026, the festive season moved
to Q3 in FY 2027, and at the same time, the last 10 days of quarter two, this year were actually
a Shradh period.

perspective. During the first half of FY 2027, sales of our customers were at about INR7,710
million, reflecting a growth of about 2.1% over the same first half of financial year 2026.

key channels, combining social media, influencer and celebrity collaborations, and stylist

Our goal at Sigma is to make India trusted manufacturing partner to the world's leading
aerospace and defense companies, one they rely on for reliability, quality, and execution on their
most demanding programs. For years, we've been building the capacity to deliver on that. This
quarter began to show in our results.

FY27, with an operational EBITDA of INR 82.28 crores at a margin of INR 19.7 crores on a
consolidated basis. What made the quarter exceptional was the new order wins from our
acquisition, which consolidates our leading position in aerospace and wings.
It's a clear sign that the investments we've made in capability, capacity, team building, and
customer relationships are now converting to performance that you can all see. Let me take you
through the strategic developments behind these numbers.
Firstly, we strengthened our global aerospace platform. We completed the acquisition of
Bromford Precision Solutions in the UK , which has already deepened our engagement with
Rolls-Royce. Bromford and Nasmyth together give us a meaningful UK platform, which is now
integrated with our India operations.
Our facility in Sri City commenced production in September, and we've already started rolling
out parts from the facility to the UK and onwards to our customers. It will be central to our
margin improvement over time. And secondly, we advanced our position in artillery

globe. Repeat orders from international customers reflect the conf idence that they place in our

Thirdly, we expanded into control systems for homeland security apart from military. In the past,

Ahmedabad – November 12th, 2026 – Dev Information Technology Limited (DEV IT), (NSE – DEVIT, BSE
- 543462 | INE060X01034), a global IT services company offering Cloud Services, Digital Transformation,
Enterprise Applications, and Managed IT Services has reported its Unaudited financials for Q2 FY27.
Key Financial Highlights
Q2 FY27 Key Financial Highlights
• Total Income of ₹63.07 Cr
• EBITDA of ₹5.21 Cr
• EBITDA Margin of 8.26%
• Net Profit of ₹2.96 Cr
• Net Profit Margin of 4.34%
• EPS of ₹0.53
H1 FY27 Key Financial Highlights
• Total Income of ₹107.72 Cr
• EBITDA of ₹9.19 Cr
• EBITDA Margin of 8.53%
• Net Profit of ₹5.03 Cr
• Net Profit Margin of 4.50%
• EPS of ₹0.89
Commenting on the Financial Performance Mr. Pranav Pandya, Chairman, Dev Information
Technology Limited, said: “Q2 FY27 was a quarter of strong growth for DEV IT. Consolidated revenue
from operations grew 29.1% year-on-year to ₹62.63 Crore, up 41.9% sequentially. EBITDA increased 36.5%
to ₹5.21 Crore, with margins improving by 50 basis points to 8.26%. Profit before exceptional items and
tax nearly doubled to ₹4.24 Crore. For H1 FY27, revenue grew 16.7% to ₹106.76 Crore, while EBITDA rose 17.2%
to ₹9.19 Crore. Despite cautious global IT spending, our underlying operating performance strengthened.
Profit comparisons reflect a one-time exceptional gain recorded in Q2 FY26.
We continue to strengthen our capabilities across digital transformation, enterprise applications and
managed IT services while expanding our presence across government and enterprise clients. Our focus
remains on enhancing service offerings, building long -term client relationships and leveraging
emerging technologies to capture new business opportunities. During the quarter, we also onboarded a
strategic investor in our subsidiary, Dhyey Consulting Services, strengthening our Microsoft Dynamics
and Power Platform capabilities for global expansion.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on converting our strong order pipeline into revenue, improving
profitability through operating efficiencies and AI -led delivery, and expanding our presence in AI,
cybersecurity, cloud and international markets, particularl y North America. With a diversified client
base and healthy pipeline, we are confident of sustaining growth momentum through H2 FY27 and
creating long-term shareholder value.”
About Dev Information Technology Limited
Dev Information Technology Limited (DEV IT), founded in 1997, listed on NSE & BSE, and certified to ISO
20000, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 & CMMI Level 5, has evolved from a small-scale business automation software
solutions provider into a global IT services powerhouse. Over the years, the company has empowered
businesses worldwide with a blend of information technology, innovation, and digital transforma tion.
Headquartered in Ahmedabad, with offices across India and Canada, the company emphasises
continuous innovation, quality, streamlined processes, and technological prowess. The company’s people-
and client-centric approach involves collaborating with clients globally to understand their specific goals
and to empower them to achieve their business objectives.
The company offers a comprehensive end -to-end range of services, including Cloud Services, Digital
Transformation, Enterprise Applications, Managed IT Services, and Application Development. The
company’s products comprise Talligence, an accounting data analytics platform, and ByteSigner, a digital
signing solution.
With its foundation in one of India’s fastest -growing metros, the company has continuously evolved to
meet the dynamic demands of the IT industry. The leadership, comprising experienced professionals,
drives the company towards achieving its vision of empo wering businesses worldwide through cutting-
edge technology solutions. The company's steadfast commitment to innovation, quality, and client
satisfaction underpins its growth and success in the IT services sector.
In conclusion, the company remains dedicated to driving digital transformation and delivering
unparalleled value to its clients. As the company moves forward, it continues to embrace new challenges
In Consolidated FY26, the company reported Total Income of ₹193.50, EBITDA of ₹7.23 and Net Profit of
₹75.60.
