Harith Ahamed: Thank you. Good morning, everyone. This is Harith from Avendus. I'd like to welcome you all
to the 2Q FY27 earnings call of Symbiotec Pharmalab Limited hosted by Avendus. We're
pleased to have with us the management team of Symbiotec represented by Mr. Anil Satwani,
Chairman and Managing Director, and Mr. Raghavender Ramachandran, Chief Financial
Officer. We'll start with the opening remarks from management, followed by a Q&A session.
Thank you, and over to you, Anil sir.
Anil Satwani: Yes, hi, Anil Satwani this side. Good morning, happy Dhanteras, and happy Diwali to all of you.
And what an auspicious day for me to be on call with my shareholders. Thank you for joining
us on our Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings conference call today to discuss operational and financial
performance.
Today I'm joined by our CFO Raghav and by my team Shubham Saboo and Kapil Mishra from
the management team, and of course by SGA, our Investor Relations Advisors. Let me quickly
begin with the highlights of the quarter, then take you through our three business verticals and
the milestones ahead.
Raghav, our CFO, will then take you, of course, the financial performance, after which we'll be
able to or we'll be happy to take your questions. Of course, the reported revenues grew 43%
year-on-year in Q2 FY27 and 25% in H1 of FY27, and reported EBITDA grew by 88% in Q2
and 29% in H1 of FY27.
Let me now take you through these three business verticals that we operate within. First, let me
begin with our API business, which is the foundation of the company. This remains steady and
very strong, delivering 16% revenue growth in Q2 and 11% in H1 FY27, led by volume and the
product mix, of course.
We have as, you know, that we have a very distinctive global presence across the top 10 steroid
and hormonal API molecules. And this is backed up by over 60 molecules that we manufacture,
over 60 molecules that we manufacture within steroid and hormones, and 44 US FDA DMFs
that we have filed and 25 European CEPs, and we are still counting.
As I explained last quarter, our customers have qualified us as their primary API source in their
own filings. We earned their position, this position through many years of consistent supply and
compliance, and needless to say, we intend to keep earning it. It is the reason this business grows
steadily.
Our regulatory track record continues to strengthen our position. Over the last 6 months, we
have successfully completed 4 major regulatory inspections, and we have received the EIR from
Symbiotec Pharmalab Limited

Page 3 of 21
the FDA for both our Rau and Pithampur SEZ facilities, alongside our EU-GMP certification
for both sites again.
Together with our leadership in these molecules, these growth drivers and our compliance
record, we continue to remain confident in the long-term trajectory for this business. Moving
quickly to our complex injectable business vertical.
Over the years, sustained R&D and our hard work, we have built a very niche capability in
manufacturing dual-chamber vials, DCVs as we, as we say, a technology that a few companies
have taken it to commercial scale and generic and CDMO platform.
Building on this very unique differentiated platform, on 30th September we signed a long-term
agreement for the US market with a leading global company for 2 complex injectable products
using our DCV, the dual-chamber platform.
Under this agreement, Symbiotec will be responsible for development, regulatory submissions,
manufacturing, and supply, while our partners will handle commercialization and distribution in
the US market to begin with. Of course, our talks for the other market continue with the same
partner, and also we are looking at other options in other geographies.
This agreement offers three revenue streams for us, the development and regulatory milestones
that we receive over a visible period of time, revenues from the product supply eventually, likely
happening next fiscal year onwards, and share of profits on the partner sales product.
So we have these three revenue streams, the development regulatory milestones, revenue from
products, and of course the profit share. During this quarter, we invoiced the completed
milestones and received INR53 crores, and this has been recognized as revenue in Q2, and the
balance is expected to be recognized in subsequent quarters. And this shall remain consistent on
same lines for next couple of years.
Of course, we expect our DCV products to get commercialized next year in FY27-'28, as we
have already filed the first ANDA for the DCV product with FDA in September and plan to file
second in Quarter 4 this fiscal year. It is worth emphasizing here that these payments relate to
just two products and only for the US market where these two products together are having an
addressable market of around USD300 million every year.
We are pursuing similar opportunities across other products and geographies for our DCV range
of products. Important to be noted, in parallel, we are developing a dual-chamber bag for critical-
care setting, which is a ready-to-use product again which takes the same dual chamber platform
into a second format.
Remember, we have the first format as dual chamber vial, and we are ready with the proof of
concept for another dual chamber format, which is dual chamber bag. And I must also let you
know that we are currently exploring the possibility of testosterone injectable CDMO, which is
a natural extension of our global positioning in testosterone and other hormone APIs that we
have. This is under the exploratory stage.

November 06, 2026

Very quickly moving on the third vertical, which is fermentation CDMO service business. I'm
extremely delighted to confirm that we have signed a pending manufacturing agreement with a
Europe-based alternate protein company. Over the years, we have been deploying capex to build
large-scale fermentation capacity to serve these customers.
And on this agreement, we begin with the technology transfer and qualification batches at Ujjain
at our existing 100 KL scale before we build a much larger scale of 250,000 liters, 250 KL, at
our same Ujjain fermentation site. Let me also update you on the contracts we already have in
our hand.
Just to remind you, we have a 10-year take-or-pay contract with a US-based alternate protein
company. In this, the commercial batches are expected in the first quarter of FY28. We are in
the last stage of building downstream capability for this unique alternate protein for the US
company and this should start manufacturing this product commercially. We already have the
regulatory approvals in place, and this should start commercial manufacturing in Q1 of FY28.
And further, let me also update you that we already have a 5-year take-or-pay contract for insulin
drug substance, which is part of our biologics range, and we expect this to be commissioned in
Q4 of this fiscal year FY27. And the sales revenues will certainly commence mid next year '27-
'28, post our regulatory approvals.
We are almost ready with this facility. We should start validation batches sometimes quarter 4
this fiscal year, and within next 2 quarters or so, once the regulatory approvals are in place, we
should be in sales sometimes late mid next fiscal year. That's a Biologics insulin drug substance
product.
As you see, our fermentation CDMO services are not limited to biopharmaceuticals just. Our
fermentation-based development and manufacturing capabilities open up a much broader
biomanufacturing opportunity spanning across industrial biotech products including bio-based
polymers, and that widens the range of industries we can serve.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Ion Exchange
(India) Limited Q2 H1 FY2027 Earnings Conference Call , hosted by
Valorem Advisors.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen -only mode, and
there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” then “0” on
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Purvangi Jain from Valor em
Advisors. Thank you, and over to you.
Purvangi Jain: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and a very warm welcome to you
all. My name is Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. We represent the
Investor Relations of Ion Exchange (India) Limited . On behalf of the
company and Val orem Advisors, I would like to thank you all for
participating in the company's earnings conference call for the 2nd
Quarter and 1st Half of the Financial Year 2027.
Before we begin, let me mention a short cautionary statement. Some of
the statements made in today's call may be forward -looking in nature.
Such forward-looking statements are subject to risk and uncertainties
which could cause actual results to differ from those anticipated. Such
statements are based on management's belief as well as assumptions
made by and information currently available to the manage ment.
Audiences are cautioned not to place any undue reliance on these
forward-looking statements in making any investment decisions. The
purpose of today's reclassification of reporting segments and earnings
call is purely to educate and bring awareness a bout the company's
fundamental business and financial quarter under review.

Let me now introduce you to the management participating with us in
today's call and hand it over to them for their opening remarks:
We have with us Mr. Aankur Patni – Vice Chairman; Mr. Indraneel Dutt
– Managing Director and CEO; Mr. Vasant Naik – Group Chief
Financial Officer; and Ms. Nikisha Solanki – Company Secretary.
Without any further delay, I request Mr. Vasant Naik to start with his
opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Vasant Naik: Thank you, Purvangi. Good afternoon, everybody. It is a pleasure to
welcome you to the Earnings Conference Call for the 2nd Quarter and
1st Half of the Financial Year 2027.
Let me begin with an overview of the company's consolidated financial
performance.
During the 2nd quarter, on a consolidated basis, the company reported
year-on-year. The EBITDA stood at a loss of INR 848 million, while the
net loss after tax for the quarter was INR 828 million. The financial
performance for the quarter was significantly impacted by changes in
the estimated cost to complete of certain legacy projects within the
Treatment Solutions segment.
For the first half of FY 2027, the company reported operating income of
INR 13,752 million, registering a year-on-year growth of just under 4%.
EBITDA stood at a loss of INR 530 million, while the net loss after tax
for the period was INR 797 million.
Let me now briefly update you on our order book and pipeline. As of
September 30th, 2026, our engineering project order book stood at
INR 100 million from the Sri Lanka project and INR 2,630 million under
INR 29,690 million.
Page 3 of 21
In addition to our existing order book, our bid pipeline now stands at
INR 93,700 million as of September end. During the quarter, the order
inflow stood at INR 8,130 million, driven primarily by the medium -
sized opportunities and a prestigious international contract from
Hyundai Engineering and Construction Company Limited valued at
USD 52.83 million. This is for the supply of filtration units in the Middle
East with a better margin profile. Our overall enquiry bank continues to
remain steady, and we remain focused on converting these opportunities
into orders and executing our existing backlog as per the planned
schedules.
Now let us go through the quarterly segmental perform ance on a
consolidated basis. Starting with the Treatment Solutions , the segment
reported revenue of INR 1,498 million during the second quarter of the
current year compared with INR 2,958 million in the corresponding
quarter last year. The EBIT stood at a loss of INR 1,215 million
compared with a loss of INR 122 million in Q2 of FY ’25-’26. For the
first half of FY 2027, revenue stood at INR 3,597 million compared with
INR 4,797 million in the corresponding period last year, while EBIT
stood at a loss of INR 1,389 million.
As mentioned earlier, the segment performance was significantly
impacted by changes in the estimated cost to complete of certain legacy
projects. Additionally, the execution of some high -value contracts is
scheduled for the second half, while certain dispatches to the GCC
region have now been deferred to the second half due to the ongoing
Middle East crisis.
Looking ahead, considering our strong order backlog and planned
execution schedules, we expect an improvement in turnover during the
second half, accompanied by a better margin profile.
Moving to the Industrial Products segment, the segment delivered strong
year-on-year to INR 1,360 million compared with INR 1,009 million in
Q2 of FY ’26. EBIT also improved to INR 86 million from INR 74

EBIT increased to INR 210 million as against INR 124 million in the
corresponding period last year. The segment continues to witness steady

coming quarters.
Coming to the Lifecycle Services, the segment recorded sequential

’26, while EBIT was INR 59 million. For the first half of FY ’27,
revenue increased to INR 1,422 million as against INR 1,329 million in

Moving to the Specialty Chemicals, the segment recorded an

quarter last year, and the EBIT stood at INR 225 million. For the first
INR 4,843 million compared with INR 4,070 million in first half of FY

The margins in this segment continue to remain under pressure due to
the input cost inflation arising from the higher RM cost due to the West
Asia crisis, along with the facility cost associ ated with our Roha plant.
We have taken steps for passing on the cost increases to the customers,
and it is now getting increased success, which will reflect in improved
margins in the coming months. Our offtake from our resin
manufacturing facility at Roha is gradually picking up, and we expect
the facility to contribute to the segment growth in the coming months.
Coming to the Consumer Product segment, it continues to deliver strong

We are continuing to invest in this business with the objective of scaling
up operations and building a signifi cantly larger revenue base. Beyond
our core segments, our advanced digital solution offerings are receiving
an encouraging response, and we believe this business can contribute
positively to our services segment in the coming months.

On our last call, we had indicated that quarter two would carry a larger inflationary impact than

growth. We are pleased to share that the quarter has delivere d on both counts. The company
reported revenue from operations of INR 630.5 crores, our highest -ever quarterly revenue, a

grew 21.2% and PAT grew 25.4%. With profits growing meaningfully faster than revenue,
sustaining this through two consecutive quarters of rising inflation, we believe the clearest
evidence that the pricing discipline and cost culture we have built are now part of how company
operates.
In Q2, our biscuit business, both domestic and exports, grew in the low teens, excluding
agencies, while our bakery business sustained its strong momentum with high-teens growth. The
quarter was more challenging than we had anticipating. A below -normal monsoon weighed on
rural sentiment, while sharp food inflation squeezed household budgets. Despite this, domestic
demand remained resilient, led by our premium and value-added portfolio, modern trade, quick
commerce, and a continued recovery in the institutional business.
Barring a further escalation in the West Asia conflict or a sharper turn in food inflation, we
remain optimistic about the second half, supported by the festive season, our innovation pipeline,
and sustained brand investments. Internationally, shipping conditions became more difficult
during the quarter. The West Asia situation sharply impacted vessel availability and freight rates,

the business for the long term. We welcome the opportunity to speak with you, explain our
performance and business strategy, and answer your questions.
Before I begin, please note that some of the statements we make today may be forward-
looking. They are based on our current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties,
so actual results may differ. Q2 and H1 FY 2027 performance.
Standalone financial highlights.
We delivered strong growth this quarter and in the six months.
Revenue from operations grew 17% for the quarter and 35% for the six months, and the profit
before tax grew 39% and 24% respectively year-on-year. Revenue from operations for the
quarter is INR 1,457 crores and INR 3,010 crores for the six months. Including other income,
total income is INR 1,521 crores for the quarter and INR 3,106 crores for the six months.
Order booking for the six months is excellent at INR 4,844 crores, and standalone orders in
hand as on September 30, 2026 are at an all-time high of INR 8,757 crores. Execution is
proceeding well in both the industrial projects and manufacturing segments. Export revenue
during the quarter is INR 172 crores, about 11% of total income, compared to INR 90 crores in
the same quarter last year.
Export revenue during the first half of the year is INR 557 crores, about 18% of total income,
up from INR 425 crores in H1 FY26. We expect exports to remain a significant share of our

revenue, though the quarterly share will vary with shipping timings. Profit before tax for the
quarter ended September 2026 was INR 154 crores, up 39% from INR 111 crores for the

These figures include the effect of transactions with our subsidiary companies, dividends
received, interest income on loans given to them, foreign exchange movements on those loans,
and the related expected credit loss provisions. In our investor presentation uploaded on the
stock exchanges today, Slide Number 19 shows profit from business operations, which
excludes these subsidiary-related items.
Accordingly, profit from business operations for the quarter is INR 124 crores compared to
INR 90 crores in the quarter ended September 2025, an increase of 38%. For the six months
ended September 2026, reported profit before tax of INR 277 crores is 24% higher than INR
223 crores for the six months ended September 2025.
On a similar basis, considering only the profit from business operations and excluding the
impact of transactions with subsidiary companies, the profit from business operations for the
six months ended September 2026 is INR 244 crores compared to INR 169 crores for the six
months ended September 2025. That is an increase of 44%.
On the margin front, manufacturing EBIT margin for the quarter is 13.7%, better than the 12%
to 13% range we guided. EBIT margin for the project business is 5.7%, better than the last few
years and close to our target of 6%. The domestic market is strong across all our product lines,
and we also have a healthy level of export inquiries from customers in Latin America and
Africa.
The company's standalone fund position improved by INR 175 crores during the six months,
and net borrowings fell to INR 206 crores compared to INR 381 crores as on March 31, 2026.
As you know, the company is investing about INR 502 crores to expand capacity for our
manufacturing segment. This net borrowing of INR 206 crores is after cumulative capital
expenditure of INR 199 crores for this capital investment, which has been funded from internal
accruals.
Impact of geopolitical tensions on our business:
Current geopolitical developments have not affected order booking or order execution.
However, the cost of some materials has risen because of the ongoing conflicts in the Middle
East, and this is having a small adverse effect on profitability. During the quarter, commodity
prices, particularly steel, copper, aluminium, and nickel, skewed up to 10% fluctuation, though
they have come down slightly in October.
Shipping and logistics for exports and imports have seen delays, reduced availability of ships
and containers, and sharply higher freight rates and surcharges. The good news is that there has
been no significant supply disruption. Most of the increased costs are expected to be absorbed
through normal contingency provisions.

I would like to point out that this conference may contain forward -looking

Shilp Chotai: Thank you so much. Good evening, everyone, and a warm welcome to Gayatri
Rubbers and Chemicals Limited's H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call.
Thank you all for joining us today. The first half of FY27 has been a strong
period for GRCL, marked by robust financial growth, improved operational
performance, and significant progress in expanding our presence across high -
value sectors. We recorded tot al income of ₹27.52 crore, registering year -on-
year growth of 58.75%.
Our EBITDA increased by 60.91% to ₹6.46 crore, with EBITDA margins
improving by 32 basis points to 23.48%. Profit after tax grew by 54.21% to ₹4.06
crore, reflecting the strength of our operating model as we continue to scale our
business.
From a business standpoint, we have made meaningful progress in strengthening
our position as a critical supplier to Indian Railways. As a Class I supplier, we
manufacture 65 out of 75 rubber products required for a single railway coach.
During the first half, we secured twin purchase orders worth ₹4.53 crore from
Indian Railways for specialised rubber -with-metal components, with execution
scheduled through May 2027.
Our specialised railway product portfolio, including UIC vestibules and
decoupling rubber, further strengthens our capabilities in this segment. Beyond
railways, we have continued to expand our customer base and sectoral presence.
We were onboarded as an o fficial vendor to KSRTC, that is, Karnataka State

Road Transport Corporation, receiving our first order worth ₹1.3 crore for
EPDM rubber glazing for their state road buses.
We also secured a pilot order for specialised EPDM rubber components from
ISRO, marking an important milestone in our entry into the aerospace and space
sector. Alongside these developments, we continue to serve customers such as
BEML and maintain our esta blished presence in the smart meter, industrial,
automotive, and architectural segments.
We are also a single-source vendor to leading listed players such as Genus Power
and HPL Power in the smart meter industry. On the operational front, our two
manufacturing facilities in Faridabad, Haryana, continue to provide a strong
foundation for growth. Plant 1, with an installed capacity of 200 metric tonnes
2, dedicated to specialised railway products, is operating at around 35%
utilisation.
This provides us with significant headroom to increase production and cater to
additional manufacturing infrastructure for current operations. Looking ahead,
our growth story is centred around three key priorities: maximising the utilisation
of our existing facilities, expanding into adjacent product categories, and
entering new high-barrier markets.
We are actively working on opportunities in bridge pads, railway pads, and
specialised rubber pipes, with supplies in the pipe segment expected to
commence in the first half of 2027. We are also progressing towards
opportunities in gas and water meter applications, where our prototype has been
accepted by Genus.
Our medium -term objective is to increase the utilisation of our existing
manufacturing facilities towards 90% to 95% while gradually expanding our
product portfolio and customer base. At GRCL, our focus remains on moving
beyond conventional rubber manufact uring towards becoming a trusted,
technology-driven partner for critical applications across infrastructure and
industrial sectors.
We believe our established railway credentials, growing customer relationships,
and expanding product capabilities position us well to capture the opportunities
ahead. With this, I would like to thank all our shareholders, investors, and
stakeholders for t heir continued confidence in the company. I now invite
everyone to share their questions, and we would be happy to address them during

our Q2 and H1 FY27 earning call, so I'll take you through the journey. So, our operating
performance for the quarter, the progress on our strategic projects, our financial results for
quarter two and first half, and our outlook for the rest of the financial year of 27. So Q2
financial year 27 was a quarter of volume recovery. Installed production capacity for the
quarter was around 20,993 metric tons, and volume rose to around 14,798 metric tons, taking
capacity utilization to around 70%, up from 62% in Q1 FY27 to 62% in Q2 FY26. volumes
grew 21% year-on-year and 14% quarter-on-quarter, with year-on-year growth of all three
product categories. For the first half, volumes stood at 27,789 metric ton at an average
utilization of about 66%. Importantly, unit economics remains well ahead of last year and
Q2 FY26, and from 10,082 in Q2 FY25. So average realization was about 1.61 lakh per ton, up
by 22% year-on-year basis. reflecting our pricing, product mix, and the pass-through of raw
material cost to the customers. Coming to the strategic developments, so our expansion in
Kutch is progressing as planned. We are investing about 20 to 25 crores in a new facility
with a capacity of about 10,000 IBCs per month, which is expected to be commissioned by
March 2027. This facility will strengthen our presence in Kutch and Western India while
providing logical benefits through lower freight cost, faster deliveries, and improved
customer service. The CAPEX will be deployed in line with actual demand, and once
commissioned, the plant will add to the operating leverage of our existing network. So, we
have also received government subsidy approvals for our WADA and BHARUCH facilities,
crore for BHARUCH. We expect to receive the WADA sanction by March 2027 and
BHARUCH application for sanction will be filed in the next phase. These incentives will
effectively reduce the cost of our investments, support cash generation, and improve project
Pyramid Technoplast Limited
economics, ROC, and payback over the long term. Our WADA facility is in full swing across
SDP drums, IBCs, and MS drums. And we expect overall utilization to reach around 80%
during this financial year. The focus now is to sustain this production and extract further
operating leverage from the infrastructure already created. Our green energy initiatives are
also contributing meaningfully. The 6-megawatt solar plant and 2.25 megawatt in
Maharashtra were commissioned in October 2025, followed by an additional 5 megawatt in
Bharuch in February 2026, with further 1 megawatt at Bharuch plant in next phase. We have
full 14.25-megawatt capacity is expected to deliver around 15 crores for annual savings. The
total investment in our solar project is at 60 crores. So about four years is the payback, what
we are estimating. Similarly, our recycling plant commissioned in October 2025 was set up
with an investment of around 8 to 10 crore and an expected payback of about 2 to 3 years.
The plant generated 33 lakhs of EBITDA in Q2 FY27 and we estimate its FY27 EBITDA
contribution at around 2 crores. Beyond the savings, the facility reduced plastic waste and
strengthened our ESG credentials also, in line with India's sustainability agenda. On the
financial front, our revenue grew by 48% year-on-year to Rs. 238 crores in Q2 FY27, and total
income, including other income, was around Rs. 238.8 crore. Growth was driven by both
higher realizations, up by 22% per ton, and higher volume, up 21%. Of the $77 crore increase
in revenue, improved realization contributed about $43.6 crore. Volume and product growth
about $24.9 crore, and trading income about $8.7 crore. Polymer drum tonnage rose 5% year-
on-year basis, and 16% quarter-on-quarter. IBC units grew 17% year-on-year basis and MS
Drums tonnage grew 73% year-on-year basis. Our value-added IBC business contributed
about 32% of the revenue in this quarter Q2 FY27.
Our customer base remains well diversified with over 500 customers. Our top customer
accounts for about 6% of the revenue and our top 10 customers together for about 29%. On
the front of GP, gross profit rose about 28% year on year, 55.3 crore. while gross margin
remained at 23% as raw metal cost rose in step with price increases.
EBITDA grew 61% year-on-year to Rs. 20.3 crore with margins at 8.5% compared with 7.8%
in Q2 FY26. Cost discipline supported this. Operating expenditure, including raw material,
rose about 14% year-on-year against revenue growth of 48%.
And employee costs were broadly flat at 6.2%. So, PAT grew by 54% on year-on-year basis
to 9.5%, with margins at about 4%. PBT rose 53% to 12.5%, even as finance cost. has
increased by 147% year-on-year basis and depreciation by 37% year-on-year basis increased
with the expanded capacity and the solar investment.
For the first half, revenue grew 42% year-on-year to $460.5 crore. By segment, polymer
drums contributed about $204 crore, IBC about $150 crore, MS drum about $64 crore, and
other operating income about $42 crore. Gross profit rose 23% to 106.7 crore, and EBITDA
grew 55% to 41.6 crore with margins improving to 9% from 8.2% and PAT grew by 42% to
improve EBITDA margins towards 11% to 12%.
With H1 revenue up to 42%, we are well ahead on growth. On margins, H1 stood at 9%, up

from 8.2% a year ago, and we expect four levers to drive further improvement in the second
half. Higher utilization, full benefit of capital solar savings, a growing contribution from the
recycling plant, and operating leverage and product mix and model. We continue to follow a
disciplined approach to capital allocation with the major phase of capacity and efficiency
investments now behind us.

filling that capacity and converting it into stronger earnings and revenue group and returns.

This is to inform you that the Board of Directors (“Board”) of the Company at its meeting held on November 12,
2026, which commenced at 10.00 a.m. and concluded at 4:00 p.m., inter-alia, has considered and approved the
following:
1) The proposal for Buy Back of up to 6,59,34,065 (Six Crores Fifty Nine Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand Sixty Five)
fully paid-up equity shares of face value ₹ 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company (“Equity Shares”) of an
amount not exceeding ₹ 6000 Million (Rupees Six Thousand Million only) (“Buy Back Size”), being 7.22% and
6.61% of the aggregate of the total paid-up Equity Share capital and free reserves of the Company based on the
latest standalone and consolidated audited financial statements of the Company respectively as at
March 31, 2026, which is within the limit of 10% of the aggregate of the total paid up equity share capital and
free reserves (including securities premium) of the Company under the Board approval route as per the
Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made thereunder (“Companies Act”) and the Securities and Exchange Board
of India (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (as amended) (“SEBI Buy Back Regulations”), at a buy back
price of ₹ 91/- (Rupees Ninety One only) per Equity Share (“Buy Back Price”), payable in cash, from the
shareholders/beneficial owners of the Equity Shares of the Company as on the record date given below,
through the “tender offer” route, on a proportionate basis as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back Regulations
provided that 15% (fifteen percent) of the number of Equity Shares which the Company proposes to Buy Back
or number of Equity Shares entitled as per the shareholding of small shareholders as on the Record Date,
whichever is higher, shall be reserved for the small shareholders as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations (hereinafter referred to as the “Buy Back”).
2) The Buy Back size does not include transaction costs viz. brokerage costs, fees, turnover charges, taxes such as
securities transaction tax and goods and services tax (if any), tax on distributed income on Buy Back, stamp
duty, advisors fees, filing fees, public announcement expenses, printing and dispatch expenses, if any, and
other incidental and related expenses and charges etc.
3) The Board has also constituted a committee for the purpose of the Buy Back (“Buy Back Committee”) and has
delegated its powers to the Buy Back Committee to do or cause to be done all such acts, deeds, matters and
things, in its discretion, deemed necessary in connection with the Buy Back.
4) Pursuant to Regulation 42 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with Regulation 9(i) of the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations, the Board has fixed Wednesday, November 25, 2026, as the Record Date for the purpose of
determining the entitlement and the names of equity shareholders who are eligible to participate in the Buy
Back.
5) The Board/Buy Back Committee may, till 1 (one) working day prior to the Record Date, increase the Buy Back
Price and decrease the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back under the Buy Back, such that
there is no change in the Buy Back Size, in terms of Regulation 5(via) of the SEBI Buy back Regulations.
6) The Board has noted the intention of the Promoters and members of the Promoter Group of the Company not
to participate in the proposed Buy Back.
7) Ms. Sangeeta Shetty, Chief Compliance Officer and Company Secretary, has been appointed as the Compliance
Officer for the purpose of the Buy Back. Emkay Global Financial Services Limited, a SEBI registered merchant
banker, has been appointed as the Manager to the Buy Back.
The public announcement and other documents in relation to the Buy Back setting out the process, record date,
timelines and other requisite details will also be released in due course in accordance with the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations.

creating sustainable long-term value for all our stakeholders.
Let me now begin with a brief overview of our business. Veegaland developers is a part of the
broader V-Guard Group, a business group with a legacy dating back to 1977. Since commencing
our real estate operations, we have focused on the developing focused on developing quality
residential communities across Kerala.
Today, our presence extends across four key markets - namely Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram,
Kozhikode, and Thrissur. Our portfolio spans multiple customer segments from mid -premium
and premium housing to our lux e offering. This allows us to address the broad range of
homebuyer requirement while remaining focused on the Kerala residential market.
Our approach has always been centered on the understanding local customer preferences,
selecting appropriate locations, and delivering homes that combine quality, functionality, and
thoughtful design. One of the key differentiators of Veegaland is our concept of biophilic urban
homes. We believe that homes should offer more than just living space, they should provide an
environment that promotes well-being and brings residents closer to nature even within the urban
city.
This philosophy is reflected in the way we approach our projects through landscaped green
spaces, natural light, ventilation, and incorporation of su itable features such as rainwater

Ref: Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”)
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors (“Board”) of the Company at its meeting held on November 12,
2026, which commenced at 10.00 a.m. and concluded at 4:00 p.m., inter-alia, has considered and approved the
following:
1) The proposal for Buy Back of up to 6,59,34,065 (Six Crores Fifty Nine Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand Sixty Five)
fully paid-up equity shares of face value ₹ 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company (“Equity Shares”) of an
amount not exceeding ₹ 6000 Million (Rupees Six Thousand Million only) (“Buy Back Size”), being 7.22% and
6.61% of the aggregate of the total paid-up Equity Share capital and free reserves of the Company based on the
latest standalone and consolidated audited financial statements of the Company respectively as at
March 31, 2026, which is within the limit of 10% of the aggregate of the total paid up equity share capital and
free reserves (including securities premium) of the Company under the Board approval route as per the
Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made thereunder (“Companies Act”) and the Securities and Exchange Board
of India (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (as amended) (“SEBI Buy Back Regulations”), at a buy back
price of ₹ 91/- (Rupees Ninety One only) per Equity Share (“Buy Back Price”), payable in cash, from the
shareholders/beneficial owners of the Equity Shares of the Company as on the record date given below,
through the “tender offer” route, on a proportionate basis as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back Regulations
provided that 15% (fifteen percent) of the number of Equity Shares which the Company proposes to Buy Back
or number of Equity Shares entitled as per the shareholding of small shareholders as on the Record Date,
whichever is higher, shall be reserved for the small shareholders as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations (hereinafter referred to as the “Buy Back”).
2) The Buy Back size does not include transaction costs viz. brokerage costs, fees, turnover charges, taxes such as
securities transaction tax and goods and services tax (if any), tax on distributed income on Buy Back, stamp
duty, advisors fees, filing fees, public announcement expenses, printing and dispatch expenses, if any, and
other incidental and related expenses and charges etc.
3) The Board has also constituted a committee for the purpose of the Buy Back (“Buy Back Committee”) and has
delegated its powers to the Buy Back Committee to do or cause to be done all such acts, deeds, matters and
things, in its discretion, deemed necessary in connection with the Buy Back.
4) Pursuant to Regulation 42 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with Regulation 9(i) of the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations, the Board has fixed Wednesday, November 25, 2026, as the Record Date for the purpose of
determining the entitlement and the names of equity shareholders who are eligible to participate in the Buy
Back.
5) The Board/Buy Back Committee may, till 1 (one) working day prior to the Record Date, increase the Buy Back
Price and decrease the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back under the Buy Back, such that
there is no change in the Buy Back Size, in terms of Regulation 5(via) of the SEBI Buy back Regulations.
6) The Board has noted the intention of the Promoters and members of the Promoter Group of the Company not
to participate in the proposed Buy Back.
7) Ms. Sangeeta Shetty, Chief Compliance Officer and Company Secretary, has been appointed as the Compliance
Officer for the purpose of the Buy Back. Emkay Global Financial Services Limited, a SEBI registered merchant
banker, has been appointed as the Manager to the Buy Back.
The public announcement and other documents in relation to the Buy Back setting out the process, record date,
timelines and other requisite details will also be released in due course in accordance with the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations.
The Pre-Buy Back shareholding of the Company as on November 6, 2026 is annexed as ‘Annexure A’. Further, the
post Buy Back shareholding of the Company will be provided upon completion of the Buy Back.
A detailed disclosure as required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the SEBI Master
Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026 is enclosed as ‘Annexure B’.
A copy of the press release which is being issued in this regard is also enclosed as ‘Annexure – C’.
Kindly take the above on record.

Investor Release
Commenting on the performance, Mr. M V Reddy, Managing Director, Astra Microwave
Products Limited, said
“H1 FY27 has been a strong first half for Astra. Our EBITDA and PAT for the half year are the
highest we have ever reported, both in absolute terms as well as margins. Standalone revenues
for H1FY27 reported were Rs.437 crores, with EBITDA of Rs.120 crores at a 27.4% margin and PAT
of Rs. 57 crores at a 13.0% margin. This healthy performance was driven by a favourable product
mix, led by execution of domestic defence production orders, alongside better control of
operating expenses.
As of September 30, 2026, our standalone order book stood at Rs. 3,937 crores and our
consolidated order book at Rs. 4,708 crores. The order book now has a larger share of production
orders for indigenous radar and electronic warfare platforms. These programmes typically run
over several years with follow-on requirements, and together with repeat orders in software-
defined radios, they give us strong revenue visibility and a clear runway for growth.
We remain focused on strengthening our position in India’s defence and aerospace ecosystem
through indigenous product development, deeper technological capabilities and expansion into
new opportunities, including exports of radar, electronic warfare and software-defined radio
systems to friendly nations. We will keep investing in R&D and production capacity to stay ahead
of this demand, and we remain committed to our long-term aspirations.”
About Astra Microwave Products Limited
Astra Microwave Products Limited (Astra) was incorporated in 1991 by a team of distinguished
scientists with experience in RF/Microwave/Digital electronics and management of projects with
high technology content. The company has grown substantially since inception with continuous
investments in infrastructure, captive test facilities and other resources.
The company has various certificates such as AS9100D & BS EN ISO 9001:2015,
ISO27001:2013, ISO9001:2015, ISO14001:2015, ISO45001:2018, ISO/IEC17025:2017. The
company’s product portfolio spans across Defence, Aerospace & Space Electronics systems,
sub-systems and components. Astra has 3 Automatic assembly lines for PCB Assembly, 7 Class
10K cleanrooms & 1 Class 100K clear room. The RF & Microwave Test Instruments &
infrastructure extends from 30MHz up to 40GHz. In-house Environment test facilities including
EMI/EMC facility and a first for any Indian Private Industry-Near Field Antenna test and
measurement range. Starting with a diverse range of microwave products like filters,
transmitters, receivers, antennas etc., the company has produced, developed & supplied space-
chain and has supplied multiple Systems to various end users in Defence, Aerospace &
Metrology segment.

Hemant Mondkar: Thank you so much. Good morning everyone. A very warm welcome to all our investors and
stakeholders. We are pleased to share that the second quarter of FY27 has been a very strong
quarter for the company with healthy growth in revenues and a meaningful imp rovement in
profitability compared to the previous quarter.
This performance reflects the strength of our existing business, our long -standing relationships
with leading OEMs, and our continued focus on operational efficiency. During the quarter, our
revenue from operations grew by 32% year on year to INR60.9 croress, reflecting healthy
demand and continued business momentum.
We are particularly encouraged by the strong sequential performance, with revenue growing
41% over the previous quarter, demonstrating the underlying strength of our business and
improving operating momentum. As you know, Hy -Tech has built a strong positio n in the
hydraulic fittings industry over more than four decades.
Our integrated manufacturing capabilities, wide product portfolio of nearly 11,000 SKUs, and
ability to deliver high -quality precision components have helped us establish ourselves as a
trusted supplier to leading OEMs. Our focus remains on strengthening this core business while
expanding our presence across international markets and higher-value industrial applications.
Coming to the business outlook, we continue to see significant opportunities in our existing
hydraulic fitting business. Our strategy is to increase our share of business with existing
customers, onboard new OEMs, and expand our presence across the international manufacturing
locations of our customers.

supported by our established customer relationships and competitive manufacturing capabilities.
To further strengthen our US presence, we have established a wholl y-owned subsidiary and a
warehouse in New Jersey. This will bring us closer to our customers, improve engagement, and
enable faster and more efficient supply chain support. We believe this initiative will strengthen
our positioning in the US market and support our long-term international growth ambitions.
Alongside our core business, we are also strengthening our product portfolio through the
development of stainless steel double ferrule fittings. We see attractive opportunities in these
segments as demand for specialized, high-quality engineering components continues to evolve.
Our existing manufacturing expertise and engineering capabilities provide us with a strong
foundation to address these requirements and gradually expand into these higher -value
applications.
I would like to emphasize that our core hydraulic fitting business will continue to remain the
primary growth engine, while these new applications provide additional opportunities to expand
our addressable market. We continue to invest in capacity expansio n, automation, and
technological upgradation to support our goal plans.
Our investments in automated machinery, including rotary transfer machines, are helping us
improve productivity, manufacturing speed, and operational efficiency. We will continue to
focus on building capacities ahead of demand while ensuring disciplined ca pital allocation and
healthy returns on our investments.
Looking ahead, we remain confident about the growth prospects of Hy -Tech Engineers. Our

Sub: Outcome of the Board Meeting held on November 12, 2026
Ref: Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”)
This is to inform you that the Board of Directors (“Board”) of the Company at its meeting held on November 12,
2026, which commenced at 10.00 a.m. and concluded at 4:00 p.m., inter-alia, has considered and approved the
following:
1) The proposal for Buy Back of up to 6,59,34,065 (Six Crores Fifty Nine Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand Sixty Five)
fully paid-up equity shares of face value ₹ 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company (“Equity Shares”) of an
amount not exceeding ₹ 6000 Million (Rupees Six Thousand Million only) (“Buy Back Size”), being 7.22% and
6.61% of the aggregate of the total paid-up Equity Share capital and free reserves of the Company based on the
latest standalone and consolidated audited financial statements of the Company respectively as at
March 31, 2026, which is within the limit of 10% of the aggregate of the total paid up equity share capital and
free reserves (including securities premium) of the Company under the Board approval route as per the
Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made thereunder (“Companies Act”) and the Securities and Exchange Board
of India (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (as amended) (“SEBI Buy Back Regulations”), at a buy back
price of ₹ 91/- (Rupees Ninety One only) per Equity Share (“Buy Back Price”), payable in cash, from the
shareholders/beneficial owners of the Equity Shares of the Company as on the record date given below,
through the “tender offer” route, on a proportionate basis as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back Regulations
provided that 15% (fifteen percent) of the number of Equity Shares which the Company proposes to Buy Back
or number of Equity Shares entitled as per the shareholding of small shareholders as on the Record Date,
whichever is higher, shall be reserved for the small shareholders as prescribed under the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations (hereinafter referred to as the “Buy Back”).
2) The Buy Back size does not include transaction costs viz. brokerage costs, fees, turnover charges, taxes such as
securities transaction tax and goods and services tax (if any), tax on distributed income on Buy Back, stamp
duty, advisors fees, filing fees, public announcement expenses, printing and dispatch expenses, if any, and
other incidental and related expenses and charges etc.
3) The Board has also constituted a committee for the purpose of the Buy Back (“Buy Back Committee”) and has
delegated its powers to the Buy Back Committee to do or cause to be done all such acts, deeds, matters and
things, in its discretion, deemed necessary in connection with the Buy Back.
4) Pursuant to Regulation 42 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with Regulation 9(i) of the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations, the Board has fixed Wednesday, November 25, 2026, as the Record Date for the purpose of
determining the entitlement and the names of equity shareholders who are eligible to participate in the Buy
Back.
5) The Board/Buy Back Committee may, till 1 (one) working day prior to the Record Date, increase the Buy Back
Price and decrease the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back under the Buy Back, such that
there is no change in the Buy Back Size, in terms of Regulation 5(via) of the SEBI Buy back Regulations.
6) The Board has noted the intention of the Promoters and members of the Promoter Group of the Company not
to participate in the proposed Buy Back.
7) Ms. Sangeeta Shetty, Chief Compliance Officer and Company Secretary, has been appointed as the Compliance
Officer for the purpose of the Buy Back. Emkay Global Financial Services Limited, a SEBI registered merchant
banker, has been appointed as the Manager to the Buy Back.
The public announcement and other documents in relation to the Buy Back setting out the process, record date,
timelines and other requisite details will also be released in due course in accordance with the SEBI Buy Back
Regulations.
The Pre-Buy Back shareholding of the Company as on November 6, 2026 is annexed as ‘Annexure A’. Further, the
post Buy Back shareholding of the Company will be provided upon completion of the Buy Back.
A detailed disclosure as required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the SEBI Master
Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026 is enclosed as ‘Annexure B’.
A copy of the press release which is being issued in this regard is also enclosed as ‘Annexure – C’.
Kindly take the above on record.
Yours truly,
For Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited
Sangeeta Shetty
Company Secretary

I now hand the conference over to Kavish Parekh from 360 ONE Capital Market. Thank you,

Kavish Parekh: Good afternoon, everyone. I would like to welcome the management and thank them for this
opportunity. We have with us today Mr. Vikram Mehra, Managing Director, Mr. Abhishek
Kapoor, CFO, and Mr. Pankaj Kedia, Executive Director, Investor Relations.
I shall now hand over the call to the management for the opening remarks. Over to you.
Vikram Mehra: Good afternoon to everyone. This quarter, our revenue from operations was INR3,143 million,
with year-on-year growth of 37%. Our adjusted EBITDA was INR1,180 million, with year-on-
year growth of 39%, and operational PBT was INR858 million, with year-on-yea r growth of
43%.
Our quarterly numbers look very healthy, but on behalf of the entire management, I would once
again reiterate: please evaluate our performance only on a rolling 12-month basis. Music is the
first vertical of ours. Global recorded music grew to USD31.7 billion in 2025, according to IFPI.
India has just a 1% share of that.
In spite of housing over 18% of the world population, we in India are operating in the most
under-penetrated large music market on earth. And our entire strategy at Saregama is built
around this next 20-year opportunity in front of us.
On a quarterly basis, the overall music vertical, comprising licensing, artist management, and
retail, recorded revenue of INR2,513 million, registering 35% year-on-year growth. Quarterly
EBITDA stood at INR1,540 million with 37% year-on-year growth and quarterly net margin at
INR1,165 million with 46% year-on-year growth.
The music vertical had a low base in the first half of Financial Year 2026, which has helped us
achieve such strong growth in this financial year. On a short-to-medium-term basis, we maintain
our guidance of 20% to 23% CAGR for the music vertical revenue.
On profitability, we had stated in Financial Year 2024 that it would take us 2 to 3 years before
the growth in EBITDA and profits begins to follow the revenue growth trajectory. We are
entering that cycle now, where content that was bought 2, 3 or 4 years ago is starting to contribute
positive margins.
The first half of this year had greater focus on non-film music, like the I -Pop Star albums in
Hindi and Tamil, which threwmultiple songs that trended on YouTube and Instagram. There
were also very strong-performing Haryanvi and Bihari songs, and Punjabi s uperstar Nijjar’s
album.
Saregama India Limited
November 04, 2026
Page 3 of 17
global number one position on YouTube’s daily music video charts during this quarter.
The second half of the year will focus more on the movie albums, prominent ones being Sanjay
Leela Bhansali's Love & War, Sivakarthikeyan's Seyon, Dharma's Kartik Aaryan starrer
Naagzilla, and a Tiger Shroff movie, which is being produced by Sanjay Leela Bhansali.
Our spend on new content this year will be between INR300 crores and INR350 crores. As
shared earlier, going forward, we will be increasing our content budgets at a nominal level, say
10% per annum. So, assuming Financial Year 2027 spends at the midpoint of INR325 crores,
we are looking at new content spends of around INR1,200 crores over the three financial years
from Financial Year 2028 to 2030.
Another data point worth sharing. In Financial Year 2026, 60% of all music revenue of Saregama
came from music which was released post-2000. So while we at Saregama proudly steward the
musical heritage of India, we are now a new -age IP company with a large part of our revenue
coming from brand-new IP.
We continue with the guidance of a 5-year payback period for all new music bought, followed
by 55 to 75 years of returns coming from that music. Music catalog is increasingly treated
globally as an infrastructure-light, inflation-linked asset class, which is why institutional capital
is now flowing into this space either through JVs or direct catalog purchases.
Our 180,000-plus song catalog, growing by 4,500 to 5,000 new releases every year, is exactly
the kind of asset that compounds value over decades. Let's spend a moment on subscription. The
push from digital platforms like Spotify, YouTube, JioSaavn to build paid subscription revenues
continues, with labels working proactively alongside them to accelerate this process. We have
already started seeing results from these initiatives.
A recent Indian consumer study done by EY and IMI stated that 64% of free music customers
are ready to shift to a reasonably priced paid service if the free service stops. As a company, we
continue with our bullish position on subscription growth in the country. Globally, the music
industry is now growing on both paid subscribers and pricing.
If we see Universal and Spotify's latest quarter results, even after so many years, subscription
revenue is still growing steadily for both Spotify, which is a platform, and Universal, which is a
label. In India, the growth is still coming entirely from ne w subscribers. So we have only one
trigger for growth, which is the addition of new subscribers. Pricing is the second growth engine
that is still ahead of us, which will start kicking in, hopefully, 2 to 3 years from now.
Let's talk about AI. Saregama's position on AI remains that it will be beneficial to the company
in the long run, both in terms of cost reduction and speed to market. But while we support
licensed innovation, we at Saregama will consistently fight against unlicensed exploitation. All
our new digital licensing agreements are building protection against dilution of our rights and
potential fraud.

As of now, data and consumer research seems to be indicating that AI-created music is winning
primarily on volume and not on consumer listening. Whatever little has popped up globally are
AI versions of existing hits. For a catalog owner, the bigger near-t erm issue is probably
unlicensed AI covers and remakes of our songs and not AI songs competing with our new
releases.
We have invested in technology that's able to track these cover versions on various streaming
platforms and we either buy them out or pull them down. We are also opening dialogue
proactively with AI creators so that we can own and distribute the AI versions of our biggest
songs.
The global industry is converging on the stance that we have held. Universal has called for AI-
generated filler to be paid less than human artistry, and Spotify is building licensed remix and
cover features with the rights holders' consent, credit and compensation. This is exactly the
model we are pushing for AI versions of our catalog, licensed, credited, and paid.
As shared earlier, we have created two AI-dedicated teams in Saregama to optimize cost and
speed. One is a content team that's using GenAI tools to create adjacent audio content like
podcasts, using Saregama's songs and building new age music videos around the older songs.
We will be releasing around 100 hours of podcast content in Q3 using these tools.
The second team is looking at every process within the company with the end objective of
optimizing these processes using AI too

Mr. Vikas Kothari - CFO, and Mr. Deepak Chaudhary - VP Finance and Investor
Relations of CERA Sanitaryware. We will start with brief opening remarks from the
management, following which we will open the call for Q&A.
A quick disclaimer before we begin. Some of the statements made in today's
conference call may be forward-looking in nature, and a detailed note in this regard
is contained in the results document that have been shared with all of you earlier. I
would now turn the call over to the management for their opening remarks. Thank
you, and over to you, Deepak.
Deepak Chaudhary: Thank you, Devrishi. Good morning, everyone, and a warm welcome to all of you for
joining us on CERA Sanitaryware Limited's Q2 FY 27 earnings conference call. I will
begin by sharing a brief overview of the operational and strategic developments
during the quarter, following which our CFO, Mr. Vikas Kothari will take you through
the financial performance in greater detail.
CERA continued to deliver healthy growth during Q2 FY 27, with revenues growing by
27.4% year -on-year. Both our sanitaryware as well as the faucetware business
performed well, growing by 24% and 38% respectively. Sanitaryware and faucetware
accounted for 45% and 43% of total revenues respectively, together contributing
quarter was predominantly volume -driven, with healthy traction across key product
categories, including sanitaryware, faucetware, tiles, and construction chemicals.
From a channel perspective, retail demand continued to recover and was
complemented by an encouraging performance in the projects business. As many of
you would be aware, the projects business has been an important contributor to our
performance over the p ast several quarters. The improving contribution from retail
channel is a positive development for the overall business. Another important aspect
of the quarter was the consistency of growth, with business momentum remaining
healthy throughout July, August, and September, rather than being concentrated in
any particular month.

It is important for the investors to appreciate that the broader industry environment
remains challenging. While demand trends have shown improvement, the operating
environment continues to be affected by elevated input costs and supply -side
challenges. Against this backdrop, we believe that CERA's performance reflects the
inherent strengths of the business model, as well as the multiple interventions we have
undertaken to further strengthen our competitive position.
Over the past few years, we have consistently worked on further developing our focus
markets by strengthening distribution and dealer relationships, improving our market
approach, and enhancing i nternal execution capabilities. These initiatives are now
beginning to yield tangible results and, we believe, have been critical factors that
have enabled us to win incremental market share.
From a geographical perspective, we are seeing healthy traction across the wider set
of markets. Uttar Pradesh has emerged as an important market for us, and the focus
markets such as Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and MP have also shown
traction. The work undertaken to strengthen our presence in these markets have
helped us broaden our geographical presence and offset relatively weaker demand
in certain traditionally strong regions. We continue to focus on deepening penetration
and addressing white spaces in existing markets while simultaneously expanding our
reach into smaller towns and emerging consumption centers.
Coming to the input cost environment, brass and gas remain elevated during the
quarter, creating challenges for the industry. We have taken calibrated price revisions
across our product portfolio over the past few quarters, including a further price
1st, 2026, to partly offset the impact of higher brass prices. The benefits of this revision
are expected to flow through the channels from later part of Q3 FY27 onwards.
As discussed in our previous earnings call, there is a lag between implementation of
price hikes and realizing their full benefits, particularly in the projects business, where
certain supplies are executed against previously agreed prices. We have therefo re
introduced measures to strengthen pricing discipline for future project commitments
and better project profitability against further increase in input costs.
Alongside these pricing actions, we continue to focus on cost optimization, process
improvements, and operating efficiencies. While the full benefits of these initiatives will
be visible progressively, initial outcomes have led to an improvement in the operating
margins on a sequential basis. We expect further benefits to flow through the coming
quarters as these measures take effect.
Our established sourcing arrangements and strong in -house manufacturing
capabilities continue to provide us with a relative advantage in navigating the
challenging cost environment. In particular, our favorable gas sourcing arrangement
has helped us to cushion the impact of higher energy costs, positioning us favorably
relative to several other industry participants.
From a manufacturing perspective, capacity utilization has improved considerably,
supported by recovery in volumes. Our sanitaryware facilities are currently operating
at utilization level of 82%. In faucetware, we have been able to increase monthly
production from 4 lakh units to 5 lakh units by adding certain balancing equipments
of plant and machinery within the same facility.
We have also selectively brought certain fast-moving products in-house, reducing our
dependence on external manufacturers and strengthening our ability to maintain
consistent product availability. This has been particularly relevant given the operating

challenges faced by several manufacturers in the Morbi cluster. Our ability to service

opportunities.
On the brand front, the core CERA brand remains the principal driver of our volume -
led growth. We remain focused on strengthening our position across the mass and
mid-premium categories through product development, distribution expansion, and
sustained bra nd-building initiatives. At the same time, we continue to invest in
strengthening our newer brands, including Senator and CERA Luxe, with a long -term
perspective.
Looking ahead, we remain confident of sustaining our growth momentum, supported
by improving demand and deeper penetration across existing and emerging
markets. The investments made in our distribution network, manufacturing
capabilities, and internal processes over the past few years have strengthened our
ability to capitalize on the opportunities ahead. While input cost inflation remains an
important challenge, we expect profitability to improve progressively during the
second half of FY 27, supported by the cumulative benefits of pricing actions, cost
efficiency initiatives, and the healthy volume growth. We are now confident of
surpassing the revenue growth target, along with the full year's EBITDA margin outlook
of 13%-14%.

CleanMax Signs MoU with Andhra Pradesh to Invest ~₹50,000 crore in an
Integrated Clean Energy Complex to Power a 2 GW Compute Factory
Highlights
• 3 GW Integrated Renewable Energy investments in AP (Including Wind & Solar energy)
and 1 GW of Pumped Storage within the next five years
• 2 GW Compute Factory being set up in Kurnool District in collaboration with Neysa, an
AI cloud provider, for using 1 GW of the compute capacity
• CleanMax will play role of powering the Compute Factory with Green energy and the
power infrastructure through generation and distribution
Mumbai and Vishakhapatnam India, November 12, 2026:
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (NSE: CLEANMAX | BSE: 544717) ("CleanMax"),
India's largest renewable energy solutions provider for the commercial and industrial ("C&I")
sector, today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Andhra Pra desh
Economic Development Board (APEDB), Government of Andhra Pradesh. Under the MoU,
CleanMax proposes to invest nearly ₹50,000 crore to develop integrated power generation
facilities aggregating 3 GW of clean energy across wind and solar energy and 1 GW of pumped
hydro facilities. These will be used to supply a Compute Factory being set up in collaboration
with Neysa, with CleanMax responsible for the power infrastructure and supplies.
CleanMax will bring generation, storage and distribution together in one integrated clean
energy system where Wind and solar projects will generate power at different times of the
day and year, while pumped storage and BESS (electrical) storage will provide the balan cing
of supply needed to meet round-the-clock demand. CleanMax's own distribution network will
deliver round-the-clock power to the 2 GW Green Compute Factory. The integrated model
aligns energy generation to compute demand with dedicated clean energy, from planning
stage through project lifecycle.
The Green Compute Factory will be developed in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh.
CleanMax has signed an MoU with Neysa, an AI cloud provider, which will anchor the park
with 1 GW of IT load.
The projects will be developed in phases, with at least 1.5 GW of renewable capacity proposed
to be developed by 2029.
The Green Compute Factory is developed differently from the ground up. It’s supported by its
own dedicated clean power, generated, stored and distributed by CleanMax. The Green
Compute Factory will use limited water by adopting direct to chip cooling technologies and
draw on water supplies allocated to industrial usage by the local administration.
To distribute power within the park, a CleanMax’s owned and operated special purpose
vehicle (“SPV”) will apply to the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (“APERC”)
for a Distribution License, giving the Green Compute Factory its own dedicated power
network.
CleanMax commits to making the following social responsibility contributions:
• Help upgrade the infrastructure of local primary schools (and Anganwadis) in
partnership with United Way of Hyderabad
• Work on “Skilling for Jobs”, in partnership with Pratham Education Foundation
(“Pratham”). CleanMax will work with the Foundation to train local youth for entry -
level roles in Compute Factories. In addition, CleanMax will also run programmes for
final-year students at local ITIs and engineering colleges to train students in advanced
cooling and power systems, with the aim of helping students secure job opportunities
in building and operating Compute Factories
• Further, CleanMax’s partner, Neysa to provide compute to top tier research institutions
in AP
Mr. Kuldeep Jain, Founder and Managing Director, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions
Limited, said, “Compute is becoming one of the largest new sources of power demand, and it
needs clean energy that is available every hour of the day. In Andhra Pradesh, we are planning
generation, storage and distribution integrated with the compute load they serve, rather than
one after the other. Andhra Pradesh's clean energy policy framework and its strong wind and
solar resources make it the right place to build this model at scale.”
About Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (NSE: CLEANMAX | BSE: 544717) (“CleanMax”) is
India’s largest pureplay Commercial & Industrial (“C&I”) renewable energy company with
more than 15 years of operations. CleanMax’s contracted RE Power Sales portfolio reached
~6.3 GW as of September 30, 2026, with ~85% of new contracted capacity driven by existing
customers, reflecting strong customer retention and long -term business visibility. The
Company today serves 606 customers across technology, digital infrastructure,
manufacturing, and industrial sectors. CleanMax’s credit rating is CRISIL AA/Stable. Its
Equinix, Ultratech, BASF, Shell, CEAT, and STT GDC India, among others
About Neysa
Neysa is an AI acceleration cloud provider helping enterprises and AI builders train, deploy
and operate AI at scale. Its portfolio includes Neysa Velocis, a managed AI cloud platform that
brings together GPU compute, orchestration, inference, observability and cost management;
and Neysa Tytan, dedicated bare-metal AI infrastructure for customers that need committed
capacity and greater architectural control.
Founded in 2023, Neysa is backed by Blackstone. The company combines experience in
building and operating large-scale data centre and cloud infrastructure with an India-based AI
infrastructure footprint.

Managing Director; Ms. Tanushree Bagrodia, Whole-Time Director and Group CEO; Mr.
Sandeep Taneja, Group CFO; and Mr. Himanshu Sharma, Head, IR and FP&A.
We must remind you that the discussions in today's call may include certain forward-looking
statements and must be, therefore, viewed in conjunction with the risks that the company may
face. I will now hand over the call to Mr. Soni to take you through the financial and business
update, subsequent to which we can open the floor for Q&A. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Gurdeep Soni: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us for the Uniparts Group earnings call for
the second quarter of FY27. As we gear up to celebrate Diwali, I am very pleased to say that this
year, the celebration is more special for the Uniparts family. Our quarter 2 FY27 has been the
highest revenue quarter in the history of the company. Revenue from operations stood at INR379
crores, which is 37% higher year-on-year and 9% higher sequentially. I want to congratulate our
teams across all our locations.
Milestones like this are not the result of one good quarter alone, but are the result of work done
patiently over many quarters often when the market was giving us very little help. And that is
the part worth reflecting on. We have delivered this in an environment that remains genuinely
uncertain.
What made this possible is threefold. One, our customer relationships, which continue to deepen;
two, the way our teams maneuver constantly taking tactical decisions quickly to keep supply
running whatever comes at us; and three, the diversity of our platforms and segments, which
means that when one part of the business is under pressure, another carries on. That is exactly
what we are seeing today. Agriculture is still working its way back, but construction is moving
strongly.
Two updates on commitments we made to you earlier: one, the restoration of this finishing shop
at Ludhiana facility is on track to be up and running by the end of this calendar year; and two,
in Mexico, our first customer dispatch will take place this month, which is an important step in
strengthening our ability to serve customers closer to their operations.
With that, let me take you through what we are seeing across our markets and then how Uniparts
performed in each one of them. Let me start with the construction equipment for the North

America and European area. In North America, construction activity linked to data centers,
power generation and AI-related infrastructure continue to drive growth.
In fact, the world's largest construction equipment manufacturer reported an increase of
backlog. In Europe, the market is steadier with activity driven primarily by infrastructure and
green energy projects.
Also in Europe, the nonresidential construction continues to grow faster than residential
construction. Against this backdrop, Uniparts sales in the construction segment grew 49% year-
on-year. Our traction is gaining new business awards and this segment remains very robust, and
we see construction as a key growth area.
Let me now talk about large agriculture market. The large agriculture has taken the hardest hit
in the farm market. Industry volumes for tractors above 100 horsepower and 4-wheel drive
tractors are down roughly 17% this year. However, yet our revenue in this segment grew 10%
year-on-year. In fact, this is a segment in which we have demonstrated the rewards of a focused
approach.
When market down 17%, we have grown. That growth has come entirely from new business
and not from the cycle. A large focus of our business development efforts are on large ag
segment as the new business awards move through the sampling and the testing and approval
into regular production, they will contribute meaningfully. When the industry cycle does turn,
we will have that on top of all this. This is why large agriculture remains a priority for us even
in a down market.
A word on the small agriculture. As we have shared previously, after 3 years of continuous
decline, the small agriculture cycle has started to turn, and we are now seeing year-on-year
growth in this segment.
Uniparts sales in small agriculture grew 25% year-on-year. The regional picture remains mixed.
The outlook for small agriculture industry is expected to be flat or up 5% in the U.S. and Canada,
expected to be flat in Europe and down about 15% to 20% in South America, where we have
very little market share. The growth in India is estimated to be about 4% to 6%.
The aftermarket has improved to 16.5% of revenue this quarter against 12.4% in Q1 of FY27
and 14.7% in Q2 of FY26. In absolute terms, the segment grew over 50% year-on-year for us.
Those of you who were on our last call will recall that we spoke about an inflation-driven pause
in buying and said we expected it to normalize through this year. That is what has happened

New business wins, in fact, have been very good, and they continue to exceed INR225 crores,

Gas Pool operator in ascertaining the contribution to pool account, considered cheaper market

Spot gas meant for Urea Operations sourced as per OOF directives. Accordingly differential price
or contribution to the pool by the company was worked out and issued debit note.

and thus needs to be subsumed in arriving at the final pool price and the same should be
considered in the subsidy of urea, since the cost of gas is a pass through.

Q2 & H1 FY2027 Earnings Call Transcript Page 3 of 13
We are pleased to report another quarter of healthy growth in
consolidated revenues of Rs. 265 crores in quarter 2 FY27, representing
an increase of 14% year-on-year. For the first half, revenue stood at Rs.
526 crores, growing 16% over the corresponding period last year, making
the highest ever H1 revenues in Allied Digital's history. This is reassuring,
given the challenging operating backdrop.
On the profitability front, EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 27 crores
with a margin of 10%, while profit before tax was Rs. 17 crores. Margins
continue to reflect investments in talent, leadership and growth
capabilities alongside the competitive pricing and operating cost
pressures. Our focus remains on strengthening the business with
progressively improving operational efficiency and profitability.
Let me turn to the industry landscape, which continues to evolve rapidly,
particularly in the terms of accelerating pace of innovation. Even as
enterprises remain committed to modernization, automation and digital
transformation, they are becoming more deliberate in their investment
decisions.
With new AI models and platforms emerging at a rapid pace and with each
new model promising superior capabilities at lowering computing costs,
customers are understandably cautious about committing to
technologies that could quickly be superseded. Consequently,
investment decisions are increasingly focused on flexibility, cost
efficiency, measurable returns and long-term relevance. This means
extended evaluation of approved cycles, particularly for larger
transformation programs.
We are witnessing these trends within our business, too. Customer
inquiries remain robust and engagements are becoming deeper and more
strategic, but large contracts are taking longer to conclude as clients
evaluate technology choices and commercial considerations more
closely. Smaller and midsized opportunities, however, converting
relatively faster and enabling us to sustain business momentum.

An important element of our strategy is to increase the contribution from
direct customer engagements. Allied Digital has built a solid track record
when participating in large partner-led projects, consortium-led projects,
which provide scale and allow execution responsibility and risk to be
shared. However, direct relationships give us greater ownership of the
customer engagement and create more opportunities to expand our
services, deepen relationships and increase our share of customer
technology spending over time.
We are, therefore, strengthening our sales organization and go-to-market
capabilities in order to build a healthier balance between partner-led,
consortium-led and direct business. We are now starting to see renewed
activity in the government segment as well.
As we highlighted in the earlier calls, the sharp increase in equipment and
hardware costs had affected the commercial viability of certain projects,
leading to delays and being more selective towards the bidding approach.
While costs remain elevated, prices have shown signs of stabilization,
and we are beginning to see projects return to active consideration. Given
our expertise in safe cities, smart cities, surveillance projects, command
and control systems and integrated digital infrastructure, we remain
encouraged by the opportunity in the pipeline in this segment.
Coming to operational developments. We secured over Rs. 74 crores in
new orders and renewals during the quarter. Among the key
developments was strategic partnership in the U.S. to deliver
infrastructure cloud and cybersecurity services through our offshore
delivery center. We also secured an engagement in the U.S. leading
healthcare service provider to implement and support 24/7 AI-powered
service desk.
In India, we were selected by MIDC to be the system integrator for
implementation, maintenance and support of its Internet leased line
connectivity solution across Maharashtra. This marks an order win from a
government agency after a gap of 3 quarters, validating our view that
domestic government ordering activity is set to pick up again.
Additionally, we renewed several long-standing customer engagements

Internally, we continue to build on the leadership augmentation taken up

and Mr. Dushyant Sood, Chief Marketing Officer.
