involve risks and uncertainties, which are difficult to predict. A detailed disclaimer has been
given in the company's investor presentation, which is uploaded on the stock exchange. Now I
would like to hand over the conference call to the management for the opening remarks. Thank
you, and over to you, sir.
Rajesh Aggarwal: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us for our Q2 and H1 Earnings call. We
appreciate your continued interest in the support of the company. Today, we'll walk you through
our performance for the second quarter, highlight the key developments across the business,
discuss the progress we have made against our strategic priorities and share our outlook for the
coming quarters.
Q2 has been an important quarter for us, and I would like to take this opportunity to reflect on
what went well, where we faced challenges and how we are positioning the business for
sustainable growth. We'll begin with our overview on our financial and operational performance,
followed by key business updates and our outlook.
We'll then open the floor for the questions. With that, let me begin with the key highlights of
Q2. First, let me talk about the industry dynamics. Super El Nino has impacted or I should say
that weather has disrupted the key agriculture regions across the country is not wrong. And it is
not only India, which got impacted, but the entire Asia, rather the entire world got impacted
because many regions saw drought and few states were badly impacted.
So along with this, the global uncertainties and the supply chain disruptions also played a very
important role because you know the crude prices went as high as $125 and it is just yesterday
night when it has come again below $100, and the impact is yet t o be seen because this is the
Diwali time, festive time.

So the things will get cleared soon. But at this moment, everything becomes so expensive,
including the sea freight that it was impacting the business adversely. So this El Nino impacted
the wet crops like sugarcane and paddy because in many parts of the country, the water
availability was a constraint.
But at the same time, even the dry crops like maize, cotton, soybean, they got an impact. And
chilli was also very adversely impacted so far after the current cyclones where, again, impact is
plus and minus. When I say plus and minus because the water became available to the crop, it is
plus. But it came along with the wind, so the crop was down, so that is minus.
So there were both type of impact which were observed from these 2 cyclones, which we have
received in the last couple of days. But as a whole, we see that the Indian farmer remain buoyant
for the new technology products. Another development is that the inflationary trend is visible in
almost all agri commodities prices.
Particularly if we leave aside the vegetables, which are -- which get impacted by the seasonal
pressures, all the agriculture crops, we see a price hike and we see farmer -- the general trend is
that they are moving towards the premium products. The number of sprays have come down,
but they are looking for better solutions for protecting their crop.
So I would say that despite of the low yield, the farmer profitability has remained intact to a
greater extent. And still, we see a good interest in crop protection amongst the farmers. Talking
about IIL performance in Q2, there is a 8% revenue growth in Q2 and if we look at H1, there is
2% degrowth.
The margins have -- we see a consistency with focus on premiumization and cost -effective
products. Kaeros continues to gain the traction as an emerging platform to expand distribution
the target to open the southern part of the country is in Q2, which means that during this year,
Kaeros will be visible across the country from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.
IIL is gearing up its crop-based solutions with ICS plots. These ICS plots IIL crop solution plots
has been a big success for us in the past few years. Last year, we were working on 30-odd plots.
This year, we have doubled that number and that number is about 70 across 4 crops, the 4 major
crops where we are working are rice, cotton, soybean and chilli.
We have demonstrated amongst the farmer that how by using the similar number of space and
sometimes the lesser number of space, generally with the lesser cost, how we have improved
their productivity, how they can make more money per acre by using the solutions suggested by
IIL and they have become so popular that thousands of farmers are attending the farmer meetings
at these plots and giving very good acceptance to the new generation products, which are
introduced by IIL.
So the marketing team has been very, very aggressive in the field activities in H1. We have
completed more than 18,000 farmer meetings across the country. There has been more than
9,000 demonstrations, and we have met more than 2.5 lakh farmers in H1. So the investment in
manufacturing has continued in Sotanala and Dahej.

inventories and debtors are at a little elevated level.

10.2% to 6.3 million pairs alongside a 6% improvement in ASP. This performance is particularly
encouraging in a relatively subdued consumption environment. More importantly, our growth
is increasingly being driven by stronger fundamentals, a broader consumer base, a richer
product portfolio, and deeper market penetration. Our continued investments in product
innovation, design, and distribution are translating into tangible results.
First, we are successfully expanding our consumer base. Our Women and Kids categories grew
by 27% and 34% respectively during first half FY’27, significantly outperforming the overall
business. These categories represent substantial opportunities to expand our addressable
market, and we believe we are still in the early stages of unlocking their potential. Second,
premiumization is emerging as a powerful structural growth driver. Our products priced at Rs.
2,000 and above have delivered volume growth exceeding 50% Y-o-Y with a contribution to the

omnichannel presence. Alongside our traditional distribution network, we are witnessing
encouraging traction across emerging digital platforms including quick commerce and our own
the quarter.
Our strategy is clear. Make Campus available wherever our consumers choose to shop while
maintaining a sharp focus on channel productivity and profitability.
Coming to profitability, our material margins remained under pressure due to significant
inflation and key input costs. While we have taken calibrated pricing actions, there is an
inherent lag between higher input costs flowing through our inventory and the corresponding
pricing benefits being fully realized. It is important to distinguish between recovering absolute
input costs and protecting a percentage margin. We believe maintaining the right balance
between growth, consumer value, and profitability is more important than pursuing aggressive
price increases for short-term margin protection. Despite these pressures, we delivered EBITDA
growth of 12.5% and PAT growth of over 21% Y-o-Y reflecting the resilience of our business.
Looking ahead, we expect a meaningful recovery in profitability during second half of the year
supported by the progressive benefits of pricing actions, improving product mix, operating
leverage and continued cost discipline. We remain confident on delivering a full year FY’27
EBITDA margin of 17%.
Stepping back, I believe campus is entering an important phase in this growth journey. FY’27 is
about sustaining growth and demonstrating operating resilience despite significant input cost
inflation. FY’28 will be about converting this stronger growth platform into accelerated
earnings and improving profitability. We remain committed to building a larger, more
diversified and increasingly profitable Campus while creating sustainable long-term value for
our stakeholders.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. I'm Kartikeyan , moderator for the conference call. Welcome to
Ester Industries Q2 and H1 FY27 Conference Call. As a reminder, all participants will be in listen-only mode
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Could you

Amit Sharma
Thank you, Kartikeyan. Good afternoon, everybody, and a very warm welcome to the earnings call of Ester
Industries Limited for the second quarter and half year ended 30
th Sept 2026. On the call today, we have
Mr. Vaibhav Jha, Chief Executive Officer and Mr. Pradeep Rustagi, Executive Director, Corporate Affairs of
the Company. The management will take us through the operational and financial performance for the
quarter and half year, following which we will open the floor for the question and answer session.
Before we begin, please note that this conference may contain forward looking statements about the
company, which are based on the company's beliefs, opinions , and expectations as of today. These
statements are not a guarantee of future performance and are subject to risks and uncertainties. I now
request Mr. Vaibhav Jha to take us through the company's performance. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Vaibhav Jha
Thank you, Amit. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I will take you through
the industry environment and the key business developments during the quarter, following which
Pradeep Ji will walk you through the financial performance. Let me begin with the industry landscape. The
operating environment for the BOPET film industry remained stable during the Q2 FY27, and the
improvement witnessed in Q1 FY27 continued through the quarter gone by.
We continue to see better demand across both domestic and export markets. In India, the increasing
adoption of polyester films in flexible packaging is being supported by favorable regulatory developments.
The plastic waste management rules, which mandate 10% post-consumer recycled content in flexible
packaging are encouraging brand owners to increasingly adopt polyester films with recycled content. To
comply with this mandatory requirement, the brand owners are shifting from other substrates to
polyester films with recycled content. On the export front, Indian manufacturers continue to benefit from
new opportunities across the international markets that emerged due to the war in West Asia and
disturbance in Middle East.
domestic market. The United States was particularly encouraging for us during the quarter. The tariff
related disruptions that affected trade between India and The U. S. During the previous financial years
have largely been resolved and our exports to the U.S have revived. Majority of the exports that we make
to U.S. are of vast products across BOPET films and specialty polymers.
Ester Industries Limited
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 05.11.2026
Trade tariffs now imposed on exports originating from India is comparable to trade tariffs imposed on
other exporting countries. Coming to the cost environment, disruptions in crude oil supplies and volatility
in crude prices arising from the ongoing geopolitical situation in West Asia and Middle East have resulted
in higher petrochemical prices. Consequently, our key raw materials, PT and MEG, have also witnessed
significant increase in prices. We have been able to pass on this increase to customers through improved
realizations. This is reflected in the performance of our films business where revenue increased by 39.6%
during the quarter against a volume growth of 13.9%.
However, the increase in raw material and freight costs, coupled with longer transit times, has resulted in
higher working capital requirements. This has particularly impacted our receivables and inventory levels,
which Pradeep Ji will explain in greater detail. Looking ahead, we expect the industry environment to
remain stable over medium to long term. New capacity additions have been relatively moderate
compared to the demand growth. Global prices have remained firm and the increasing adoption of BOPET
and recycled content polyester films continues to provide structural growth opportunities.
While industry cycles will continue to influence the business, our strategic focus remains on increasing the
contribution of value added and specialty products. We believe this transition will improve the quality of
our earnings and provide greater resilience across industry cycles.
Moving to the business performance, let me begin with our p olyester film segment. We witnessed a
healthy improvement in performance in the segment during the quarter over the corresponding quarter
last year. Consolidated film sales volume increased by 13.9% YoY to 24,291 metric tons in Q2 FY27,
compared with 21,329 metric tons in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the first half, consolidated film sales volume increased by 8.3% to 46,412 metric tons. In value terms,
film segment revenue, including rPET and chips, grew by 39.6% YoY to INR 414.5 crores during Q2 FY27.
For H1 FY27, revenue increased by 38.7% to INR 813.9 crore. The higher growth in revenue compared to
volume reflects the improved realization, the pass through of the increased feedstock cost and a better
product mix. More importantly, the segment delivered an EBIT o f INR 34.5 crores during the quarter
compared to an EBIT loss of INR 6.2 crores in Q2 FY26.
The EBIT margin stood at 8.3%. For the first half, the segment EBIT improved significantly to INR 73.6
crores with an EBIT margin of 9% compared with INR 0.8 crore in H1 FY 26. An important contributor to
this improvement has been consistent increase in proportion of the value -added and specialty films
portfolio. During Q2 FY 27, sales of value -added and specialty films increased to 6,200 metric tons,
the corresponding quarter last year.
The volume of VAS products registered a significant growth of 25.8%. I must mention that we clocked
27% of total film volume compared with 10,107 metric ton in H1 FY26 , registering a healthy growth of
Q4 FY27 and further to around 50-60% over next two to three years. This remains a key strategic priority
for us.
As proportion of differentiated products increases, our ability to compete will increasingly be driven by
differentiated product offerings addressing varied application requirement and customer qualifications
Ester Industries Limited
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 05.11.2026
rather than pricing alone. We will continue to invest in product development, customer approvals and
capabilities to serve more specialized applications. Coming to our rPETbusiness, we continue to witness
healthy growth during the quarter. rPETT sales volume increased by 37.4% YoY to 1,437 metric tons in Q2
FY27, while revenue grew by 51% to INR 18.4 crore. For H1 FY27, volumes increased by 27.7% to 2,831
metric tons, while revenue grew by 36.7% to 35.8 crores.
We currently have an installed rPETT capacity of 28,000 metric tons per annum across our Sitarganj and
Hyderabad facilities. Major share of the production of rPET T is consumed captively for production of
BOPET films with recycled content. Our primary strategic objective in r PET is to use recycled r PET as a
feedstock for our own recycled content for BOPET films. Therefore, the overall strategic value of this
business extends beyond the external revenue generated from standalone rPET sales.

• Revenue was Rs. 14,396 million growing by 11.5% YOY

remained elevated, our pr ofitability has remained within our planned range. With positive demand
trends, strong brand momentum, an exciting pipeline of new product ranges and ongoing initiatives to
improve operational efficiency, we look ahead with confidence.”

input costs.

- Good afternoon and thank you for joining us for Linc Limited's Q2 FY26-27 investor call.
- We are pleased to report double -digit sales growth in the second quarter supported by
focused sales promotion initiatives and healthy growth in categories beyond writing
instruments.
- Operating income stood at ₹15,412 lakhs, representing growth of 10.8% year-on-year and
10.9% sequentially.
- The operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹1,131 lakhs, with a margin of 7.3%,
compared with 11.3% in the second quarter last year and 8.7% in quarter one of this year.
attributable to higher raw material cost and 200 basis points to increased sales
expenditures.
- On the raw material front, geopolitical uncertainties drove price increases across certain
inputs. The extent of these increases varied across materials, with some remaining
relatively less affected. Our raw material mix , therefore helped cushion the overall cost
impact, although input cost pressures continued to weigh on margins.
- We also increased sales promotion activities to stimulate demand while maintaining our
underlying pricing structure. These initiatives helped stimulate demand and support the
double-digit growth achieved during the quarter.
- While the higher expenditure weighed on near -term margins, it reflects our focus on
gaining market share and building sustained sales momentum. We continue to broaden
our product offering through new introductions across the Pentonic and linked portfolios.
These launches support our efforts to address a wider range of consumer preferences and
strengthen our presence across price points.
- We are also expanding our presence in lifestyle drinkw are to Tri -Tonic, our brand of
Tritan-based bottles for everyday use, active lifestyles and children. This category allows
us to apply our expertise in polymers while drawing on our established brand and
distribution capabilities.
- Our Stackoo experience centers in Kolkata and Mumbai support this broader portfolio
strategy by bringing our writing instruments, stationery and allied products together in an
engaging retail environment.
- Our international growth initiatives continue to progress. Uni-Linc, our joint venture with
Mitsubishi Pencil Company, Japan, remained operationally stable with exports accounting
for more than 50% of its revenue during the first half.
- Operations at our joint venture in Turkey also continued to progress steadily.
- The development of our subsidiary with Morris of Korea remains linked to the
commissioning of the West Bengal manufacturing facility which is expected to become
operational in the third quarter. We expect the commissioning of this facility to support
business traction and export volumes.
- Sales momentum at our Kenya subsidiary continues to improve and we expect this trend
to strengthen over the coming quarters.
- Linc On is also growing at a healthy rate and is expected to gain further momentum.
- Looking ahead, our priority is to sustain sales growth while improving the balance
between growth investments and profitability. We will continue to monitor raw material
cost, evaluate promotional spending and build on the encouraging performance of
categories beyond writing instruments.
- Alongside these efforts, our new product launches and strategic partnerships remain
central to strengthening the business over the long term.

Q2 FY27: Delivers Highest Ever Core Business EBITDA
Consolidated EBITDA at ₹190 crore, up 86.6% YoY; consolidated PAT grew 121.7% YoY to ₹82 crore
Mumbai, 12 th November 2026: MAN Industries (India) Limited (BSE: 513269, NSE: MANINDS), one of India's leading
manufacturers of large -diameter carbon steel line pipes and coating systems for the oil & gas sector, today announced its
financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
Key Highlights — Q2 FY27
• Record Core Business Revenue & EBITDA: Consolidated EBITDA of ₹190 crore, the highest -ever for a quarter, was
up 86.6% YoY and 22.4% QoQ, with margin expanding 310 bps YoY to 15.6%, driven mainly by the contribution of
NPC, which has been consolidated since its acquisition on 21 May 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations grew
49.3% YoY to ₹1,216 crore, while consolidated PAT rose 121.7% YoY to ₹82 crore.
• Impact of Shipping Disruption: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia has disrupted key maritime routes, particularly the
Strait of Hormuz, causing port congestion and delays in dispatches of finished goods. As a result, revenue of
since nominated alternate ports, and these shipments are being executed.
• NPC Performance: In Q3 CY26 (July–September 2026), Saudi Arabia -based National Pipe Company (NPC) reported
revenue of SAR 191 million (~₹486 crore) and EBITDA of SAR 34 million (~₹88 crore), with EBITDA margin of ~18%;
PAT was SAR 30 million (~₹77 crore), with net margin of 15.8%.
For 9M CY26 (January–September 2026), including the period before its acquisition by MAN, NPC reported revenue
of SAR 415 million (~₹1,062 crore) and EBITDA of SAR 76 million (~₹194 crore), with EBITDA margin of 18.2%; PAT
was SAR 67 million (~₹171 crore), with net margin of 16.1%.
MAN completed the acquisition of NPC on 21 May 2026 and has consolidated it from that date. For the period from
21 May to 30 September 2026, NPC contributed revenue of SAR 208 million (~₹532 crore), EBITDA of SAR 37 million
(~₹94 crore) and PAT of SAR 31 million (~₹79 crore) to MAN’s consolidated results.
• Consolidated Order Book: Order book stands at ~₹ 3,500 crore across India and Saudi Arabia, with the majority
executable over the next 6–9 months.
• Merino Shelters Progress: The joint development agreement (JDA) project with the Paradise Group at Navi Mumbai
was launched on 26 October 2026. Cash flows of ₹700–800 crore is expected over the next 5–6 years.
• Jammu Greenfield Update: Implementation of the greenfield stainless steel seamless pipe plant at Jammu is on
track, with production expected by April 2027.
• Dammam Coating & Double Jointing Facility: Operations are targeted to commence by March 2027, further
strengthening MAN’s integrated manufacturing and value-added processing capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
• Establishment of Manufacturing Facility in USA: Establishment of a HSAW pipe facility in USA with a capacity of
350,000 MTPA and planned capex of US$110 million through its wholly owned subsidiary.

Balaxi Pharmaceuticals Limited

Listing Department,
National Stock Exchange of India Limited
Exchange Plaza, Plot No C-1, Block G, Bandra Kurla Complex,
Bandra (E), Mumbai — 400051
NSE Symbol: BALAXI
Dear Sir/Madam,
Subject: Outcome of Board Meeting
In reference to our letter dated 27 October, 2026, we wish to inform you that the Board of
Directors at their meeting held today i.e., on 12% November, 2026; have inter-alia, approved
the following:
1. Standalone and Consolidated Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for
the quarter and half year ended 30" September, 2026:
Pursuant to Regulation 33 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)
Regulations, 2015, we enclose herewith a copy of the Standalone and Consolidated
Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended
30% September, 2026, accompanied by Limited Review Reports thereon by the
Statutory Auditors of the Company as Annexure A & Annexure B respectively.
2. Change in Designation of Mr. Pranav Maheshwari, Key Managerial Personnel of
the Company:
Based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the
Board of Directors of the Company have approved the change in designation of
Mr. Pranav Maheshwari from ‘Senior Vice President — Business Development’ to
‘President — Business and Corporate Strategy’ with effect from
12" November, 2026. He continues to be a Key Managerial Personnel of the
Company.
The information as required in terms of the SEBI Master Circular No.
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/1/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026 is enclosed
as Annexure — C.
3. Took Note of the Progress of the Company's Pharmaceutical Formulation Plant
at Jadcherla, Hyderabad:
The Board of Directors took note of the progress of the Company's pharmaceutical
formulation manufacturing facility at Jadcherla, Hyderabad, as apprised by the
Managing Director.
Registered Office:
Plot No. 409, H. No. 8-2-293, Maps Towers, 3rd Floor, Phase |II, Road No. 81, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad (T.G.) - 500 096
The Board was apprised that the Company has achieved a significant milestone with
the receipt of WHO-GMP certification from CDSCO for its phannaceutical
formulation manufacturing facility. The certification establishes the facility's
compliance with WHO-GMP standards, further strengthening the Company's
manufacturing credentials and enhancing its capabilities to cater to domestic and
international market opportunities.
The Board further noted that commercial production at the facility is being
progressively scaled up, initially catering to the Angola and Dominican Republic
markets. So far, the facility has successfully manufactured 22 different products,
with the product portfolio expected to expand progressively based on regulatory
approvals and market demand.
The Board was also apprised that the Company continues to receive manufacturing
product permissions from the regulatory authorities. In addition to the initial 31
product pennissions, the Company has received approvals for 3 additional products,
taking the total approved product portfolio to 34 products. The Company will
continue to pursue further product approvals and progressively expand its
manufacturing portfolio in line with business requirements and market opportunities.
The Board expressed satisfaction with the progress achieved, particularly the receipt
of WHO-GMP certification, and noted that the facility is steadily scaling up its
commercial manufacturing operations, strengthening the Company's manufacturing
capabilities and providing a platform for its future growth and expansion.
The Board meeting commenced at 11 :45 AM. (IST) and concluded at 01:50 P.M. (1ST).
This is for your information and records.
Thanking y OU.
Yours faithfully,
For Balaxi Pharmaceuticals Limited

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call
of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. The call will begin with a brief discussion by the
company's management on the Q2 FY27 performance, followed by a question-and-answer
session.
We have with us today Mr. Ashish Dikshit, Managing Director; Mr. Suraj Bahirwani, CEO
Pantaloons; and Mr. Jagdish Bajaj, CFO. I want to thank the management team on behalf of all
participants for taking valuable time to be with us.
I must remind you that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking statements and
must be viewed therefore in conjunction with the risks that the company faces. Please restrict
your questions to the quarter performance and to strategic questions only. Housekeeping
With this, I hand the conference over to Mr. Jagdish Bajaj. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Jagdish Bajaj: Thank you. Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I would like to welcome
you all to the Q2 FY27 earnings call of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. Looking back
at the quarter, demand trends remained broadly in line with the previous quarters. However, the
Y-o-Y performance was influenced by the shift in festive calendar, including Pujo into Q3 this
year, along with a subdued wedding season.
This led to a shift in the timing of consumer purchases, particularly across Pantaloons and our
ethnic businesses, which together account for nearly 80% of our portfolio, thereby weighing on
overall revenue growth and operating leverage during the quarter. It is, therefore, important to
view Q2 performance in this context. Against this backdrop, we saw momentum across our
businesses, with our emerging growth platforms gaining scale.
Now moving to the financial performance of the quarter, ABFRL closed Q2 with revenue of
INR2,030 crores, registering 2% Y-o-Y growth. While the festive shift moderated growth in our
larger businesses, our emerging businesses delivered a broader contribution to overall growth.
Our ethnic portfolio, excluding TCNS, grew by 12%. Luxury delivered 11% growth, and
TMRW grew by 10%. OWND continues its strong growth trajectory, recording 58% year-on-
year growth, supported by the contribution from newer stores.
This growing contribution from our emerging businesses is an encouraging development and
reinforces the growth potential of our portfolio. Pantaloons segment, on a festive-adjusted basis,
delivered 10% Y-o-Y growth in Q2.
Moving to profitability, EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR67 crores. The decline was driven
primarily by the shift in festive consumption to Q3, which impacted operating leverage during
the quarter, the continued investment towards scaling our newer businesses.
While these factors impacted the profitability, focusing on profitable growth remains a key
priority as we build scale across our businesses. Our efforts remain directed towards improving
operating efficiencies, enhancing store productivity, and building a more profitable business
over time.
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited
November 06, 2026

Turning to our balance sheet, we closed Q2 with gross cash of INR 1,143 crores at the
consolidated level and INR 628 crores at the standalone level, providing sufficient liquidity to
support our business requirement. Historically, H2 has been stronger for us in terms of both
revenue and profitability, and we expect this trend, along with the release of working capital
following the festive inventory buildup, to support cash generation in the second half.
Coming to our retail network, we continue to expand our presence in a calibrated manner. During
the quarter, we added 35 stores, taking total additions in the first half to over 80 stores. Our
expansion strategy remains focused on building a more productive retail network across brands,

Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care Ltd. (PGHH) today announced
its financial results for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company reported sales of ₹
1145 crores, flat versus year ago. Profit After Tax (PAT) was reported at ₹196 crores, down 7% versus year
ago.
In the quarter, the Company experienced a double-digit impact on profitability driven by commodity
cost fluctuations and headwinds like raw material and energy costs, as well as unfavorable foreign
exchange rates. However, a significant portion of this was offset by the robust productivity program. In
the quarter, the company also continued to significantly invest back in innovation and advertising &
promotion (versus past quarter) - in an endeavor to position the company for long-term competitiveness
and value creation.
Kumar Venkatasubramanian, Managing Director, Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care Ltd.
said, “We continue to invest strategically in our brands, innovation and market capabilities, even as
the macro-economic landscape remains challenging. We continue to believe that our strategic
priorities, combined with the strength of our brands and organizational capabilities, position us well to
leverage future growth opportunities and create sustainable long-term value for all our stakeholders.
We are excited about the future.”
He added, “We are confident in our Integrated Growth Strategy of a focused product portfolio of daily
use categories where performance drives brand choice, superiority (of product performance, packaging,
brand communication, retail execution and value), productivity, constructive disruption, and an agile
and accountable organization; to deliver balanced growth and value creation.”
The first half of FY 2026–27 was marked by sustained innovation across our vectors of superiority. Key
milestones include the launches of the upgraded Vicks ZzzQuil with Ashwagandha and Vicks medicated
lozenges, alongside the ongoing evolution of our media model to better engage consumers where they
are. The Company continues to focus on, and drive, Whisper Period Pants to delight consumers with 360-
degree leakage protection. Recently, the company also participated in P&G Loop, a first-of-its-kind, mega
immersive brand experience event organized for content creators.
About Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care Limited

body:
Dated: 12.11.2026

(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and Para B(8) of Part A of Schedule III thereto –
Litigation/Dispute involving Larica LED Products Private Limited.
Dear Sir/Madam,
Pursuant to the provisions of Regulation 30(3) read with Regulation 30(4)(i)(c) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("SEBI LODR Regulations"), read with Para B(8) of Part A of
Schedule III thereto, the Company is required to di sclose the pendency of any litigation(s) or dispute(s), the
outcome of which can reasonably be expected to have an impact on the listed entity, upon application of the
materiality criteria prescribed under the aforesaid Regulations.
In this regard, the Com pany wishes to inform that disputes arose between the Company and Larica LED
Products Private Limited in relation to the supply of products by the Company to Larica LED Products Private
Limited for onward supply to Public Sector Undertakings. The matter su bsequently resulted in arbitration
proceedings and proceedings before the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Kolkata.
Upon review of the aforesaid matter and application of the quantitative materiality criteria prescribed under
Regulation 30(4)( i)(c) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, the Company has determined that the matter meets the
applicable materiality threshold for disclosure under the aforesaid Regulations.
The Company submits that the disclosure could not be made at the relevant time due to an inadvertent
omission in the internal identification and escalation of the aforesaid litigation for the purpose of determining
brought to the attenti on of the concerned officials for making the requisite disclosure within the prescribed
timeline.
Upon receipt of the clarification sought by the Stock Exchange and subsequent review of the matter, the
Company has taken steps to make the requisite disclosu re under Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations.
Accordingly, the detailed disclosure containing the particulars of the litigation/dispute is enclosed herewith
The Company has also taken note of the matter and is strengthening its internal reporting a nd monitoring
disclosed to the Stock Exchanges within the prescribed timelines.

NEW YORK, US and MUMBAI, INDIA – Nov 12, 2026 – eClerx Services Ltd. (NSE: ECLERX; BSE: 532927),
a global leader in AI-powered analytics, digital operations, automation and business process
management, today announced the acquisition of RegEdge.
RegEdge is a boutique consulting firm that helps financial institutions strengthen compliance programs,
transform regulatory operations, and manage risk across the full trade lifecycle. With this acquisition,
eClerx will further deepen its risk and regulatory capabilities, bringing together AI, technology and global
delivery expertise to help clients navigate complex regulatory requirements more effectively.
Kapil Jain, CEO & Managing Director, eClerx, said, “Strategic acquisitions are an important part of how
we expand our capabilities, deepen our domain expertise, and pursue new growth opportunities . We are
pleased to welcome the RegEdge team to eClerx, and look forward to creating greater value for our clients.”
Harshad Pitkar, Founder and CEO, RegEdge, said, “RegEdge was founded on the belief that navigating
regulatory complexity requires more than advisory expertise; it calls for a hands-on approach and practical
solutions that work within the realities of financial institutions. Becoming part of eClerx enables us to take
our expertise and proprietary solutions to a wider range of institutions, while helping clients further
strengthen their compliance programs, improve operational effectiveness and respond with g reater agility to
an evolving regulatory environment.”
About eClerx
eClerx provides AI-powered analytics, digital operations services, automation, and business process management
to help clients unlock growth and drive business outcomes. eClerx partners wi th Fortune 500 enterprises across
company, eClerx operates across 17 countries with over 23,300 employees, serving clients globally across th e
Americas, APAC, and EMEA.
About RegEdge
RegEdge is a risk and regulatory consulting firm founded in 2019 and headquartered in United States. The
company helps financial institutions address regulatory, risk and compliance challenges across trade and
transaction reporting, surveillance, financial crime compliance, regulatory change, and risk and controls.

description: Lakshya Powertech Limited (LAKSHYA) filed a "Press Release" announcement on NSE on 12 Nov 2026: Lakshya Powertech Limited has informed the Exchange regarding a press release dated November 12, 2026, titled "Press Release of Financial Results pertaining to H1 FY 2026-27".
body:
Lakshya Powertech Limited Announces H1 FY27 ResultsTotal Income at₹8280.06 Lakh | EBITDA at₹1075.33 LakhAhmedabad, Gujarat, India November 12, 2026:Lakshya Powertech Limited (NSE: LAKSHYA),an engineering solutions provider delivering integrated Engineering, Procurement,Construction and Commissioning (EPCC), Operations & Maintenance (O&M) and specialisedtechnical services across the oil & gas, power, renewable energy, industrial and datacentre sectors, has announced its unaudited financial results for the half year endedSeptember 30, 2026.H1 FY27 FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS(₹in Lakh, except EPS and margins)Particulars H1 FY27Total Income 8,280.06EBITDA 1,075.33EBITDA Margin (%) 12.99%Net Profit 440.37Net ProfitMargin (%) 5.32%EPS (₹) 4.37ORDER BOOK AND KEY ORDERS■New orders aggregating₹972 croresecured during H1 FY27, with an unexecuted orderbook of₹953 croreas of September 30, 2026, significantly strengthening long-termrevenue visibility■Vedanta –₹641.92 crore: Integrated Service contract for O&M of Cairn Assets forthe RJ-ON-90/1 Block, covering RJ North Well Pads across Mangala, Bhagyam andAishwarya in Rajasthan, for a period of 4 years■Vedanta Oil & Gas –₹276.38 crore: Integrated Service contract for O&M of theCairn Asset at Ravva, Andhra Pradesh, for a period of 3 years plus 2 provisionalyears■Micron Electricals –₹21.24 crore(including GST): manufacture, supply, erectionand commissioning of 11 x 90 KL horizontal underground bulk storage diesel tanksfor the data centre domain■Powerica Limited –₹14.07 crore: positioning, testing and commissioning of the DGsets, along with allied services, to be executed over 5 months■Powerica Limited –₹11.28 crore: positioning, testing and commissioning of the DGSets, along with allied services, to be executed over 4 months
■Powerica Limited –₹2.52 crore: hot air chamber walkway platforms and panel DGroofing at NAV 2 data centre project in Airoli,and erection material andinstallation of 6 x 2,250 KVA DG sets for Powerica LimitedMANAGEMENT COMMENTARYCommenting on the performance,Mr. Rajesh Gopala Anne, Chairman & Managing Director,Lakshya Powertech Limited, said:“During H1 FY27, Total Income stood at₹8280.06 lakh and EBITDA at₹1075.33 lakh,with our EBITDA margin improving by 22 bps to 13.0%. More importantly, the half wasmarked by strong order inflows, led by two large Integrated O&M contracts fromVedanta worth₹918.30 crore, along with orders from data centre and powerinfrastructure clients, significantly strengthening our long-term revenue visibility.Our journey continues to be guided by a clear objective – to build Lakshya Powertechinto a diversified engineering and services organisation with strong technicalcapabilities, enduring customer relationships and an increasing contribution fromlong-duration and specialised service businesses.The Integrated O&M contracts from Vedanta represent the continuing evolution of ourbusiness from predominantly project-based assignments towards a stronger combinationof project execution and long-duration recurring service contracts.”

The second quarter was marked by a challenging operating environment. El Niño intensified
into a super event, with the monsoon ending about 13% below normal and reservoir levels at a
10-year low, creating uncertainty for the Rabi season. Geopolitical volatility and inflation across
milk, feed, and packaging continued to pressure input costs.
Despite these headwinds, our diversified portfolio, disciplined execution, and risk management
helped us deliver a strong performance. Strength in animal nutrition offset pressure in crop care,
dairy, and Astec, while our transformation agenda continued to progress.
We delivered double -digit revenue growth, with Q2 consolidated revenue growing 17% year -
on-year to INR2,995 crores, driven by higher realizations and volume growth, led by animal
nutrition, oil palm, and our B2C food segment, while our Bangladesh JV maintained strong
momentum.
EBITDA remained stable at INR222 crores, despite significant cost inflation, with margin at
7.4%. Profit before tax grew 5% to INR131 crores, and PAT was up 22% to INR103 crores.

The complex brings together every stage of the oil palm value chain under one roof: seed and

unfavourable product mix. While revenue grew on a lower base, profitability declined, partly
mitigated by our diversification into newer crop care segments. We continue to scale
differentiated products such as Ashitaka®, though demand conditions remain challenging.
At Astec LifeSciences, weak enterprise demand offset growth in the CDMO business. EBITDA
was also impacted due to lower realizations and elevated input costs. However, we remain
focused on transformation through new products, capacity utilization, and cost optimization.
Dairy revenue grew 6%, led by calibrated pricing and growth in value -added products, which
now account for 49% of the portfolio. Profitability remained affected by elevated milk
procurement, packaging, and logistics costs.
Godrej Foods continued to shift towards higher-value products, with B2C growing by 50% and

PAT stood at INR231 crores.

from 32 days last year. Absolute working capital reduced to INR655 crores, strengthening

Good evening, everyone. I'm Indranil. I'm the CFO of Elgi and apologies to all of you. Really sorry. Dr.
Jai is trying to get in the call still, but he's requested us to go ahead. So , I'll be initiating the
presentation. Can we move to the next slide, please? Yeah, so as we start the year, we've had a good
quarter. Growth over previous year is at 17%. Out of the 17% growth, around 4% is driven by foreign
exchange and the EBITDA and consequent to that 17% growth, our EBITDA has grown year on year by
28%. Can you move to the next slide? This is our sales mix, Compressors kind of continue to drive 92%
of our overall revenues. The mix has not changed, but when it comes to India and Rest of the World
(ROW), in particular, in this quarter, India has overperformed over ROW markets and that's how you
see a mix of 52% and 48%, I'll talk through a little bit more around that in my subsequent slides. If you
take a look at the geographical sales trend, India has shown tremendous improvement both year on
year and sequential quarters. So is the case with North America. Sequentially, we are able to maintain
a higher trajectory of revenue and there has been significant growth over previous year. In Europe,
our industrial business has seen growth year on year, but our portables business in Italy has seen
muted performance primarily because of economic downturn in various markets of Europe. As far as
Australia is concerned, we have seen good growth in our units business, whereas service has remained
slightly muted. Can we move to the next slide? So , this is our EBITDA reconciliation, if you start with
the reconciliation due to the volume growth of 17%, our EBITDA should have gone up by Rs. 650
million, we have seen an impact of increase in material costs throughout the year that started
progressively going up in the second quarter of the year and that's how you see an impact of Rs. 170
million inspite of increase in volume , the resulting contribution had its impact on the EBITDA. We
benefited due to foreign exchange compared to our results of the previous year, both in terms of INR
dollar and INR euro has remained positive, that has given us a positive benefit on the bottom line and
we've had increase in other expenses, as we mentioned, which comprises of increase in employee
cost and increase in other fixed expenses in relation to our overall business. So, this has landed up in
our overall EBITDA of Rs. 1850 million. This is the overall performance , P&L for the quarter, starting
previous year and sequentially the previous quarter. If you largely see, the EBITDA is actually grown
from 14.9% to 16.3%. We also had called out earlier during the quarter that we will be receiving a
tariff refund from the US and that's something which is baked in here and overall, after considering
the impact of that, we landed up with an overall PBT of 15%. Our net cash continues to grow . This
quarter we have added around, close to Rs. 200 million of cash, Of course, this is a quarter in which
we also paid out dividend, so, excluding the impact of dividend, that's seen on the right-hand side, the
cash profit from April to September has been healthy, Rs. 337 crores and we've invested in net working

conference over to Ms. Sakshi Mehta from MUFG Intime. Thank you and over to you, ma'am.
Sakshi Mehta: Good evening, everyone and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of
Tega Industries Limited. Today, we are joined by the senior management teams of Tega
Industries and Molycop. Representing Tega Industries are Mr. Mehul Mohanka, Managing
Director and Group CEO, Sourav Sen, CEO, Tega McNally, Mr. Pratik Basu Roy President,
Product Management and Mr. Ravi Joshi, Chief Financial Officer. Representing Molycop are
Mr. Lance Dawber, Chief Operating Officer and Mr. Patrick Koley, Chief Financial Officer.
I would now like to hand over the call to Mr. Mehul Mohanka for his opening remarks. Thank
you, and over to you, sir.
Mehul Mohanka: Thank you, Sakshi. Good evening and a warm welcome to all the participants on the call. Thank
you for joining us today. It's a pleasure to connect with our valued investors, analysts, and
stakeholders. I hope you and your families are keeping well. I'm pleased to share that the H1 of
FY 2027 was a period of strong growth and transformation for the Tega Group.
Our core business delivered its highest-ever first-half revenue, with healthy double-digit growth
in both revenue and EBITDA. The second quarter marked the first full quarter of Molycop's
consolidation, significantly expanding the scale and global reach of the group. For the first half
FY 2027, Tega Group on a consolidated basis delivered a revenue of INR59,775 million
compared to INR7,614 million in H1 of FY 2026, reflecting the complete consolidation of
Molycop from 1st of June 2026. EBITDA before one-time expenses was INR8,720 million, with
an EBITDA margin of 14.4%. One-time expenses of INR2,576 million relate to the Molycop
acquisition. In addition, an exceptional item of INR117 million reflects the inventory step-up
charge pursuant to the purchase price allocation. These costs are non-recurring in nature.
For the first half of FY 2027, for the Tega legacy business of consumables and equipment,
revenue from operations grew 20% to INR9,143 million from INR7,614 million in H1 of FY
2026, our highest-ever first-half revenue. EBITDA before one-time expenses grew 25% to
INR1,949 million from INR1,561 million, with margins expanding by 70 basis points to 20.4%
compared to the previous year of 19.7%, a clear demonstration of operating leverage.
Gross margins improved to 61% compared to 59% for the same period last year, supported by
favorable product mix and pricing discipline. For our consumables business, revenue grew a
robust 30% to INR8,117 million compared to the previous year period of INR6,264 million.
EBITDA grew 42% to INR1,916 million compared to the same period previous year of
INR1,346 million, with margins expanding by 190 basis points to 22.4%.

For our equipment business, revenue for the first half stood at INR973 million, reflecting the
timing of project execution. Importantly, we saw a strong sequential recovery in quarter two,
and our order book gives us a strong visibility of the second half.
For the second quarter of FY 2027, for the Tega legacy business of equipment and consumables,
revenue from operations grew 19% to INR4,825 million. Our highest-ever second-quarter
revenue, and grew 11% sequentially over quarter one. EBITDA before one-time expenses grew
11% to INR937 million, with an EBITDA margin of 18.8%. Consumables revenue grew 26% to
INR4,209 million, with EBITDA up 28% to INR905 million and margins improving to 20.8%.
Equipment revenue grew 72% sequentially to INR615 million from INR358 million in quarter
one, returning to positive EBITDA. Gross margins remain healthy at 60%.
For our grinding media business, the second quarter of FY 2027, which is our first full quarter,
revenue was INR37,716 million, which is equivalent to about US$396 million, and EBITDA of
For first half of FY 2027, for our grinding media business, which is June through September, a
period of four months, revenue stood at about INR50,632 million and an EBITDA of INR6,772
million. Transaction-related to one-time costs have tapered meaningfully from INR1,853 million
in quarter one to INR650 million in quarter two, with the bulk of these costs now behind us.
For the second quarter of FY 2027, Tega Group consolidated revenue from operations stood at
INR42,540 million and EBITDA before one-time expenses of INR6,081 million, at a margin of
14.2%. Our order book as of 30th September 2026, excluding our grinding media business,
stands at INR13,976 million, up 14% from INR12,313 million at the end of quarter one, with
INR11,576 million executable within the next 12 months.
This provides strong visibility and confidence in our growth trajectory. Within just a few months
of coming together, both Tega and Molycop teams have been working hard to deliver cross-
selling synergies, and we have initiated the journey towards realizing commercial synergies.
I am pleased to share that we have made a trial supply of Molycop's grinding media to one of
Tega's existing customers, starting with an initial volume of 500 tons. This trial creates an
opportunity for annualized supplies of over 30,000 tons. It is an early proof of our cross-selling
strategy, offering our combined portfolio to customers who already trust the Molycop and Tega
brands.
I want to thank our employees for their unwavering commitment, our customers for their trust,

after the acquisition and the working capital. This will help the audience to appreciate our

regional languages to strengthen critical risk identification while developing 40 certified

to deepen our relationships with global pharmaceutical companies, expand the range and complexity
of services we offer, and build the capacity and capabiliti es required to support customers over the
long term.

increased traction from our integrated outsourcing model, and steady progress on our capacity
expansion programme.

Tailwinds supporting supply chain diversification continue. We remain focused on converting these
opportunities into sustainable business growth.

Ministry of Science and Technology have proposed a dditional controls on the export of selected

relationships with global innovators, our integrated capabilities, our track record of supporting
customers across discovery, development, and manufacturing. The advantage increasingly lies with
CRDMOs that have scientific depth, infrastructure, and customer relationships to take on larger, more

incremental costs wherever applicable.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the PI Industries Q2 and FY27
earnings conference call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only
mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an
conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Siddharth from
CDR India. Thank you and over to you, Siddharth.
Siddharth Rangnekar: Good afternoon and tha nk you for joining us on the PI Industries Q2 and H1 FY27
earnings conference call. Today we are joined by senior members of the
management team including:
• Mr. Mayank Singhal, Executive Vice Chairperson and Managing Director
• Mr. Sanjay Agarwal, Group Chief Financial Officer
• Dr. Atul Gupta, CEO, CSM AgChem and Executive Director
• Mr. Jagresh Rana, Global CEO of PI AgSciences
We shall commence with key perspectives from Mr. Singhal, following which we will
have Mr. Agarwal sharing his views on the company's financial performance.
Thereafter, the forum will be open for question-and-answer session.
Before we begin, I would like to underline that certain statements made on today's
call could be forward-looking in nature. A disclaimer to this effect has been included
With that, I would like to invite Mr. Singhal to share his perspectives with you. Thank
you and over to you, sir.
Page 2 of 21
Mayank Singhal: Good afternoon, everybody and thank you for joining the call today. This has been a
difficult quarter in a difficult year for the industry. The global crop protection cycle is
at low points , and we are feeling like everyone in the business. What I want to do
this cycle stronger, more differentiated and more valuable.
PI has been through cycles before. In each one, we have made the same choice.
Keep investing in the capabilities that matter, take the hard decisions earlier than
later and come out the other side with a better business. This is exactly what we are
doing now. We have a strong track record of identifying emerging opportunities early,
investing ahead of the curve and translating differentiated capabilities into scalable
businesses.
PI has always taken opportunistic and unique approaches to business. We start with
innovative led agri -distribution, moved into CSM three decades ago and now I am
proud to say, with our investment in R&D beginning 12 years ago, we are now India's
first and only agchem innovator. With this long-term vision, we have consistently
delivered stronger execution and value creation.
We see similar potential in the platforms we are building today across the pharma
CRDMO, global biologicals and specialty & electronic chemical manufacturing driven
by continued innovation, capability development and customer engagement. These
platforms are in the buil d-out phase, and we are confident these investments will
increasingly contribute to our growth in time to come.
PI's core is reflected in our innovation, manufacturing and marketing excellence
through a decade of experience. We have been able to build the best-in-class assets,
leveraging differentiated technologies and assess newer areas of the market. We
talk a lot about innovation. We do so as the only Indian ag innovator. We continue to
invest in deploying and building a moat around scientific talent, infrastructure,
technology platform and product portfolios. These investments propel us into a
differentiated category from molecules to markets deepening customer engagement
and helping us build multi-engines for future growth.
Turning to the global crop protection market, channel stocks are back to normal
levels, and that part of the correction is behind the industry. Uneven weather across
the key geographies, rising input costs, tight channel credits meant growers bought
late, bought less and bought cheaper. Generic pricing pressure compounded that.
None of this changes the structural picture. The world has to feed more peopl e with
less land, less water, tighter regulations on what can be used. That is the only
Page 3 of 21
possibility with innovation in products and with supply chains that partner can trust.
Those are the two things PI spent decades building.
In India, the season was defined by the weakest monsoon in over a decade with
prolonged dry spells , delayed sowing and, as a result , lower pest pressure . Kharif
acreage was flat and the season was lacklustre. Going into rabi, soil moisture and
reservoir levels are below last year in several rain-fed belts, so we are planning for
a cautious Rabi and will respond to how the season actually develops.
On the brighter side, prices of major commodities have firmed up from their lows ,
which, if sustained, points to better farm economics in the next season.
Now let me take you to the PI businesses. Let me address our export business.
The environment remains hard : subdued crop economics, elevated input costs,
genericization arriving faster than the industry expected and pricing pressures
across the board. Considering the global market situation, we took pragmatic pricing
decisions in order to compete for a higher volume that comes with genericization.
Conversely, we have commercialized 20 plus molecules in the last three to five years
in different parts of the life cycle, carrying differentiated process technology and
innovator margins. Coupled with the ongoing diversification in our pipeline, they are
the engines of the next leg of growth in the business. Customers increasingly see PI
not just as a manufacturing partner but a trusted scientific partner who is capable

Adani’s Kutch Copper and Chile’s Codelco Sign Strategic MoU

Editor’s Synopsis
 Kutch Copper Ltd and Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile have signed a MoU
for exploration of Kaburkaala project in Chile.
 The MoU sets out terms for potential exploration partnership at the Kaburkaala
copper project in Chile’s Calama copper belt.
 The partnership links Chilean copper resources with Adani’s integrated copper
smelter complex at Mundra, India.
Ahmedabad/Santiago, November 12, 2026: Kutch Copper Ltd (KCL), a unit of Adani Enterprises
Ltd, and Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile (Codelco) today said they have signed a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for setting key terms of cooperation for forming a
strategic exploration partnership at the Kaburkaala project in Calama copper belt of the
Antofagasta Region in northern Chile, one of the most prolific copper districts in the world.
The MoU was signed recently in presence of Shri. Jeet Adani, Director KCL, Dr. Vinay Prakash,
CEO Adani Natural Resources and Mr Bernando Fontaine, Chairman Codelco, at LME Week 2026
in London.
“Critical resources, led by copper, are at the very heart of our future transformation. More than
just a mining asset, we view this strategic partnership as a long-term investment in India's
future. By securing robust access to global copper resources, we are building supply chain
resilience for the critical industries driving our nation's growth—spanning renewable energy,
advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, and technology. This partnership is a testament to our
commitment to enhancing India’s resource security and supporting its journey to becoming a
global economic powerhouse,” said Jeet Adani, Director, KCL.
“This MoU represents an important step in the work we have carried out with Adani over the
past year. This process demonstrates Codelco’s ability to attract world-class partners and create
value from its exploration portfolio, while safeguarding the long-term interests of the company
and the State of Chile,” said Bernardo Fontaine, Chairman of the Board, Codelco.
Page 2
For Adani, the proposed partnership, is a strategic step in building an integrated globally
diversified copper value chain, linking upstream resources in Chile with its copper smelter
complex at Mundra, India and securing long term access to a mineral that is key to
electrification and global energy transition.
For Codelco, this initiative is part of its strategy to create value from its exploration portfolio
through public private partnerships, sharing risks and accelerating the advancement of copper
projects with development potential.
The collaboration also strengthens India-Chile cooperation in critical minerals at a time when
resource security has become a strategic priority for both nations.
The proposed partnership would enable exploration of the Kaburkaala project to advance
through Adani’s contribution of capital, technology-led exploration and large-scale project
execution capability, combined with Codelco’s deep geological knowledge and international
experience, with both companies focused on responsible exploration, high standards of safety
and environmental stewardship, and long-term value creation.

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Parag Milk Foods Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen -only mode and there
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing st ar then zero on
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Brian D'Penha, Head of Investor Relations at Parag Milk
Foods Limited. Thank you, and over to you.
Brian D’Penha: Good day, everyone, and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call of Parag Milk Foods
Limited. From the management, we have with us Ms. Akshali Shah, Executive Director; Mr.
Rahul Kumar Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer; Mr. Rakesh Kothari, Chief Financial Officer;
Mr. Ankit Jain, Chief Strategy Officer; and myself, Brian D'Penha, Head, Investor Relations.
Before we begin, please note that some statements on this call may be forward -looking and
involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially. The full disclaimer is in the
earnings presentation shared with the stock exchanges. After the presentation concludes, we will
commence with the Q&A session.
Just a couple of points to remember. While asking a question, we request you to announce your
name and organization. We request that you limit your participation to one question at a time
and rejoin the queue if you have additional questions.
I now hand over to Ms. Akshali Shah for opening remarks. Over to you, Akshali.
Akshali Shah: Thank you, Brian. A very good afternoon to all of you, and thank you for joining us today. I'm
happy to connect with you once again with another strong quarter for Parag with highest ever
revenue of INR1,241 crores. In the same quarter last year, we crossed INR1,000 crores for the
first time ever.
And over the past 12 months, we have further added INR233 crores to that base, taking revenue
growth to 23%. What is equally important is the quality of the growth. Volumes grew by 12%
this quarter, which accounts to about half of the increase and the remainder came from pricing
and product mix.
For the first half, the revenue grew by 18% to INR2,185 crores, supported by 8% volume growth.
The quarter was, therefore, not as a one -off, but as the entire half of the year has moved to a
higher level.
Let me take you through where the growth came from. Our Flagship Categories, that is ghee,
cheese, paneer, curd remain the backbone of the business. They now make up to 63% of the
revenue at INR778 crores and grew 20% in value with 7% growth in volume. Alongside that,
our New Age business that is Pride of Cows and Avvatar has been scaling up rapidly. It grew
71% to INR154 crores, and it now contributes to 12% of our revenue, up from 9% a year ago.
Parag Milk Foods Limited
November 04, 2026
Page 3 of 21
Turning to the broader industry view. The Indian dairy sector continues to present attractive
long-term opportunities, supported by a growing shift towards organized and branded dairy
products. Consumers are increasingly prioritizing quality, safety, nutri tion and product
consistency.
Within this landscape, value -added dairy continues to emerge as an important growth driver,
reflecting evolving consumption preference, increasing demand for differentiated products. For
us, this evolving landscape presents an opportunity to build our stre ngth, sharpen our focus on
consumer needs and drive growth through differentiated product portfolios across our core and
value-added categories.
Awareness of protein and its role in balanced diet has risen considerably. And consumers are
increasingly seeking protein -rich products, lactose -free options and products with no added
sugar, along with greater transparency on the origin of their food.
Growing concern about adulteration has sharpened this further. And the consumers are placing
more trust in brands that they can rely on for purity and traceability. Parag is well placed to meet
these needs. Our integrated business model that is from our ow n farm, our own procurement
facilities gives us control over quality at every step and allows us to offer with assurance.
On the supply side, raw milk output is expected to grow by only 4% this year on account of
weather condition and higher product cost. With demand growing faster than supply, the
company's best placed to perform are those with sound procurement capabilities , differentiated
product portfolios and the ability to price in a measured manner. This is where Parag is
positioned, which then brings me to milk, the foundation of our business.
On an average, we procured 21 lakh litres of milk per day, which is about 5% more than a year
ago. And our average price this quarter was about INR45 per litre, that is 18% higher than a year
ago, when it was INR38 and about 7% higher than the sequential quarter.
It is insightful to look at the economics on per litre basis, wherein we see that as compared to
last year, our milk cost has increased by about INR7 per litre, while the gross margin per litre
has inched up from INR14 to INR17 per litre. This demonstrates our ability not only to navigate
the cost push, but also improve the overall profitability with richer product mix.
The result is that our gross profit for the quarter grew by 24% to INR323 crores with our gross
margins 26% versus 25.8% last year. The other expense grew mainly led by ASP spend and
other variable expense. ASP spend was pulled up for brand -building initiatives, while overall
ASP for the year is expected to be in range bound. During last year, there was a one-off item of
reversal of forex MTM post the conversion of FCCB into equity.
Excluding the same, EBITDA for the quarter has reached INR101 crores with 37% growth year-
on-year. EBITDA margin improved from 7.3% to 8.1% this quarter. PAT for the quarter grew
to INR42 crores with a growth of 42% year-on-year despite the current tax impact in the current
year.

description: Rain Industries Limited (RAIN) filed a "General Updates" announcement on NSE on 11 Nov 2026: Rain Industries Limited has informed the Exchange about Management Commentary on Un-Audited Financial Results of the Company (Standalone, Consolidated and Segment) for the Third Quarter ended September 30, 2026
body:
RAIN INDUSTRIES LIMITED

Sarang
Good day, ladies and gentlemen.
Welcome to Rain Industries Limited’s Question-and-Answer Session
for the third quarter of 2026. My name is Saranga Pani, and I am the
General Manager of Corporate Reporting and Investor Relations at
Rain Industries Limited.
The speakers for today are:
Mr. Jagan Reddy Nellore – Managing Director of Rain Industries
Limited;
Mr. Gerard Sweeney – Vice Chairman of Rain Carbon Inc.; and
Mr. T. Srinivasa Rao – Chief Financial Officer of Rain Industries
Limited.
Following the Earnings Presentation and Management Commentary
released on November 6, 2026, we received a wide range of questions
from investors and analysts covering near-term market conditions, our
medium- to long-term strategic priorities across business segments, and
balance-sheet management.
We will try to address these in a structured manner, providing as much
clarity as possible while keeping our responses focused and concise.
Page 2 of 26
Before we begin, management would like to note that today’s
discussion may include forward-looking statements concerning matters
such as expected outcomes, trends, targets, and strategic priorities.
These statements are based on our current expectations and are subject
to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ
materially. Investors should therefore consider the relevant risk factors
when assessing these statements.
With that, I will now request Gerard Sweeney to take the first set of
questions.
Sarang
Gerry, management previously highlighted that growth in aluminium
smelting outside China would expand our addressable market.
However, with significant Chinese -backed capacity additions and
intensifying competition in regions such as Indonesia and West Asia,
how competitive are we on delivered cost and logistics? In addition,
have competitors’ supply constraints enabled us to gain new customers
in either the Carbon or Advanced Materials segments?
Gerard Sweeney
Thank you, Sarang. On the first part of the question, every tonne of new
primary aluminium capacity, wherever it is built, adds to global
demand for CPC and coal tar pitch. With China operating close to its
government-imposed production cap, Chinese -backed producers are,
Page 3 of 26
for the first time, building smelting capacity outside China, notably in
Indonesia, Angola, Kazakhstan, etc., while smelters in the Middle East
and South Asia, especially India, have announced further expansions.
There are anode plants also being built in some of these countries to
supply anodes for the new smelters. Much of this new capacity lies
within economic shipping distance of our plants in India, North
America and Europe. Our long -term investments in flexible, multi -
modal logistics, together with our global blending model, allow us to
source raw materials widely and to supply customers from more than
one plant, which we believe keeps our delivered cost s competitive as
regional competition intensifies. The third quarter illustrated this
flexibility: as shipping in the Persian Gulf partially recovered, we
resumed deliveries to Middle East smelters, having made none in the
second quarter. On the second part, we are in regular contact with
almost every smelter and major carbon user, and our volumes to each
depend on market conditions, freight costs and competitors’ supply
constraints. While we would not describe these as entirely new
customer relationships, we have increased sales to certain less -
traditional Carbon and Advanced Materials customers in regions where
competitors faced supply constraints , and we see scope to build on
these relationships as new smelting capacity comes on stream.
Sarang
Thanks, Gerry. As European regulations such as the Carbon Border
Adjustment Mechanism , or CBAM , take firmer shape, how are our
Page 4 of 26
European carbon-distillation and calcination operations positioned
with respect to carbon costs? What capital expenditure may be required
over the medium term to maintain compliance and support the green
transition?
Gerard Sweeney
CBAM entered its definitive phase on 1 January 2026. Importers of
covered goods into the European Union now accrue a carbon cost on
the embedded emissions of those goods, with certificates priced off the
EU Emissions Trading System at about 75 euros per tonne of CO2 in
the first half of 2026. CBAM currently covers cement, iron and steel,
aluminium, fertilisers , electricity and hydrogen, and the European
Commission’s December 2025 proposal would extend it to downstream
steel and aluminium products. The vast majority of RAIN’s products ,
including CPC, coal tar pitch and our principal Advanced Materials
products, fall outside this scope, so we do not foresee CBAM-driven
capital expenditure at our European plants. Independently of CBAM,
we continue to reduce the carbon footprint of these plants by lowering
natural gas consumption and buying more green electricity, within our
normal, disciplined capital program. CBAM may also benefit RAIN
indirectly. By placing a carbon cost on higher -emission steel and
aluminium imports, it supports EU steelmakers, which supply the coal
tar processed at our European distillation plants , and EU aluminium
smelters, which buy our carbon products. We will continue to monitor
Page 5 of 26
the legislative process closely, particularly any further extension of its
scope.
Sarang
Thanks, Gerry. Continuing with the earlier topic, what is the current
operating and margin position of our European businesses, particularly
the HHCR plant and regional coal -tar pitch supply dynamics? Are we
seeing structural consolidation in Europe that could strengthen pricing
power? Also, following changes or exits in competitors’ footprints,
what is our strategic direction in North America?
Gerard Sweeney
This is another two -part question, so I will take it piece by piece. Our
HHCR plant and our coal tar distillation plants in Europe serve
different raw material and end -product markets. HHCR sales are
continuing, but we have temporarily taken HHCR production off -line
because European natural gas costs remain high relative to the prices
of HHCR imported into Europe from Asia, and we will keep this
decision under review as energy costs evolve. Coal tar pitch, by
contrast, is driven mainly by raw material availability. Several
permanent reductions in coal tar production have been announced in

Commenting on the results, Ms. Anisha Shastri, Director of Intense Technologies Limited, said:
“In the last quarter, we added three new clients to our portfolio, including two in the BFSI sector. These
wins reflect the continued relevance of our technology platforms and our ability to address evolving
enterprise requirements across customer communications, digital customer engagement, and
specialised technology services.
We remain focused on expanding our presence in India while strengthening our footprint in key
international markets, particularly the UAE and the UK. Our approach is centered on building stronger
client relationships, deepening our presence in strategic sectors, and identifying opportunities that
align with our core platform capabilities.
With the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) bringing data privacy and consent governance
into sharper focus, enterprises will increasingly need integrated capabilities to manage consent,
orchestrate consent-driven campaigns, and govern customer communications. Our Unified DPDP
Governance Platform is designed to address these requirements by embedding consent validation,
communication controls, and auditability into enterprise workflows, helping organisations strengthen
compliance readiness and reduce regulatory risks. Alongside this, we continue to advance our Al-led
platform strategy to enable hyper-personalised and context-aware customer engagement.
We are also pleased to be recognised in the TriAxis Matrix™ Customer Communication Management
(CCM), Q4 2026 Enterprise Market Assessment by AxisCube Research™. This recognition reinforces our
continued focus on building comprehensive enterprise communication capabilities.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on expanding our client portfolio, strengthening our market
presence, and scaling our platform-led business while delivering measurable value to customers and
creating sustainable growth for our stakeholders.
The moderation in revenue during H1 FY 2026-27, as compared to H1 FY 2025-26, is mainly due to the
completion of certain high-value, one-time projects that contributed substantially to revenues in the
previous corresponding period. With the successful closure of these engagements, the current period
reflects the absence of such project-based revenues, resulting in a temporary decline in the top line.”

LLP (“OMR”), both Promoter Group entities of the Company, under Reg ulation 7(2)(a) of the SEBI PIT

held by EPDPL and the re -creation of pledge over an equivalent number of equity shares of the
Company held by EPDPL and OMR, during the period from November 06, 2026 to November 11,
2026 (the “Transaction”).
Based on the disclosures received from the Promoter Group, we wish to place on record that:
(a) No additional pledge: the aggregate number of equity shares of the Company under
pledge by the Promoter Group remains unchanged before and after the Transaction. No
additional encumbrance has been created;
(b) No additional borrowing: the Promoter Group has not availed any new, additional or
enhanced borrowing or facility. There is no change in the underlying financing arrangement;
(c) Sole purpose – regulatory compliance: the Transaction has been undertaken solely to
comply with the lock -in requirements under Chapter V of the ICDR Regulations (defined
below).
The Company had, on October 12, 2026, allotted 3,25,18,900 convertible warrants (“Warrants”),
on a preferential basis to EPDPL, a member of the Promoter Group, under Chapter V of the
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure R equirements)
Regulations, 2018 (“ICDR Regulations”). In terms of the ICDR Regulations, the entire pre -
preferential shareholding of the allottee is required to be locked-in from the relevant date up to 90
(ninety) trading days from the date of allotment of such Warrants. As these 9,79,05,440 shares were
under pledge, the pledge was released to enable the lock-in, and thereafter an equivalent number
of shares was re-pledged.
The Promoter Group has converted all the Warrants at ₹111.51 per equity share, well ahead of
₹362.62 crore into the Company.
The full and early conversion of the warrants at ₹ 111.51 per share reflects the Promoter Group’s
continued commitment to, and confidence in, the long -term growth prospects of the
Company. Pursuant to the conversion, the shareholding of the Promoter Group in the
Company has increased from 42.68% to 43.99% of the paid-up equity share capital.
We reiterate that there has been no additional pledge and no additional borrowing by the

(SRE) 2410, 'Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the
Entity', issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Ind ia. This standard requires that we plan
and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material
misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of
persons responsib le for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review
procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with the
Standards on Auditing specified under section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013, and consequently
does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might
be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.
4. Basis for Qualified Conclusion
a. Proceedings under the PMLA concerning the Ebix group

by Provisional Attachment Order (“PAO”/ “Order”) No. 16/2026 dated June 05, 2026 under section

holding company of DWML, in Ebix Inc., USA, an intermediate holding company of DWML,
amounting to ₹8,930.30 million, and certain other assets of persons named in the Order. The Order
also contains restrictions concerning alienation, sale, transfer, modification or creation of any lien
or charge over assets and investments of Ebix Inc. and its subsidiaries, which include DWML and
its subsidiary Ebix Travels Private Limited (‘ETPL’), to the extent of ₹8,930.30 million. The ED's

Khushi Solanki: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone. On behalf of Arihant Capital, I welcome you to the earnings
