Balkishan Jalan: Yes. Thank you. Good afternoon everyone and welcome to our earnings call to discuss the
performance of second quarter and the first half year of the Financial Year 2027. In the interest of
those who are new to the company, let me first give a brief overview. Gala Precision is a preferred
manufacturing of the high quality precision components.
We serve sectors like renewable energy, industrial, and mobility, and we are geographically
diversified across India, Europe, and USA market. We supply to OEM, Tier 1, and channel partners
manufacturing customized products of over 800 SKUs for almost 175 active global customers across
25 countries.
Our facilities are fully equipped with the advanced technology and integrated capabilities for design,
development, and manufacturing. We achieved a 4-year revenue, EBITDA, and PAT at a CAGR of
22% 28% and 52% respectively. We have also established a new fastener manufacturing facility at
Chennai with installed capacity of 4,600 metric tons, focused on high tensile fasteners including
bolts.
The capacity utilization for this facility was 35% in FY26 last year and expected to go up 70% in
FY27 current year. The facility complement to our existing portfolio and offers strategic location
advantage through proximity to a customer across local job work vendor and nearby raw material
supplier, thereby supporting operational efficiency and customer serving.

Additionally, in alignment with the future growth plan, we already acquired 10 acre land parcel in
Wada near to the current plant location. Coming to the quarter under review, to deliver a highly
healthy performance supported by a strong order book growth and continued progress across all
strategy initiatives.
Order book grew by 44% year on year, crossing INR100 crores for the first time in a single quarter,
reflecting a healthy demand across all key end-user industries. On the revenue mix for the first half,
16%.
By end-user industry, renewable energy contributes 42%, industrial 33%, and mobility 25%. Export
customer approval for critical application in railway safety, offshore wind, and mining equipment.
We continue to make progress in the new product development across emerging applications
including offshore wind, electrolyzers, and railway safety.
crores, supported by the healthy development pipeline. On operational front, we commissioned over
1.2 megawatt AC open-access solar power plant at Nanded, Maharashtra on October 30th, 2026,
We also successfully implemented SAP HANA across all our manufacturing plants, with the system
go live on October 7th, 2026. Additionally, we secured a bank finance of INR58 crores comprising
the INR15 crores fund-based working capital, INR10 crores non-fund working capital for NCBG
facility, and INR28 crores for term loan.
Overall, we remain focused on strengthening our manufacturing capabilities, expanding our product
portfolio, deepening customer engagement across existing and emerging applications. Our growth
strategy includes identifying opportunities for Gala's existing products in emerging technologies like
hydrogen value chain, electrolyzer, electric vehicle, high-speed train.
Second, expand product range in fasteners and springs to address larger market size. Third, increase
presence in export market by hiring locals and having warehouse logistic tie-up in the Europe and
USA market. Fourth, moving up the value chain by offering advanced materials, kitting solution,

with us our group CEO and MD - Dr. Anish Shah, ED and CEO of our Auto and Farm business
- Mr. Rajesh Jejurikar and our Group CFO - Mr. Amarjoti Barua. Once the presentation
concludes, we will commence with the Q&A session.
For the purpose of completeness, I wish to read out the safe harbor. Certain statements in this
meeting with regard to our future growth projects are forward looking statements, which involve
a number of risks and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ materially from
those in such forward-looking statements.
With that, now I hand over to Dr. Shah for group overview.
Anish Shah: Thank you, Divya. And good afternoon, everyone. It's great to have you here with us. And good
morning, afternoon, and evening to folks online as well.
The keyword for this quarter is resilience. And you'll see that as we talk about what each of our
businesses has done. I guess all of you have seen the results already by now. So, we start with
the headline results, revenue up 25%, profit after tax up 25%, and ROE at 21%. In some cases,
this might sound as business as usual for us.
But this quarter has been a tough one. It has been one where we've seen multiple issues from
commodity prices to geopolitical issues to monsoon deficits and various other things. And
therefore, resilience has been really the center of focus for us and for each of our businesses.
There have been multiple proactive actions that businesses have taken that have helped drive
these numbers, and we'll talk about them. And while everyone's so focused on the short term, we
also want to take a step back from that and talk about the momentum that we still have for what
we promised you a couple of years ago, and where are we on that momentum to be able to build
businesses at scale with a significant level of profitability. So that's what we'll talk about today
as well, which is beyond what we usually talk about around the short term only.
Starting with consolidated results, revenue at ₹57,553 crores, up 25%. Profit after tax, ₹4,588
crore, 25% as well. Also, an important number on the bottom right-hand side of the screen, which
is year-to-date profits up 29%. So, a good start in the first half of the year, again, despite multiple
challenges that we've seen.
Where has this come from? And this is the one other important aspect of performance is that
multiple businesses have driven this. And that's what you're starting to see over the last few
quarters, is that it's not just the Auto and Farm business, which has always driven profits for us,
but multiple businesses are now playing an important role in driving profit.
Growth Gems are up again 3X, as they were last quarter.
This time we've got logistics playing a significant role . A huge turnaround in logistics, up to a
very good level of profitability as compared to where it was in fact loss-making last year.
We have Accelo up 70% as well, and their steel prices have had some role to play for Accelo's
growth.
Mahindra Finance up 61%, following the previous quarter where it was up 55% as well. So last
two quarters, Mahindra Finance has been on a very strong track, driven operationally, driven by
lower asset quality, tech and data making a huge difference. Back to growth now, an d I'll talk a
little more about Mahindra Finance in subsequent pages.
Auto up 55%, SUV volume, demand continuing to be strong, PLI plays a role in this number also
and offset by commodity inflation.
Tech M on track with the plan that we've outlined, and that's driving good growth and profits up
33%.
Farm down 9%, but given everything that's happened in this industry, we'll take this number.
And in addition to it, it's also something which Farm has solved for many international issues
and therefore is in a better place today than it was even a quarter ago.

What you also see is we did not have any monetization this quarter, but we did last year, and
therefore there is some takeaway in a sense from investments, which in the overall scheme of
results is not a bad thing as the operating company is driving perfor mance rather than any
monetization that's driving performance.
What we have always said is 15% to 20% EPS growth and 18% RoE. You've seen a broader
version of this chart, we've decided to just keep three years now here, and you see a 34%
compounded annual growth for EPS, RoE we are at 21%. I will repeat what I always say is 18%
is still our target. We may go slightly up, we may go slightly down, but we will stay with 18 as
a target. We will continue to stay with these commitments, even in tough environments. 15% to
20% EPS growth and 18% RoE is what we continue to stay as a commitment.
Resilience. Let's take a few businesses as examples here. Our Auto business, commodity and
supply chain constraints, both playing a key role. The offsetting factors were the actions taken
by the team on pricing, on hedging, on product mix . Diversifying the supplier base, increasing
capacity, we will be up 27% by the end of this year.
On the Farm side, in addition to inflation, it's monsoon deficit and international demand being
off quite significantly. There again, pricing, product refresh, accelerating exports in some areas,
completing some exits that we had to make internationally.
So, as we look at this combined, here's a view on what we've seen for commodity and in some
ways forecasting your question on what do you see for this quarter, what quarter three and what
do you see for next year? We haven't put numbers for inflation becau se you have them across
multiple commodities, but the 5 key areas that we see are around steel and base metals, rubber,
precious metals, currency and oil prices. We have increased prices in Auto by 5%, in Farm by
4%. We have taken cost actions as well as leverage from an operating standpoint that's benefited
us and that's helped us control the inflation aspect and be reasonably close in terms of where we
wanted our margins to be. Yes, we are o bviously lower as everyone is, but we are much less
lower as compared to anyone else in our respective industries.
As you look at Q3, we do see some marginal upticks possibly on steel and possibly on rubber,
but we do see precious metals coming down. They already have started coming down quite
significantly.
Currency can't forecast. We're seeing some strength over the last day, but not really going to

significant story, the business we have built over the past years and what sets it apart in Indian
out-of-home media space.
Our first half performance was more or less influenced by 2 external factors; the timing of the
festive calendar this year and measured approach to spend among multinational or global clients
as Navratri began on 11th of October this year vis-a-vis 22nd September last year that moved a
significant share of budget or wallet to the Q3 of this year.
At the same time, the multinational and the large corporate advertisers were careful because of
the global scenarios and the cost of fuel, which has challenging most of the consumers to sustain
with their second quarter budgets. That was felt most with the agency-led businesses, which are
more aligned businesses or intermediaries, which connects with us as a business partner.
Despite these headwinds, revenue from the half year has grew by 6%, the number INR286.8
crores is what we achieved. PAT rose by 11% to INR34.5 crores. The operating cash, which was
a struggle now has tripled to INR61.4 crores of greater significance.
However, in this direction which the business is moving, our core strength of digital media now
accounts for 1/3 of our revenue compared with a quarter or a year ago. The direct advertiser
relationship by Syed Arfath and team for about last 3 quarters has grown.

less reliant on the intermediaries businesses. As you all know, our listing journey started in 2024.

We thought we will focus more on our strategic priorities and some of the deliverables that we
have been working on and some of the deliverables that we will continue to work on. Just to set
the clock back in January of 2022, management of ICRA presented f ive strategic priorities for
the group that we have been working on, and we will continue to work on.
So these priorities have not changed. I'll take you through each one of these individually. The
first one relates to our Ratings business. Our primary focus here was obviously to continue to
grow the top line year after year and to expand our margins. And so me of you might recall in
2020 and 2021, our margins in this business were actually quite subdued.
So these two were primarily deliverables for us. I mean, as you can expect, any strategic plan
will have financial metrics articulated, which is naturally for our internal consumption and
monitoring.
Now in the last 5 years, that is between FY21 and FY26, the Ratings business has generated

The second strategic priority relates to the non -Ratings business, what we now refer to as the
Risk & Analytics business. Here, of course, we had two deliverables. One was to increase the
contribution of the Risk & Analytics business itself overall to the group revenues. This was
roughly about a third of the group revenues 5 years ago at the present time, or at least as of FY26
end, this is 50%, so which is the sort of mix that we as a management team would like to have.

and reduce the predominance of the KnowTech business. Not to suggest th at the KnowTech

BankTech and CapTech businesses. So this at the present time is roughly around 60:40 in terms
of mix. The KnowTech business contributes about 60% to the Risk & Analytics business and
40% is contributed to by the other businesses. Growing revenues as far as the Risk & Analytics
business again was a key imperative, and we have grown from INR 114.9 crores, which is what
we were at 5 years before, and we closed FY26 at INR 313 crores. The other deliverable for us
was to reduce the dominance of our anchor client from a revenue share standpoint. So that is

From an overall group perspective, our revenues more than doubled in the last 5 years. Group
revenues were at INR 301 crores in FY21, and this expanded to INR 646.9 crores at the end of
FY26. So these two are the two main priorities as far as revenues are concerned. And as you can
imagine, there are multiple levers that we have identified under these priorities, which we keep

But all I can say with respect to the last 5 years is that we have delivered with respect to whatever

among other things. So, we've been looking at a number of things over the last 5 years, and this

footprint, we have achieved our best to p-line performance across both standalone and
consolidated operations.
Our consolidated quarterly revenue crossed th e INR2,000 crores threshold, reaching INR2,257
crores, our best quarter ever, representing a growth of 17% year-on-year and 14% quarter-on-
quarter.
On a standalone basis, revenue scaled to an all-time high of INR1,722 crores, registering an
increase of 19% year-on-year and 18% sequentially. This performance was anchored by strong
execution across our primary growth engines, power generation, our distribution and aftermarket

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of Cohance
Lifesciences.
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today’s discussion may include forward-looking
statements that are subject to risk and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those
expressed or implied. We encourage you to review the disclosures filed by the company.
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Cyndrella Carvalho. Thank you, and over to you.
Cyndrella Carvalho: Thank you, Yash. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining the Cohance
Lifesciences earnings conference call to discuss our financial results the second quarter and the first
half of FY27. Today, we have with us: Umang Vohra, Executive Chairman and Group CEO; Yann
D'Herve, CEO Pharma CDMO; Gunjan Singh, CEO API+; Amrit Singh, CEO Specialty Chemicals;
and our new member, Abhimanyu Ojha, CFO. I will now hand over to Umang for his opening
remarks.
Umang Vohra: Thank you, Cyndrella. Good evening and good morning to everyone. Before I move to the speech, I
would like to say that we are deeply saddened by the loss of our colleague following the incident at
our Suryapet facility, and our thoughts are with his family and loved ones. We take this incident
extremely seriously and have initiated the necessary corrective and preventive action.
Safety and compliance will remain an absolute priority across all our operations. When we spoke at
the end ofQ1, we had said that Q1would represent the low point for the quarter. We expected
performance to improve sequentially fromQ2, followed by a return to year-on-year growth in the
second half. Q2 has progressed in line with that trajectory. Revenue increased 13% sequentially to
INR4767 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased to INR458 million, with the adjusted EBITDA
margin improving to 10%.
As we enterH2, our operating visibility is stronger. In small molecules, the order and reload position
for Q3and Q4has improved. We have also secured two new commercial programs and one late-stage
program with large global pharmaceutical customers, strengthening our relationships with these
customers and broadening the medium-term opportunity base.
In ADCs, we are seeing encouraging signs of development funnel, with improving order activity and
visibility, particularly towards the second half. The reorganization at NJ Bio is sharpening our
commercial focus and bringing our bioconjugation capabilities closer to Cohance is payload linker,
and manufacturing capabilities in India. Our bioconjugation capacity expansion remains on track for
commercial availability by early FY2028, further strengthening our end-to-end ADC offering.
Page 2 of 11
With the broader funding environment improving, alongside better momentum in the development
pipeline and order activity, our focus is on improving utilization and operating performance at NJ Bio,
with a clear objective of moving the business to breakeven. In nucleic acids, Sapala continues to
perform strongly. We are increasingly integrating its specialized chemistry and customer relationships
with Cohance’s development and manufacturing network.
This is one of the clearest examples of how the capabilities we have brought together can create a
broader proposition for our customers. Our API+ business continues to provide resilience to our
portfolio, while in Spec Chem, we are progressively repositioning the business towards a broader
innovator-led portfolio. Taken all together, we are beginning to see the different parts of Cohance
operate more effectively as one platform. Capital allocation and capability building are an important
part of our strategy.
We also have a broader capital program directed towards growth capabilities as well as quality,
safety, sustainability, and maintenance. We are planning to supplement the capabilities we already
have and build the adjacencies required to unlock the full integration potential of the Cohance
platform. This includes strengthening bioconjugation, building a more integrated ADC payload linker
capability, and enhancing our R&D infrastructure across payload linkers, APIs, and specialty
chemicals.
While we remain disciplined in deploying capital, with investments phased against customer
visibility, the objective is to address a larger part of our customer value chain, improve program
conversion, and create a more integrated development to manufacturing proposition. On quality and
compliance, we have completed USFDA inspections at Pashamylaram, Shamshabad, and
Jaggayyapeta and submitted our comprehensive responses. We are progressing the required CAPA
actions within the committed timelines, with regulatory compliance remaining an absolute priority
across all our facilities.
At this stage, we are also assessing any further impact from the Suryapet closure order. Based on the
visibility we have today, we continue to expect H2of FY 2027 to deliver year-on-year growth on both
revenue and EBITDA. This represents an important transition for us, from sequential recovery in
Q2to year-on-year growth in theH2. As I look ahead, I believe there is significant value yet to be
unlocked from the Cohance platform. There is a long way to go as we integrate our capabilities and
realize the full potential of our platform. With that, let me hand over to Yann.
Yann D'Herve: Thank you, Umang. I will build on Umang’s comments and focus on the operating progress across
small molecules, ADCs, and nucleic acids. Pharma CDMO led our sequential recovery in Q2, with
revenues growth of 34.5% quarter-on-quarter, primarily driven by a higher contribution from small
molecules. ADCs continue to see inventory destocking in commercial programs during the H1.
Also, improving orders visibility gives us greater confidence in the H2 trajectory. While Pharma
CDMO revenues remain lower by 27% year-on-year in Q2 and 32% in H1, we expect the sequential
momentum to sustain through the H2. Niche technologies contributed 13.7% of revenue in Q2 and
14.4% in H1. At Cohance standalone, commercial revenues remained healthy at around 78% of sales.
Also, the quarter had an adverse product mix. The forward position has strengthened considerably.
We have received multiple reload orders across existing commercial programs, providing better
visibility into Q3 and Q4, as well as next year.
Page 3 of 11
During Q2, we also secured three significant lateral programmes from large global pharmaceutical
customers, two commercial programs, and one phase III program. These awards are important
because they deepen our participation with strategic customers. Our late-stage and commercial RFP
activity has also strengthened. Our phase III programs stood at net 11, and our commercial products
moved to 19.
On quality, the improvement program continues to progress. Turning to ADCs, H1 performance was
affected by continued customer destocking across two established commercial programs. While this
has affected near-term payload demand, the development funnel is moving in the right direction. We
are seeing a broader range of RFQs across payload and linkers, including opportunities that can
potentially be developed and manufactured from India. We are also progressing a customized payload
program for a large pharmaceutical customer through scale-up, which could generate higher potential
in the coming fiscal year.
At NJ Bio, we have increased and refocused business development resources and sharpened
commercial accountability. From a capability perspective, our investments are intended to connect
payload and linker development and manufacturing in India with bioconjugation, analytical, and
development capabilities at NJ Bio.
This is important because it allows us to participate across a larger part of the ADC value chain. We
are beginning to see this translate into execution. During Q2, NJ Bio successfully delivered two ADC

Siddharth Borkar: Thank you, Jyotiraditya, for hosting us. Hello and welcome everyone to the Q2 FY27 results for
Orkla India. I am Siddharth Borkar, Head of M&A and Investor Relations. At Orkla India. I am
joined by Mr. Sanjay Sharma, Managing Director and CEO at Orkla Indi a, and Ms. Suniana
Calapa, CFO at Orkla India.
I hope you have gone through the investor presentation and other materials that we have
uploaded. In today's call, we will walk you through some of the key highlights of the quarter,
and then we'll open the floor for Q&A. I would want to draw your attentio n to the disclaimer
slide as stated in our earnings presentation. With that, I hand it over to Sanjay.
Sanjay Sharma: Thank you, Siddharth, and a very good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us. I am
Sanjay Sharma, Managing Director and CEO for Orkla India, and I'm also joined by our CFO
Suniana Calapa to take you through our results. For those people who have joined us for the first
time, we are going to be tracking the presentation that we've uploaded and if you are following
the same, I will keep talking about the slide numbers that we are on.
But for those people who are joining us for the first time, I would encourage you to refer to slide
spending time on that today. Let me start with the 3 key messages, that I would like you to take
away from today.
First the growth has accelerated and is broad -based. The revenues have grown by about 18.4%
in Q2, and volume growth is improving. The second, the profitability remains healthy despite
elevated input costs. Brands and strategic growth initiatives. Third, two of our strategic projects
that we've been talking about in the past calls also, which is Project Bolt and Kerala distribution
restructuring, are translating into tangible results on ground.
Now let me take you through our performance for Q2 FY27. So if you now move to Slide 7,
which gives you an executive summary of the results. Overall, we are encouraged by how our
business has progressed in Q2. Building on the start in Q1, the revenue growth has actually
accelerated further to 18.4%, with volumes growing 2.9% and EBITDA growing at 12.6%.
Orkla India Limited
November 04, 2026
Page 3 of 16
As mentioned in the last quarter, the growth continues to be broad -based across categories as
well as geographies. Spices grew at 25.1% across all geographies, with Kerala driving the overall
growth. A large part of this was price-led, and volumes were positive as well. Convenience foods
grew at 7.7% against a higher base as last year's Q2 included the festive period.
Our domestic business was particularly strong, growing at 20%, with Eastern leading the growth,
driven by a resilient Indian economy, healthy consumer demand, and a strong execution focus
that we have had across our portfolio. Our international business co ntinued its upward growth
trajectory, growing at 11.7%, with GCC growing 22.7 % in a continuing volatile geopolitical
environment.
Innovations remain an important pillar of our growth strategy, and we have maintained a strong
pace of launches, 23 in the last quarter and another 15 in this quarter, bringing it to 38 in the first
half. These address emerging consumer needs, particularly amongst younger consumers in the
top metro cities.
And finally, on profitability, the input cost environment remains elevated and we continue to
invest behind our brands and strategic growth initiatives. So EBITDA grew more slowly than
revenues. Even so, the margins remain healthy at 15.9%. We move to Slide 8. Before I hand
over to Sunaina for the financials, let me give you a quick update on the 2 key projects, starting
with Project Bolt.
Project Bolt is an endeavor to strengthen our play in the emerging quick commerce segment and
now enters the final quarter of its implementation and realization. Strategically, our goal is to
build our business across the top 28 cities in India by strengthening our ca pabilities. We are
doing this at 2 levels. First, we're building our current portfolio. We've increased our ANSP
investments in consumer reach and demand generation as part of the investments behind our
brands and growth initiatives that I mentioned earlier. We are already seeing a meaningful
expansion in our digital reach. Consumer reach has tripled through scaled social media content.
Second, build a Gen Z-focused portfolio through innovations. We are using digital commerce to
take differentiated propositions to our target consumer cohorts and to test and scale products
beyond their traditional markets. This is an attractive platform to take relevant innovations and
our South Indian food propositions to consumers across India. These interventions are
translating into business outcomes.
Digital commerce increased its contribution to our domestic business from 8.9% in Q1 FY27 to
10% in Q2 FY27. At the same time, digital commerce revenues from rest of India has grown at
33.6% year-on-year in Q2, encouraging evidence that the channel can hel p our brands travel
beyond their traditional strongholds.
So Project Bolt brings together targeted brand investments, greater consumer engagement, and
innovation to build digital commerce into a meaningful growth platform for Orkla India while
progressively expanding our addressable market across India. Let me now turn to our s econd
project, the Kerala distribution restructuring, and we can move to Slide 9.
Orkla India Limited
November 04, 2026
Page 4 of 16
The second part the second project is the Kerala distribution restructuring, which continues to
progress as planned. As we discussed last quarter, the objective is to build a more fit-for-purpose
route-to-market across our key categories and channels. There are 3 priorities: strengthening
convenience foods, improving our position in standalone modern trade, and expanding outlet
coverage for spices. Let me take them in turn.
In convenience food, our execution continues to improve. Sales productivity, which reflected
the number of bills invoiced, has increased to 1.27 times the Q4 levels, Q4 FY26 levels. Effective
coverage, which measures the number of outlets served, has increased by 1.1x. Importantly, both
metrics have improved sequentially through Q1 and Q2, giving us confidence that the new model
is helping us serve more outlets while also improving sales productivity.
In standalone modern trade, the restructuring commenced in June and has moved into
implementation. Here too, early signs are encouraging.

Quarter 2 of financial year '27 marks an important step in Saatvik's journey. It was a quarter in
which our execution caught up with our order book and one of significant progress on our
strategic priority, the transition to a more integrated solar manufacturing platform.
Before I take you through the quarter, let me place it in the context of where Saatvik stands
today. Our established manufacturing base is at Ambala in Haryana, where we have 4.8
gigawatt of module capacity and 2 gigawatt of encapsulant capacity.
Our next-generation integrated hub is at Gopalpur in Odisha, which is where the next phase of
our growth is being built. Our scale and quality have been recognized externally. We were
ranked among the world's top 21 solar PV module manufacturers by Terawatt PV Research in
the first quarter of 2026 and amongst India's top four leading module suppliers by Mercom
India.

Let me begin with an update on our Odisha integrated manufacturing project, which is the key
milestone in this transition. The phase one project, spread across 57 acres, comprises 2.4
gigawatt of cell manufacturing capacity and 4 gigawatt of module manufacturing capacity. I
am pleased to share that commercial production at our 1.3 gigawatt module manufacturing
facility in Gopalpur commenced successfully on 2nd November, 2026, and we expect the full
4 gigawatt capacity to be in place by December 2026. This will take our operational module
capacity from 4.8 gigawatt at Ambala to 8.8 gigawatt, both combined Ambala and Odisha.
On the cell manufacturing side, the 2.4 gigawatt line has moved from installation to trial run,
which has commenced, and we are targeting production ramp-up by December 2026. The
ALMM List-II inspection has been called for and is planned within November 2026. The
Odisha facility represents a significant step forward in strengthening our manufacturing
capabilities.
With both cell and module capacities coming up at the same location, we will be able to serve
customers with a more integrated and resilient manufacturing platform. Beyond phase one, we
are progressing with the next stages of our manufacturing expansion. Phase two, spread across
27 acres, envisages an additional 3.6 gigawatt of cell manufacturing capacity, taking our total
cell capacity to 6 gigawatt, with completion targeted in FY 2028.
In parallel, we have initiated planning for phase three, which envisages 6 gigawatt of ingot and
wafer manufacturing capacity. Phase three is targeted for completion in FY 2029 and is
aligned with the ALMM List-III requirement, which applies from June 2028. Taken together,
this is how our value chain is being built.
In modules, we have 6.1 gigawatt live today and will add 2.7 gigawatt by December 2026,
taking us to 8.8 gigawatt. In cells, the 2.4 gigawatt line has commenced trial runs, with
production ramp-up targeted for December 2026, followed by 3.6 gigawatt in phase two in FY
2028. In encapsulants, we have 2 gigawatt live and are adding 3 gigawatt by FY 2028, taking
us to 5 gigawatt. In ingots and wafers, 6 gigawatt is planned for FY 2029.
Each stage has a defined capital plan and a defined timeline, and together, they will
progressively deepen our backward integration, strengthen supply chain resilience, and build a
more comprehensive domestic solar manufacturing ecosystem. Against this backdrop, Q2
FY27 was a quarter of improved execution.

Tata Power Delivers Highest-Ever Quarterly Profit Driven by
Broad-Based Growth Across Businesses
• Records Highest-Ever Quarterly PAT of ₹ 1,652 crore; H1 FY27 PAT reaches all-time
high to ₹ 3,053 crore
• Capital Expenditure close to ₹10,000 Crore in H1 FY27 & on track to meet annual
guidance and to support India's Clean Energy and Grid Infrastructure Build-Out
• Disciplined Capital allocation strengthens Integrated Energy Play leading to growth
across RE, T&D and Generation clusters
• RE Platform comprising Genco, Manufacturing, Rooftop Solar and storage continues
as a key earnings growth driver, posting sustainable and scalable growth
Result Highlights:
• Record profitability: Q2 FY27 PAT rises to an all -time high of ₹ 1,652 crore, up 33% YoY,
driven by strong performance across all business clusters and H1 FY27 Reported PAT
reaches ₹ 3,053 Cr up 22% YoY.
PAT Before Exceptional Items is ₹ 1,521 crore, up 22% YoY for Q2 FY27 and ₹ 2,922 crore,
up 17% YoY for H1 FY27
• Strong financial momentum: Revenue grows 26 % YoY to ₹ 19,886 crore, while EBITDA
increases 5% YoY to ₹ 4,245 crore during Q2 FY27.
• Sustained H1 performance: H1 FY27 PAT, Revenue and EBITDA reach record levels,
reinforcing the strength of Tata Power's diversified portfolio. Revenue grows 17 % YoY to ₹
38,784 crore, while EBITDA increases 7% YoY to ₹ 8,494 crore in H1 FY27.
• Investing ahead of growth: Capital expenditure of ~ ₹10,000 crore in H1 FY27 reflects
accelerated execution across renewable energy, transmission infrastructure, pumped storage
and distribution networks. Renewables deployed ~₹6,000 crore of capex in H1 FY27.
Growth Levers:
• Installed 765 MW of Clean & Green generation capacity in H1 FY27, taking the total installed
Clean & Green capacity to 8.6 GW
• Renewables continue to lead growth: Improved profitability driven by utility-scale projects,
increasing rooftop solar adoption and solar manufacturing delivering robust margins.
• Solar manufacturing gains scale: in Q2 FY27 Produced 0.9 GW of solar cells (1.8 GW in
H1 FY27) and 1 GW of solar modules (2.0 GW in H1 FY27) , in addition profitability was
aided by better sales mix and industry leading module yield of 97%
• Rooftop solar leadership strengthened: Market-leading position with 426 MWp installations
in the quarter, reinforced through expanding installations, channel partnerships and consumer
financing initiatives.
• Transmission and Distribution deliver strong earnings growth: Expansion of network
assets and improved operational efficiencies continue to support profitability. Our Odisha
discoms continues to build efficiencies, leading to reduced AT&C losses
• Building National & Regional energy security: Construction progresses on track for the
600 MW Khorlochhu Hydropower Project, where Tata Power has 40% stake and the 1,000
MW Bhivpuri Pumped Storage Project.
• Accelerating Clean Energy Integration: Executed a 60 MWh BESS project in
Mumbai to support renewable energy growth, strengthen grid stability and deliver
reliable 24x7 power.
National, November 11, 2026: Tata Power, one of India's largest integrated power companies,
delivered its highest-ever quarterly Profit After Tax (PAT) of ₹ 1,652 crore in Q2 FY27, up 33% year-
on-year, demonstrating the strength of its diversified and future-ready energy portfolio. Revenue rose
26% to ₹ 19,886 crore and EBITDA increased 5% to ₹ 4,245 crore during the quarter.
For H1 FY27, the Company reported record PAT of ₹ 3,053 crore, up 22% year -on-year, while
Revenue grew to ₹ 38,784 crore and EBITDA reached ₹ 8,494 crore, refl ecting strong operational
performance across businesses.
The quarter's performance was driven by broad-based growth across Generation, Renewables,
Transmission & Distribution and emerging consumer -focused green businesses. The quality and
resilience of the earnings continue to strengthen, with regulated and long-term contracted businesses
accounting for an increasing share of EBITDA, providing greater predictability and visibility of cash
flows and profitability.
During H1 FY27, the Company invested ~₹10,000 crore, its highest half -yearly capital deployment,
reinforcing its commitment to building critical infrastructure to meet India's growing energy needs and
support its transition towards a secure, reliable and sustainable energy future.
India's electricity demand continued to witness sustained growth in H1 FY27, driven by industrial and
economic activity, agricultural consumption, rising household demand, increasing EV adoption and
the expanding data centre ecosystem. Extreme heatwaves and a delayed monsoon further
accelerated cooling-related consumption, reinforcing the need for reliable and uninterrupted supply.
Tata Power is well-positioned to address this evolving demand through its diversified portfolio of fuel-
secure thermal generation assets, expanding renewable energy capacity, energy storage solutions
and robust transmission and distribution infrastructure.
Renewable businesses remained a key driver of earnings growth, underpinned by 1.4 GW of capacity
additions over the last twelve months, strong manufacturing margins and yields, and continued
leadership in rooftop EPC with over 5.1 GWp of cumulative installations. Odisha distribution continued
its strong operational performance, with AT&C losses improving by 5.7% over Q1 FY27. Following
Cyclone Arnab, electricity supply was restored within 48-72 hours in affected area, highlighting the
resilience of the tech powered network and operational capabilities of field teams. AI-led digitalisation
is being scaled across operations to drive efficiency, pred ictive maintenance and improve customer
experience.
The Company’s Conventional generation assets delivered strong operating and financial
performance. Mundra plant continues to operate at full capacity and runs currently under Section 11
till December end. Company is actively advancing discussions with multiple states to secure
Supplementary Power Purchase Agreements (SPPAs), which are at an advanced stage.
Tata Power is also advancing its pumped storage hydro portfolio, with construction at Bhivpuri PSP
progressing on schedule and Board approval secured for the capital commitment for the Shirwata
project, reinforcing its commitment to building long-duration energy storage capacity to support India’s
evolving power requirements.

0:0:7.538 --> 0:0:26.338, Don Devprakash
Hello All. Good afternoon and good evening wherever you are, in different parts of the world. We have
Amit, the Joint Managing Director, and Mr Shashikanth, the Manging Director on the call today. Amit
will be leading the call today, and Mr Shashikanth will come in during the Q&A session. Over to you,
Amit.
0:0:30.858 --> 0:0:34.738, Amit Dixit
Yeah, thanks, Don. Can you confirm that you can see my slides?
0:0:36.498 --> 0:0:37.218, Don Devprakash
Yes, Amit.
0:0:37.978 --> 0:0:40.418, Amit Dixit
Okay, good evening, everybody. So, I'll start with the slides. First, the usual disclaimer. There will be
forward-looking statements. There may be forward-looking statements in the call, which are based on
our belief today, and the actual results might be different.
So, for those who are new to the company, we design and supply critical control intensive electronic
control units, that is ECUs. So, our main products are ECUs. Many of the ECUs that we sell have some
unique technologies, novel technologies that we have built in-house. So, the entire product
development, technology development, as well as manufacturing, is all done in-house. We don't have
any technical collaboration. And our customers are OEMs of vehicles or industrial equipment in India,
US, and Europe. In the chart, you see the number of control intensive ECUs that we have sold over the
past 12 months, trailing 12 months, ending at Q2 FY27 and for the three previous periods. We publish
this information of the number of control intensive ECUs sold every quarter. So, at the start of the next
quarter, towards the early start of next quarter, we publish this information. And since today, you
know, pretty much all our revenue comes from the sale of ECUs. This number has a fairly strong
correlation with our revenue. You know, those who have followed us for some time would be aware of
this. So, if you look at the numbers for TTM Q2 FY27, we have sold nearly 4.6 million of this control
intensive ECUs, and you know, of course, apart from this, we also sell other types of ECUs as well. This
4.6 million number, is 44% growth on a year-on-year basis. Okay, so with respect to this 3.2 million. So,
it's a fairly strong growth.
Coming to the Q2 and H1 numbers, from FY25 to FY26, we had very strong growth, about 60%
revenue growth, and the growth has continued in FY27 as well, on the back of, you know, already what
was a very strong growth. Both Q2 and H1 have been the highest ever for us. In both cases, 40% plus
revenue growth is seen. In terms of percentage, EBITDA, there has been a bit of a dip. And the main
reason for this is the raw material cost increase. As we would all know, we are in the middle of a, you
know, sort of a high inflation of pretty much all commodities. For some commodities, it's effectively a
hyperinflation sort of a stage. That is the primary reason for the dip in the EBITDA percentage. In fact,
because of the strong revenue growth, we have had operating leverage kick in, which has offset some
part of the raw material increase. Okay, and on the PAT, there is some unevenness, mainly because this
financial year we have moved to the new tax regime, compared to the old tax regime that we had in
the previous financial year.
Now coming to the TTM numbers, for the last four years, so this gives a sort of a filtered view which
takes out the sort of seasonal fluctuations and gives a sort of a longer view, longer term view. Our
three-year strong revenue growth CAGR, has continued, so about 38% three-year CAGR and about
48% year on year. So, you can, see this 48% correlates with the 44% rise in the number of control
intensive ECUs. So, we have a very strong CAGR on the revenue growth, three-year CAGR and even
higher in the profitability matrix, obviously on account of the operating leverage. On the ROCE, there
is a bit of a dip, and it is mainly happening because we are investing aggressively for the last few
quarters on increasing our manufacturing infrastructure. So, we are investing in two new plants, and
those plants are yet to become operational. So naturally, there is a dip in ROCE, but still, it's quite a
healthy number. So today we continue to have a very strong combination of high revenue growth,
very healthy profitability, and a very strong capital efficiency.
Now coming to business updates for our current markets, on the mobility side. So, these are the
updates from H1 FY27. On the mobility side, our ISG ECU for export ICE 3 wheelers have fully ramped
up. This was launched in the last financial year. Now it has fully ramped up. So now there is
widespread penetration of our ISG ECU in both domestic, as well as export ICE three-wheelers. Our
electric two-wheeler MCU, which was also launched in FY26, has also fully ramped up. And as we will
see later in the slides, the percentage revenue from EV is in keeping with the E2/3 wheeler penetration
for us.
Our ISG+EFI ECUs are also seeing a solid ramp up. Within 2 years of the first introduction, we have
shipped more than 1 million in quantity. This is going to be a key product for us going ahead, since it
creates the case for ISG adoption a lot more compelling.
We had mentioned at the start of the year that we are expecting the introduction of our ISG on 3 top
10 motorcycle models, and two of them have already happened and are also fully ramped up. And
one of these two models is expected to shift to ISG+EFI in the coming financial year, FY28. So, this is
another example of value proposition of ISG+EFI, where we are able to get more business, in this case,
the EFI portion of it, on account of having a strong product and a strong competitive position.
We have also had a business win for the ISG ECU and the Electric Motor, that is the Magneto Kit from
a European 2/3-wheeler OEM. And the start of production is likely to happen in H1 of FY28.
Now coming to the industrial side, there was a weaker 2025 Atlantic hurricane season activity in North
America, which has a sort of correlation with the home standby generators that get bought in North
America. So, because of this, there has been a reduced demand for EFI ECUs. But for H1 we have
already started seeing signs of some demand recovery. So going ahead, we expect this to recover.
On the markets under development, on the commercial vehicle side, both engine powered as well as
electric, we expect a set of products to get into production. We had mentioned this in the last call as
well, and things are on track. So, our after-treatment controller, EFI ECUs and MCUs should get into
production in the coming few quarters. On the power tool side, the electric power tool side, our motor
controller along with the sensor less control technology, which we are a pioneer, is expected to get
into production in H1 of the next financial year. This particular opportunity is not a very high volume
one, but it is an entry into a massive market. The number of power tools that get made, which require
this sort of a motor controller is in hundreds of millions. Okay, so if we end up having some sort of

in the listen -only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the

Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star
hand this conference over to Rajesh Majumdar. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Rajesh Majumdar: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on Balrampur Chini Mills
Q2 FY 2027 Results Conference Call. We have with us today Mr. Vivek Saraogi, Chairman and
Managing Director of Balrampur Chini Mills, Ms. Avantika Saraogi, Executive Director, and
Mr. Pramod Patwari, Chief Financial Officer of the company. We would now like to begin the
call with brief opening remarks from the management, following which we will have the forum
open for the question-and-answer session.
Before we start, I would like to point out that some statements made in today's call may be
forward-looking in nature . And a disclaimer to this effect has been included in the results
presentation shared earlier. I would now like to invite Mr. Saraogi to make his opening remarks.
Over to you, sir.
Vivek Saraogi: Thank you, Rajesh, and a very warm good afternoon to everybody, and thank you for joining us
on our conference call. I trust all of you have had the opportunity to go through our results
presentation, providing details of our operational and financial perf ormance. I will give you a
brief update on the sector, followed by our company's highlights.
The 2025 -2026 sugar season has turned out to be tighter than expected, with lower -than-
expected production, resulting in a drawdown in inventory. The closing stock for the season is
3.6 million tonnes, providing an initial cushion for domestic availability. The tighter demand -
supply balance has led to firming up of domestic sugar prices, providing relief to millers and
offsetting higher cane costs and pressure on ethanol margin. Looking ahead to the 2026 -2027
season, production is expected to decline, and the demand-supply balance, we will talk about it.
I will give you a detailed thought in the question-answer session.
This is owing to predominantly lower production expected in Maharashtra and Karnataka, owing
to the El Niño conditions, while production in U.P. is expected to be relatively stable because of
the water availability and better irrigation facilities. These factors, we expect that domestic prices
will hence remain firm. Government has taken various measures to ensure adequate availability
to contain the sharp rise in prices. And currently, the first step is to allow TRQ of 10 lakh tons.
In this environment, maintaining the right balance between sugar availability and imports will be important to maintain stable
prices and healthy industry economics, together with balancing the needs for our other
stakeholders, the farmer and the consumer.
Turning to our performance, company has delivered a strong performance during a seasonally
weak quarter. Strong volume coupled with improved realization resulted in sugar segment PBIT
to increase by 166% to INR140 crores during Q2 2027 as compared to corresponding quarter

again over three years. FRP is increased by 16%, ethanol price has not gone up. Including this
year 20% with no corresponding increase in ethanol price. U.P. government is yet to announce

The industry prospects will remain closely aligned with the cane price announcement and the
import policy of the government, together with the domestic production.

is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Mohit Kumar from ICICI Securities.
Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Mohit Kumar: Thank you, Alaric. Good morning. On behalf of ICICI Securities, I welcome you all to Premier
Energies Q2 FY27 earnings conference call. Today, we have with us from the management, Mr.
Chiranjeev Singh Saluja, Managing Director, Mr. Nand Kishore Khandelwal, Chief Financial
Officer, Mr. Vinay Rustagi, Chief Business Officer, and Mr. Sudhir Moola, Chief Strategy
Officer. Now, I would like to hand over the floor to the management for the opening remarks,
post which we will open the floor for Q&A. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Chiranjeev Saluja: Thank you, Mohit. Am I audible?
Mohit Kumar: Yes, sir, you are. Please go ahead.
Chiranjeev Saluja: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today for our Q2 earnings call. I am
Chiranjeev Saluja, Managing Director at Premier Energies, and I am joined today by my
colleagues, Mr. N.K. Khandelwal, Group CFO, Sudhir Reddy, Director, and Vinay Rustagi,
Chief Business Officer. The company has reported another sterling quarter with total revenue
increasing by 38.2% Y-o-Y to INR2,656 crores on a consol basis.
EBITDA and PAT have grown by 17.8% and 30.8% Y-o-Y to INR760 crores and INR462 crores
respectively. EBITDA and PAT margins in the solar manufacturing business came in at 29.3%
and 17.9% respectively. The PAT margin has moderated slightly because of increase in
depreciation and reduction in other income. Transcon, our subsidiary, has reported another good
quarter with revenue and PAT of INR122 crores and INR18 crores respectively. EBITDA and
PAT margins came in at 15% and 8%.
Amongst key business update, our 7 GW TOPCon cell line has been commissioned. Trial runs
are currently underway, and commercial production is expected to start later this month. Our
operational cell plants delivered a record capacity utilization in the quarter, showcasing our all-
round operational excellence. A highlight of the quarter was new order wins totaling INR4,001
crores for cells and modules in a highly competitive market, taking our total order book to
INR16,260 crores.
The transformer business also saw a healthy intake, reflecting higher capacities, taking the total
order book in the transformer company to INR330 crores. I am happy to update that all our
expansion initiatives, including battery energy storage, are on track. Solar capacity addition has
been steady throughout this year, with growth in PM Surya Ghar Yojana compensating for slight
weakness in the utility scale segment.
We expect project commissioning progress to accelerate over the next six months, taking the
annual capacity addition to around 50 GW AC territory, surpassing last year's numbers. More
Premier Energies Limited

importantly, the long-term outlook for the sector remains compelling, with the government
looking to reduce dependence on fossil fuel imports and fighting climate change.
Recent policy announcements on bolstering transmission and storage capacity additions are
expected to unlock the next cycle of growth for the solar sector. Commodity price inflation in
wake of the Middle East war has hit the solar sector with material increases in prices of key raw
materials and delay in delivery timelines. However, I am pleased to say that we are navigating
this period successfully with careful supply chain management and investments in scale and
technology. As new capacity ramp up over the next few quarters, we expect a major step up in
financial performance of the company.
At the same time, we are also evaluating several new primary and secondary growth
opportunities. Our balance sheet strength, as reflected in low cost of capital and an A+ credit
rating, is a key pillar of our business competitiveness. We remain focused on disciplined growth,
leveraging our key operational strength alongside prudent risk allocation. Thank you. We are
now open for questions.

localize in the near term to achieve the 40% DCR requirement? Second would be, what is the
status of our approval of new 7 GW capacity from MNRE, and has it stabilized?

Shubham Borade: Yes, sure. What is the status of our approval of new 7 GW capacity from MNRE, and has it
stabilized? I hope I was audible.
Chiranjeev Saluja: Sure. Okay, I'll let Sudhir Reddy answer the first question on our battery manufacturing plans
and localization plans, and the second question, I will take it after him. Sudhir.
Sudhir Moola: Thank you. On the Battery Energy Storage System, we expect to operationalize the Battery
Energy Storage System in Q2 2027. With respect to localization, we are working out on
localizing the container manufacturing. We are trying to localize some of the fire suppression
systems inside it to achieve the 40% localization that is being asked by the government for the
various subsidy programs. Also, on the software part also, we have tied up for providing Indian-
made EMS for the Battery Energy Storage System. So that's our plan on the Battery Energy
Storage. I hope that's clear.
Chiranjeev Saluja: Yes. So our plan is to do cell to pack and pack to container. This is what the manufacturing plant,
what we are setting up. On your second question on 7 GW cell line at Naidupeta, we have already
made our application to the National Institute of Solar Energy for the inspection of our plant and
to get it enrolled in the ALMM. We are expecting the inspection to happen anytime in the third

Earnings Call_Q 2 & H1_FY 26-27_Vasa Denticity Ltd - Transcript
Esha: Good morning everyone and a very warm welcome to al l of you. On behalf of Vasa
Denticity Limited, I welcome you all to the earnings conference call to discuss the operational
and financial performance of the company for the qu arter and half year ended on 30th
September 2026. From the management team, we have with us today:
Dr. Vikas Agarwal (Managing Director),
Mr. Sandeep Aggarwal (Whole-time Director),
Mr. Mayank Bawari (VP of Supply Chain),
Mr. Shahid (VP of Marketing), and
Ms. Ananya Bhav Abrol (AVP of People Excellence).
The financial results and the investor presentation for the quarter and half year ended on 30th
September 2026 have already been filed with the sto ck exchange. We hope you have had the
opportunity to go through the same ahead of this ca ll. Before we begin, I may state a few
instructions for all the investors for your conveni ence. The instructions are as under. All
participant lines will be in listen-only mode during the management's opening remarks. Further,
investors who wish to ask any question may use the raise hand feature, and before asking the
question they may state their name and the name of the company or organization from where
they are participating. To give every participant an opportunity, each participant may ask a
maximum of one or two questions at a time. If you ha ve further questions, we request you to
rejoin the queue and we will take them up if time permits. Also, we would request you to please
avoid raising questions on any information that has not already been made public since the
management will not be in a position to comment on the same. Please note that this call is being
line with our disclosure obligations under SEBI regulations.
Now, I would like to invite Dr. Vikas Aggarwal for his opening remarks. Over to you sir.
Dr Vikas Aggarwal: Thank you Esha. Good morning everybody. First of al l, a very warm
welcome to all of you and a belated Happy Diwali and all the associated festivals with it. Dear
share owners, 10 years ago we started with one beli ef: a dentist in a small town deserves the
same products, price and speed as a dentist in Sout h Delhi. This quarter, at an annualized
revenue run rate of ₹348 crores, that belief broke p ast the ₹200 to 250 crore ceiling where a
traditional dental distributor in India has historically stalled.
Revenue grew 19.4% YoY to ₹87.1 crores, taking the half year to ₹170 crores. Growth was led
Revenue per customer rose 12.7% to ₹11,428 and onlin e order value rose 27.6% to ₹3,454.
Most importantly, operating EBITDA rose 23.9% YoY an d 42.9% QoQ to ₹7.24 crores. Our
operating EBITDA margin of 8.31% beat last year's 8.01% even with gross margins nearly six
points lower, because our operating cost fell struct urally. Gross margins climbed back as we
restored availability across our own brands after l ast year's stockouts and rupee depreciation.
Over time, we see gross margins moving within a 25 t o 30% band. The business can price
higher, but we will not push margin up at the cost of customer trust. Anything above 30%, we
would rather pass back to the dentist through sharp er prices. In a recurring consumable
business, building the buying habit matters more than squeezing an extra point of gross margin.
Today, operating cost fell 10.5% on a year ago while revenue grew close to 20%, dropping
from 25.2% of revenue to 18.9%. Technology and automati on now do work that people used
to do. Our long-term benchmark for operating cost is 12% of revenue, roughly 4% each for
logistics, people and everything else. We are reinvesting part of today's savings into leadership
depth. 16 experienced professionals at manager level and above joined us in 2026, especially
in the H1. Our first decade was built by homegrown generalists. Our next decade requires
domain specialists who raise the bar from day one. With operating cost heading towards 12%
and gross margin adding up to three points as avail ability normalizes, we see operating
EBITDA compounding into the 13 to 18% range over time. Orders per customer eased to 2.66
as clinics consolidated smaller top-ups into larger planned baskets. We do not optimize for
parcel counts. We optimize for total spend and prof it per dentist. Larger baskets mean fewer
boxes to pack and ship.
Which is why operating EBITDA per order rose 18.8% to ₹353 from ₹297 a year ago. Cost per
order fell 8.2% YoY to ₹804, and it sits at ₹789 exc luding the one-off ₹30 lakhs of severance
cost we have paid as we upgraded the team, alongside higher courier tariffs and fewer parcels.
We also moved exhibition shipping to marketing and inbound freight to cost of goods, so every
cost line reflects true unit economics. We added cl ose to 15,000 new customers this quarter
without heavy acquisition spend. But our real prize is the 3.1 lakh dentists, out of the 4.1 lakh
dentists registered with the National Dental Commis sion, who have already ordered from us
before. Dental buying is specialized. A returning de ntist already trusts our app, notifications,
refunds and the whole process of buying a dental pr oduct. Winning back past buyers and
deepening our share of their ₹1.2 lakh annualized c linic consumable spend is the fastest path
to scale. Our Plus members show what that habit looks like at maturity: each spends 2.7 times
as much as a non-member.
AI chat assistant, which now handles roughly 60% of the customer queries. In clinical
commerce, a fast, no-questions-asked refund builds lo ng-term habit. What we have zero
tolerance for is shipping a damaged or wrong item, and we are fixing those at the source through
clearer sizing guides on product pages and tighter warehouse barcode checks. Inventory stands
stockouts, launching new lines, meeting supplier min imum order quantities, and backing
demand across five warehouses as well as future demand projections. That buffer cut stockouts
on our top 2,500 SKUs from a 33% peak last year at this exact time to 8.8% today, on the way
to below 5% as I have promised. When we secure a CD SCO medical device import license, a
regulatory process that takes roughly 12 to 24 months per product category, we buy from global
suppliers.
It may take 6 months to sell through, but that produ ct is exclusively ours, competition rarely
follows, and we stock the full clinical depth. For example, there is a root canal file which starts
from size 6 and goes up to 140. Where a local dealer stops at 30 or 35, we keep the whole range
till 140. Those long-tail variants turn slower, but they carry superior margins and make
Dentalkart indispensable to a clinic. With availabi lity now restored, our board reviews
inventory ageing every quarter. Slow variants clear through short-expiry sales, and inventory
days will come down as sales scale. Half year opera ting cash flow went directly into building
this stock. Even after that investment, we hold close to ₹40 crores in cash and liquid
investments with virtually zero debt, and H2 sell-through will convert that inventory back into
cash. Only about 4% of Indian dental clinics are digi tal today. Every intraoral scanner, 3D
printer or milling machine we install locks in five to seven years of high-margin zirconia
blocks, resins and lab work through our EBITDA-posi tive Smileworks lab, and recurring
consumables already make up 17% of our digital division revenue, alongside our own brands,
which we will grow only as fast as they deliver superior value to dentists.
We are building the operating system where every Indian dentist starts the day: to buy, to learn
and to grow. We are building for the next decade, not for the next quarter. Thank you for being
with us. Over t

Moderator: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference
Call of Tata Chemicals Limited. Please note that this conference is being recorded. As a
reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen -only mode, and there will be an opportunity
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this
We have with us today Mr. R. Mukundan, Managing Director and CEO, and Mr. Nandakumar
Tirumalai, Chief Financial Officer of Tata Chemicals Limited. Before we begin, I would like to
mention that some of the statements made in today's discussion may be forwar d-looking in
nature and may involve risks and uncertainties. I now hand the conference over to Mr. R.
Mukundan to begin with the proceedings of the call. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
R. Mukundan: Thank you, Swapnali. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to our Q2 FY 27 and H1 FY 27
earnings call. It's a pleasure to connect with all of you during this festive season, and I would
like to start by wishing you and your families a very happy and prosperous Diwali.
I begin with a brief overview of the industry landscape, followed by key operational business
highlights across our markets and geographies during the quarter and first half of the year.
Starting with the customer end, which is the demand scenario across v arious segments and
geographies. In the Living Essentials, which is mainly bicarbonate, salt, and FOS, the demand
outlook remains supported by premiumization, increasing consumption across food, feed,
pharma, and beverage applications . Salt and bicarbonate are expected to continue to provide
stable growth, while prebiotics offer attractive long -term opportunities driven by increasing
customer focus on gut health and wellness.
In terms of Industrial Essentials, which is mainly soda ash and silica, the near- to medium-term
outlookfor the global soda ash industry continues to remain challenging. Market conditions are
characterized by persistent oversupply, subdued industrial demand, especially in China, and
intense competition across export markets. Significant capacity additions in China over the last
two years, coupled with slower -than-expected demand recovery in end -use sectors, have
continued to pressure global soda ash prices and producer margins. The ongoing conflict in the
Middle East, including disruptions impacting regional shipping routes and energy markets, has
increased freight volatility and supply chain risks. While large-scale demand destruction has not
materialized, in fact, in some parts of the world, the demand is robust, customers remain cautious
in procurement decisions amid macroeconomic uncertainty. China remains the key determinant
of global market dynamics. High operating rates, continued exports and competitive pricingfrom
Chinese producers continue to influence global soda ash prices and trade flows. This is coupled
with weak domestic demand from China's real estate and construction sectors, resulting in
additional export volumes entering the international market.
Amidst all this, India continues to outperform most global markets. Demand growth remains
healthy, supported by strong activity right across segments. Capacity expansion by solar glass
manufacturers and continued infrastructure investments are expected to continue to provide
above-average global demand growth. Southeast Asia remains highly competitive. While the

region is growing, it remains competitive, especially from Chinese exports, which continue to
gain market sharein that region.
In terms of Farm Essentials, uneven rainfall and delayed sowing affected demand during parts
of the quarter. Although Kharif acreage subsequently recovered, the broader agriculture outlook
remains cautious, supported by crop coverage, improving irrigation, policy support, technology
adoption, and resilient rural demand. However, weather volatility, crop price mov ements, and
elevated input costs continue to weigh and remain a near-term risk.
In terms of supply scenario, broadly, mainland China continues to be the driver of supplies,
including in bicarbonate, which saw increased sup ply on account of new capacity. The global
soda ash market, as has already been highlighted, is beset with high Chinese capacity growth
and inventory levels. Export volumes from China remain elevated. By the end of September,
producer inventory had reached nearly 1.89 million metric tons. Inner Mongolia Berun's phase
one, 5 million tons, underwent maintenance outages in October. This capacity is expected to
return to full operating rates at the end of the month. Meanwhile, Qinghai Salt Lake, a Solvay -
based soda ash producer, will reduce operating rates at the end of October. The magnitude and
duration of these impacts remain uncertain. In addition, Jinjing Technology, parent company of
Shandong Haitian, also annou nced that they will close its soda ash and bicarbonate production
lines. Recent announcement by a U.S. producer to reduce production at Wyoming by 1.5 million
tons and exit uneconomic export volume underscores the severity of current market conditions.
This remains one of the key concerns, that is, persistent low export realization and the structural
demand-supply imbalance which are facing the global soda ash industry.
Within India, DGTR has recommended quantity restrictions on soda ash imports for two years
after concluding that imports have surged and are causing serious injury to domestic industry.
Imports increased by 89% in FY202 4 and have remained at elevated levels, driven by global
oversupply and capacity additions in export countries and diversion of export volumes to India.
The pricing environment remains under pressure for soda ash. The Indian domestic pricing
softened towards the later part of the year following improved import availability and increased
domestic supply. U.S. export pricing remains under pressure. Looking ahead, pricing is expected
to remain range bound as market participantscontinue to contend with elevated inventory level.
Any sustained improvement in prices is likely to depend on a combination of supply
rationalizationand strong demand growth in the applications and in the geographies.
Now, I will turn to the operational highlights and TCL performance in Q2 and H1. The company
delivered a relatively resilient operating performance in a very challenging global environment.
Higher sales, production volume, improved operating efficiencies, and cost managementhelped
mitigate the impact of continued pressureon soda ash prices. The elevated input and energy and
logistics costsweighed on the results. Despite a resilient operating standalone performance, our
consolidated results were sharply impacted by natural gas cost increases in U.K. The prolonged
Middle East conflict continued to drive input costs both in CO2as well as in freight and logistics.
These were additionally weighed down by temporary suspension of operations in Kenya on the
consolidated performance.

Dear Sir/ Madam,
Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on Wednesday, 11th November 2026.
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Part A of Schedule III and Regulation 33 of the SEBI
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and other regulations,
if applicable, we hereby inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its
meeting held on Wednesday, 11 th November, 2026 (i.e. Today) have inter-alia, considered
and approved the following items of business:
i. The Un audited Standalone Financial Results of the Company along with Limited
review report for the half -year ended 30 th September, 2026. Copy of Unaudited
Standalone Financial Results of the Company along with Limited review report issued
by the Statutory Audito rs for the half -year ended 30 th September, 2026 is attached

Arab Emirates (UAE), with a view to expanding the Company's business operations,
strengthening its international presence and facilitating business development in the
Middle East region and Africa, subject to applicable laws, rules and regulations.
iii. The proposal t o explore the possibility of availing space in Cochin Special Economic
Zone ( CSEZ) in Kochi, Kerala, for setting up business premises to facilitate the
Company's export activities.

Firm of Company Secretaries in Practice, as the Secretarial Auditor of the Company to
conduct secretarial audit of the Company for the Financial Year 2026 -2027 pursuant to
Section 204 of Companies Act, 2013 , based on the recommendation of Audit

Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI circular dated 13th July 2023 are

We are very pleased to report a strong performance in Q2 FY27, marking
significant milestones for the Company as we crossed INR 500 crore in quarterly
total income and INR 100 crore in quarterly EBITDA for the first time. Our
performance reflects sustained business momentum, healthy customer demand
across our p ackaging segment and a continued focus on operational efficiencies,
customer relationships and profitable growth.
On a consolidated basis, total income for Q2 FY27 stood at INR 564.6 crore,
registering a growth of 20.2% year -on-year. EBITDA, including other income,
100 basis points to 17.7%. PAT increased by 57.7% to INR 45.3 crore, while cash

by 67.2% to INR 85.3 crore, while cash profit increased by 49.5% to INR 160.5

environment, which continues to be impacted by elevated raw material and
logistics costs. Our ability to improve margins while delivering strong revenue
growth reflects the benefits of p ricing actions, favourable product mix and positive
operating leverage, supported by our continued focus on execution.

across paperboard and flexible packaging. Our domestic business has sustained
double-digit growth, supported by healthy customer demand and deeper
relationships with existing customers. Export performance has also been
satisfactory, especially keeping in mind the challenging geopolitical environment.
We remain focused on expanding our product offerings, strengthening our position

customer requirements.

undertake our lithium-ion battery separator films business. This initiative represents
an important step in our efforts to diversify our business portfolio and establish an

recognition for its excellence in packaging, innovation and design. During the year,

and six honours at the IFCA Awards 2026 across Folding Cartons and Flexible
Packaging categories. These accolades reflect our continued commitment to
innovation, creativity and delivering high -quality packaging so lutions for our
customers, while further reinforcing our position as a trusted packaging partner to
lead consumer brands.
Looking ahead, we remain positive about the growth opportunities across our
paperboard and flexible packaging businesses. We will continue to build on this
growth through improved operational efficiencies and a focus on profitability.
Overall, our endeavour is to sustain our historical revenue growth trajectory while
enhancing cash generation and creating long-term value for our stakeholders.
Before handing over the call to the moderator to open the forum, I would also like
to share that we are joined today by our esteemed Director, Dr. Andreas Blaschke
and also my brother, Rishav Kanoria. So, we have almost full house today. Thank
you.
With that, I will hand over the call to the moderator to open the forum for any
questions or suggestions that you may have.
Moderator: Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. We will
take our first question from the line of Rohan Kalle from InCred Capital.
Rohan Kalle: Congrats to the team on a strong set of numbers. I have a few questions , first one
being, can you give some colour on maybe how much of this growth was price -led
or maybe how much was an improvement in the export business? And do you see
this as a sustainable trend going into the second half?
Akshay Kanoria: Yes. So, there was a good mix of price and volume growth. Volume growth was
quite strong , especially in the domestic segment and in our flexible packagin g
business, where we had a very strong performance. So i t is quite broad -based
Page 4 of 14
overall. And our export performance, as I said, has been quite satisfactory. We
have had growth there as well. So, the performance has been domestic led.
Rohan Kalle: Understood. And on margins, we have done very well in the first half. Do you see
this trend that is being maybe sustainable in the second half?
Akshay Kanoria: So, the margin improvement has been obviously driven substantially, thanks to the
overall level of working and scale improvement. As long as that continues, we can
see the margins following. Of course, nobody knows wha t is going to happen. So,
things are quite unpredictable.
Rohan Kalle: Sure. And on the battery separator films business, what kind of revenue potential
do you see from Phase 1? When do you think this would be achievable? And just a
follow-up there, over, let us say, the next five, six years, where do you see the films
business in terms of contribution to the overall business?
Akshay Kanoria: So, we are taking a baby step in the first phase, with sufficient land and
infrastructure in place to scale up over the next five to six years and build a
substantial revenue base . I think , we had shared some numbers when we had
announced our foray that we are looking at up to INR 200 crore on the current
investment, but then it can go to INR 1,000 crore INR 2,000 crore in the full scale in
a couple of years. So tha t is where we want to take it as soon as we can. And it
really depends on a couple of things. One is that how the Indian domestic battery
ecosystem flourishes over the next few years. Then the second thing, of course, is
our own performance and of course, the global market environment at that time. So
far, it seems things are moving quite positive.

security solutions to our customers. Since 2022, we also have offered LED TVs, monitors, interactive touch

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Augmont Enterprises Limited Q2 and
H1 27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen only
mode. There will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the management's
commentary concludes. Please note that this call is being recorded. I now hand the conference
over to Mr. Diwakar Pingle from Ernst & Young. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Diwakar Pingle: Thank you very much, Inba. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. On
behalf of Augmont Enterprises Limited, it gives me great pleasure to welcome you to the
company's first earnings conference call following its listing. We will discuss the
performance for Q2 and H1 FY27. We are delighted to have you with us as we begin this
new chapter in Augmont's journeys as a listed company. Joining us from the management
team are Mr. Ketan Kothari, Whole-Time Director, Mr. Mahendra Kumar Bafna, Whole-
Time Director, Mr. Amitkumar Solanki, Non-Executive Director, and Mr. Sachin Kothari,
Non-Executive Director. Before we proceed, I would like to draw your attention to the safe
harbor statement contained in the investor presentation. Certain statements made on today's
call may be forward looking in nature, and the relevant safe harbor provisions will apply. We
will start with the management's opening commentary, following which we will open the
floor for questions and answers. With that, I would now like to hand over the call to Ketan.
Over to you, Ketan.
Ketan Kothari: Thank you, Diwakar. Good evening, everyone. Thank you so much for joining us today for
our maiden earnings call following a listing in August. So we will be covering Q2 and H1
FY27, but before I begin, we would like to take a moment to thank all our shareholders and
investors for this trust and confidence that you have placed in us. Our listing marks an
important milestone in our journey, and we are very grateful to everyone who has supported
us along the way. As we begin this new chapter as a listed company, we remain focused on
executing our strategy, strengthening our business, creating sustainable long-term value for
all our stakeholders. I would like to take some time to explain the entire business, because of
the fact that this is the first call, and we do not really have a listed peer, so it is very important

of deliver value and command value. That framework has guided the organization to a second
consecutive quarter of profitability. Looking at the quarter gone by, Q2 FY27 was essentially a
tale of two distinct phases.
During July and August, we witnessed general market softness and sluggish demand across
several trade corridors. However, September marked a visible inflection with market activity
and demand sentiment improving meaningfully. What is particularly encouraging is not just the
market recovery in September, but the speed and responsiveness of our organization.

able to quickly adapt to our network capacity, pivot resources and capture volume momentum

admin overhead costs. This tight operational control has protected our unit economics and
enabled continued sustainable profit. Turning to our Consultative Logistics vertical.

Since 2005, we have raised four funds in our flagship strategy with more than INR4,200 crores
