secondaries. For those who are new to the company, a word on why we are public. India's savings
pool is growing fast, as the growth of the mutual fund industry shows. Yet, alternatives, meaning
private equity and venture capital investments in unlisted businesses, remain accessible to a very
small share of investors because alternative investment funds are restricted to qualified investors.
A listed alternatives AMC changes that. Any investor can now own the manager and with it the
economics of every fund the platform raises. This follows a proven global playbook. Listed

listing nearly 20 years ago, and institutional AMCs are very much preferred by institutional LPs
or fund investors, making fundraising faster and less expensive.

INR111.8 crores, a growth of 28%. Our cost-to-income ratio for the half year was 29% against
38% a year ago.

four things. First, income came from three of our funds. During the quarter, we earned income

that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking statements. Therefore, they must be

Marshal Sonavane: Thanks Garima. Good afternoon, everyone and a warm welcome to GHCL Textiles’ earnings
conference call for the second quarter and half year ended September 30th 2026. Our results and
investor presentation are available on the stock exchanges.
Let me begin with the operating environment. The global backdrop continues to present a case
of cautious optimism with the demand tailwinds continuing and potential to strengthen further
with the signing of FTAs, and at the same time increasing raw materia l prices and a volatile
global situation creating resistances.
Domestic demand across our segments continued to remain steady with a strong order flow.
However, the sharp rise in cotton and yarn prices towards the end of Q2 led buyers to limit
purchases to immediate needs. The export markets as well did not face any c hallenge in terms
of volume. UK and New Zealand FTAs are now in force, and the benefits of the same will be
visible in a year's time.
The India-EU agreement is expected to be operational in early 2027, and there seems to be steady
progress on other discussions -- other in-discussion FTAs. Overall, the demand scenario remains
positive.
On the cotton front, global and domestic output has declined while consumption has remained
stable or increased. Within India, the crop size is expected to be lower due to the El Niño effect.

extending it till December are steps in the right direction and will help stabilize the cotton prices
and availability.

the quarter and have remained around INR67,000 since. This price is at parity with global cotton,
helping in the competitiveness of Indian yarn. We follow a robust co tton procurement process
from both domestic and imported cotton to ensure our high standards of product quality and at
sustainable prices.
Turning to our own operations, we continue to operate at around 99% capacity utilization. Our
Meenakshi unit has reached full capacity and the share of fabric in our revenue increased to 16%
from 11% in the same quarter last year. Overall, we delivered a robust Q2.
Our revenue has reached INR446 crores, up 31% year -on-year. EBITDA came in at INR92
crores, up 141% with margin improving to 20.6% from 11.2% and PAT adjusted for the
exceptional loss was INR56 crores, up 249%. Reported PAT is INR36 crores, up 124%. For H1
FY27, revenue was INR856 crores, up 40%, EBITDA at INR162 crores, up 129% and adjusted
PAT at INR95 crores, up 223%. Reported PAT is INR75 crores, which is up 155% compared to
last year.
On a sequential basis, revenue grew 9%, EBITDA grew 31% and adjusted PAT grew 42%. All

August '26. There was no impact on our manufacturing operations due to this incident. The
Our balance sheet remains strong. During the half year, we repaid about INR74 crores of debt
and now net debt is at INR48 crores, a net debt -to-equity of 0.03x. Our strong balance sheet
enables our growth plan. Of the INR1,035 crores committed under the MO U with the TN
government, INR675 crores have been invested. Our planned knitting expansion will be
completed in Q3 with receipt of balance machines.
11-megawatt ground solar project is under progress and will be commissioned by end of Q3.
This will take the total green energy installation to 76 megawatts. We have received the land
allocation at PM MITRA Park, a total of 56 acres, which will be used primarily for processing.
In addition, we have received a board approval for an investment of INR410 crores which
includes margin money on working capital requirements, towards adding 58,368 spindles along
with 5 megawatts of rooftop solar. This project will generate a revenue of I NR400 crores to
INR420 crores at an EBITDA of 14% to 15%. We expect to complete this project by end of
FY28, and the full benefit can be expected in FY29.
Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic. Underlying demand is steady and should gain
momentum as FTA benefits take effect. However, higher raw material prices will take time to
be absorbed and margins may see some near -term pressure as cotton prices move up. Our

Pushpa Mani: Thanks, Ashi. Good evening, everyone. I welcome you all to the Q2 and H1FY27 results
discussion. You must have received the results, press release and investor deck of the company,
As usual, we will start the forum with the opening remarks by our MD and CEO, followed by
CFO and then we will open the floor for the question-and-answer session. If any of your
questions remain unanswered, you may reach out to us afterwards.
The management on today's call would be represented by Mr. Ajay Rajan, MD and CEO, Mr.
V. Easwaran, Whole-Time Director and COO, Mr. Rakesh Dosi, Chief Business and Products
Officer, Mr. Sandeep Mantri, CFO and myself.
Before we begin, I would like to mention that some of the statements in today's discussion may
be forward-looking in nature and we believe that the expectations contained in these statements
are reasonable. However, these statements involve a number of risks and uncertainties that may
lead to different results.
With this, I invite our MD, Mr. Ajay Rajan. Thank you and over to you.
Ajay Rajan: Thank you, Pushpa, good evening, everyone and thank you for joining us for our Q2FY27
Earnings Call. This quarter marks an important milestone for Protean. The two large RFP
mandates where we invested a lot of our bandwidth and capital over the year, the CERSAI
CKYCRR 2.0 and the UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra project, both are now nearing
implementation completion.
The investments required to deliver them are largely behind us and we will have better
predictability on both revenue and margins in the quarters ahead. I had also set out in my first
interaction with you how I see Protean's next chapter, our three pillars, which is deepening our
core DPI franchise, bundling solutions for enterprises in addition to selling bespoke products
and taking the India's DPI model to the world.
Over the quarter, we have moved from articulating that strategy to starting to execute it and I
will spend the second half of my remarks on what that execution looks like on the ground. First,
let me take you through the numbers. In terms of financial performance, Protean delivered a
steady and resilient performance in Q2FY27.
Revenue from operations grew 8% year-on-year to INR 271 crores, driven by continued
momentum across our core and new businesses and led by market share gains across all our key
offerings. Our EBITDA stood at INR 43 crores in Q2FY27, with an EBITDA margin of 15%.
Similar to last quarter, the margin for this quarter also factored some upfront investments of INR
10 crores towards implementation of our strategic RFP project. Excluding these investments, the
EBITDA would have been INR 53 crores, which is an increase of 22% year-on-year and an
EBITDA margin of 18%. The profit after tax stood at INR 16 crores in Q2FY27. Excluding the
impact of the investments which I mentioned about towards the RFP project, normalized PAT
would have been INR 24 crores.
I would also like to reiterate from last year that we will see over a few quarters a timing gap
between cost and revenue pertaining to our Aadhaar Seva Kendra project, since we had to spend
first to build the capability and the revenue would follow as the service volume expands. With
150 Aadhaar Seva Kendra’s open till September and 187 out of the mandated 192 ASK centres
live as of October’26, the major investments are all behind us and as the network matures, we
expect the related revenue to exceed the cost over the next couple of quarters and continued
momentum thereafter. The early signs that we are seeing are alluding towards this direction.
From a balance sheet perspective, we remain in strong financial position, zero debt and
This gives us the flexibility to not only invest in our products and systems upgrades, but also
pursue business growth, which we will do while maintaining fiscal discipline. Our approach to
capital allocation will remain rigorous, we will continue to evaluate our portfolio and prioritize
investments and opportunities where we see the strongest potential for revenue growth, margin
improvement and long-term value creation.
Let me run you through the business performance. Our Tax Service business, which is a source
of transactional revenue, grew 13% year-on-year to INR 121 crores. In a de-growing market, we
have cemented our dominance by increasing our market share to 65.8%, an increase of 330 basis
points sequentially and 780 basis points on a year-on-year basis. We issued 1.3 crores PAN cards
this quarter, of which 70% of the applications came through the assisted mode via our vast
network spread across 18,000 PIN codes in India. The strength of this distribution network is a
key USP and differentiator for us, which is very hard to replicate, and it matters for assisted
delivery models like PAN issuance and other G2C services that we plan to offer through that.
Our CRA service business, which comprises majorly annuity revenue, continues to present a
significant long-term opportunity. We onboarded 4.7 million new subscribers during the quarter,
up 15% year-on-year, which is 95% of all new subscribers in the CRA ecosystem. We also
onboarded more than 1,400 new corporates, our highest-ever corporate onboarding in a single
quarter and a clear proof of our focus on the non-government segment, where the penetration is
low, but the annuity opportunity is the largest. Our combined market share across NPS, APY
and UPS stands at 97%. Under NPS Vatsalya, we added around 1.5 lakh subscribers, which is
the highest-ever quarterly addition under the scheme. We continue to do well on the government
segment.
On the revenue side, CRA grew 2% year-on-year to INR 80 crores, given some of the regulatory
pricing impact we had. As informed in the previous quarter, the charge structure now also
includes the AUM link fee, which means our revenue per subscriber rises as the assets in each
account grow. This growth will be market-led and compounds over time. So, the subscribers that
we add today will become a growing annuity-like income stream in the coming years as the
ecosystem grows.
I believe strongly, as much as the pension regulator and the pension ecosystem, that the
opportunity ahead of us is very substantial. We expect pension coverage and the AUM to witness
significantly high growth in the years to come, in line with the Government's vision of taking
pension to all. Pension coverage in India is still below 7%, compared to 70% in economies such
as U.S. and Europe.
With the concentrated efforts of PFRDA and the ecosystem, that gap is set to narrow, with the
NPS ecosystem projected to reach 40 crores subscribers over the next five years and private
sector employees will be the key driver to complement the Government sector base. The
regulator also expects the AUM to reach INR 100 lakh crores by 2040.
There is also renewed push from the regulator, which is widening the product funnel by

BUSINESS UPDATE | 11 NOVEMBER 2026
AkikoPay reaches 1 lakh customers
Akiko Global expands its digital customer platform across payments, credit and everyday financial
services
New Delhi, 11 November 2026: Akiko Global Services Limited (NSE: AKIKO) announces that AkikoPay
has reached 1,00,000 customers onboarded. The milestone marks progress in the Company's expansion from
financial product distribution into an ongoing digital relationship with customers.
Available on Android and iOS, AkikoPay brings together wallet and prepaid -card services, credit
information, access to financial products and lifestyle services. The Company's objective is to give customers
more reasons to return to one platform as their payment, borrowing and other financial needs evolve.
What the milestone means
The onboarded customer base creates an opportunity to introduce more customers to relevant services,
support repeat usage and strengthen customer retent ion. Management's next focus is on completing
verification, encouraging activation and improving the customer experience as the platform scales.
The figure refers to cumulative customer onboarding, based on management information, and is unaudited.
KYC and activation continue across the customer base; the milestone does not represent 1,00,000 fully KYC-
verified, active or transacting customers.
Services available on AkikoPay
Wallet and prepaid card. Eligible customers can load their wallet through supported UPI or credit -card
channels, transfer eligible wallet balances to bank accounts and use the RuPay prepaid card for supported
online purchases, subject to applicable limits and charges.
Credit information. Customers can access credit score and report infor mation to better understand their
credit profile and explore relevant product eligibility.
Credit products. The platform facilitates access to credit cards, FD-backed credit-card options and personal,
home and car loan journeys through partner institutions, subject to their eligibility criteria and approval.
Travel and other services. Gift vouchers, travel bookings, visa services and Niyo zero -forex account -
opening access broaden the range of customer needs that the platform can serve.
Financial products an d approvals are provided by the respective regulated partners. AkikoPay facilitates
access and does not itself undertake lending or credit underwriting.

Building the next phase of AkikoPay
From customer acquisition to ongoing engagement
Akiko Global's financial distribution relationships and assisted service network provide a foundation for
AkikoPay's growth. The Company aims to connect this existing distribution capability with a digital platform
that can support customers before, during and after a financial product application.
The strategy is to acquire customers, help them discover suitable products, support their applications through
partners and retain the relationship through useful payment and service journeys. A broader relationship may
create additional distribution and service income opportunities over time. These opportunities depend on
customer activation, sustained usage, partner terms and conversion, and are not a revenue or profitability
forecast.
Priorities for the next stage
Customer a ctivation and service quality. Progress KYC completion, simplify onboarding, strengthen
customer support and encourage customers to use the services already available.
Payment capabilities. Work towards UPI Scan & Pay and expanded bill -payment capabilities through the
required approvals, partner arrangements and technical integrations. UPI wallet loading is already available;
outgoing UPI Scan & Pay remains planned.
Relevant product access. Improve product discovery and eligibility journeys, expand suitable partner
offerings and support responsible cross-selling based on customer needs and consent.
Longer-term product development. Explore insurance distribution, wealth products and MSME -focused
services through appropriate partners, subject to applicable approvals and implementation readiness.
Long-term direction
The Company's ambition is to make AkikoPay a regular destination for customers' financial needs, extending
engagement beyond a single loan or card application. Reaching 1 lakh onboarded customers is an early step
in that direction; the emphasis now is on turning customer acquisition into lasting, useful relationships.

Akiko Global Services Limited is an NSE -listed financial services distribution company. Through its bank
and NBFC relationships, digital channels and assisted distribution network, the Company facilitates access
to credit cards and loan products. AkikoPay complements this business with a consumer platform for
payments, financial information and partner-led services.

ICRA upgrades Aye Finance to [ICRA]A+ (Stable Outlook) from [ICRA]A
Follows India Ratings & Research’s rating upgrade in June 2026, driven by stronger capitalisation,
improving asset quality and a recovery in profitability
Aye Finance, India’s leading technology-driven lender focused on the micro enterprise sector,
announced that ICRA has upgraded its rating from [ICRA]A to [ICRA]A+ with a Stable Outlook. The
upgrade follows India Ratings & Research’s upgrade to A+ in June 2026, making it the Company’s
second rating upgrade in this financial year. Achieving it amid an uncertain macroeconomic
environment underscores the resilience of the Company’s underwriting framework, the quality of its
portfolio and the strength of its balance sheet.
ICRA’s rating upgrade is underpinned by improvement across capital, asset quality, liquidity and
earnings
 Stronger capitalisation: Capital adequacy ratio of 41% and net worth of INR 2695 Crores as
on September 2026 with managed gearing of 2.4X. ICRA noted that the improved
capitalisation profile supports Aye’s envisaged scale-up of operations.
 Improved asset quality: Gross stage 3 assets declined to 4.2% as on September 30, 2026,
from 4.8% as on March 31, 2026.
 Diversified franchise: AUM of INR 7,597 Crore as on September 30, 2026, up 26% year-on-
year, spread across 571 districts in 21 states and union territories The top three states account
for 43% of AUM and the top ten districts for about 4%. ICRA noted that the Company continues
to maintain healthy geographical diversification.
as on September 30, 2026.
 Higher profitability: Lower credit costs (3.6% of average managed assets vs 4.3% in FY26) and
tighter operating costs (8.1% vs 8.8%) lifted H1 FY27 profit after tax to ~INR161 crore. The
FY26 PAT was INR 194 Crores.
Mr Sanjay Sharma, Managing Director of Aye Finance commented on the development “Our second
rating upgrade in FY27 reflects a stronger balance sheet following our IPO, a measurable improvement
in asset quality and a business that continues to scale across geographies without compromising on
underwriting discipline. The A+ rating broadens our access to diversified, competitively priced funding
from banks, debt capital markets and securitisation. This should lend further support to profitability
as we enter the seasonally stronger part of the financial year.”
Aye Finance Limited is a RBI-registered NBFC focused on the credit needs of India’s micro enterprises,
lenders. Operating since 2014, the Company serves 7 lakh active customers through a pan-India
presence across 18 states and 3 union territories. In Q2 FY27, Aye Finance reported a 151% year-on-
year increase in profit after tax and 26% year-on-year growth in assets under management to INR
7,597 crore.

Mumbai, November 11, 2026 : EAAA India Alternatives Limited (Edelweiss Alternatives), a diversified,
multi-strategy institutionalized platform with an established track record of over 17 years, today announced
its unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September
30, 2026, its first results since listing on BSE and NSE earlier this month.
Declares Interim Dividend
The Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of ₹7 per equity share (140%) of face value ₹5
each for the financial year 2026-27.
Robust growth in Key Metrics
• Building Scale Through Sustained FPAUM Growth - FPAUM, a key indicator of earnings visibility
and revenue-generating assets, grew to ₹49,164 Cr as at September 30, 2026 from ₹38,552 Cr a year
earlier, representing a growth of 28% YoY. The growth in FPAUM reflects the ability to consistently
raise, deploy and realise capital across strategies, while increasing the share of assets that contribute
to recurring management fees.
• Revenue Expansion driven by growth in fee -paying assets - Total Income rose by 35% YoY to
₹616 Cr in H1FY27 from ₹457 Cr in H1FY26, and by 14% YoY to ₹280 Cr in Q2FY27 from ₹246 Cr in
Q2FY26, supported by sustained growth in FPAUM and the continued scaling of the platform.
• Strong Profit Growth Driven by Scale - PAT increased by 35% YoY to ₹169 Cr in H1FY27 and by
27% YoY to ₹88 Cr in Q2FY27, demonstrating the ability to translate sustained growth in FPAUM into
profitable growth.
• Improved Capital Efficiency - RoE stood at 29.4% in Q2FY27, an improvement of 275 bps YoY,
reflecting stronger profitability, disciplined capital allocation and the increasing ability of the platform to
generate earnings from its growing asset base.
Key Business Updates
• Consistent fundraising, deployment and realisation on a 12-quarter rolling average highlights
the robustness of the platform
The ability to execute across each of these vectors in a measured approach is critical to sustaining long-
term growth and delivering value for investors.
• Investing Across Highways, Offices and Operating Companies
Demonstrating the breadth of the alternatives platform, Edelweiss Alternatives through its investment
strategies continue to deploy capital across strategies, focusing on high -quality assets and businesses
with strong long-term value creation potential.
o Infrastructure Yield Strategy: Strengthened participation in India's transport infrastructure
sector through the acquisition of two operational toll road assets in Tamil Nadu under NHAI's TOT
Bundle 19, reinforcing its role in the monetisation of mature national highway assets
occupancy, adding a high-quality, income-generating property with strong tenant metrics to the
portfolio.
o Special Situations & Performing Credit Strategy: Invested in Cyient Semiconductors, a
business focused on custom chip design and power semiconductor solutions, providing exposure
to a high-growth sector aligned with India's digital and manufacturing ambitions.
o Private Equity Strategy: Achieved a successful public market listing of portfolio company
Rentomojo, underscoring its ability to support businesses through their growth journey and create
liquidity and value for investors.
Client Franchise continues its growth trajectory
The strength of Edelweiss Alternatives' investor franchise is demonstrated by 77% of AUM coming from
repeat clients, underscoring deep and enduring investor relationships. The AUM base is balanced across
over 5,750 client relationships spanning global and domestic markets, the platform benefits from a
diversified capital base.
A Successful IPO - Further Institutionalizing the Platform
The equity shares of Edelweiss Alternatives listed on the stock exchanges with oversubscription across
every investor category – QIB book at 13.79x, contributing ~72% of total demand. Marquee investors
including the top 5 mutual fund companies, Norges Bank, Hornbill Capital and Schroders participated in the
issue. The IPO, an offer for sale of ₹1,200 Cr, was subscribed 4.17x.

we enter this phase with an even greater commitment to further institutionalising our alternative asset
management platform through transparency, accountability, and responsibility.
Our alternatives business focuses on channelling patient capital of our clients into private market assets
through closed ended funds. Our focus remains on sustained FPAUM growth, consistent performance of
our funds and value creation for all stakeholders over the long term.

call. Thank you for joining us. Today, we will take you through our performance for the
quarter, along with the strategic priorities that we believe will shape the Aurobindo’s next
phase of growth. We are working to translate the scale of the established business, strength
of our development pipeline and the capacities created through recent investment into
sustainable commercial growth.

strengthening our U S presence and expanding our capabilities in complex and controlled

plans to expand in these differentiated segments.

efficiency as levers to strengthen profitability.
Total capital expenditure stood at 89 million, of which 47 million towards the development
capabilities and 42 million towards strategic priorities respectively, thereby supporting our
future growth plan.
R&D expenditure for the quarter stood at 376 crores against INR 344 crores in previous
quarter. Our development investments are directed towards advancing differentiated
products and building a pipeline with meaningful long-term commercial potential.
We have generated a very strong cash flow of USD 146 million during the quarter after funding
strategic investments and capital allocation initiatives, and closed with a net cash position of
USD 189 million. Our balance sheet provides a sound foundation to support planned

shareholders, analysts, investors, members and all other stakeholders on this call. Let me first talk a

structural resilience despite a volatile global environment marked by intensifying geopolitical tensions,
fluctuating crude oil prices and prolonged tightening of global financial conditions.
Against this challenging backdrop, India's core macroeconomic fundamentals remain exceptionally
robust. Real GDP expanded by 7.8% in Q1 of FY27, fundamentally driven by sustained momentum
across private consumption, capital investment, manufacturing output and a resurgent services sector.
Importantly, institutional market dynamics have evolved to provide unparalleled systemic stability.
While foreign institutional investors adopted a cautious stance amid macro uncertainties resulting in a
during the same period.

liquidity and validating long-term confidence in the Indian growth narrative. Indian capital markets are
now increasingly anchored by domestic long-term financial savings.

expansion during the first half of FY27. The compounding participation of both household and
institutional investors underscores the self-sustaining nature, maturation and expanding capacity of the
domestic financial ecosystem.

during the first half of FY27. Consolidated revenues for H1 FY27 stood at Rs. 3,257 crores compared
with Rs. 2,184 crores in the corresponding period last year, representing a robust year-on-year growth
of 49%.

September 30, 2026, as compared to the previous year. Operational revenues have grown by 48% to
Rs. 2,999 crores from Rs. 2,026 crores.

clearing house segments registered a substantial increase of 60%, rising to Rs. 2,456 crores from Rs.

expenses are attributable to regulatory fees and clearing and settlement expenses, all of which is
directly correlated to increasing transaction volumes. The operating EBITDA, including contribution to
core SGF has increased by 55% to Rs. 2,019 crores as compared to Rs. 1,306 crores with margins
expanding to 67% from 64%.

to reach Rs. 1,680 crores from Rs. 1,095 crores representing a robust year-on-year growth of 53% with
a net profit margin of 52%. The continued growth of BSE's investor base remains an encouraging
indicator of the growing reach of India's capital markets. Investor accounts registered on BSE have now
reached 26.8 crores, 3.9 crores new accounts added over the past year.

than 1 crore investor reach, reflecting the widening geographic reach of the capital markets across the
country.

BSE. We conducted 2,328 investor awareness programs during H1 FY27 reaching over 1.2 lakhs
participants. Looking ahead, BSE remains deeply committed to expanding investor awareness and
advancing financial literacy.

safeguarding investor interest and securing the long-term sustainable growth of India's financial
ecosystem. The consistent improvement across both our revenue streams and operating margins is
direct evidence of our disciplined strategic execution. By expanding market participation and driving key
platform efficiencies, we are continuously enhancing the depth of India's financial ecosystem while
reinforcing BSE's structural position at the center of India's capital market expansion.

seen very strong momentum during the first half of FY27 with a record 71 main board IPOs, raising over

growing confidence of companies in accessing the public markets for capital formation.

India's growing equity capital markets. Alongside the strong momentum in the main board IPO market,

has shifted towards soft oil refining with an installed capacity of 400 tonnes per day each at
Bathinda and Kharagpur.
While we acknowledge the near-term headwinds in the ethanol industry arising from oversupply,
we remain cautiously optimistic about the emerging opportunities across the broader biofuel
sector, supported by our existing infrastructure and operational readiness.
Moving to our financial performance for the quarter. Consolidated revenue from operations for
second quarter of FY27 stood at INR695 crores, while revenue for first half of FY27 stood at
INR1,319 crores.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR66 crores with EBITDA margin holding steady at 9.5%.
For first half of FY27, EBITDA stood at INR132 crores, up 5.9% year-on-year with the margins
improving by 191 basis points to 10%. PAT for the quarter stood at INR29 crores with a PAT
margin of 4.2%.
On a segmental basis, our distillery business reported an EBITDA margin of 11.9% in Quarter
2 of FY27, compared to 11% in quarter 2 of FY26, marking an improvement of 90 basis points
year-on-year. This improvement came despite higher maize prices during the quarter and reflects
our enhanced operational efficiencies through shared infrastructure.
In our oil refinery business, revenue for second quarter of FY27 stood at INR188 crores with an
EBITDA margin of 3.7%. Other income f or the quarter also includes one -time gain of INR2
crores from the sale of assets from our former oil and vanaspati unit at Bathinda.
As we move forward, we will remain focused on strengthening our core businesses while
leveraging our procurement expertise to create sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.

environmental compliance requirements, and growing focus on water recycling continue to
support demand for ZLD (zero liquid discharge ), wastewater recycling, desalination, and
membrane-based treatment solutions.

Now, I would like to invite Anil ji to share his views.
Anil Mittal: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us for KRBL's Q2 FY27 earnings call. I will
briefly cover the global and Indian rice outlook, the new basmati crop and paddy prices, the
export environment, and the company's performance. Let me begin with global picture, which
is broadly unchanged since our last call. As per USDA's October estimate, the world rice
production in 2026 -27 is expected to fall to 537 million tons from 546 million tons last year ,
with India accounting for most of the decline.
Consumption, meanwhile, is expected to rise to a record of about 539 million tons. Global stocks
are therefore expected to draw down. India continues to hold close to 30% of world rice trade,
and USDA expects Indian exports of about 24 million tons in 2026-27, higher than the previous
year. For India, U SDA now estimates for 26 -27 production at about 147 million metric tons
against a record of 154 million tons last year, reflecting a weaker monsoon.
India will remain alongside China, one of the two largest rice producers in the world, and
domestic consumption is expected to rise by about 4 million tons. The 2026 monsoon ended
about 13% below normal nationally, the weakest since 2015 under a strong El Nino. Last quarter,
I flagged the risk this posed to the basmati belt. I am glad to say that risk largely d id not
materialize. Northwest India finished about 6% below normal.

Irrigation carried the crop through, and trade estimates currently put the year's basmati crop
modestly above last year's. The unseasonal rain in part of Punjab in the mid -October wet some
harvested paddy in the mandis and flattened standing crop in places. The damage appears
localized and will have a clear picture as arrivals progress.
Despite a larger crop, basmati paddy prices have risen sharply. Major varieties are trading at
around INR4,500-INR5,200 per quintal, well above last year's paddy price. There are three
reasons.
First, the industry has entered this season with almost no carryover stock. Second, the export
realization have stayed high. And third, buyers across the Middle East need to rebuild depleted
inventories, and the trade is pricing that demand in. Our procurement approach reflects this. We
will not chase the market.
We are buying in a staggered manner across the season with a firm focus on quality, low
moisture, high recovery paddy. And our inventory position gives us the flexibility to be patient
whenever prices run ahead of fundamentals. On exports, between April and August, India
shipped about 2.5 million tons of basmati against 2.7 million tons in the same period last year.
The entire decline was in the Middle East. Shipments to the rest of the world were unchanged.
Realizations were about 21% higher in rupee terms. So, the rupee value of India's basmati export
actually rose by around 12%. In August, volumes were back over last year's level. As I said last
quarter, this remains a logistics problem and not a demand problem.
The situation in the Gulf remains unsettled. Transit through the Strait of Hormuz has been
intermittent, and freight and war risk premiums remain elevated and sensitive to every
development. Marine cover continues to be available, priced shipment by shipment, and buyers
have largely absorbed the higher cost because food security leaves them little alternative.
Trade has adapted around the disruptions. Basmati shipment to Jordan, largely for onward
movement to Iraq, are up almost six fold this year, more than offsetting the fall in direct
shipments to Iraq.
Iran is the exception. Payment and banking channels have become considerably more difficult
since U.S. sanctions were tightened in August, and that market will take longer to normalize.
Our view of recovery is unchanged. Inventories in t he region are low, and when the route
becomes dependable, restocking will be significant but w e expect that normalization to be
gradual rather than sudden.
Now coming to KRBL's performance. KRBL recorded its highest -ever quarterly revenue of
INR1,727 crores, up 14% on the same quarter last year, driven by 33% growth in domestic
revenue. Export revenue for the first half was INR541 crores, lower by 41%. The decline was
almost entirely in bulk export to the Middle East, where three factors weighted on the business.
Payment channel in parts of the region became more difficult, movement through the Strait of
Hormuz became more restricted, and weighing risk against reward.

Exports to market outside the Middle East grew 14% in the first half. These markets are doing

Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Sangam India Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings

presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an
recorded.
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Garima Singla from Go India Advisors LLP. Thank you,
and over to you, ma'am.
Garima Singla: Thank you. Good afternoon, one and all. It's my pleasure to welcome you on behalf of Sangam
India Limited. Thank you for joining us today for Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings conference call.
This call is being hosted by Go India Advisors. Please note that today's discussion may include
certain forward-looking statements. Therefore, they must be viewed in conjunction with the risk
that the company faces. Today on the call, we are joined by Mr. Anurag Soni, Managing
Director.
I now invite Mr. Soni to present the company's business outlook and performance, after which
we will open the floor for Q&A. Thank you, and over to you, sir.
Anurag Soni: Thank you, Garima. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Diwali is just a
few days away, so let me begin by wishing you and your families a very happy and prosperous
Diwali. For those who are new to Sangam, I would like to take a moment to introduce ourselves.
We are an integrated textile company.
On the synthetic side, we make recycled polyester fiber from plastic waste, PV-dyed yarn, and
suiting fabrics. On the cotton side, we make cotton yarns and denim fabrics along with open-
end yarns. We also have a small seamless garment business which is about 2% of our revenue.
All of this happens across 8 locations in Rajasthan with over 12,000 people.
Capacity utilization remains high across all our divisions today. Quarter 2 has been the best
quarter in Sangam's history. Revenue crossed INR1,000 crores in a quarter for the first time at
INR1,045 crores, up 33% over last year. EBITDA was INR127 crores and PAT INR53 crores,
both the highest we have ever reported.
For the half year, revenue stood at INR1,906 crores and PAT at INR94 crores, which is already
more than what we earned in the whole of last year. When we spoke in April, I talked about one
simple principle: better than before. For 5 quarters in a row now, our EBITDA and PAT have
been better than the quarter before. This is now showing in our balance sheet as well.
Return on capital employed has gone up from 7% 2 years ago to about 13% today, and return on
equity from about 4% to nearly 14%. Net debt to EBITDA has come down from 4.5x to 3.25x.
In October, India Ratings upgraded our long-term rating to IND A with a stable outlook.
Our debtor days have gone up in the current quarter from 67 days in March to 77 days in
September, and there are mainly 2 reasons for it. First, we are growing our business, and with
Sangam India Limited

the focus also on government tenders, which was close to INR200 crores in the first half, it is a
business we intend to build, but these payments come on a longer cycle and a good part of it is
yet to be collected.
Second, the export shipments are taking longer to reach customers these days, which is why we
have been more measured on exports this year. We aspire to bring debtor days back to March
levels in the second half of the year. Coming to the future, our plants are running close to full
capacity, so the next leg of growth needs fresh investment, and we have started on that.
Our first focus is cost. Energy is our biggest cost, and we are bringing it down with our own
renewable power. Last year, captive power met close to 10% of our needs. Today it is close to
about 35%, and by the end of this financial year it will be close to about 50%, before stabilizing
at about 70% in Q1 of next year.
Our next focus is capacity, including modernizing and expanding our spinning and making more
of our own raw materials. The work is on track, and the larger benefits will start coming in from
the next financial year. In April, I said we aspire to double our PAT this year. At the halfway
mark, I'm happy to say we are well on that path.
I want to finish by thanking our 12,000+ colleagues, our customers, our bankers, and all our
shareholders for their trust in Sangam. There's a lot more to do, and we're looking forward to it.
With that, I'm happy to take your questions. Thank you.

been disclosed in the presentation.
The other work is still in progress, and probably as time goes, probably in the next few quarters,

So I think I will leave it at that. The broad guidance we've already shared in the last quarter that

Company at its meeting held on November 10, 2026 , approved the revision in remuneration of Ketan Krishna,

governance functions of the Company. The revision, which relates to the fixed and variable components of his
remuneration, has been approved after considering his role, responsibilities and performance, the performance of the

Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as applicable.

• Rohan Ajeet Kulkarni, VP - Finance & Accounts

as the Designated Chief Information Security Officer, in each case with effect from November 10, 2026, following
the approval of the NRC and, in the case of Prabhat Verma , subject to completion of the required employment
documentation.

experience, contribution towards the growth and operations of the Company and the increased responsibilities
associated with the Company’s operations as a listed entity, in accordance with the Company’s Nomination and
Remuneration Policy and the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations

may use the chat option to interact with the moderator. Please note that this conference is being recorded.
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Vaibhav Sachdeva, Investor Relations from Lenskart. Thank you, and
over to you.
Vaibhav Sachdeva: Thank you. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining Lenskart's Earning Call for the second quarter
of Fiscal Year 2027. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today
may be forward-looking in nature and are subject to risks and uncertainties. The conference call may contain
forward-looking statements about the company which are based on the belief s, opinions, and expectations
of the company as on the date of this call.
These statements are not a guarantee of future performance and involve risk s and uncertainties that are
and stock exchanges. Please note that consistent with our IPO prospectus, the numbers we present today
are on a pro forma basis for like-to-like comparison unless stated otherwise.
Pro forma financials consider Dealskart, Meller and GeoIQ as if they had always been part of the company,
whereas reported financials include them only from their acquisition dates. From Q3 Fiscal 2026 onwards,
the two are identical; the difference exists, only, in the prior year comparatives, Q2 Fiscal 2026 and H1 Fiscal
2026.
We will begin today's session with opening remarks from Peyush and Abhishek. During this time, everyone
will be on mute. Following the presentation, we will open up for Q&A. With that, I would like to hand over to
Peyush.
Peyush Bansal: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us. As always, we are grateful for the trust you place in us
with your capital and with your eyes. The size and depth of the vision care problem are far greater than we
can imagine. Last quarter I touched upon this, and numbers this quarter only reinforce our belief in the scale
of the problem and opportunity.
To begin with, let me take you through the key financial highlights of the quarter. Revenue grew 32.5% year-
on-year to ₹2,845 crores. EBITDA grew to ₹624 crores, a 46.6% jump year on year. EBITDA Pre-Ind AS grew
65%, twice as fast as revenue, with margin expanding from 11.1% to 13.8%. PAT more than doubled to ₹232
crores.
Lenskart Solutions Limited

For the half year, revenue of ₹5,559 crores increased 1.3x year -on-year. EBITDA Pre-Ind AS increased 1.8x
year-on-year to ₹753 crores. PAT of ₹461 crores is already 87% of the whole of FY26. And on a trailing 12 -
month basis, we have now crossed ₹10,000 crores of revenue, ₹2,200 crores of EBITDA, ₹1,300 crores of Pre-
Ind AS EBITDA, and close to ₹800 crores of PAT on 40 million eyewear units.
Like I always say, measure us over years, not quarters. Behind the financials, this quarter we conducted 80
lakh eye tests globally, up 40% year on year. In India, around 70 lakhs, that is 78,000 Indians a day. Units grew
27.1% year on year. We added 165 net new stores globally, taking the network now to 3,624 stores.
In Q2, India delivered same-store sales growth of 20.8%. With same pin code growth of 27.1%. We have said
too little about Hustlr Club. A face scan on the app and a complete pair, frame, lenses, and warranty, all for
₹500. Lakhs joined this quarter, many owning glasses for first time. It is one of the ways how we hope the
next 100 million Indians find us.
Also, this quarter, Lenskart Gold crossed 1 crore active members in India, up 39% year -on-year, with ₹73
crores of gold fees collected in the quarter, up 55% from last year. It is the quietest and most powerful thing
we are building. Our brands are also learning to speak the culture.
This quarter we have launched John Jacobs with Masaba. We also launched Shunya, which brings Indian
classical music into a frame, a beautiful collection right down to details inspired by the sitar and flute. We
brought it to life with Sounds of Shunya, 10 artists across 5 evenings including classical vocalists, sitarists,
and popular musician duo The Backstage Siblings.
In Singapore, we launched a Game of Thrones collection. From the iconic emblems of the great houses,
temples shaped by swords and armor, to the 3 words every fan knows Winter is coming - every detail of that
world is captured on the frame.
And this week only, we have launched John Jacobs with designers Shantanu and Nikhil. If you look closely,
you will see the intricate details - the S&N mark on the frame, a thin metal line along the temples, and their
signature navy and cherry red colors tucked into the hinges. This is the kind of craft we are building into our
frames, and Meller’s unique take on Diwali is launching today.
And now the number we watch most closely. Our Net Promoter Score. Opening a store a day while holding
our standard is hard. India NPS, as you are aware, dipped to 77.6 in June, but we assured you that we have
been working hard to get back to our NPS levels . I'm happy to share with you that in this quarter it is back at
79.6. That recovery, on a ship this size, is what we are proudest of this quarter.
Last quarter we told you Indians - India has not bought its glasses yet. By 2030, 94 crore Indians will require
glasses, and this is the goal. It is why we say India needs at least 10,000+ Lenskart stores. It is only fair that
We believe it needs 4 things this industry never had. First, it will be an engineering company. The hardest
problem in eyewear, the eye test above all, will not be solved by hiring more or spending more. 100 million
pairs a year needs 80 million eye tests. So, we are engineering the eye test. Remote optometry now in 934
stores, and also Drysh, the AI-assisted eye test, is in pilot.

like to begin by spending a few minutes on what we do, how we have grown, and where we are
headed. Then I will take you through the quarter's results.
BLS E-Services was set up in 2016 as part of the BLS Group with a simple belief that every
Indian, wherever they live, should have easy access to banking, credit, and government services.
Millions of people in rural and semi -urban India still live far from a bank branch or a
government office.
For them, a trusted service point in their own village or neighborhood makes a real difference
to everyday life. The BLS Group already had deep experience in running large technology -
enabled citizen services for the governments. We saw an opportunity to apply that same strength
at home by building a network that brings formal financial and public services to the last mile.
That remains our purpose today. We operate through our 4 business segments. The first business
segment is our largest, which is the Business Correspondence Servic es. We act as a banking
outlet for our partner banks in villages and small towns, offering account opening, deposits,
withdrawals, remittances, pensions, and government benefit payments.
Page 3 of 6

Our second segment is loan disbursement, where through Aadifidelis, and our BC network, we
source and process loans for banks and NBFCs and connect lenders with rural and semi -urban
borrowers.
Our third segment is e -governance. Here we work with state governments to deliver citizen
services such as Aadhaar enrollment, land records, utility bill collection, and welfare support
schemes.
Our fourth segment is assisted e -services. Here local merchants use our platform to offer
customers.
Now behind all our 4 segments is one operating model which is asset -light and merchant-led.
Our touchpoints are owned or run by local entrepreneurs who invest in their own premises and
equipment. We provide the technology platform, the BLS brand, training, and the partnerships
with banks, financial institutions, and governments. This model has 3 clear advantages. First, it
allows us to expand quickly without large capital spending. Second, our technology costs are
shared across a very large network, so profitability improves as volumes grow.
Third, customers come to us through trusted local merchants, which means we spend very little
on customer acquisition. Our revenue is also well diversified. It comes from transaction
commissions, loan distribution income, registration and renewal fees, and multi -year
government contracts. No single stream dominates. Which makes the business more resilient.
What sets us apart now? Several things set BLS E-Services apart. First, we built one of India's
largest last-mile networks over many years of on -ground work, and this reach is difficult and
time-consuming for anyone else to replicate. Alongside this, we have long -standing
relationships with public and private sector ban ks, NBFCs, insurers, and several state
governments built on trust and consistent delivery.
Next, because every touchpoint can earn from multiple services, each new product we add
brings in revenue without adding much cost. We also have proven acquisition track record with
every acquisition integrated successfully and adding both scale and earnings. Finally, we have
a strong debt-free balance sheet and the backing of the BLS Group, which gives us the flexibility
to keep investing for growth.
Now, if you look at the growth of our business, it has come from steady organic expansion
combined with carefully chosen acquisitions. We began our journey with focus on assisted
digital and citizen services. In 2018, we acquired Star fin India, which gave us our business
correspondent platform and remains the backbone of our banking business today.
In 2022, we acquired Zero Mass, which significantly scaled our BC network and reach. In the
same year, we also acquired BLS Kendras, which strengthened our government -to-citizen

services. In 2024, we listed on the NSE and BSE after a successful IPO and acquired a majority
stake in Aadifidelis Solutions, marking our entry into loan disbursement business.
More recently, in July 2026, we completed the acquisition of Atyati Technologies, which further
increased our scale in the business correspondent business. Each step has added a new capability
or a step change in reach. Over this period, we have grown from a single service provider into
multi-service platform that today serves banks, NBFCs, insurers, state governments, and
millions of citizens.
Let me now give you a quick update on our business. Our loan distribution business together
with Aadifidelis Solutions continues to be an important growth engine. Credit demand in rural
and semi-urban India is strong, and our network gives lenders reach they find hard to build on
their own.
We are now working on co-origination models for micro and agri loans, and on selling insurance
and saving products at the point of loan origination. In e-governance, we offer over 330 citizen
services through our BLS touchpoints. This includes Aadhaar enro llment in Rajasthan, sub -
registrar digitization in Chhattisgarh, and bill collection in Uttar Pradesh.
Earlier this year, we also won mandate from the Government of West Bengal for beneficiary
verification under the Ayushman Bharat schemes. In assisted e-services through our BLS Seva
platform, our merchants now offer more than 700 services from insurance and bill payments to
service shop center for its community.
On technology front, we continue to invest in modern cloud-ready platform, AI-based tools for
reconciliation and agent support and stronger cybersecurity. Our asset -light model helps us
grow quickly while keeping the balance sheet debt-free.
Let me take you to the highlights of the second quarter and the first half of this financial year.

the reduction in interest income.

towards the acquisition of stakes in GScale Energy Private Limited and GL Hakko Company

Director for Dhoot Transmission. In the 2nd Quarter , the automotive industry saw another
strong volume growth performance.
For the two-wheeler industry, the last quarter was one of the best quarters with 16% growth.
Comparing Y-o-Y performance for the quarter, domestic EV industry grew in excess of 100%
and ICE in excess of 10%. Export for two-wheeler grew about 28% as per CM data. Against the
same, Dhoot Transmission saw a very strong growth of 60% on Y-o-Y basis. Revenue from
wiring harness grew 44.6% , Y-o-Y and from non -wiring harness business by 124%. Multilink
acquisition contributed to about Rs. 160 crores during the quarter. EV revenue in the same
quarter grew 108% for us and with this, the overall contribution of EV revenue has now reached
31% of our total sales, up from 27% in Q1 and from 24% of FY 2026. We have started ramping
up volume for the powertrain battery with our new South India-based customer. I am happy
to inform you that in spite of the hard cycle of commodities, our organic adjusted EBITDA
margins remained consistent at 15.2%. Reported EBITDA margins after considering 0.5% ESOP
impact and Multilink consolidation is 14.3%. We expect Multilink margins to improve after the
completion of integration. Pre-exceptional PAT for the quarter is at Rs. 162 crores, which is an
increase of 30% over the same quarter last year. Other than this, we have fully repaid the debt
which was to be repaid out of IPO proceeds and our net cash, bank and FD balance is at Rs. 900

crores, which is in line with our expectations. During the first 6 months, we added two battery
manufacturing plants, one in South and one in West. Both of them have commenced
production. Our new wiring harness plant at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar got functional and we
are already running at full capacity in that plant.

surprised us positively on the growth and provided opportunities. The opportunities have led
us to consider incremental investments in the capacities and acceleration of those. As a result,

various customers. We expect to share more updates in the next quarter on this. Our NPD

Brace Port targets to Double Revenue in FY 28; Strengthens Expansion Plans Through
SageRoute Investment
venture entity projected to generate ₹70–75 crore in revenue over the next 12 months
New Delhi, November 10, 2026: Brace Port Logistics Limited reported a strong financial
performance for the half year ended September 30, 2026, with consolidated revenue from
operations rising 34.9% year-on-year to ₹44.43 crore, compared with ₹32.94 crore in the
corresponding period last year. Profit after tax (PAT) increased 39.5% to ₹3.47 crore, against
₹2.49 crore in H1 FY26, while profit before tax (PBT) grew 38.7% to ₹4.67 crore.
Building on this performance, the management is targeting a doubling of revenue in FY28 and
remains bullish on the business outlook for H2 FY27. The company is focused on scaling its
integrated logistics operations, expanding its service capabilities and pursuing strategic
opportunities to strengthen its position across the logistics value chain.
As part of this strategic expansion strategy, the Board has approved the acquisition of a 76%
stake in SageRoute Logistics Private Limited for a consideration of ₹0.76 lakh, following
which it will become a subsidiary of the Company. The Board has also approved a further
investment of ₹75.24 lakh in SageRoute Logistics Private Limited, alongside a proportionate
investment of ₹23.76 lakh by the other shareholder.
The company’s expansion plans also include a proposed investment of up to ₹7.50 crore in
warehousing infrastructure and related services, including third-party logistics (3PL) and
fourth-party logistics (4PL), subject to the necessary statutory and regulatory approvals.
Commenting on the performance and outlook, Mr. Sachin Arora, Chairman and Managing
Director, Brace Port Logistics Limited, said:
“Our H1 FY27 performance reflects the growth momentum in our business, with revenue
increasing by nearly 35% and profit after tax growing by close to 40% year-on-year. We remain
bullish on the outlook for H2 and are working towards our ambition of doubling revenue in
FY28. Our investment in SageRoute, alongside our plans to expand warehousing and 3PL and
4PL capabilities, is aimed at building scale, broadening our service portfolio and creating new
avenues for growth. We remain focused on strengthening our integrated logistics offering and
delivering sustainable value to our customers and stakeholders.”
The financial results for H1 FY27 were reviewed by the company’s Statutory Auditors, who
issued an unmodified conclusion.

Sohan Lal Agarwal: Thank you, ma'am. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us for Websol Energy
System Limited's earnings call. Wishing you and your loved ones a very happy and prosperous
Deepavali. Before getting into the quarterly numbers, I want to spend a few minutes on the

There is a lot of excitement around renewable energy and solar manufacturing in India today,
and rightly so. We are witnessing a fundamental shift in how India thinks about energy security,
domestic manufacturing, and the role of renewable energy in our future. After more than 30
years in this business, I see a real opportunity for Indian manufacturers who can translate rising
demand into consistent production. High product quality and reliable customer delivery.
This is where I believe our experience gives us an advantage. India added about 30.8 gigawatts
of solar capacity in the first 6 months of this financial year. That is very significant number. The
first half of Calendar Year 2027 has witnessed India's highest ever Solar installation for a 6-

and government programs. With storage and hybrid projects becoming more important, the way
in which solar power is being used are also changing. For a manufacturer like Websol, however,
I see two sides of this opportunity. The first is demand. The second is the structure of
manufacturing itself.
India has built a very large modern manufacturing base, but making reliable, high-efficiency
solar cells is a different challenge. It requires technology, process control, experienced people,
and time to get the right yields. The ALMM List 2 framework is important because it encourages
more domestic cell manufacturing.
The government has allowed a limited commission window for certain projects, but the larger
direction towards domestic value addition remains clear in my view. The companies that do well
will be the ones that can manufacture consistently, control costs, and adapt quickly when the
market changes.
That is the backdrop against which I look at our quarter. Our solar cell line operated at 91%
utilization in Quarter 2. We produced a little over 255 megawatt of cells. I attach importance to
this because it is one thing to install equipment and the other to keep it running at these levels

Backward integration gives us a structural cost advantage, not a temporary pricing benefit.

and capacity building. And we will keep investing in backward integration across our core
portfolio.
Let me now take you through the key financial highlights. In Q2 FY27, revenue from
operations stood at INR316 crores, a growth of 30% over Q2 FY26 and 53% over Q1, driven
by strong volumes and improving price realization. Gross profit, including manufacturing
expenses, rose 41% to INR111 crores and gross margin expanded to 35%.
EBITDA stood at INR68 crores, a growth of 40% with margins expanding 145 basis points to
21%, aided by operating leverage. PAT grew 57% to INR39.6 crores, a PAT margin of
moved from 34% in Q4 FY26 to 36% in Q1 and 35% this quarter.
This was slightly below Q1, but well above the 32% a year ago, driven by backward
integration. EBITDA margins have moved from 17% to 20% and now 21% driven by
operating leverage. For H1 FY27, revenue grew 19% to INR523 crores. EBITDA grew 24% to
INR109 crores, a margin of 21%. PAT grew 36% to INR 59.8 crores. Including our share of
VKT profit, net profit grew 33% to INR60.8 crores.
Moving to our performance by therapeutic area. Our growth this half was broad -based. ARV
and anti-inflammatory led the way. In first half, ARVs grew 47% to INR150 crores on market

share gains and anti -inflammatory grew 25% to INR110 crores on ibuprofen demand from
regulated markets.
Our other therapeutic areas also contributed . Anti-migraine grew 32%, anti -epileptic 44%,
anti-anginal 45% and anti-ED 52%. Across the portfolio, high-value APIs continue to climb as
a share of our revenue to 49% in the first half from 47% in FY26. We are growing our market
share in products where economies of scale and backward integration give us a structural
advantage.
I will now share some key updates on our business. Starting with R&D, our team has over 200
professionals and has completed 19 DMF and CEP filings over the last 24 months. We
continued that momentum into this quarter. So far we have completed 6 filings, 4 in the first
half and 2 more in October, well on track for our FY27 target of 10.
They cover anti -ulcer, anti -migraine, antidepressant, antifungal and antifibrotic APIs. As a
result of these APIs, we now expect 6 to 8 new molecules to sta rt commercial production in
FY28. As they scale up over the following six quarters, we expect them to be EBITDA
accretive and to diversify our revenue.
On ibuprofen, we expect to complete our remaining capex in the coming quarters. This will
take our total capacity to 9,600 tons a year and the volumes will ramp up gradually over the
next few quarters. Turning to our capex program , we have deployed INR160 crores of the
INR280 crores program so far and the program remains on track for completion by FY27.
It adds capacity for few of our existing molecules and for the 6 to 8 new molecules in our
pipeline. Coming to peptides and CDMO, we have set up SMS Peptides Private Limited, a
99.9% owned subsidiary to build a dedicated peptide business. Its peptides R&D facility is
now fully operational.
To support its expansion, the Board recently approved a loan of INR50 crores to the
subsidiary. Pilot scale production is targeted for Q4 FY27 and we expect our first CRO
revenue from it in Q2 FY28. We have also set up SMS coLab Private Limited, a wholly owned
subsidiary which will serve as a dedicated CDMO platform for APIs and peptides.
Finally, let me turn to our outlook. For FY27, guidance was revenue growth of 15% with an
EBITDA margin of 20% . With pricing in our key APIs expected to remain stable in the near
term and on the back of a strong first half and the outlook for the rest of the year, we now

With that, let me introduce the management team present on call today. We have with us Mr.

Pranav Amin: Thank you, Isha. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us to discuss the Alembic

quarter, performance across our businesses, and a revised outlook for FY2 7. I will also discuss
the collaboration we announced with DifGen in the U.S. market, and then Krishnan will take
you through the financials in detail.
The second quarter builds decisively on the momentum of our first quarter and marks an
important step up in the quality of our performance. Consolidated revenue for the quarter was
at INR2,603 crores, representing a growth of 36% Y-on-Y, driven by strong performances across
all the business.
Coming to the India business, it delivered a 14% year-on-year growth in the quarter, led by the
Human Health, which returned to double -digit growth at 11%. The commercial interventions
initiated over the past few quarters are translating into visible impro vement in field force
productivity and execution. Growth is being supported by chronic and specialty therapies with
strong performance in gynecology, cardiology, and emerging therapies.
The specialty portfolio grew about 200 basis points ahead of the Indian pharmaceutical market
during the quarter, and the overall growth gap versus the market has narrowed meaningfully.
We expect the acute portfolio to improve progressively over the coming quarters as well. Animal
Health maintained its strong momentum, growing 23% in Q2 FY27.
In India, our near term objective is to reach market level growth in the next 2 to 3 quarters. We
expect this to be driven by sharper execution in focused brands and priority markets, stronger

presence in metros and a higher contribution from chronic and specialty therapies while broadly
maintaining the current field force scale.
Moving on to the international business. The U.S. Generics delivered an exceptional quarter
with revenue growing at 72% year -on-year. The performance was supported by strong volume
growth in the base portfolio as well as meaningful contributions from recent launches. While the
new launches, including bosutinib, provided an important uplift, the underlying business also
demonstrated healthy operating momentum, growing at 23%.

Moving to the U.S. branded business , the portfolio is now in place and commercial traction is

to long-term potential.

validation of our strategic transition to a pure-play finished dosage formulation platform. Operating
scale and an improved product mix have driven significant operating leverage, margin expansion,

partnerships with major CDMO partners are progressing rapidly on track to del iver ₹100 to ₹130

have crossed 900+ across 85 countries, backed by 2,100+ filed dossiers. Over 330 additional
product registrations are expected in FY27. Warehouse development adjacent to our 100% EOU
Derabassi facility is underway to support export volumes. Concurrently, the ₹45 crore upgrade of
our Samba facility to EU -GMP and PIC/S standards is on schedule to unlock regulated market
access for topical and oral formulations, and it shall supplement both CDMO and own -branding
business of our company.

verticals continue to provide steady cash flow stability with 17.3% of total sales. Own brands
contributed 55.75% of quarterly sales, representing 69% of export sales, driven by direct marketing
and field force expansion across GCC countries, Central Asia, and Africa. Contract manufacturing
accounted for 26.99% of sales, supported by scaling supplies to global generic majors. Branded
generics accounted for 6.84% via our Healthcare and Agile divisions. Ethical division contributed
5.43%, led by chronic, pediatric, and gynecology therapies. Contract manufacturing stood at 5%,
supported by 39 repeat domestic clients.

This quarter marks another important milestone for Redington. We delivered the strongest
quarterly revenue and profit after tax in our history, not in the benign envi ronment, but against
a backdrop of geopolitical disruption, changing component prices and continued supply chain
complexity.
The outcome says as much about the quality of our execution as it does about the strength of
demand across our markets. We are in like a multi-verse phenomenon. Consolidated revenue for
Q2 FY27 was INR43,002 crores, up 48% year -on-year. Profit after tax, excluding exceptional
items, rose 50% to INR581 crores. Excluding Arena, this looks even better. Revenue expanded
54% and profit after tax increased 55% to INR657 crores.
Growth remained broad and the core business converted that growth into stronger earnings. For
the first half of '27, consolidated revenue reached INR77,967 crores, a growth of 41% year-on-
year, while profit after tax, excluding exceptional items reached INR1,067 crores, growing at
61%. Both are the highest Redington has recorded in any first half…
These results are not built around a single brand market or technology cycle. They reflect a
portfolio designed for resilience, scale businesses that generate reach, value business that deepen
relevance and emerging capabilities that prepare us for the nex t phase of technology adoption
over the next few years.

world excluding Arena grew 38%. Contributions by GCCL. These are the GCC countries in the
Levant countries outside of UAE and Saudi grew 121%. UAE grew 39% and Africa grew 35%.

demonstrates the relevance of our portfolio across these markets.

Chennai, November 10th, 2026: Vishnusurya Projects & Infra Limited, a leading Indian infrastructure
company, engaged in EPC projects and manufacturing of construction aggregates & manufactured
sand, announced its un-audited financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September

Management Commentary
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Sanal Kumar, Director and CEO said:
“While the underlying business continues to offer opportunities for growth, the operating environment
during Q2 FY27 remained challenging. A slowdown in tendering activity, increased competitive intensity
and temporary disruptions at our Hosur facility, coupled with higher raw material costs, impacted our
performance. Consolidated revenue stood at ₹69 crore, while EBITDA was ₹8 crore.
On the EPC front, the pace of new tendering activity remained relatively slow and at the same time,
increased competition led to aggressive bidding across certain projects. In this environment, we have
remained selective in pursuing opportunities, prioritising projects that offer sustainable margins and
execution visibility rather than focusing solely on order inflows.
Our unexecuted order book stood at ₹327.70 crore as of September 30, 2026, providing visibility for
future execution. We remain focused on progressing our existing projects, improving operational
efficiencies and strengthening our order pipeline.
Looking ahead, we anticipate a gradual improvement in tendering activity and the potential
resumption of operations at Hosur, subject to regulatory and legal developments, would also support
our operational recovery. Our priority remains disciplined execution, margin protection and converting
opportunities into profitable growth over the coming quarters.”
About Vishnusurya Projects and Infra Limited:
Vishnusurya Projects and Infra Limited (NSE: SME: VISHNUINFR) have a diverse set of business spread
across Engineering Procurement and Constructions (EPC), manufacturing of aggregates &
manufactured- sand, solid waste management, leasing of commercial space etc. Company is engaged
in mining rough stones and manufacturing aggregates & manufactured sand by using Crushing Plants
and Sand washing plants. In EPC projects division the Company has delivered across all key sectors such
as water, transportation, rail, resources, and institutional development. The Company also designs and
constructs various infrastructure projects for the government, autonomous and private bodies in state
of Tamil Nadu. Vishnusurya collaborates extensively with clients and partners to execute projects that

Kunal Shah: Yes. Good afternoon. Welcome to the 2Q F27 Earnings Call of Container Corporation of India.
We have the management being represented by Mr. Ajit Kumar, the Chairman and Managing
Director. I would like to hand over the call to Ajit sir for his opening remarks, post which we
can take up the Q&A. Thanks, and over to you sir.
Ajit Kumar Panda: Good morning, Mr. Kunal, and good morning to all the participants who have joined this
conference call. Along with me, we have got the management team, Mr. Vijoy Singh, our
Director, International Marketing and Operations; Mr. Vivek Gupta, Director (Finance);
Principal Executive Director (Finance) and Company Secretary, Mr. Harish Chandra.
And our Group General Manager, International Marketing, Mr. Paresh Agarwal. So you are now
welcome to ask your questions. Before you ask the questions, I will give my opening remarks.
I'm very happy to announce a fairly decent results under very challenging geopolitical
circumstances.
CONCOR has demonstrated remarkable resilience amidst the adverse circumstances. We have
recorded highest ever physical performance in any quarter by posting total handling volume of
1,448,379 TEUs. We have posted highest ever operating turnover at INR2,373 crores and
highest ever total income in any quarter, INR2,466 crores. The revenue growth has been 0.93%.
We have announced a dividend of INR1.9 per share, and the total dividend has now gone up to
INR3.5 per share in the first half.
We have also reported handsome profits. The profits -- stand-alone profit before tax has been
INR462 crores, that is amounting INR154 crores per month, a very remarkable performance
given the adverse circumstances through which we have gone. As all of you are aware, a
ceasefire, which was announced in the Gulf, it collapsed in a few days and the Strait of Hormuz
for container traffic remains practically closed.
The ports, which were the engines of trade in West Asia, they are not handling that. The trade
has shifted to new ports of Khor Fakkan and Fujairah. And also our ports on both on the Western
side and Eastern side, they are doing handling. They are doing transhipment of cargo, which
used to be transhipped in the ports of the Gulf region.
Therefore, there has been lots of turbulence in the trade. But despite that, we have posted
handsome results. Throughput in the H1 in the EXIM segment has increased by 4.57% and
domestic segment, 4.22%, total 4.48%.

more containers. Total containers have increased to about 1,100 and the volume we have
reported about 12,000 TEUs vis-a-vis the entire year of 14,000 TEUs last year. We have added
13 new rakes in the quarter, taking the total 32 in the half year. Total number of rakes now stands
at 456.
We have added 414 containers and we have also added 7 reach stackers into our fleet. Capex

as I saw it when I was coming into the organisation, and what I believe I have

performance and what we're going to be doing next.

day one at Dabur felt, right? This is truly an amazing organisation with a very
rich heritage. We're all aware: for 142 years, we've been here building on a lot
of trust that the consumers have bestowed on us during this time. It feels great
to have the privilege and the honour to be part of this business. And now, to
be able to look to take it forward as we speak. You're familiar with the fact that
Dabur is in 8 out of 10 Indian households. We always keep talking about the
distribution reach that Dabur has. But, you know, when I look at the portfolio,

but more importantly, they are robust category leaders, defining category,
defining brands, with a lot of headroom, given that we still have low levels of
penetration here. I think the exciting part is what you see at the bottom. These
are the brands, the brands of the future. The brands that have a lot of potential.
And anyone who gets the opportunity to get a stable of brands that looks like
this should consider themselves as a leader, lucky to be at the helm of driving
change or driving what comes next. Now, our aim, or ambition, is to be, or to

create demand for specialized welding consumables, wear protection products, heavy handling
equipment, and maintenance solutions.
