Conference Call hosted by Valorem Advisors.
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need any assistance
during this conference, please signal for an operator by pressing “*” and then “0” on your
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. Thank you and
over to you ma'am.
Purvangi Jain: Thank you. Good afternoon , everyone and a very warm welcome to you all. My name is
Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors.
We represent the investor relations of PRICOL Limited. On behalf of the company and Valorem
Advisors, I would like to thank you all for participating in the Company's Earnings Conference
Call for the second quarter of the financial year 2027.
Before we begin, let me mention a short cautionary statement. Some of the statements made
in today's earnings call may be forward-looking in nature. Such forward-looking statements are
subject to risk and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ from those
anticipated. Such statements are based on management's belief as well as assumptions made
by and information currently available to the management. Audiences are cautioned not to
place any undue reliance on these forward -looking statements in making any investment
decisions.
The purpose of today's earnings call is purely to educate and bring awareness about the
company's fundamental business and financial quarter under review.
I would now like to introduce you to the management team joining us on today's call. We have
with us Mr. P.M. Ganesh – Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director , Mr. Siddharth
Manoharan – Group Executive Director, Business Strategy , Ms. Madhura Mohan – Executive
Director, Customer Relationship Management and ESG and Mr. Priyadarsi Bastia – Chief
Financial Officer.
Without any further delay, I request Mr. P.M. Ganesh to start with his opening remarks. Thank
you and over to you, sir.
P.M. Ganesh: Thank you, Purvangi. Good evening to all. Welcome to the Q2 earnings call. It is our pleasure
in connecting with all of you once again. I am sure that you had some time to go through our
uploaded presentation. So without any further waiting, let me go into the financial
performance straight away.
The Q2 financial performance, we have crossed more than a Rs. 1,000 crores in quarter 2. Rs.
1334.02 crores has been our revenue from operations. We are at an EBITDA margin of 11.82%.
It could have been better. If you recall in the previous earnings call, we have explained that we
continue to face very strong headwinds , primarily because of the rising input cost. This has
been the condition even during Q1 and it is continuing in Q2 as well.
Primarily because of three reasons: 1) One is the strong dollar appreciation against the rupee
and rupee has been continuously weakening. And due to the large import content in our
product, the bill of material cost has been rising. 2) Second, as we all know that the bare PCB
cost has been continuously increasing, which is a major ingredient in the instrument cluster.
Primarily because of the West Asia crisis. 3) And third is the memory cost increase which has
gone up primarily because of surge in the AI. We expect these strong headwinds to continue
for a few more quarters before everything gets settled down.
Coming to the PAT:
PAT has been at Rs. 85.21 crores. The margin is at 6.39%. On H1 performance for financial year
2027, our operation stands at Rs. 2417.60 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.64%. The PAT
stood at 6.30% with EPS at 12.49.
Coming to the Quarter-on-Quarter comparison:
Q2 for financial year 20 27 when compared to the previous quarter of last financial year, the
growth has been 35.03% in terms of revenue from operation. The EBITDA growth has been
27.87%. On a H1 performance basis when compared to the previous year, the growth has been
29.59% with an EBITDA growth of 24.95%.
With this, I will hand over the mic back to Purvangi for the Q&A session. Thank you.
Moderator: Thank you very much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin with the question and
answer session. The first question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from Goldman Sachs. Please
go ahead.
Rishabh Rathi: Good evening, sir, and thank you for taking my question. My first question is around the gross
margin impact. If you look at the gross margin, it has declined 150 bps quarter-on-quarter. But
on the EBITDA margin, we have been able to sustain roughly similar margins. I just wanted to
understand has some pass -through happened already or otherwise if there was no gross
margin impact, while the plants are still ramping up, what could have been the EBITDA margin
percentage in 2Q?
P.M. Ganesh: That is what I have mentioned. The input material cost has been continuously going up because
of the three factors, whatever I just mentioned during the opening remark. And this is expected
to continue for at least a few quarters before it is getting normalized. And that is the reason
why you find that the EBITDA level is lower than the growth, whatever we approach in terms
of the top line.
Rishabh Rathi: Could some settlement happen in 3Q or 4Q?
P.M. Ganesh: Yes, actually, many of the cases we have already taken up with our customers, and customers
are evaluating that. But as you know that there are new contents in the rising cost, primarily
bare PCBs and memory cost and sharp increases in the labor cost. These things are something
that the customers are evaluating because these are first -time rising costs. So you know
customers also cannot pass on all the increases into the market. So this is currently under
evaluation and discussion with our customers. And hopefully, we should be in a position to
conclude it during the next quarter. But however, we expect that we would not be in a position
to 100% recover from the customers, considering that everything the customer also cannot
pass on to the end customer.
Rishabh Rathi: Right. And just for clarification, PCBs and
semiconductor would not form a large part of our
build of material right? Could the impact be somewhere around 10 bps to 20 bps, or could it
be larger than that?
P.M. Ganesh: See, I would not be in a position to give you the exact breakup detail, but bare PCBs do have a
major content in the build -off material. I would also request that one question at a time, and
then maybe you can join the queue for further questions, please.
Rishabh Rathi: Got it. Thank you.
Moderator: Thank you. The next question is from the line of Hitesh Goyal from Origin Capital. Please go
ahead.
Hitesh Goyal: Thanks for taking my question. Sir, can you give us the growth rates in the DIS business, ACFMS
P.M. Ganesh: We have overall, Hitesh, grown by 35%, okay? And all the three divisions have seen more or
less the same level of growth. So that is why you find when compared to the previous year,
quarter 2, we have grown by 35%.
Hitesh Goyal: Okay. So no segment has grown?
P.M. Ganesh: All our vertical has grown actually at the same rate, whatever I mentioned to you.
Hitesh Goyal: And sir, you said that, just for clarification, you said that next quarter also you will see the
headwinds, you can see that. But are you saying that gross margin could deteriorate further in
the next quarter? We will see at this 11%, 12% kind of EBITDA range?

advanced features continue to expand our content per vehicle opportunity. In Q2 FY 2027, SJS

TeamLease Quarter Two FY 2027 earnings call. Today, we have with us the management team
of TeamLease, represented by Ms. Suparna Mitra, Managing Director and CEO, Ms. Ramani
Dathi, CFO and COO, Ms. Neeti Sharma, CEO of Specialized Staffing, and Mr. Bala A, Senior

Suparna Mitra: Thank you so much. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for being with us today.
I will share my perspective on the quarter and the priorities, after which, of course, we will take
your questions. The first half of FY 2027 has been a period of d eliberate reset for TeamLease.
We recognize that this quarter's results fell short of our own aspirations and of the expectations
of our stakeholders. At the same time, the actions we are taking will positio n the business on a
stronger and more profitable footing in the future.
The revenue for the quarter was INR3,086 crores, which is up 1% seq uentially and year-on-year.
For the half year, revenue grew 4% to INR6,142 crores. Operating EBITDA was INR44 crores,
up 17% sequentially and 5% year-on-year. For the half year, it grew 11% to INR82 crores.
It is encouraging that our operating businesses are growing profit faster than revenue. Reported
EBITDA was INR36 crores, a margin of 1.2%, and higher sequentially. Year-on-year, it reflects
our investment in a brand and marketing revamp and buyback-related costs held in unallocated.
Profit before tax was INR30 crores, up 2% year-on-year. For the half year, it was INR66 crores,
up 19%. For clarity, this includes other income, such as interest on income tax refund received
in quarter one.
Operating EBITDA remains a better indicator of underlying progress. Profit a fter tax was INR26
crores. Our headcount moderated to about 333,200. Sorry, 333,2 00. We added 114 new logos,
including 32 in general staffing, of which more than three-quarters were on boarded under the
variable engagement model. 30% of the associates we hired were first-time jo b seekers, which
remains central to our purpose of putting India to work.
DSO held at six days. Specialized staffing continues to be a strong con tributor. Revenue was
INR190 crores, with EBITDA growing in double digits sequentially. The India business earned
a 7.6% EBITDA margin and global 4.3%. GCCs contributed over 69% of the segment revenue,

and we now serve more than 135 plus GCC clients, up from over 110 at the end of last year.
This is the profile of business we intend to grow.
In HR services, revenue rose sequentially on EdTech seasonality, with a segm ent EBITDA
margin of 3%. We are focused on strengthening the commercial engine of HR tech solutions,
where the opportunity is significant. Our priorities rest on three pillars. First, a sharper focus on
higher-margin businesses. We will direct capital, talent, and leadership atte ntion to businesses
with the strongest returns, including international geographies, while pursuing growth in general
staffing. Second, disciplined portfolio management.
Every business and investment will be assessed on returns, strategic fit. The divestment of our
30% stake in Crystal HR, completed this quarter with no loss on capital investe d, is an early
example. We may have to weed some of the non-aligned businesses, which allow bandwidth to
seed new verticals. Third, to establish TeamLease as a holistic talent solutions partner.
We bring recruitment, staffing, apprenticeship, productivity, compliance , and HR technology

about 2,500 in March. These investments weigh modestly on near -term margins and on
productivity per core employee. We expect them to build a stronger platform for the years ahead.

July, we hold INR350 crores worth of net free cash, with about INR160 crores of TDS receivable
outstanding. Funding exposure in staffing was 16%. The long-term opp ortunity is compelling.
The formalization of India's workforce is deepening. The central rules under Labour Codes have
been notified, and GCCs continue to create demand for specialized talen t. TeamLease is
positioning itself to lead in that environment.

and happy to take your questions after that.

quarter with over 7,000 associates.

continued to shift into tier 2 and tier 3 markets. That progress was outweigh ed by reductions in

Moderator: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Conference Call of Muthoot Capital
Services Limited, arranged by Concept Investor Relations to discuss its Q2 and H1 FY27 Results.
Before we begin, let me mention a quick short cautionary statement. Some of the statements
made in today's earnings call may be forward -looking in natur e. Such forward -looking
statements are subject to risk and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ from
those anticipated. Such statements made on the management's belief as well as assumptions
made by the information currently available to the management.
Audiences are cautioned not to place any undue reliance on these forward-looking statements
in making any investment decisions. The purpose of today's Earnings Call is purely to educate
and bring awareness about the company's fundamental business and the financial quota under
review. Let me now introduce you to the Management.
We have with us today Mr. Mathews -Markose – Chief Executive Officer, and Mr. Ramandee p
Gill – Chief Financial Officer. Please note that this conference will be recorded. I would now like
to hand the floor to Mr. Mattews-Markose – Chief Executive Officer.
Thank you and over to you, sir.
Mathews Markose: Thank you, Neerav. And good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining us for the
Muthoot Capital Services Earnings Call for the 2nd Quarter and H1 for September ‘26.
Let me begin by wishing all our shareholders, investors, lenders, and business partners a very
Happy Dhanteras and Diwali and a great festive season ahead.
Talking about the first half of the year, it's been a period of consolidation, strengthening of our
institutional capabilities and building a stronger foundation for sustainable growth. But along
with that, made meaningful progress across several important areas like asset quality, credit
underwriting, diversification of our funding, and of course, as usual, on technology.
I wish to highlight some of the developments that we were able to achieve during the first half
of the year. Firstly, our institutional strength and credit standing got a boost with the rating
upgrade to AA from Brickwork’s. This reflects the company's improving financial performance,
discipline, governance, and strengthening business fundamentals.
Page 3 of 14
It's a very, very important milestone for us because it reimburses our ability to access
diversified funding sources, including going PAN India for our FD product. As you are aware, we
are deposit-taking NBFC, and we were restricted to accepting deposits from the state of Kerala
alone. But with this AA rating and through the digital platform, we are now allowed to go PAN
India, and we have already launched our Pan India FD campaign.
Secondly, on the business performance and growth, the vehicle finance industry has witnessed
very healthy momentum in H1, though there were apprehensions about the war and increasing
oil prices, etc., but the industry has beaten all odds and shown up 21% growth in the first half
of the year. Two-wheeler segment has recorded about 16% growth, and both passenger as well
as commercial vehicle has registered very healthy growth rate in H1. And against this industry
backdrop, we achieved a cumulative disbursement in excess of Rs. 1,200 crores.
More details on the numbers will be given by CFO, Ramandeep. Our commercial vehicle and
construction equipment disbursements increased significantly by over 100%, and so has been
the case with our used car financing, though the base has been small, but we' ve been able to
make very significant strides in both these businesses, and those continue to be our core area
of focus. Going forward while two-wheeler will continue to be the warhorse.
Another milestone that we crossed in H1 was that our AUM crossed Rs. 3,500 crores as on
September, reflecting a continued expansion of our core lending franchise. We are also
consciously working towards a more diversified portfolio and channel mix by increasing the
share of partners, getting into more OEMs by getting into preferred financial tie-ups, as well as
increasing the product diversification. This is an important indicator of the improvement in our
origination, quality, and collection effectiveness.
We have also strengthened our early warning mechanism, improving collection interventions
and focusing on resolution of the existing stress portfolios. Moving forward, our asset quality
and collection remains a very, very important priority for us, and we have made encouraging
progress in strengthening our collection. Collection efficiency in all our buckets have improved,
and the most heartening part is that our forward flow to NPA has reduced by 31% over the last
year's same time.
In the last year, we had a forward flow of about 0.78%, which has come down to 0.5%, which
is a very, very significant improvement. We have also made significant progress in
strengthening our liability franchise. Our deposit book grew by over 100%, and largely because
of the online intervention that we started in the beginning of this year.
And with us going PAN India, as I mentioned before, this will further add weight to that. On
technology, we've been continuously investing, and with the help of AI, we've been able to
bring in -house a lot of the scorecards, BREs that we were currently outsourcing to various
vendors. What it has done is that our time to market has significantly improved.
Page 4 of 14
Earlier, whenever we would want to make a change in any of our policies on the BREs front, it
would attract a change request with the vendor, and the request would be placed to the
vendor. There will be a commercial involved, and there would be an internal approval to be
taken. And therefore, all of these would delay the time to market.
Now, on the entire two -wheeler piece, all the BREs and the scorecards have been moved in -
house with our own data science team, and the risk separation has been much better than the
scorecards built by the vendors earlier. So, I think it's a very, very significant milestone for us
in that respect. This quarter, we will be also bringing in all the BREs and the scorecards for
commercial vehicles and used cars also in-house.
And the timeline that we have taken internally is December for that. Looking ahead, our
priorities for the second half are accelerating disbursement, improving productivity across our
channels, including dealer and alternate channels, scaling our commercial vehicle construction
equipment and used car businesses, and building our Pan-India FD franchise. At the same time,
we will remain disciplined on credit quality, collections, operating costs, and capital efficiency.
We don't intend to pursue growth at the expense of asset quality. Our emphasis will always be
on a profitable growth supported by stronger underwriting and better risk management. With
that opening remark, I would like to hand over to Ramandeep Gil l, our CFO, for taking you all
through the financials. Thank you very much. O

across 10,000 circuit kilometers of lines, 34,000 MVA substation capacity, around 1.5 gigawatt

Let me start with the headlines for the first half. For the past 2 years, our growth was around

testing, alongside the continued expansion of our network.

priorities. The broad picture of the industry remains consistent with what we have shared with
you before. The market is stable and the structural shift from unorganized to organized segment
continues, driven by a greater emphasis on quality and accuracy, rising demand for specialty
testing, technology-led convenience and the move to preventive health care , and wider access
in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. Diagnostics is not merely a price -driven business. It is a
fundamental business driven by science, accuracy, service quality and the trust of doctors and
patients.
Putting in a simple way, the market is moving towards quality and science, and that's exactly
where Metropolis has been built to compete. What is new today and what I would like to spend
time on is the increasingly constructive role of government towards h ealth care. Over the past
several months, we have seen the government move to raise the bar on the diagnostics industry
on quality, transparency and access rather than controlling price.
Together, these developments move the industry in a direction that clearly favors organized,

and service. Firstly, on price cap on pharma products for hospitals. There has been a lot of

aimed at hospital pricing.
They do not extend to diagnostics, and there is no move towards price capping or price parity in
our segment. Diagnostic pricing at organized chains is also transparent and, in most cases,
significantly lower than comparable tests in a hospital setting. Se cond, the display of rates at
centers. The requirement of display rates at centers at the point of service is a welcome change

production for the season 2026-27 with a downside risk, knowing that diversion

edge and strengthening the Core.
Safe Harbour Statement
So, this is a safe harbor statement. This presentation contains forward -looking statements regarding

statements are inherently uncertain and subject to risks. So, while Kalyani Forge endeavors to ensure

Q2 FY27 Highlights

a Rs.45 crore funding plan. With an indicative mix of equity around 10 crores, debt 20 crores, and non -
core asset and inventory monetization up to 20 crores. To strengthen liquidity and fund, the order book
ramp up. This is historic milestone, and we are now becoming much more structurally, Strategic about
funding. Which is logically the next step in our transformation roadmap.
So going forward, more and more funding is going to be a core discussion point in the board, and top
management level at Kalyani Forge. H1 FY27 PBT was 9.39 crores, up 118% YOY . PAT is, 6.64 crores, up

H1 FY26, which is the same period last year.

consecutive quarter above 14%. And PBT, 3.24 crores, is up for 42.9% YOY , PAT, 2.16 crores, and earnings
per share, Rs.5.94. The drug segment has been up 75% year-on-year to 23.3 crores, now around 43% of
sales.
There's a big market pull from the truck segment, and it is going to continue. Over, foreseeable future.
Cars, trucks, and industrial are 97% of sales against 82% a year ago. And this, lines up with our strategic
market segment and customer mix targets planned transitions absorbed in Q2.
So, we had 2 months of reconditioning of a 2,500-ton press, and relocation of the driveline mac hining
plant to MCD1. This was a major, operational initiatives that were taken as part of the Vriddhi Council

And the axle business is also a fast-growing segment, both in commercial vehicles and passenger cars.
Growth Formula

the, team members of that plant. So, this will increase efficiencies, going forward, and hence we have

Along with that, the reconditioning of a major press, required some downtime, due to which we had to

leverage, improved business mix and enhanced operational efficiencies.
• Strong PAT Growth: Profit After Tax increased by 126.29% with PAT margins improving from 8.12% to 9.52%,
reflecting the Company’s ability to translate business growth into improved profitability.
• Sustainable Business Expansion: The Company continues to strengthen its business ecosystem through product
innovation, an expanding distribution network, customer relationships and increasing participation in India’s
fast-growing solar and energy storage markets.

GP Eco Solutions continues to witness healthy demand across its solar and energy storage portfolio, supported by its
growing customer base and expanding project pipeline.
As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s under execution order book stood at ₹534.59 crore, providing strong
revenue visibility for the coming quarters. The Company has also highlighted a consolidated order book position of
₹769 crore, reflecting the scale of business opportunities and project visibility across its operations.
Management Commentary

said:
We are pleased to report a strong H1 FY27 performance, with revenue growing by 92.97%, EBITDA by 176.78% and
Profit After Tax by 126.29% year-on-year, alongside improved EBITDA and PAT margins, reflecting enhanced
operational efficiency and profitable growth.
Our growth reflects increasing traction across solar inverters, battery energy storage system (BESS), rooftop solar
and EPC businesses. We remain focused on scaling our proprietary Invergy™ brand, expanding our product portfolio
and strengthening our integrated renewable energy platform through GPES Green.
With an under-execution order book of ₹534.59 crore and a consolidated order book of ₹769 crore, we have
encouraging business visibility. Our focus remains on timely execution, geographical expansion, strengthening
customer relationships and capturing emerging opportunities in the solar and energy storage markets.
India’s growing renewable energy landscape presents significant opportunities. We aim to build GP Eco Solutions
into a trusted and scalable renewable energy enterprise, delivering sustainable growth and long-term stakeholder
value.

wholly-owned subsidiaries, the Company has an established presence across North India and remains committed to
supporting India's clean energy transition.

geopolitical situations mainly arising out of the conflict in West Asia. This has resulted in a squeezing of

costs. The industry is still in reactionary mode and events are evolving on a regular basis. The company

at the end of March 2026 to 0.55 at the end of September 2026.

secure by diversifying its crude sourcing basket. When Middle East term cargoes were curtailed by the
situation in the Strait of Hormuz, we stepped up domestic crude and spot purchases. In Q2, domestic

MRPL. MRPL's investment will be to the tune of %12.5 crore. This JV is formed for marketing of
petrochemicals and related products. It is expected to enhance the petrochemical business and
operational planning, and reduce costs through improved logistics, warehousing, grade optimisation and
customer management.

petroleum products (ATF) pipeline from Devanagonthi to Bengaluru airport. This is expected to be

at the end of March 2026 to 0.55 at the end of September 2026.

secure by diversifying its crude sourcing basket. When Middle East term cargoes were curtailed by the
situation in the Strait of Hormuz, we stepped up domestic crude and spot purchases. In Q2, domestic
crude made up about a quarter of our intake, term contracts about a fifth, and spot purchases the balance,
drawn mainly from West Africa, the Americas, the Middle East and Russia. Russian barrels made up about
decided on delivered economics.
Andhra Pradesh. The half-yearly retail margin continued to be marginally negative. The capex for financial
year 2026-27 is expected to be in the range of %1,200 crore to 21,500 crore, which includes refinery
maintenance, revamping, and small-value IRR projects including retail projects.

is, ONGC Petrochemicals Marketing Limited, with a 50% stake held by ONGC, 25% by OPal and 25% by

date kept for submission of declaration and other forms and deduct TDS accordingly.
d. Valid PAN will be mandatorily required. However, if the PAN is not updated or is

then the higher rate as per the Act (i.e., 20%) would apply subject to threshold

under section 395 of the Act for TDS at a lower/Nil rate, tax will be deducted at the
rate specified in the said certificate subject to furnishing a self-attested copy of the

quarter and first half of FY27 Earnings Call.
We gained momentum in the second quarter , with revenue growing by 20%,
operating EBITDA by 18% and PAT by 10%. Demand for quality healthcare remains
strong across the hospital Network, with occupancy holding steady at 77% , despite
a 14% year-on-year increase in operational bed capacity.
Occupancy and revenue across all 3 brownfield expansions, namely Max Nanavati
in Mumbai, Max Mohali and Max Smart at Saket, Delhi, have ramped up very well
and in line with our expectations. At Max Smart, the newly commissioned 260 beds
achieved EBITDA breakeven within 3 months of operations and are now witnessing

on EBITDA of Saket Complex during Q2. Excluding the Saket complex, revenue grew
by 20% and EBITDA by 25%. We expect to commission the remaining 140 beds after
Diwali puja.
Encouraged by these quick ramp -ups, we continue to explore opportunities to add
capacity at our existing hospitals. In this regard, the Board has approved an
investment of INR 415 crore towards addition of 209 brownfield beds at Max Noida,
Max Vaishali and BLK-Max, along with a multi-level car park (MLCP) tower at BLK at
crore. Most of this capacity is expected to becom e available over the next 18 to 24
months.
During the quarter, 202 brownfield beds were added to the operational capacity,
mainly at Max Smart, Max Lucknow, Max Noida and Max Dwarka. Services have
also commenced at the new oncology block at Max Dwarka, wh ich will enable
addition of around 20 beds to the hospital in Q3 FY27.
Following the rights issue by Kalinga Hospital Limited, our shareholding has
increased to 66%. A new leadership team has taken charge of Max Bhubaneswar
and clinical teams have been ad ded across gastroenterology, GI surgery,
neurosurgery and orthopaedics. The hospital reported a revenue of INR 38 crore and
EBITDA of INR 4 crore for the quarter. We have commenced renovation of this
facility, and the first part will start rolling out towards the end of the year.

1) Average occupancy for the Network was 77%, similar to last year, despite a 14%
increase in operational bed capacity.
2) Occupied bed day s (OBDs) were up by 13% year -on-year and 7% quarter -on-
quarter.
3) Average revenue per patient (IP ARPP) for the quarter stood at INR 2.31 lakhs,
growing by 8% year -on-year. This growth was partly driven by a decline in
institutional bed share to 29%, from 34% last year.
4) Network gross revenue stood at INR 3,219 crore compared to INR 2,692 crore
in Q2 last year and INR 2,982 crore in the previous quarter. This reflects an
increase of 20% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter.

oncology for in-patient revenues dropped to 21%, from 26% in Q2 FY26.
Excluding oncology, gross revenue grew by 25% and ARPP grew by 11% year-
on-year.
5) International patient revenue was INR 307 crore, registering significant growth of
33% year -on-year and now accounts for 10% of healthcare revenue from
hospitals.
6) Digital revenue from online marketing activities, web -based appointments and
quarter, growing by 44% year-on-year.
7) Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 820 crore versus INR 694 crore
in Q2 FY26 and INR 704 crore in the previous quarter, reflecting growth of 18%
year-on-year and a significant growth of 16% quarter-on-quarter. While EBITDA
per bed grew by 4% year-on-year to INR 77 lakhs per annum.
8) Operating EBITDA margin was 26.8%, similar to Q2 FY26, despite 14% increase

points over the trailing quarter.
9) Profit after tax (PAT) for the Network was INR 448 crore, against INR 406 crore

In the second quarter, total income was INR 209 crore, up nearly 20% over last year. The EBITDA was INR
51.3 crore at a margin of 24.5%; and profit after tax was INR 33.4 crore, up 26% on YoY basis. For the first

single line of business.
As our scale has increased, so have our working capital needs. Receivables have grown in line with the
business; however, in terms of the number of days, it remains around the same level. Though the revenue
has increased, we have paid the creditors without delay resulting in decline in creditors in spite of the
increase in revenue. And this has weighed on the operating cash flow in the first half. Our incremental
planned CapEx for the year is around INR 23 crore.
We continue to open new doors this quarter. In Africa, we won the national PK I for Nigeria's certifying
authority regulator; our entry into that market. In CAS, we secured our first win in Kazakhstan with a

our IP, we move at our own pace without depending on anyone else's roadmap.

eight intermediate certificates within one of our public TLS hierarchies created during a key -generation
ceremony in April 2025. We revoked all eight the very next day. None of them had been used to issue any
certificate to end customers and our root keys were not affected. Our infrastructure was not
compromised, no data was breached, and security controls remained intact.
As a precaution, the browser programs have distrusted the related route. We moved potentially affected
customers to replacement certificates from other trusted providers at no cost to them. We have
appointed KPMG as an independent external reviewer and a full review of our ceremony procedures is
underway. We take this seriously, and we will share what we learned.
In the last two weeks, we did see some impact on our reputation as customers sought to understand what
the incident meant for them. The impact has not been as pronounced as it might have been , thanks to
our diversification across geographies, across product, across service lanes and brands, and it is slowly
settling down. We continue to be transparent about what happened, what we have learned, and how we
are committed to improving ourselves.
I also want to be clear about the scope. This affected only our publicly trusted TLS business, which was
about 1% of our revenue. Our digital signatures, e sign, and all five enterprise platforms are not affected.
Given the limited returns from TLS relative to our overall business, we have decided to exit the sale of
publicly trusted TLS certificates and focus fully on our core platform. In the US, the only customer,
University Federation, who will be directly affected was using our CertiN ext product and TLS certificate.
They have decided to continue to work with us and asked us to provide the TLS certificate to any other
TLS vendor on a subcontract model.
This is a big morale boost for us, and this is likely to considerably reduce our reputation risk in The US

we are on track to achieve the target set out of 500 MW.

year, basically, we are at 145 kW or million units. On the financial performance of Ravindra Energy, this
basically includes the entire solar business, which is basically the IPP, the EPC of our projects, and the
electricity generation and trading. For the quarter ended, the turnover for electricity generation was INR 31
crores. Electricity trading , we are at INR 26 crores . And t he revenue from EPC and service concession

the lower EPC and CA revenue book in the comparative period Q1 this year versus last year.

Rural markets continue to outperform urban markets, although urban consumption is showing
signs of gradual recovery. Modern trade and e-commerce and quick commerce maintained
strong growth, while general trade remained subdued.
The FMCG sector continues to face a challenging operating environment with geopolitical
uncertainty, elevated commodity prices and changing consumer behavior affecting both growth
and profitability.
The ongoing conflict in West Asia has resulted in sharp increases in crude derivatives, chemicals
and packaging costs, while the deficient monsoon has raised concerns around agricultural output,
food inflation and rural purchasing power. The immediate challenge for the industry is managing
input cost inflation without affecting consumer affordability and demand.
Against this backdrop, let me turn to Jyothy Lab's performance. Q2 was particularly challenging
for profitability, although our underlying business continued to deliver healthy growth. Revenue
from operations increased by 3.3% to INR760 crores, while reported volumes declined
marginally, primarily reflecting the exit of the Pril and Fa businesses following the expiry of the
brand license agreement in May 2026.
Excluding Pril and Fa, the company delivered a healthy 12.4% value growth and 8.1% volume
growth during the quarter, supported by our core brands, selective pricing, new launches and
distribution expansion. For the first half, the corresponding growth was 10.2% in value and 6.2%
in volume.

10.4% value growth. Detergent powders and bars maintained their growth momentum.

White. Our fabric conditioner, Ujala Young & Fresh continues to perform well, reinforcing our
confidence in these emerging formats and their long-term growth potential.

Mahesh Iyer: Thank you, Purva. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us as we
discuss the Q2 FY27 financial and operating performance. Before we begin, I would like to introduce
the management team joining me on the call today. Vikram Lalvani, Managing Di rector and CEO of
Sterling Holiday Resorts; K.S. Ramakrishnan, Managing Director of DEI; Vishal Suri, Managing
Director of SOTC; Debasis Nandy, who is the Group CFO for Thomas Cook (India) Group; Mr. Brijesh
Modi, who is the CFO at Thomas Cook (India) Limi ted; Krishna Kumar, who is the CFO at Sterling
Holiday Resorts; and Urvashi Butani, who heads Investor Relationships.
Quarter 2 was a quarter in which we began to see recovery with momentum improving across parts
of our business, although at varying levels. The external environment continues to be uncertain, and
some of our international operations are still working throu gh the effects of the geopolitical
disruptions. But the quarter also showed us where the demand is holding up, where activity is
picking up and importantly, how the cost agility we have built into our operations is helping us
respond to changing business conditions. This flexibility allows us to better align costs with business
volumes, manage the impact on profitability and protect our underlying performance even as we
navigate an uneven recovery.
The quarter's performance reflects 2 things. First, the strong recovery and growth in parts of our
India portfolio; second, the impact of conflict in West Asia, which is largely limited to a few
businesses with direct exposure to the region, that is Desert Adventures and DEI and parts of our
long-haul outbound portfolio. These businesses are still not where we would like them to be, but
they are clearly better than they were 3 months ago.
Some of the key performance highlights for the quarter.
Our consolidated total income stood at INR 20,030 million, shows a 5% decline over the same
quarter last year. Our India Travel segment saw clear signs of recovery, and I will detail this in a little
more when I talk about the segments. We ended the quarter just 6% below last year with EBIT
margins holding a healthy 3.8%. Our international business continued to face a challenging
environment, particularly given the geopolitical situation, which had a direct impact on the
operations of Desert Adventures and DEI.
Overall, EBIT margins for the Travel segment have shown an improvement on a sequential basis
from 2.4% to 2.9% in Q2 of FY 2027. Our consolidated PBT before exceptional item stood at INR 848
million, which was broadly at the same level as last year despite the reduction in overall income.
This is particularly noteworthy given the shortfall of almost over INR 1,036 million in income from
operations coming largely out of Desert Adventures and DEI.
What is also encouraging is that we have actually managed to improve our PBT margin to 4.2%
compared to 4% last year despite the pressure on top line. On the distribution front, we continue
to expand our reach with the branch network growing by 7% year -on-year via the franchisee route
to 310 branches at the end of September 2026 compared to 289 branches. This takes our network
to its highest ever level, further strengthening our presence and accessibility across markets.
In terms of technology, we have further enhanced our AI -powered chatbot with the integration of
DynaPack, our dynamic inventory customization feature. While still it is in the initial phase, this
enables the bot to generate personalized travel itineraries with real -time pricing, allowing
customers to explore holiday options based on their individual preferences.

Anoop Poojari: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on HealthCare Global
Enterprises Q2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings conference call. We have with us Dr. Manish Mattoo,
Executive Director and CEO of the company, Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Chief Financial Officer, and
Mr. Ravi Gothwal, Head of Investor Relations. We would like to begin the call with opening
remarks from Manish, following which we will have the forum open for an interactive question-
and-answer session.
Before we start, I would like to point out that some statements made in today's call may be
forward-looking in nature, and a disclaimer to this effect has been included in the earnings
presentation shared with you earlier. I would now like to invite Manish to make his opening
remarks.
Manish Mattoo: Thank you, Anoop. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us for HCG's Quarter
2 and H1 FY27 earnings call.
I am pleased to share that we have sustained our growth momentum into the second quarter,
supported by healthy patient demand and improving revenue mix, and steady progress across
our strategic and operational priorities. As highlighted in our previous earnings call, our strategic
priorities remain centered on profitable growth, improving asset utilization, strengthening
clinical differentiation, and optimizing our revenue mix.
We are encouraged by the progress made during the quarter across all these areas. Coming to
our financial performance, I would like to highlight that all financial figures presented today
exclude the Milann Fertility business, which was divested in June 20 26. The corresponding
prior-year figures have also been adjusted accordingly to ensure a like-for-like comparison.
In Quarter 2 FY 2027, HCG delivered revenue of INR 7,318 million, representing a growth of
16% year- on- year. Revenue growth, excluding our North Bengaluru new hospital, was 14%

year- on- year. The growth was broad -based across our operating clusters, primarily driven by
a 9% increase in patient volumes, while average revenue per patient increased by 7% year -on-
year.
The improvement in ARPP was supported by a favorable pay or mix and an increasing
contribution from high -complexity oncology treatments. This included a 37% year -on-year
increase in robotic surgeries, alongside growing adoption of other advanced therapies and
surgical procedures across our network.
As we have consistently emphasized, our objective is not merely to drive higher patient
volumes, but to enhance the quantity and quality of our revenues through a greater contribution
from complex oncology procedures and improved pay or mix, superior clinical outcomes, and
higher productivity across our specialized oncology ecosystem.
In line with this strategy, we continue to focus on expanding our non-institutional business while
progressively optimizing our exposure to lower-realization segments. These efforts are yielding
encouraging results, with non-institutional revenue growing by 21% year-on-year, resulting in
an improvement of over 300 basis points in its revenue share to 69%.
On the profitability front, EBITDA for the quarter, including North Bengaluru loss of INR 61
million, was INR 1,425 million, representing growth of 17% year -on-year, with EBITDA
margins improved to 19.7% compared to 19.2% in Q2FY26.

If you really look at it on a like -to-like basis, excluding the wage revision impact, EBITDA

good progress, with its EBITDA loss reducing to INR 61 million during this quarter. Our focus
remains on accelerating clinical ramp -up, improving capacity utilization, and progressively
reducing operating losses.
Let me now take you through the performance across our operating clusters.
Starting with the South cluster, the revenue stood at INR 2,941 million. Delivering a strong
growth of 18% and contributing to 40% of our overall revenue. Growth was supported by a 14%
improvement in ARPP and a 4% increase in patient volumes, with a strong contribution from
our Bengaluru Center of Excellence and the progressive ramp -up of our North Bengaluru
hospital.
ARPP improvement across the cluster was also aided by a favorable payor mix and higher
contribution of high-end procedures and therapies.
Moving to the West cluster. Revenue stood at INR 3,147 million, registering 10% year-on-year
growth and contributing 43% to overall revenue. Growth was primarily driven by a 7% increase
in patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 3%, supported by a favorable payor mix.

The Maharashtra region delivered a strong performance with a mid -teens growth, driven by
healthy patient demand and improved realization, led by a favorable pay or mix shift. This was
partially offset by relatively moderated growth across our Gujarat centers, largely on account of
deliberate rationalization of institutional mix to improve profitability.
Turning to the East cluster. Revenue stood at INR 928 million, representing 23% year-on-year

patient volumes, while ARPP improved by 5% year -on-year. Growth was broad -based across

Performance was supported by stronger patient inflows across radiation oncology, aided by the
addition of a new radiation therapy machine, as well as increased medical oncology therapies
following the addition of 13 new beds.
I would also like to highlight some of the key developments during the quarter.
During Q2 FY 2027, we added 25 operational beds across our network, comprising 13 beds in
Kenya, seven beds in Kolkata, and five beds at Nagpur. With these additions, we have
operationalized a total of 146 beds in H1 FY 2027, further strengthening our capa city across
existing and newer facilities.
Alongside capacity expansion, we continued to invest in advanced medical technologies. During
the quarter, we operationalized the MR -LINAC, a highly advanced adaptive radiation therapy
system at our North Bengaluru hospital, and added a cardiac surgical robotic system at our multi-
specialty hospital in Ahmedabad, further strengthening our technology -led treatment
capabilities.
On the clinical front, key milestones included the first CAR T-cell therapy at HCG Ahmedabad,

to invite Mr. Paresh Dattani, the Chairman and Managing Director, to share his opening remarks.
Paresh Dattani: Thank you, Jude, and a very good evening to everyone joining us today. When we spoke to you
in the last call, the first quarter of FY 2027 had unfolded against a backdrop of significant global
volatility, driven largely by the conflict in West Asia and its effect on energy and raw material
markets in general.
In that environment, our priorities were clear: secure raw material supplies, place our offerings
with customers, and keep our plants running without disruption and at high efficiency. The
second quarter built on that groundwork as raw material and product prices stabilized. Customers
who had deferred purchases during the uncertainty of Q1 returned to normal buying patterns.
Domestic demand for our products stayed strong throughout the period. Our performance this
quarter was driven primarily by the continued ramping up of our Punjab facility, which is now
contributing meaningfully to volumes, along with higher capacity utilizations across our
operations.
Consolidated sales volumes rose to 1.22 lakh metric tons from 96,000 metric tons in the first
quarter. As a result, consolidated revenue from operations grew 35.16% quarter -on-quarter to
INR1,804 crore s, driven by the ramp -up at Punjab and higher selling prices. Consolidated
EBITDA rose 43.2% sequentially and 144.94% year-on-year to INR155 crores.
With higher volumes in Punjab, our fixed costs were absorbed over a larger base, and a better

sequentially, while consolidated EBITDA rose by about INR47 crore s quarter-on-quarter.
Further, I am happy to inform that this quarter, our Punjab plant has become PAT positive, due

INR61 crores, and 204% year-on-year.

IDC has since released its numbers for the September quarter, and the decline has come in at 20.1% year-on-year, which is 62.7 million units shipped as against 78.5 million shipped in the same quarter last year. That's close to 16 million fewer computers in a single quarter. IDC attributes this to higher prices, supply constraints and inventory challenges and expects a decline of similar order in December quarter as well and prices are expected to remain elevated. For the full year 2026, IDC continues to project a decline of 11.3%, which is on a base of 284 million computers sold in 2025 that's roughly 30 million decline of computers sold over last year and we are not factoring in any growth in computing demand. This is a very sharp decline for this industry and it is coming totally in the second half, that's from July to December of 2026. Now how long does this last? I would rather you hear it from the people who make the components and people who make the computers than from me. Michael Dell, the founder of Dell Technologies, said in an interview with CNBC on 13th October that he expects the memory shortage to get worse next year in terms of demand and supply. And that in his own words, it may well be a 4-year problem because there's just not enough supply. Sanjay Mehrotra, the Chief Executive of Micron, one of the 3 largest memory manufacturers in the world, said on its earnings call on 30th September 2026 that Micron expects memory and storage supply conditions to be and I quote "much tighter in fiscal year 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026" and it does not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance. The Chief Financial Officer, Kim Woo-hyun, said and I quote "Memory supply cannot keep pace with this level of demand and growth" and described the shortfall as a constraint projected to continue through 2030. Thermal, around 36 or almost 39 gigawatt is under construction and further 23 gigawatt has been awarded as the government targets towards almost 300 gigawatt of thermal capacity by FY '30. And this gives us a steady pipeline of boiler and turbine to lift. Nuclear power. The Shanti Act has opened up the sector to private players and groups such as Tata, Reliance, Adani has responded to the first small modular reactor tender. So capacity is targeted to grow from 8.8 gigawatt to 22.5 gigawatt by FY '30. Wind, which is our one of the dominant segment has added a record 6 gigawatt in FY26, up by 46% with 29 gigawatts under construction and a target of 100 gigawatt by 2030. So while we remain watchful of pressure in steel cost escalation, our presence across these sectors reduces our dependence on any single cycle. Let me talk about performance. Pradeep touched upon briefly, and I will be quick here. So we delivered a strong first half. Revenue from operations grew 36% to INR656 crores. EBITDA grew by 25% and PAT grew by 22%. And in Q2, revenue grew by 32% with an EBITDA margin of 20%. As Pradeep mentioned, our order book in just 13 weeks grew by 26%, and we are close to almost INR600 crores of order booking with an inquiry pipeline of INR6,700 crores, which gives us a strong visibility for the rest of the year. So in terms of utilization was 78% for the first half with a yield of 2.24% in line with FY26 levels and within our historical range of 73% to 84%. As Pradeep touch upon the seasonality aspect. So Q2 utilization in India was 71% compared to 86% in Q1, reflecting the normal monsoon slowdown. However, it was ahead of the 70% we reported last year and a yield improvement to 2.20% from 2.04. Middle East utilization was 86% for the first half, rising to 87% in Q2 and at a yield of 3.8%, well above our target of 3.5%. So we now enter the second half, our seasonally strongest period when utilization in India typically picks up sharply as project activity resumes after monsoon. So our revenue mix is changing, and I will not dwell too much into it because Pradeep has already mentioned. So looking ahead, we are confident that we have a strong wind runway, support from our core business, growing asset-light crane stream and 2 growth engines. I mean, Saudi capex is deferred. Let me give a quick update on the Middle East as well. So shipping and port disruption in West Asia have delayed new crane deployment in Saudi Arabia, and we have moved part of the capex to FY28. So this is a timing issue, not a demand issue.

PRESS RELEASE
Shyam Metalics Reaffirms Credit Ratings of ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and ‘CRISIL A1+’; Bank
Debt Ratings Enhanced to ₹4,500 Crore
Kolkata, November 09, 2026 — Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (SMEL), one of India’s leading
integrated multi-metal producing companies, announced today that CRISIL Ratings Limited has reaffirmed
the company’s long-term rating at ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’ and short-term rating at ‘CRISIL A1+’. CRISIL
has enhanced the rated bank debt amount to ₹4,500 Crore (up from ₹3,600 Crore), and reaffirmed the rating
for its ₹50 Crore Commercial Paper programme at ‘CRISIL A1+’.
The reaffirmation underscores the Shyam Metalics Group’s established market position in the steel sector,
strong financial risk profile, healthy operating performance, and high operational efficiency driven by
deeply integrated operations.
Key Highlights Driving the Rating Reaffirmation
 Robust Operating Performance & Growth: Operating profitability and top-line growth continue
to strengthen, supported by higher sales volumes across core product segments. Profitability
metrics are projected to expand further in the upcoming fiscal year.
 Capacity Expansion & Diversification: The group continues to scale its aggregate production
capacities. Strategic expansion into flat steel, pig iron, stainless steel, and aluminium foils
reinforces its product diversification and market reach.
 Integrated Value Chain & Efficiency: Operations cover the complete value chain from raw
materials to value-added finished products. Operational efficiency is heavily supported by captive
power generation, waste heat recovery plants, coal washeries, and dedicated railway sidings.
Planned coal block operationalization will further strengthen long-term energy and raw material
security.
 Strong Balance Sheet & Conservative Leverage: The group maintains a conservative financial
structure with a strong net worth, significant liquidity surplus, and minimal debt reliance, leading
to low gearing and strong interest coverage.
 Disciplined Funding of Growth Capex: Multi-year capital expenditure plans for capacity
expansion will be funded predominantly through strong annual internal accruals and available cash
reserves, ensuring debt metrics remain at safe levels.
 Commitment to ESG & Sustainability: SMEL continues to advance its environmental goals by
increasing its renewable energy consumption, maintaining Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD)
operations for full water reuse, and adhering to international standards for emissions reporting.

Management Commentary
"The reaffirmation of our 'CRISIL AA+/Stable' and 'CRISIL A1+' ratings, along with the enhancement of
our rated bank facilities, validates the strength of our business strategy, robust balance sheet, and disciplined
execution capabilities. Even as we undertake major brownfield capacity expansions to enhance scale and
product diversification, our focus remains anchored on prudent capital allocation, maintaining strong
liquidity, and creating long-term value for all stakeholders." - Mr. Brij Bhushan Agarwal, Chairman &
Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited
